policy_statement: Approve and implement Armenia's updated NDC (2021-2030) with an unconditional target of 40% GHG emissions reduction below 1990 levels by 2030.
source_quote: “Thus, The Republic of Armenia ratified the Paris Agreement in 2017, and on April 22, 2021 the Government of Armenia approved Armenia's Nationally Determined Contributions for a ten-year implementation period (2021-2030), setting the new unconditional mitigation target of 40 per cent reduction below 1990 emissions levels, to be achieved in 2030.”
extraction_rationale: This is a formal government-approved target with a quantified reduction level and deadline, meeting the criteria for a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Increase the share of solar electricity generation to at least 15% (or 1.8 billion kWh) by 2030 under the Energy Sector Development Strategic Program.
source_quote: “The most recently adopted Energy Sector Development Strategic Program aimed at increasing the share of solar energy generation in total to at least 15% by 2030.”
extraction_rationale: A quantified renewable energy target with a deadline constitutes a mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Join the NDC Partnership to support implementation of Armenia's NDCs.
source_quote: “In 2018, the Republic of Armenia joined the NDC Partnership to support the implementation of "Nationally Determined Contributions".”
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional commitment (joining an implementation partnership) explicitly tied to NDC implementation.

policy_statement: Raise Lake Sevan water level by 6.5 meters within 30 years to increase water reserves.
source_quote: “It is planned to raise the level of Lake Sevan by 6.5 m within a period of 30 years. This will provide additional water reserves, which will serve as a highly important and strategically significant natural resource for energy and other economic sectors.”
section_header: 1.1 Location, State Administration, Climate and Natural Resources
extraction_rationale: A planned quantified water-reserve intervention with a timeframe; while not explicitly framed as climate adaptation, it is a water-resource resilience measure.

policy_statement: Apply energy-saving and energy-efficiency measures in state-funded construction via a 2014 government decree.
source_quote: “For this reason, back in 2014 the RA Government adopted a Decree "On the application of measures aimed at energy saving and increasing energy efficiency in facilities built at the expense of state funds"...”
extraction_rationale: A government decree is a binding mechanism requiring energy-saving measures in publicly funded buildings.

policy_statement: Mandate compliance with energy-efficiency requirements for new residential buildings and state-funded construction/renovation via amendments to the Energy Saving and Renewable Energy Law (2016) and technical regulation (2018).
source_quote: “...later Amendment to the 'RA Energy Saving and Renewable Energy" Law, 2016, providing for mandatory compliance with the EE requirements in newly constructed residential buildings and in facilities under construction (reconstructed, repaired) at the expense of state funds, with the subsequent adoption of technical regulation setting energy requirements for energy saving in the mentioned facilities (2018).”
extraction_rationale: Explicit mandatory compliance and technical regulation constitute enforceable building energy-efficiency policy.

policy_statement: Implement forest sector reforms (concept, strategy, action plan) to establish sustainable forest management, increase forest cover, improve species composition, and mitigate climate change impacts on forest ecosystems.
source_quote: “On November 30, 2017, the Government of the RA approved the concept of reforms, strategy and action plan for Forest Sector. The reforms aimed at the establishment of a sustainable forest management system to develop and implement state unified policy in the field of preservation, protection, reproduction and use of the forests in Armenia, elimination or mitigation of the negative impact of climate change on the sustainability of forest ecosystems, increase of forest covered areas and improving the species composition...”
extraction_rationale: A government-approved strategy/action plan with specific forest management interventions and explicit climate-change impact mitigation on ecosystems.

policy_statement: Approve a five-year list of measures and responsible agencies to fulfill UNFCCC/Paris obligations, including a 2017-2021 measures list approved by Protocol Decree N49-8 (Dec 8, 2016).
source_quote: “Since the ratification of the UNFCCC, the Government of Armenia once every five years approves a list of measures as well as assigns responsible agencies for implementing the country's commitments under international environmental conventions, including the UNFCCC. The list of measures to be implemented during 2017-2021 to fulfill obligations and provisions arising from the UNFCCC and Paris Agreement was approved by the Government Protocol Decree N 49-8 of December 8, 2016.”
section_header: 1.11 Institutional arrangements for continuous development of national communications and biennial update reports
extraction_rationale: A formal government decree establishing measures and responsibilities for climate commitments is a policy instrument (governance/MRV enabling).

policy_statement: Establish an Inter-agency Coordinating Council on UNFCCC implementation (2012) to coordinate climate policy and approve national reports (inventories, NCs, BURs).
source_quote: “National climate change policies and actions are coordinated by the Inter-agency Coordinating Council for Implementation of Requirements and Provision of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, which was established in 2012 by the Prime Minister's Decree. The Council has the authority to coordinate reporting on climate change and ensure coherent policies for achievement of Armenia's commitments under UNFCCC and is the decisionmaking body that approves the final drafts such as the national GHG inventories, NCs, BURs.”
section_header: 1.11 Institutional arrangements for continuous development of national communications and biennial update reports
extraction_rationale: A Prime Minister’s decree establishing a coordinating/approving body is a concrete governance policy enabling climate action and reporting.

policy_statement: Develop a comprehensive domestic MRV framework through the UNDP-GEF CBIT project to shift from ad hoc reporting to continuous MRV and track NDC progress.
source_quote: “However, the main support with establishment of an enhanced transparency framework enabling shifting from the current practice of ad hoc reporting to a continuous process of MRV is to be provided through the UNDP-GEF 'Building Armenia's national transparency framework under Paris Agreement' project to be implemented under the Capacity Building Initiative for Transparency (CBIT). This will allow the country to track its progress against its commitments under the NDC and ensure national reporting under the Convention and the Paris Agreement.”
extraction_rationale: A named project with a defined institutional outcome (continuous MRV) directly tied to Paris Agreement transparency and NDC tracking.

policy_statement: Implement the Republic of Armenia Energy Sector Development Strategic Program (till 2040) and its Action Plan to maximize renewables and energy savings, extend nuclear plant life, build North-South 400 kV corridor, and liberalize the electricity market.
source_quote: “The Strategy defines the main priorities for the development of the Energy sector, which are the maximum utilization of renewable energy and energy saving potential, life extension of the Armenian Nuclear Power Plant, construction of North-South transit corridor with 400 kV power transmission line and gradual liberalization of the electricity market.”
section_header: 3.2 Assessment of mitigation potential in Energy Sector

section_header: 3.2 Assessment of mitigation potential in Energy Sector

section_header: 3.2 Assessment of mitigation potential in Energy Sector

section_header: 3.2 Assessment of mitigation potential in Energy Sector
extraction_rationale: A specific market rule enabling distributed solar economics; clear regulatory mechanism.

section_header: 3.2 Assessment of mitigation potential in Energy Sector
extraction_rationale: Binding procurement requirement is a concrete policy instrument driving efficiency.

source_quote: “By 2030, the City will have a network of intelligent charging that supports grid reliability and resilience, maximized efficiency, reduced emissions, accessibility for all, and lower costs for all residents. Incentivize internet-connected charging infrastructure with the ability to manage the start and end time and charge rate across 24 hours while still meeting the driver's needs.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit incentive for smart charging and a 2030 network outcome; implementable program.

parent_statement: Transportation Electrification Goal 2
policy_statement: Adopt new energy and building codes to simplify EV charging deployment and lower barriers, including requirements for EV chargers/EV-ready construction.
source_quote: “Adopt new energy and building codes that address future EV charging needs and enable a more equitable approach by simplifying the charging network and lowering barriers to entry for installing EV charging.”
extraction_rationale: Regulatory commitment (code adoption) to enable charging infrastructure; concrete policy lever.

policy_statement: Transportation Electrification Goal 3: Make the Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos area a leader in transportation electrification by adopting policies and technologies that maximize economic and health benefits and support industry growth.
source_quote: “The Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos area is a leader in transportation electrification by adopting policies and technologies that maximize economic and health benefits while supporting the growth of this emerging industry.”
extraction_rationale: Stated regional leadership goal with associated strategies; umbrella goal.

parent_statement: Transportation Electrification Goal 3
policy_statement: Create a regional coalition within the five-county MSA to support EV adoption with inclusive government, business, and community stakeholders.
source_quote: “The City will take the lead in creating a regional coalition to support EV adoption within the fivecounty MSA. The coalition will consist of an inclusive group of government, business, and community stakeholders.”
extraction_rationale: Specific governance/coordination action to accelerate EV adoption regionally.

parent_statement: Transportation Electrification Goal 3
policy_statement: Pursue grant funding to pilot emerging transportation electrification technologies and scale successful pilots, ensuring low-income communities and communities of color benefit first.
source_quote: “Pursue grant funding opportunities to test new technologies and take successful pilots into more widespread applications. Increase engagement with governmental agencies, research institutions, etc.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit pursuit of grants and piloting/scaling; funding mechanism is named.

policy_statement: Food and Product Consumption Goal 1: By 2030, ensure access to a community-driven food system that addresses food insecurity, prioritizes regenerative agriculture, promotes plant-based foods, and minimizes food waste.
source_quote: “By 2030, ensure all Austinites can access a food system that is communitydriven, addresses food insecurity, prioritizes regenerative agriculture, supports dietary and health agency, promotes plant-based foods, and minimizes food waste.”
extraction_rationale: Time-bound goal with defined system attributes; umbrella goal with strategies.

parent_statement: Food and Product Consumption Goal 1
policy_statement: Apply a purchasing framework and build regional networks to increase institutional and corporate procurement of pro-climate, pro-health food options.
source_quote: “Apply a purchasing framework, support supply-chain infrastructure, and build a regional food system network to bolster institutional and corporate food procurement of proclimate, pro-health options.”
extraction_rationale: Specific intervention (purchasing framework and network) to shift food procurement; actionable policy/program.

parent_statement: Food and Product Consumption Goal 1
policy_statement: Implement community-driven programs with economic incentives for local food establishments to increase plant-based menu choices and generate funding for local pro-climate food organizations/producers.
source_quote: “Implement community-driven programs to incentivize and promote more affordable and culturally relevant pro-climate, pro-health choices in prepared and retail food options, focusing on minimizing displacement. Offer economic incentives for local food establishments that offer an increasing minimum percentage of plant-based menu choices.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit incentives and program implementation; financial instrument to shift diets and reduce emissions.

parent_statement: Food and Product Consumption Goal 1
policy_statement: Conduct a food waste root cause analysis and implement changes to increase food waste reduction practices by 50%.
source_quote: “Conduct a food waste root cause analysis and implement changes informed by the analysis to increase food waste reduction practices by 50%. These practices should support the U.S. EPA Food Recovery Hierarchy's highest and best-use model and include single-family, multi-family, and commercial properties.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified target (50% increase in reduction practices) and specific analytic step; actionable policy.

policy_statement: Food and Product Consumption Goal 2: By 2030, reduce greenhouse gas emissions from institutional, commercial, and government purchasing by at least 50%.
source_quote: “By 2030, reduce greenhouse gas emissions from institutional, commercial, and government purchasing by at least 50%.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified emissions-reduction target with deadline; umbrella goal with strategies.

parent_statement: Food and Product Consumption Goal 2
policy_statement: Develop a methodology and baseline to measure lifecycle GHG emissions and other impacts from non-residential purchasing.
source_quote: “Develop a methodology to measure lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions and other environmental and social impacts from non-residential purchasing and identify a baseline for tracking progress.”
extraction_rationale: Concrete measurement/baseline development action necessary for implementing the purchasing emissions goal.

parent_statement: Food and Product Consumption Goal 2
policy_statement: Recruit at least 50% of large institutional purchasers (2,500+ employees) and at least 2,500 local organizations to adopt sustainability procurement standards/guidelines.
source_quote: “Recruit at least 50% of local large institutional purchasers (2,500+ employees) and at least 2,500 local organizations of all sizes to collaboratively adopt a set of environmental and social sustainability procurement standards and/or guidelines.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified recruitment targets and adoption of standards; concrete policy/program action.

policy_statement: Food and Product Consumption Goal 3: Aggressively pursue waste reduction, organics composting, and recycling to meet the 2023 Austin Resource Recovery Comprehensive Plan disposal-rate goals (4 lb/day near term; 1 lb/day over time).
source_quote: “Aggressively pursue waste reduction, organics composting, and recycling to achieve the waste reduction goals in the 2023 Austin Resource Recovery Comprehensive Plan*. *The plan calls for maintaining a community-wide per capita disposal rate of 4 pounds disposed per Austin Resource Recovery (ARR)-serviced household per day in the near term and working to achieve 1 pound disposed per ARR-serviced household per day over time.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit quantified disposal-rate targets and commitment to pursue waste reduction/composting/recycling; umbrella goal with strategies.

parent_statement: Food and Product Consumption Goal 3
policy_statement: Create equitably distributed Eco-hubs for borrowing, reuse, and repair services, with demographic tracking of users.
source_quote: “Create 'Eco-hubs' that provide equitably distributed in-person neighborhood centers for borrowing, reuse, and repair services. Collect and publish demographic data on Eco-hub users to ensure equitable accessibility and use.”
extraction_rationale: Specific program creation with equity monitoring; concrete intervention to reduce waste.

parent_statement: Food and Product Consumption Goal 3
policy_statement: Offer financial incentives (e.g., point-of-sale rebates or sales tax holiday) for lower-impact products, repair services, and rentals, including alternatives to single-use plastics.
source_quote: “Offer financial incentives, such as point-of-sale rebates or a sales tax holiday, to encourage consumers to choose products, repair services, and rentals with lower negative environmental and social impact, including alternatives to single-use plastics.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit financial incentive instruments; concrete policy lever to reduce consumption and waste.

policy_statement: Natural Systems Goal 1: By 2030, legally protect an additional 20,000 acres of carbon pools and manage all new and existing natural areas (~70,000 acres total) focusing on resilience.
source_quote: “By 2030, legally protect an additional 20,000 acres of carbon pools on natural lands and manage all new and existing natural areas (approximately 70,000 acres total), focusing on resilience.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified land protection and management target with deadline; umbrella goal with strategies.

parent_statement: Natural Systems Goal 1
policy_statement: Legally protect natural lands via acquisition and conservation easements, prioritizing new conservation lands in Travis County Eastern Planning Areas and benefits for low-income communities and communities of color.
source_quote: “Identify additional woodland, grassland, and wetland systems for protection, focusing on new conservation lands in the Travis County Eastern Planning Areas while prioritizing benefits for lowincome communities and communities of color. Legally protect lands through mechanisms such as fee simple acquisition and conservation easements.”
extraction_rationale: Specific land protection mechanisms and geographic/equity priorities; implementable conservation policy.

parent_statement: Natural Systems Goal 1
policy_statement: Pursue innovative financial methods to purchase/protect lands, including sales tax revenue, development fees, bonds, and local carbon credit/offset markets.
source_quote: “Identify and pursue innovative financial methods to purchase or protect lands such as: - Use sales tax revenue, development fees, or bonds, especially when linked to multibenefits and resilience for low-income communities and communities of color. - Consider local carbon credit markets or offset programs that include natural lands, sustainable working lands, and the potential for stormwater credit trading.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit financing mechanisms for conservation; qualifies as financial instruments supporting climate-related land protection.

parent_statement: Natural Systems Goal 1
policy_statement: Manage protected natural lands for climate resilience through restoration/management guides, soil health, native diversity, and facilitating shifts to more resilient states.
source_quote: “Prepare natural lands for climate change and avoid catastrophic loss of carbon pools through active, intentional, and holistic management. Create, update, and implement restoration and management guides for all protected lands under City and County jurisdiction.”
extraction_rationale: Concrete management commitment to address climate impacts and protect carbon pools; adaptation-focused NBS action.

parent_statement: Natural Systems Goal 1
policy_statement: Protect municipal source water quantity and quality against climate threats (heat, drought, flood, wildfire) through land protection, partnerships, and green infrastructure/riparian restoration.
source_quote: “Protect quantity and quality of source water for municipal supply and regional environmental flows - especially in the face of climate change-driven threats like heat, drought, flood, and wildfire. Improve groundwater recharge through expanding green infrastructure, riparian restoration programs, and incentives on public and private lands in Austin and upstream.”
extraction_rationale: Explicitly hazard-motivated water-source protection actions; clear adaptation policy using ecosystem measures.

policy_statement: Natural Systems Goal 2: By 2030, protect 500,000 acres of farmland from development in the five-county region through legal protections or regenerative agriculture programs.
source_quote: “By 2030, protect 500,000 acres of farmland from development in the fivecounty region* through legal protections or regenerative agriculture programs.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified acreage protection target with deadline; umbrella goal with strategies.

parent_statement: Natural Systems Goal 2
policy_statement: Protect prime farmland soils from development using conservation bonds, land trusts, conservation easements, and similar methods.
source_quote: “Identify lands with prime farmland soils and farmlands of unique and local significance as defined by the Sustainable SITES Initiative in the 5-county region and protect them from development. This can be done through land conservation bonds, agricultural land trusts such as the American Farmland Trust, Natural Resource Conservation Service and Trust for Public Lands programs, Travis County Conservation Easements, and similar methods.”
extraction_rationale: Specific legal/financial mechanisms for farmland protection; concrete conservation policy.

parent_statement: Natural Systems Goal 2
policy_statement: Provide direct financial assistance for farmers (especially farmers of color) to implement carbon-related soil programs or regenerative practices, including City-funded micro-grants and down payment support.
source_quote: “Support farmers in the 5-county region who want to implement carbon-related soil programs or regenerative agricultural practices by providing direct financial assistance, specifically for farmers of color. Provide City-funded micro-grants to help cover startup costs for regenerative agriculture or conservation irrigation equipment for small-scale and local farmers.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit direct financial assistance and micro-grants; clear financial instrument supporting climate-relevant land management.

policy_statement: Natural Systems Goal 3: Achieve at least 50% citywide tree canopy cover by 2050, focusing on equitable canopy increases.
source_quote: “Achieve at least 50% citywide tree canopy cover by 2050, focusing on increasing canopy cover equitably.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified canopy target with deadline; umbrella goal with strategies.

parent_statement: Natural Systems Goal 3
policy_statement: Adopt a 'no net loss' policy for tree canopy on public lands, including replacement requirements and canopy targets by public land type.
source_quote: “Adopt a 'no net loss' policy for tree canopy on public lands. Require tree canopy replacement for any necessary tree removal on public lands. Allow for on- or off-site canopy mitigation.”
extraction_rationale: Regulatory/operational policy commitment with clear rule (no net loss) and replacement requirement.

parent_statement: Natural Systems Goal 3
policy_statement: Increase City funding for community tree-planting programs focused on low-income communities and communities of color.
source_quote: “Increase City funding for community tree-planting programs focused on low-income communities and communities of color.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit funding increase for tree planting; financial instrument supporting canopy expansion.

policy_statement: Natural Systems Goal 4: By 2030, include all City-owned lands under a management plan that results in neutral or negative carbon emissions and maximizes community co-benefits.
source_quote: “By 2030, include all City-owned lands under a management plan that results in neutral or negative carbon emissions and maximizes community co-benefits.”
extraction_rationale: Time-bound management planning requirement with carbon outcome; umbrella goal with strategies.

parent_statement: Natural Systems Goal 4
policy_statement: Use carbon-negative or low-carbon land management practices on public lands (e.g., soil protection, limited/no mowing, converting high-water-use landscapes to native plantings).
source_quote: “Use carbon-negative or low-carbon management practices, such as soil protection, limited mowing, no-mow, and conversion of high water use landscapes into native plantings.”
extraction_rationale: Specific operational practices to achieve carbon-neutral/negative land management; concrete action.

parent_statement: Natural Systems Goal 4
policy_statement: Reclaim underused public spaces and convert unnecessary impervious cover to green infrastructure/green spaces, including a study to convert an ambitious share of City surface parking lots.
source_quote: “Convert non-functional or unnecessary impervious cover to green infrastructure, green spaces, or natural vegetation that provides open space access or ecosystem functions. This should especially be done on City lands, such as parks with underutilized parking areas. A study should be conducted to examine the use of surface-level parking lots on City property to develop a plan to convert an ambitious percentage of these to functional green uses when feasible.”
extraction_rationale: Specific land conversion actions plus a required study/plan; concrete nature-based infrastructure policy.

policy_statement: Create reporting mechanisms: annual implementation status report, annual community GHG inventory calculation, and progress reports from implementation teams to boards/commissions, with public posting and delivery to City Council.
source_quote: “In collaboration with City departments and other organizations, the Office of Sustainability will create the following reporting mechanisms to keep stakeholders updated on progress: - An annual report summarizing the implementation status of the Climate Equity Plan's strategies - Annual calculation of the Austin Community Greenhouse Gas Inventory - Progress reports from Implementation Teams to City Boards and Commissions, where appropriate”
extraction_rationale: Concrete accountability and reporting commitments with specified outputs and cadence; supports climate governance.

policy_statement: Implement Bahrain's building codes enacted in 2009 requiring the ground floor of new buildings to be 1.5 meters above the pavement surface level.
source_quote: “Some adaptation measures have already taken place in certain sectors. For example, while not explicitly in reference to sea level rise, Bahrain's building codes enacted in 2009 call for the height of the ground floor of a new building being 1.5 meters above the level of the pavement surface (KoB, 2009). This can build resilience of future buildings against future sea level rise, at least in a scenario where future sea level rise is limited to 1.5 meters above current MSL.”
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory requirement (building code specification with a numeric standard) that functions as an adaptation measure for sea level rise/flooding risk.

policy_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP): achieve 5% of energy (255 MW installed capacity) from renewable sources by 2025 and 10% (710 MW installed capacity) by 2035, using solar, wind, and waste-to-energy technologies.
source_quote: “NREAP has two primary targets: having 5% of energy (255 MW of installed capacity) from renewable sources by 2025, and 10% (710 MW of installed capacity) by 2035 (SEU, 2017a). The plan seeks to realize these targets by a mixture of solar, wind, and waste-to-energy technologies and involves a mixture of public and private investment.”
extraction_rationale: This is a named national plan with quantified renewable energy targets and implementation mechanisms, qualifying as a mitigation policy umbrella with sub-policies listed.

parent_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP): achieve 5% of energy (255 MW installed capacity) from renewable sources by 2025 and 10% (710 MW installed capacity) by 2035, using solar, wind, and waste-to-energy technologies.
policy_statement: Implement net metering to enable consumers to generate on-site, grid-connected renewable energy (e.g., rooftop solar).
source_quote: “Three main policies have been established to realize the targets, as follows: - Net metering: This will enable consumers to generate on-site, grid-connected, renewable energy, for example via the installation of solar panels on roofs;”
extraction_rationale: A specific policy instrument (net metering) is explicitly established to deliver renewable deployment under NREAP.

parent_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP): achieve 5% of energy (255 MW installed capacity) from renewable sources by 2025 and 10% (710 MW installed capacity) by 2035, using solar, wind, and waste-to-energy technologies.
policy_statement: Implement feed-in tariffs via a tender-based mechanism with long-term power purchase agreements to support renewable energy.
source_quote: “Three main policies have been established to realize the targets, as follows: - Feed-in tariffs: This is a tender-based mechanism to support renewable energy characterized by long-term power purchase agreements;”
extraction_rationale: A defined economic support mechanism (feed-in tariffs with PPAs) is established to incentivize renewable generation.

parent_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP): achieve 5% of energy (255 MW installed capacity) from renewable sources by 2025 and 10% (710 MW installed capacity) by 2035, using solar, wind, and waste-to-energy technologies.
policy_statement: Adopt renewable energy mandates for new buildings.
source_quote: “Three main policies have been established to realize the targets, as follows: - Mandates: This refers to renewable energy mandates for new buildings.”
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit mandate (regulatory requirement) tied to renewable energy uptake.

policy_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP): implement 22 initiatives across sectors to reduce final energy consumption by 6% by 2025 relative to average 2009–2013 energy use.
source_quote: “After extensive consultations with stakeholders, the SEU established the target of a 6% reduction (about 6,000 GWh) in final energy consumption by 2025. It is estimated that this would lead to a cumulative reduction in greenhouse gas emissions of 3.4 million tonnes of CO2 by 2025. Twenty two main initiatives have been established to realize this target, including:”
extraction_rationale: A named national plan with a quantified energy reduction target and a defined package of initiatives; qualifies as an umbrella policy with sub-actions.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP): implement 22 initiatives across sectors to reduce final energy consumption by 6% by 2025 relative to average 2009–2013 energy use.
policy_statement: Integrate energy efficiency objectives into building codes and regulations for design, construction, and maintenance of structures (NEEAP building codes initiative).
source_quote: “Twenty two main initiatives have been established to realize this target, including: - Building codes: This involves the integration of energy efficiency objectives into regulations governing the design, construction, and maintenance of structures.”
extraction_rationale: Specific regulatory intervention (building codes) explicitly listed as an initiative under NEEAP.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP): implement 22 initiatives across sectors to reduce final energy consumption by 6% by 2025 relative to average 2009–2013 energy use.
policy_statement: Adopt demand-side efficiency standards including minimum standards for lighting, appliances, motor vehicles, and street lighting.
source_quote: “Twenty two main initiatives have been established to realize this target, including: - Demand-side efficiency standards: This involves new minimum standards for lighting, appliances, motor vehicles, and street lighting;”
extraction_rationale: Explicit minimum standards are a regulatory policy instrument to reduce energy demand.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP): implement 22 initiatives across sectors to reduce final energy consumption by 6% by 2025 relative to average 2009–2013 energy use.
policy_statement: Adopt supply-side efficiency standards for electricity generation including transmission and distribution efficiency enhancements and installation of smart meters.
source_quote: “Twenty two main initiatives have been established to realize this target, including: - Supply-side efficiency standards: This focuses on electricity generation, including efficiency enhancements for the transmission and distribution of electricity, and the installation of smart meters;”
extraction_rationale: Specific operational/technical standards and smart metering are named interventions to improve power-sector efficiency.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP): implement 22 initiatives across sectors to reduce final energy consumption by 6% by 2025 relative to average 2009–2013 energy use.
policy_statement: Introduce district cooling using highly efficient industrial-grade equipment and an insulated underground piping network.
source_quote: “Twenty two main initiatives have been established to realize this target, including: - District cooling: This involves the introduction of highly efficient, industrial-grade equipment to produce space cooling for buildings through an insulated underground piping network;”
extraction_rationale: Named technology/program intervention to reduce cooling energy demand.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP): implement 22 initiatives across sectors to reduce final energy consumption by 6% by 2025 relative to average 2009–2013 energy use.
policy_statement: Retrofit government buildings and pursue other green building initiatives.
source_quote: “Twenty two main initiatives have been established to realize this target, including: - Green building initiatives: This involves retrofitting of government buildings; and other initiatives; and”
extraction_rationale: Specific implementation action (retrofitting government buildings) to improve building performance.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP): implement 22 initiatives across sectors to reduce final energy consumption by 6% by 2025 relative to average 2009–2013 energy use.
policy_statement: Reform power and transport subsidies to offset perverse incentives for wasteful consumption.
source_quote: “Twenty two main initiatives have been established to realize this target, including: - Subsidy reform: This involves reforms to both power subsidies and those that affect transport to offset perverse incentives for wasteful consumption.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit subsidy reform is a fiscal/economic policy lever intended to reduce energy use and emissions.

policy_statement: Launch project-level carbon recovery initiatives: BAPCO carbon recovery plan and GPIC carbon dioxide recovery unit (2009).
source_quote: “Project-level initiatives: Two projects have been launched. The first is BAPCO's carbon recovery plan, which finds industrial applications for the waste CO2 associated with its oil extraction activities. The other is a carbon dioxide recovery unit launched by Gulf Petrochemicals Industries Company (GPIC) in 2009, a first for a petrochemicals company in the Middle East.”
extraction_rationale: These are specific named mitigation projects targeting CO2 capture/recovery and utilization, qualifying as concrete interventions.

policy_statement: Pursue education-based initiatives to improve climate change education and awareness by introducing changes in primary school curricula and delivering educational reform proposals to the Ministry of Education.
source_quote: “Education-based initiatives: This involves improving education and awareness on climate change primarily by introducing changes in educational curricula in primary schools. In addition, specific proposals for educational reforms were delivered to the Ministry of Education on the basis of studies of how other countries have introduced climate change into educational curricula.”
extraction_rationale: This is a stated government initiative to change curricula and deliver reform proposals; while somewhat broad, it specifies the intervention (curriculum changes) and responsible institution.

policy_statement: Implement a policy of expansion in the re-use of treated wastewater in irrigation, including free delivery of treated wastewater to farms to protect groundwater and meet irrigation/landscaping demand.
source_quote: “At present, Bahrain is pursuing a policy of expansion in the re-use of treated wastewater in irrigation. The primary objectives are to protect groundwater from further lowering of the groundwater table, deterioration in water quality, and satisfying demands for irrigation and landscaping. The policy incentivizes farmers to use treated wastewater instead of groundwater by providing free delivery of treated wastewater to the farmer lands.”
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit ongoing policy with a defined mechanism (free delivery/incentive) and stated objectives tied to water scarcity and resilience.

policy_statement: Reduce per capita municipal water demand by 33% by 2035 (from 183 to 122 m3/person/year) starting in 2016.
source_quote: “The first intervention aims to achieve a 33% reduction in per capita municipal water demand, from the current level of 183 to 122 m3 per person per year by 2035, with a policy start year of 2016.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified demand-management target with baseline, endpoint, and timeline; framed as an adaptation intervention under climate change.

policy_statement: Reduce leakage in the municipal water distribution network to achieve a 22% reduction in annual water production by 2035 relative to business-as-usual.
source_quote: “The second initiative aims to reduce leakage in the water distribution network to achieve reductions of 22% of annual water production by 2035 relative to water production in that year under business-as-usual conditions.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified infrastructure efficiency target with a deadline and BAU comparator; directly linked to adaptation planning for water under climate change.

policy_statement: Formulate a clear, comprehensive, and integrated national water resources policy and strategy based on IWRM principles, building on reactivation of the National Water Resources Council in 2016.
source_quote: “It is imperative for the Kingdom of Bahrain to formulate a clear, comprehensive, and integrated water resources policy and strategy in order to manage its water resources efficiently and obtain a considerable degree of sustainability under conditions of climate change. Institutional reforms that build upon the reactivation of the National Water Resources Council in 2016 are essential.”
extraction_rationale: A stated imperative/commitment to develop a national policy and strategy with an institutional anchor (Council reactivation); somewhat broad but constitutes a policy/planning commitment for adaptation.

policy_statement: Establish a cooperation mechanism with Saudi Arabia to develop and manage transboundary groundwater resources, including artificial recharge/storage enhancement using surplus tertiary treated wastewater.
source_quote: “Further deterioration of groundwater resources should be addressed by establishing a cooperation mechanism between Bahrain and Saudi Arabia in the development and management of transboundary groundwater resources, including groundwater artificial recharge/storage enhancement using surplus tertiary treated wastewater.”
extraction_rationale: Specific institutional mechanism and intervention (artificial recharge using treated wastewater) to address climate-exacerbated groundwater risks.

policy_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP): implement 22 initiatives to reduce energy use by 6% by 2025 relative to average 2009–2013 energy use.
source_quote: “Launched in 2017, the National Energy Efficiency Action Plan lays out 22 a comprehensive set of initiatives to increase energy efficiency potential in Bahrain. The Plan identifies 22 new initiatives across all sectors to achieve a reduction in energy use of 6% by 2025 relative to average energy use over the period 2009-2013.”
extraction_rationale: This repeats the NEEAP target in the mitigation chapter; extracted as an individual policy statement but deduplicated conceptually with the earlier NEEAP parent (kept there as parent with sub-actions).

policy_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP): achieve renewable energy target of 5% of peak capacity by 2025 and 10% by 2035 (478 GWh by 2025 and 1,456 GWh by 2035).
source_quote: “Launched in the same year, the National Renewable Energy Action Plan identified feasible solar, wind and biogas renewable energy options for Bahrain, establishing a national renewable energy target of 5% of peak capacity by 2025 and 10% by 2035, relative to the projected peak capacities in those years. On an electric generation basis, this amounts to 478 GWh and 1,456 GWh of renewable electricity by 2025 and 2035, respectively.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified renewable target with timelines and generation equivalents; overlaps with NREAP parent already extracted but provides additional explicit GWh figures.

policy_statement: Develop a climate change awareness plan specifying activities, target groups, input requirements, and institutional roles.
source_quote: “Other major findings include the need to make better use of social media to build awareness, as well as print and televised media, including the use of slogans. Based on these findings, a climate change awareness plan was developed that specified activities, target groups, input requirements, and institutional roles.”
extraction_rationale: A concrete plan is stated as developed with defined components; while not a mitigation/adaptation measure itself, it is a policy instrument for climate governance and public engagement.

policy_statement: Provide an enabling environment for technology transfer in renewable energy technologies based on a technology needs assessment.
source_quote: “To promote strategic technology transfer, advancement on the following measures will be necessary: - Provision of an enabling environment for technology transfer in renewable energy technologies in light of the findings of a previously conducted technology needs assessment;”
extraction_rationale: Explicit measure to enable technology transfer for renewables; a means-of-implementation policy supporting mitigation.

policy_statement: Enforce intellectual property rights to increase private-sector investor confidence for technology transfer.
source_quote: “To promote strategic technology transfer, advancement on the following measures will be necessary: - Enforcing intellectual property rights to provide confidence to prospective private sector investors;”
extraction_rationale: Regulatory/legal reform explicitly listed as necessary for climate-related technology transfer; indirect but material to mitigation enabling conditions.

policy_statement: Improve knowledge management processes and platforms for knowledge sharing to support technology transfer.
source_quote: “To promote strategic technology transfer, advancement on the following measures will be necessary: - Improving knowledge management processes and platforms for knowledge sharing;”
extraction_rationale: Institutional capacity/knowledge platform measure explicitly tied to technology transfer for climate technologies.

policy_statement: Enhance funding for R&D in green and climate technologies for SMEs.
source_quote: “To promote strategic technology transfer, advancement on the following measures will be necessary: - Enhancing funding for research and development (R&D) in green technology and climate technologies for smalland medium-sized enterprises;”
extraction_rationale: Explicit funding enhancement for climate/green tech R&D; qualifies as a financial instrument commitment (though amount not specified).

policy_statement: Develop technology transfer policies and integrate them within technology action plans.
source_quote: “To promote strategic technology transfer, advancement on the following measures will be necessary: - Developing technology transfer policies and integrating them within technology actions plans; and”
extraction_rationale: Explicit policy development and integration commitment for technology transfer; enabling measure for mitigation/adaptation technologies.

policy_statement: Enhance human capacity to support science-policy dialogues, build public awareness, and manage technology information for technology transfer.
source_quote: “To promote strategic technology transfer, advancement on the following measures will be necessary: - Enhancing human capacity to support sciencepolicy dialogues, build public awareness, and manage technology information.”
extraction_rationale: Capacity-building measure explicitly listed under technology transfer needs; supports implementation of climate technology policies.

policy_statement: Establish and enforce a national statistical data system to log operational and production data in government and private organizations for GHG inventory development.
source_quote: “Recommendations to address these challenges include the following: - Establish and enforce a national statistical data system, which logs operational, and production data and information, in governmental and private organizations;”
extraction_rationale: Concrete institutional/data-system recommendation with an enforcement element; enables ongoing emissions accounting and mitigation planning.

policy_statement: Establish strategic collaboration agreements between SCE and public organizations to ensure a sustainable supply of GHG-related data.
source_quote: “Recommendations to address these challenges include the following: - Establish strategic collaboration agreements between SCE and public organizations to ensure a sustainable supply of related data;”
extraction_rationale: Specific institutional mechanism (collaboration agreements) to secure data for national inventory and climate policy.

policy_statement: Develop a National Inventory System (NIS) in cooperation with key sectors in the country.
source_quote: “Recommendations to address these challenges include the following: - Given the above two points, a National Inventory System (NIS) is developed in cooperation with key sectors in the country;”
extraction_rationale: Explicit commitment to develop an NIS; a concrete institutional system for emissions tracking supporting mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Hold periodic workshops for public organizations to train and educate authorities on the IPCC emissions inventory system.
source_quote: “Recommendations to address these challenges include the following: - Hold periodic workshops for public organizations for training and educating critical authorities with the IPCC emissions inventory system;”
extraction_rationale: Specific capacity-building action (workshops) to improve inventory quality and institutional capability.

policy_statement: Support a national project to determine local emission factors related to indigenous resources.
source_quote: “Recommendations to address these challenges include the following: - Call for and support the conduction of a national project to determine local emission factors related to the indigenous resources;”
extraction_rationale: Concrete project support to improve emissions estimation accuracy; enables better mitigation targeting.

policy_statement: Establish a GHG inventory committee with high-level representation and clear oversight and coordination authority.
source_quote: “Recommendations to address these challenges include the following: - Establish a GHG inventory committee with high-level representation from key ministries/ institutions, having clear oversight and coordination authority; and”
extraction_rationale: Institutional governance reform with defined structure and authority; supports sustained climate MRV and policy development.

policy_statement: Develop an integrated database of relevant information including annual statistical abstracts and annual reports from specific entities for GHG inventory.
source_quote: “Recommendations to address these challenges include the following: - Develop an integrated database of relevant information including annual statistical abstracts and annual reports from specific entities.”
extraction_rationale: Concrete data infrastructure action to support inventory and climate policy analysis.

policy_statement: Develop an adaptation framework for sea level rise addressing protection, accommodation, retreat, and avoidance, and increase institutional capacity to incorporate sea level rise risks within development planning.
source_quote: “Going forward, it is recommended that systematic adaptation planning efforts be organized within an adaptation framework that address strategies for protection, accommodation, retreat, and avoidance. In the near-term, the focus should be on the following elements, with the aim of increasing institutional capacity to incorporate sea level rise risks within development planning:”
extraction_rationale: A clear planning commitment/recommendation for a structured adaptation framework explicitly tied to sea level rise risk integration into development planning.

policy_statement: Implement planning tools for sea level rise adaptation including coastal hazards assessment, coastal risk modeling/management, and emergency preparedness strategies.
source_quote: “Planning tools: Planning tools include activities of setting an overall policy to mitigate the effect of sea level rise. At minimum, it should incorporate assessment of coastal hazards, coastal risk modeling/management, and development of emergency preparedness strategies.”
extraction_rationale: Specific set of planning interventions explicitly recommended for sea level rise adaptation.

policy_statement: Implement regulatory tools for sea level rise adaptation including zoning offsets from the coastline, adjusting building codes, and accounting for sea level rise in real estate development permits (including no-build zones).
source_quote: “Regulatory tools: These include tools such as enacting land use regulations (e.g., zoning offsets from the coastline), adjusting building codes (e.g., increasing the distance from pavement to ground floor) and accounting for sea level rise in real estate development permits (e.g., identification of no-build zones).”
extraction_rationale: Explicit regulatory measures proposed for adaptation; includes concrete examples of zoning and permitting changes.

policy_statement: Implement land-use tools for sea level rise adaptation including land acquisition/transfer of development rights, added restrictions for high-risk areas, rezoning vulnerable land for low-risk uses, and subdivision regulation with conservation requirements.
source_quote: “Land use tools: These refer to tools in support of strategic adaptation and include such as land acquisition (i.e., purchase/transfer of development rights), reclamation (e.g., adding more restrictions on top of basic zoning requirements for certain high-risk areas), zoning (i.e., reclassifying highly vulnerable land for low risk uses) and subdivision regulation (e.g., minimum conservation requirements)”
extraction_rationale: Specific land-use policy instruments recommended for adaptation planning; concrete mechanisms are listed.

policy_statement: Use hard and soft structural coastal protection tools, including dikes/breakwaters and soft measures such as mangrove plantations and beach nourishment, guided by assessment frameworks.
source_quote: “Hard and soft structural tools: Structural tools include assessment frameworks by which to assess the optimality of coastal protection with either hard measures (e.g., dikes, breakwaters) or soft measures (e.g., mangrove plantations, beach nourishment).”
extraction_rationale: Explicit adaptation interventions for coastal protection, including nature-based and engineered options.

policy_statement: Introduce strengthened block water tariffs for non-household users starting 1 March 2016 under EWA's new tariff schedule.
source_quote: “Effective 1 March 2016, water tariffs for commercial, industrial, touristic, and other non-household users are being gradually strengthened in accordance with the new tariff schedule established by EWA. The block water tariff structure is shown in Figure 3-25.”
extraction_rationale: A specific tariff reform with an effective date and defined target group; functions as a financial instrument to reduce demand and improve resilience.

policy_statement: Introduce new legislation to promote water efficiency and conservation, including strengthening building codes and promoting water-saving devices (e.g., low-flow shower heads, faucet aerators, automatic shut-off nozzles) for new and existing buildings.
source_quote: “New legislation: To promote water use efficiency and conservation, new legislation would be needed to strengthen existing building codes, promote water saving devices such as low-flow shower heads, faucet aerators, automatic shut-off nozzles and others for new buildings while existing buildings would be retrofitted.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit legislative action proposed with specific device interventions; qualifies as a policy commitment though phrased as 'would be needed' (somewhat prospective).

policy_statement: Strengthen leak detection and control by expanding EWA's leak detection programme and technologies and implementing active leakage control, pressure management, network rehabilitation, and improved repair speed/quality.
source_quote: “Leak detection: This would involve the strengthening of the leak detection programme within EWA's Leakage Detection and Control Group to perform more frequent leak detection surveys and expand the use of leak detection technologies (e.g., leak noise correlators, thermography free-floating inline leak detectors, etc). Leak control: This would involve several available currently technologies including Active Leakage Control, Pressure Management, Networks Rehabilitations and Speed & Quality of Repair (Lambert, 2003).”
extraction_rationale: Specific operational measures and technologies are identified to reduce leakage; supports the quantified leakage reduction policy.

policy_statement: Implement transport subsidy reform by increasing gasoline prices (91 Octane +42% from US$0.21 to US$0.30; 95 Octane +60% from US$0.26 to US$0.42) as part of reforms underway since 2016.
source_quote: “Transport Subsidy Reform: This initiative aims for a 4% reduction in annual fuel use in the light duty vehicle fleet. It will accomplish this through modification to the retail price of gasoline and diesel fuel, a reform process that has been underway since 2016. The price of regular grade gasoline (91 Octane) is being increased by 42%, from US$ 0.21 to US$ 0.30, while the price of premium grade gasoline (95 Octane) is being increased by 60%, from US$ 0.26 to US$ 0.42.”
extraction_rationale: A quantified price reform policy instrument aimed at reducing fuel use; clearly a fiscal instrument with explicit price changes.

policy_statement: Implement electricity subsidy reform by increasing electricity tariffs to reflect actual generation costs (e.g., residential first 3,000 kWh/month from US$0.008 to US$0.08 by 2019; industrial above 5,000 kWh/month from US$0.04 to US$0.08 by 2019) to reduce electricity use.
source_quote: “Electricity Subsidy Reform: This initiative aims to gradually increase electricity tariffs to reflect the actual costs of power generation and promote more efficient electricity consumption. Electricity tariff reform has been underway since 2016. For the first 3,000 kWh per month, the residential rate will be gradually increased from US$ 0.008/kWh to US$ 0.08/kWh by 2019.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit tariff reform with numeric tariff levels and timeline; a financial instrument intended to reduce electricity consumption and emissions.

policy_statement: Implement vehicle efficiency standards and labeling, including minimum fuel economy standards and mandatory fuel economy labels for new vehicles (implemented for model year 2018).
source_quote: “Vehicle Efficiency Standards & Labeling: This initiative aims to improve efficiency in the transport sector by setting minimum fuel economy standards for light duty vehicles; and by making vehicle fuel economy an explicit part of the purchase decision by ensuring that labels are appropriately displayed thereby increasing consumer awareness. The fuel economy labels for light duty vehicles were implemented on all new vehicles of model 2018.”
extraction_rationale: Regulatory standards and labeling requirement with an implementation milestone (model 2018).

policy_statement: Establish a carbon emission credits fund where emitters receive credits for verified emissions-reduction projects and the government purchases credits, financed by removal of electricity tariff subsidies.
source_quote: “Carbon emission credits: An emissions reduction fund could be established where emitters are granted credits for projects that reduce verifiable carbon emissions. When validated, the government would purchase these credits to encourage further reductions. These credits could be financed by the removal of electricity tariff subsidies.”
extraction_rationale: Proposed market/finance mechanism (fund + credit purchases) explicitly designed to incentivize verified emissions reductions; clearly a financial instrument though framed as a recommendation ('could be established').

policy_statement: Mandate ISO 50001 Energy Management certification for industrial processes to address energy efficiency and carbon emissions.
source_quote: “Industrial energy efficiency: ISO50001 Energy Management certification could be mandated to ensure that energy efficiency is addressed in industrial processes that lead to substantial carbon emissions.”
extraction_rationale: A specific regulatory mandate proposal for industrial energy management; concrete mechanism though phrased as 'could be mandated'.

policy_statement: Unconditionally reduce economy-wide GHG emissions by 20% below BAU by 2030 and conditionally reduce by 31% below BAU by 2030.
source_quote: This NDC represents a progression beyond Lebanon's 2015 NDC by unconditionally increasing its Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emission target relative to the Business-As-Usual (BAU) scenario from 15% to 20%, and conditionally increasing its GHG emission target relative to the BAU scenario from 30% to 31%. Moreover, Lebanon commits to unconditionally reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 20% below its Business-As-Usual (BAU) scenario (amounting to 7,790 Gg. CO2eq.) and to conditionally reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 31% below its Business-As-Usual (BAU) scenario in 2030 (amounting to 12,075 Gg. CO2eq.)
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified national mitigation target with a deadline (2030) and explicit unconditional/conditional levels, meeting the criteria for a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Unconditionally generate 18% of electricity demand and 11% of building-sector heat demand from renewable energy by 2030; conditionally generate 30% of electricity demand and 16.5% of building-sector heat demand from renewable energy by 2030.
source_quote: Moreover, Lebanon commits to unconditionally generate 18% of the power demand (i.e. electricity demand) and 11% of its heat demand (in the building sector) from renewable energy sources in 2030, compared to a combined 15% in 2015. Conditionally, Lebanon commits to generate 30% of the power demand (i.e. electricity demand) and 16.5% of its heat demand (in the building sector) from renewable energy sources in 2030, compared to a combined 20% in 2015 (guided by the IRENA Renewable Energy Outlook: Lebanon).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable energy deployment target with a clear timeframe (2030), constituting a mitigation policy commitment.

policy_statement: Unconditionally reduce power demand through energy-efficiency measures by 3% under BAU by 2030; conditionally reduce power demand through energy-efficiency measures by 10% under BAU by 2030.
source_quote: 3. A 3% reduction in power demand through energy-efficiency measures in 2030 compared to the demand under the BAU scenario. 3. A 10% reduction in power demand through energy-efficiency in 2030 compared to the demand under the BAU scenario.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified energy-efficiency target with a deadline (2030). Although framed as power-demand reduction, it is explicitly part of the mitigation contribution.

policy_statement: Establish a transparency framework to improve institutional arrangements, data availability and periodicity, and monitoring and evaluation of mitigation and adaptation projects.
source_quote: In order to enhance the impacts of policymaking, and to successfully participate in tracking the global progress of the climate fight, a transparency framework will be established to improve institutional arrangements, data availability and periodicity, as well as monitoring and evaluation of mitigation and adaptation projects.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional commitment (“will be established”) to create a monitoring/transparency framework for climate action implementation.

policy_statement: Revise the policymaking process to include gender institutions, youth groups, and vulnerable communities in climate and recovery solutions.
source_quote: Integrated solutions to the climate crisis, as well as economic recovery, cannot be performed without the effective inclusion of gender institutions, youth groups and vulnerable communities. Lebanon plans to revise its policymaking process to include these groups which are key to the success of the NDC and are the most impacted by climate impacts.
extraction_rationale: This is a stated governance reform commitment (“plans to revise its policymaking process”) tied to NDC success and climate impacts; somewhat process-oriented but anchored as a planned institutional change.

policy_statement: Stimulate research and development for low-carbon and sustainable technologies and foster an innovative environment including public investments for research and piloting and partnerships with academic bodies.
source_quote: Lebanon aims to reduce the carbon intensity of its economy through stimulating Research and Development for low carbon and sustainable technologies. It is therefore important to foster an innovative environment by sustainably enhancing the capabilities of the private sector, driving large public investments for research and piloting, partnering with academic bodies to provide the needed readiness for transformational change, and encouraging innovation labs.
section_header: ## CAE4: Innovative Research and Development Encouraged
extraction_rationale: This is a policy direction with specific interventions (R&D stimulation, public investments for piloting, innovation labs) explicitly aimed at reducing carbon intensity; funding is mentioned but not as a defined instrument/amount.

policy_statement: Derisk climate-relevant investments and apply fiscal incentives/disincentives to operationalize the Polluter Pays Principle across emitting sectors, including via existing decrees/laws on clean technology uptake, EV/hybrid tax incentives, and water pollution penalties.
source_quote: Lebanon strives to derisk climate-relevant investments both for the public and private sectors, as it is of the essence to accelerate the deployment of climate-friendly technologies, especially renewable energy. Additionally, fiscal incentives and disincentives are necessary to operationalize the 'Polluter Pays Principle' across all relevant emitting sectors to fast-track the shift to greener options, such as Decree 167/2017 which reduces corporate tax/customs fees based on clean technology uptake, Article 55 of 2018 Budget Law which provides tax exemptions for electric vehicles and tax reductions for hybrid vehicles, and Law 77/2018 and its amended version 192/2020, where the Water Code lists penalties for polluters.
section_header: ## CAE2: Incentivized Action and Fiscal Reform
extraction_rationale: This describes fiscal policy tools (tax reductions/exemptions, penalties) and an investment-derisking approach to accelerate climate-friendly technologies; it is a clear policy commitment area with named legal instruments.

policy_statement: Develop a climate-proofing methodology to assess and reduce impacts of climate-negative projects and potentially guide investment evaluation through a climate lens; explore greening foreign investments including ODA and include ESS and gender-responsiveness in project evaluation and implementation.
source_quote: Moreover, Lebanon is currently developing a climate-proofing methodology which aims to assess and reduce the impacts of climate-negative projects, as well as potentially guide the evaluation of investments, through a climate lens. Ultimately, Lebanon intends to explore the possibility of greening foreign investments including Official Development Assistance (ODA) to accelerate the achievement of the NDC and avoid locking in carbon emissions on the longterm.
section_header: ## 6. Support Needed for NDC Implementation and Achievement
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planned tool (methodology) for screening investments and an explicit intention to green foreign investment/ODA; somewhat exploratory (“intends to explore”) but anchored to a defined intervention (climate-proofing methodology).

policy_statement: Establish the Lebanon Green Investment Facility (LGIF) to provide climate and green finance instruments and technical assistance to create bankable projects and increase investment in climate-friendly projects for NDC implementation.
source_quote: Therefore, Lebanon is working towards the establishment of the Lebanon Green Investment Facility (LGIF) as stipulated in the Government's Financial Recovery Plan, to provide climate and green finance through accessible and affordable finance instruments for both the public and private sectors, as well as to provide needed technical assistance to various entities to create bankable projects. The LGIF is foreseen to substantially contribute to the implementation of the NDC by increasing investments to climate-friendly projects, through strong donor and investor coordination mechanism and capitalization strategy.
section_header: ## 6. Support Needed for NDC Implementation and Achievement
extraction_rationale: This is a named facility with an explicit purpose to provide finance instruments and technical assistance; it is a financial instrument/program supporting climate action.

policy_statement: Guiding Adaptation Principles (six principles) to steer Lebanon’s adaptation action, including food and water security, resilient infrastructure, resilient health systems, nature-based solutions, land degradation neutrality, and disaster risk reduction.
source_quote:
Below are guiding principles and sectoral adaptation priorities which, together, aim to preserve and restore the natural capital and enhance and protect the built capital, as well as livelihoods, to ensure sustainable growth and resilience to climate change.

## Guiding Adaptation Principles
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella framework explicitly presented as guiding principles for adaptation action, with multiple listed sub-items beneath it.

parent_statement: Guiding Adaptation Principles
policy_statement: Achieve food and water security through the sustainable management of resources.
source_quote:
## Guiding Adaptation Principles

|   1. | Achieve food and water security through the sustainable management of resources |
extraction_rationale: This is a stated adaptation principle guiding government action; it is somewhat broad but is explicitly part of the adaptation policy framework.

parent_statement: Guiding Adaptation Principles
policy_statement: Enhance the resilience of infrastructure and urban and rural areas to withstand climate-related disasters.
source_quote:
## Guiding Adaptation Principles

|    2 | Enhance the resilience of the infrastructure, urban and rural areas to subsist climate- related disasters |
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit resilience/disaster-focused adaptation principle.

parent_statement: Guiding Adaptation Principles
policy_statement: Ensure and protect public health, well-being and safety through climate-resilient systems.
source_quote:
## Guiding Adaptation Principles

|    3 | Ensure and protect public health, well-being and safety of all communities through climate- resilient systems |
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit adaptation principle focused on climate-resilient health and safety systems.

parent_statement: Guiding Adaptation Principles
policy_statement: Incorporate Nature-Based Solutions as a first line of defense against adverse climate change impacts.
source_quote:
## Guiding Adaptation Principles

|    4 | Incorporate Nature-Based Solutions as a first line of defense from adverse impacts of climate change |
extraction_rationale: This explicitly commits to using NBS for climate defense; primary mechanism is ecosystem-based protection.

parent_statement: Guiding Adaptation Principles
policy_statement: Combat desertification and land degradation by achieving Land Degradation Neutrality.
source_quote:
## Guiding Adaptation Principles

|    5 | Combat desertification and land degradation by achieving Land Degradation Neutrality |
extraction_rationale: This is a defined land policy objective (LDN) linked to climate impacts; it implies ecosystem restoration/land management.

parent_statement: Guiding Adaptation Principles
policy_statement: Substantially reduce the risk of climate and non-climate related disasters to protect lives, the economy, and physical and natural assets.
source_quote:
## Guiding Adaptation Principles

|    6 | Substantially reduce the risk of climate and non-climate related disasters to protect lives, the economy and physical and natural assets |
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit disaster risk reduction principle tied to climate-related disasters.

policy_statement: Adaptation priorities (seven sectoral priorities) forming part of Lebanon’s Adaptation Communication under the Paris Agreement.
source_quote:
Therefore, the below priorities constitute part of Lebanon's Adaptation Comm unication in accordance with paragraph 10 of Article 7 of the Paris Agreement and Law 115/2019.

## Adaptation priorities
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella set of sectoral adaptation priorities with multiple numbered priorities and key activities listed beneath, fitting a parent policy structure.

parent_statement: Adaptation priorities
policy_statement: Strengthen the agricultural sector's resilience to enhance agricultural output in a climate-smart manner, including restoring livelihoods, increasing productivity, improving value chains, encouraging private investment and access to climate finance/insurance, and strengthening institutions.
source_quote:
| Adaptation priority 1    | Strengthen the agricultural sector's resilience to enhance Lebanon's agricultural output in a climate-smart manner |
| Key activities           | • Restore the livelihoods and productive capacity of farmers and producers; • Increase agricultural production and productivity; • Enhance efficiency and competitiveness of agri-food value chains including fisheries; • Encourage private investment along the agri-food value chain including innovative technical solutions and improved access to climate finance and insurance; • Strengthen the enabling institutional environment; • Increase resilience of households with reference to food and nutrition security. |
extraction_rationale: This is a defined sectoral adaptation priority with a package of specific actions; includes explicit climate-smart framing and access to climate finance/insurance.

parent_statement: Adaptation priorities
policy_statement: Promote sustainable use of natural resources, restore degraded landscapes, and increase forest cover through sustainable forest management, including achieving Brummana Declaration goals, halting land degradation, controlling erosion, improving water quality/soil productivity, establishing improved production sites, and promoting sustainable rangeland management.
source_quote:
| Adaptation priority 2    | Promote the sustainable use of natural resources, restore degraded landscapes, and increase Lebanon's forest cover while meeting the ecological, social and economic needs of sustainable forest management |
| Key activities           | • Achieve the goals listed in the Brummana Declaration for the Role of Mediterranean Forests to Fulfil the NDCs 10 ; • Adapt forest systems to climate change by halting land degradation, controlling erosion of topsoil, improving water quality and soil productivity; • Establish sites with improved production capacity linking with the development of wood and non- wood forest product processing industry and with the people's needs in terms of goods and services and improved employment opportunities; • Promote sustainable rangeland management; |
extraction_rationale: This is a nature/land management adaptation priority with explicit actions; it also explicitly notes mitigation co-benefits via carbon sinks (reforestation/afforestation).

parent_statement: Adaptation priorities
policy_statement: Develop sustainable water services (including irrigation) by implementing the Beirut Water Declaration, improving irrigation efficiency and surface water supply, supporting renewable energy use in irrigation and drinking water supply, strengthening legal/institutional frameworks, developing financing tools, and improving monitoring and transparency.
source_quote:
| Adaptation priority 3    | Structure and develop sustainable water services, including irrigation, in order to improve people's living conditions |
| Key activities           | • Implement the Beirut Water Declaration 11 ; • Enhance the efficient use of irrigation water and expand the supply of surface water sources for irrigation; • Encourage and support the use of renewable energy in agricultural irrigation and in drinking water supply; • Build an operational and sustainable legal and institutional framework to ensure a proper management of the water sector allowing the development of sustainable and efficient services; • Develop financing tools for the sector to set-up financial mechanisms allowing the sustainability and the financial balance of the services; • Involve all actors in the service chain and establish sustainable mechanisms for collaboration and coordination to improve the sector monitoring and transparency. |
extraction_rationale: This is a defined adaptation priority with specific actions and includes explicit renewable energy use and financing tools; primary mechanism is water-sector resilience/services.

parent_statement: Adaptation priorities
policy_statement: Manage terrestrial and marine biodiversity by identifying species status and conserving threatened species, protecting at least 20% of ecosystems, expanding nature reserves to at least 5% of Lebanon’s area, sustainably managing 50% of ecosystems in spatial planning, controlling non-indigenous biodiversity, identifying climate-vulnerable ecosystems and implementing adaptation plans, and rehabilitating at least 20% of degraded sites.
source_quote:
| Adaptation priority 4    | Value and sustainably manage Lebanon's terrestrial and marine biodiversity for the preservation and conservation of its ecosystems and habitats and the species they harbour |
| Key activities           | • Identify the status of 75% of known flora and fauna species and implement conservation actions on 50% of threatened species; • Protect at least 20% of natural terrestrial and marine ecosystems and represent all types of ecosystems in the protected areas network; • Increase the total percent coverage of nature reserves to reach at least 5% of Lebanon's area; • Sustainably manage 50% of all natural ecosystems and properly consider them in spatial planning implementation; • Establish effective measures to control the introduction and diffusion of non- indigenous biodiversity into the environment; • Identify vulnerable ecosystems to climate change and develop and implement appropriate adaptation plans; • Implement rehabilitation plans in at least 20% of degraded sites so that they can safeguard the sustained delivery of ecosystem services.
extraction_rationale: This contains multiple quantified conservation/protection targets and explicit climate adaptation planning for vulnerable ecosystems; primary mechanism is ecosystem-based management.

parent_statement: Adaptation priorities
policy_statement: Reduce vulnerability of coastal zones by assessing seawater intrusion, enhancing artificial aquifer recharge, updating aquifer water budgets, modelling aquifers, increasing coastal protective capacity against storm surges and sea-level rise, and promoting sustainable resource use such as fisheries.
source_quote:
| Adaptation priority 5   | Reduce the vulnerability of climate change impacts on coastal zones, especially in cities |
| Key activities          | • Assess the sea-water intrusion in the major coastal aquifers; • Enhance the Artificial Recharge of some selected aquifers; • Refresh the water budgeting of all aquifers progressively; • Perform the modelling of the karstic, saline and porous aquifer; • Increase the protective capacity of coasts against storm surges and sea-level rise; • Promote sustainable use of natural resources, such as fisheries. |
extraction_rationale: This is a coastal adaptation priority with specific technical measures and explicit hazards (storm surges, sea-level rise).

parent_statement: Adaptation priorities
policy_statement: Ensure public health and safety through climate-resilient health systems, including vulnerability assessment, early warning systems, capacity building, sustaining environmental health functions for hazards (droughts, heat waves, floods), upgrading epidemiological surveillance, integrating climate data into health information systems, and integrating response strategies into national health strategies.
source_quote:
| Adaptation priority 6   | Ensure overall public health and safety through climate-resilient health systems |
