source_quote:
Provisions  have  been  made  for  the  refurbishment  of several,  mainly  cultural  and  social  institutions  maintained  by  the Municipality by 2023, such as:

- L ibraries No. XVIII/3, XIX/1, XIII/8, III/5 of Metropolitan Ervin Szabó Library
- Budapest City Archives
- Old People's Homes of Alacskai road, Kamaraerdei road, Pesti road, Gödöllő, Baross street and Kútvölgyi road of the Municipality of Budapest

Annual volume of energy to be saved: 10000 MWh GHG mitigation: 2020 tCO2
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention (building refurbishments) with quantified expected savings, qualifying as a policy action under Má-1.

parent_statement: Má-1: Improve energy efficiency of buildings/industry/tertiary sector and increase the share of renewables.
policy_statement: M2: Replace outdated public lighting luminaires with LEDs to achieve electricity savings by 2027.
source_quote:
According to the data of BDK, of the 183 thousand luminaries used in Budapest for public lighting, about 110 thousand are worn-out and technically outdated and of high energy consumption and operating cost and will need to be replaced in the next 5 years.

Considering the experience of the recent period and the composition of the current portfolio of 110,000 luminaries, the power per unit is expected to be reduced by 40 W/pcs on the average, based on which the target value of the savings on electricity can be 18,242 MWh/annum.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete infrastructure retrofit program with a quantified energy-savings target and timeline.

parent_statement: Má-1: Improve energy efficiency of buildings/industry/tertiary sector and increase the share of renewables.
policy_statement: M3: Implement a residential building refurbishment program (insulation, heating modernization, renewables) targeting renovation of one-third of residential buildings by 2030.
source_quote:
One of the most effective ways to mitigate GHG emissions in Budapest is to reduce the  energy demand of residential buildings, resulting in the mitigation of the consumption of electricity, natural gas and other  energy sources.

The renovation of one third of the residential buildings in Budapest has a saving potential of 4,809,105 MWh energy and 981,977 t CO2 per annum.
extraction_rationale: This is a named measure with defined intervention components and quantified expected savings by the target year.

parent_statement: Má-1: Improve energy efficiency of buildings/industry/tertiary sector and increase the share of renewables.
policy_statement: M4: Promote photovoltaic deployment to reach up to 1,500 MW installed solar capacity potential by 2030 and deliver CO2 savings.
source_quote:
According to the data available, the portion of the buildings and roofs in Budapest which are suitable for the installation of solar panels and the areas suitable for being used for this purpose are sufficient for the installation of solar panels of a total installed capacity of 1500 MW (1750 MWp).

This measure has a CO2 savings potential of 467 thousand tons, which corresponds to the CO2 emission of the residential electricity use in 2015.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific renewable-energy deployment policy with quantified capacity and emissions-savings potential.

parent_statement: Má-1: Improve energy efficiency of buildings/industry/tertiary sector and increase the share of renewables.
policy_statement: M5: Reconstruct and expand district heating to increase efficiency and raise renewable/waste-heat shares to qualify as 'efficient district heating and cooling' by 2030.
source_quote:
The purpose of the district heating development program is to refurbish and develop the district heating system (own heat  generators,  pipelines,  heat  centres),  and  to  increase  the  ratio  of  renewable  energy  resources  as  well  as  to  realize 'efficient district heating and cooling' in terms of Article 2, Section 41 of Directive 2012/27/EU.

According to the Directive, 'efficient district heating and cooling' means a district heating or cooling system using at least 50% renewable ene rgy, 50% waste heat, 75% cogenerated heat or 50% of a combination of such energy and heat.
extraction_rationale: This is a defined infrastructure program with an explicit performance standard (EU definition) and target year.

parent_statement: Má-1: Improve energy efficiency of buildings/industry/tertiary sector and increase the share of renewables.
policy_statement: M6: Conduct surveys and research to map renewable potentials and building data and develop circular-economy/life-cycle analysis foundations by 2022.
source_quote:
Appropriate planning, emission reduction and increasing the ratio of renewables substantially necessitate a more precise presentation  of  the  possibilities  for  the  residential  and  non-residential  application  of  renewable  energy  resources  in Budapest (solar panel and geothermal potentials primarily).

As part of this, it is important to survey and model the existing buildings in detail, to create a database (including their location in the city structure and other regional analyses), as well as to explore administrative requirements and restrictions.
extraction_rationale: This is a funded, time-bound municipal action (research/surveys and database creation) enabling mitigation planning; it is specific enough to qualify.

parent_statement: Má-1: Improve energy efficiency of buildings/industry/tertiary sector and increase the share of renewables.
policy_statement: M7: Support industrial and tertiary-sector decarbonisation by informing businesses about technologies and helping them find financing through 2030.
source_quote:
The municipality plays a role in this respect primarily in providing information to businesses, making them acquainted with state-of-the-art technologies and providing assistance in finding the necessary financing for applying those technologies (see Measure SZ4).

| Type of measure                              | Mitigation                                                                                                             |
extraction_rationale: This is a defined municipal support intervention (information and financing assistance) with an implementation timeframe, though somewhat programmatic.

policy_statement: Má-2: Improve energy efficiency of transport infrastructure and support environmentally friendly transport modes.
source_quote:
## Má -2 Improving the energy efficiency of transport infrastructures, supporting and developing environmentally friendly forms of transport

- M8 -Development of public transport with attractive vehicles and services and better infrastructure
- M9 -Development of the cycling and pedestrian infrastructure
- M10 -Facilitation of the use of electric driven or low emission motor vehicles
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella transport mitigation objective with enumerated sub-measures (M8-M12).

parent_statement: Má-2: Improve energy efficiency of transport infrastructure and support environmentally friendly transport modes.
policy_statement: M8: Increase public transport mode share to 50% by 2030 and modernize/expand public transport vehicles and infrastructure.
source_quote:
According to  the  Budapest Mobility Plan (BMP), the share of public transport shall be  increased to 50% by 2030 with consideration to the distances covered.

The modernisation of the  vehicle  fleet  needs  to  be  continued.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified modal-share target with associated investment/modernization commitments.

parent_statement: Má-2: Improve energy efficiency of transport infrastructure and support environmentally friendly transport modes.
policy_statement: M9: Expand cycling and pedestrian infrastructure to raise cycling share to 5% and walking to 15% by 2030.
source_quote:
By means of the preferred development of cycling traffic, the share of cycling should be increased to 5% by 2030 based on the distances covered.

In addition to developing the cycling infrastructure, giving priority to pedestrian traffic is also extremely important.
extraction_rationale: This is a mode-shift policy with explicit targets and a defined infrastructure development program.

parent_statement: Má-2: Improve energy efficiency of transport infrastructure and support environmentally friendly transport modes.
policy_statement: M10: Support electric/low-emission vehicles by enabling charging infrastructure and incentives such as free parking (initially) through 2030.
source_quote:
The Municipality of Budapest can provide support as opposed to traditional vehicles by offering free parking in zones subject to limited waiting period  on  the  one  hand  (which  obviously  cannot  be  maintained  after  the  reaching  of  a  certain  ratio)  and  by  establishing charging  stations  for  private  transport  on  the  other  hand.

The establishment and operation of charging stations in public places must be supported.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete municipal intervention package (incentives + infrastructure) to accelerate e-mobility.

parent_statement: Má-2: Improve energy efficiency of transport infrastructure and support environmentally friendly transport modes.
policy_statement: M11: Establish rules and promote integrated car-sharing and car-pooling systems, including encouraging electrification of shared fleets.
source_quote:
The  objective  of  the  integrated  transport  organisation  entity  of  Budapest  is  to  establish  the  rules  of  a  uniform, transparent, universally accessible and, last but not least, environmentally friendly, integrated community system of car rental or car sharing.

Service providers need to be encouraged to gradually replace the vehicles using traditional fuels by electric vehicles.
extraction_rationale: This is a defined policy action (rule-setting and promotion) aimed at reducing transport emissions via shared mobility.

parent_statement: Má-2: Improve energy efficiency of transport infrastructure and support environmentally friendly transport modes.
policy_statement: M12: Implement traffic control measures including low-emission/climate protection zones, expand P+R parking, and introduce an emission-proportionate congestion charge (planned 2021–2025) to reduce car use.
source_quote:
The designation of climate  protection  zones  may  be  the  'ante -room'  to  the  banning  of  combustion  engines  in the  farther  future.

A prognosticated in the BMP, the congestion charge would  be  introduced  for  passenger  traffic  in  the  period  of  2021-2025.
extraction_rationale: This includes specific regulatory/economic instruments (zones, congestion charge) with an indicated implementation period.

policy_statement: Aá-1: Develop green-blue infrastructure (green areas and water surfaces) to improve climate adaptation.
source_quote:
## Aá -1 Development of the green -blue infrastructure

- A1 -Increasing the ratio of green areas and water surfaces
- A2 -Improving the ratio of green area and forest area
- A3 -Blue infrastructure development (revitalization of small watercourses)
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation objective with enumerated sub-measures (A1-A7).

parent_statement: Aá-1: Develop green-blue infrastructure (green areas and water surfaces) to improve climate adaptation.
policy_statement: A1: Increase and improve municipal green areas and water surfaces, including green roofs/façades and expanded support/tender funds for green infrastructure, targeting higher green area intensity by 2030.
source_quote:
The primary task is to increase the quantity and improve the quality of the areas owned and managed by the Municipality of  Budapest  by  the  implementation  of  programs  and  projects  suited  to  the  priority  objectives determined in the  Green Infrastructure Development and Maintenance Action Plan.

It is recommended to widen the scope and  enhance  the  volume  of  tender  funds  which  support  the  establishing  of  green  community  areas,  green  roofs,  roof gardens, green walls (e.g. Environmental Protection Fund).
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation/green infrastructure policy with implementation mechanisms (planning instruments and support funds) and a 2030 indicator target.

parent_statement: Aá-1: Develop green-blue infrastructure (green areas and water surfaces) to improve climate adaptation.
policy_statement: A2: Increase per-capita public green area supply to 7 m²/person by 2030 (and 9 m²/person by 2050) and establish new parks/forests, especially on the Pest side.
source_quote:
By realizing the planned increase in the per capita green area supply by 1 m 2 by 2030, CO2 absorption could be increased by 140 t CO2/annum.

The internationally recommended target value to be attained by 2050 is 9 m 2 /person.
extraction_rationale: This sets explicit per-capita green space targets with timelines, qualifying as a policy objective with planned interventions.

parent_statement: Aá-1: Develop green-blue infrastructure (green areas and water surfaces) to improve climate adaptation.
policy_statement: A3: Implement small watercourse revitalization programs (blue infrastructure), including a Rákos creek pilot and 10 km of revitalized sections by 2026.
source_quote:
Rákos creek can be a suitable pilot project, as the master plan for the Budapest section of the creek has already been compiled and additional technical drawings for the implementation are being prepared at the moment.

In the first step, the Rákos creek ecotourism corrid or  project  will  be  implemented until 2024 with a total budget of HUF 2.3 billion, the major element of which will be the construction of a cycling track.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific nature/blue-infrastructure intervention with a pilot project, budget, and timeline.

parent_statement: Aá-1: Develop green-blue infrastructure (green areas and water surfaces) to improve climate adaptation.
policy_statement: A4: Prepare a 10-year rolling plan for planting trees in public spaces, including annual schedules, budgets, and communication protocols.
source_quote:
It  is  necessary  to  elaborate  a  10  years'  plan  for  planting  trees  in public  spaces,  then  to  continue  rolling  planning, specifying  an  annual  timetable  including  not  only  the  venues  and  the  numbers,  but  also  data  relevant  to  quality development, as well as the budgeted costs of modern and planned technical preparation.

To  this  end,  a  communication  protocol  needs  to  be  elaborated  for  the  felling  of  trees.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planning commitment with defined scope (10 years) and implementation elements.

parent_statement: Aá-1: Develop green-blue infrastructure (green areas and water surfaces) to improve climate adaptation.
policy_statement: A5: Amend higher-level and municipal legal rules to strengthen tree protection, require expert involvement for felling decisions, and update standards in public procurement.
source_quote:
It is necessary to initiate the amendment of higher-level legal rules to ensure the more effective protection of trees.

The  relevant  regulation  of  the  Municipality  of  Budapest  (Regulation  No.  10/2005.  (III.  8.)  of  the  General  Assembly) requires  some  update  to  include  provisions  concerning  the  planting  and  protection  of  avenues  and  individual  trees.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory policy commitment (legal amendments and procurement standards) with clear intended governance changes.

parent_statement: Aá-1: Develop green-blue infrastructure (green areas and water surfaces) to improve climate adaptation.
policy_statement: A6: Create and operate a uniform, up-to-date green space cadastre for all Budapest in cooperation with districts by 2024.
source_quote:
It is necessary to create an up-to-date green space cadastre encompassing the entire public administrative area of Budapest based on a uniform methodology in cooperation with the district municipalities and organisations concerned, which shall take stock not only of trees, but of parks, forests, semi-natural areas and gardens as well.

It is advisable to further develop the FATÁR application created by FŐKERT so that the green areas, avenues and other green area managed by district municipalities and other green area managers also appear in the database.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional/data-system intervention with a stated need and timeframe.

parent_statement: Aá-1: Develop green-blue infrastructure (green areas and water surfaces) to improve climate adaptation.
policy_statement: A7: Promote brownfield revitalization by updating/publishing brownfield cadastres, prioritizing green-area land use in planning, and creating support schemes for brownfield renewal through 2030.
source_quote:
By the regular updating and publishing of the cadastre of brown-field areas and sites subject to remediation obligation, the Municipality of Budapest can promote the renewal of areas in need of rehabilitation and the information of the citizens living in the neighbourhood.

As brown-field areas are typically not municipal properties, it is necessary to incorporate such support schemes and funds in urban and green area development which promote the revitalisation of abandoned brown-field areas.
extraction_rationale: This is a planning and support policy aimed at shifting development to brownfields and enabling interim greening; it includes concrete instruments (cadastre, planning priorities, support schemes).

policy_statement: Aá-2: Mitigate the urban heat island effect in the built environment.
source_quote:
## Aá -2 Mitigation of the heat island effect in the built environment

- A8 -Protection of ventilation corridors, ensuring sufficient airspace ratio in streets
- A9 -Promotion of the application of climate friendly construction materials and technologies
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation objective with enumerated sub-measures (A8-A9).

parent_statement: Aá-2: Mitigate the urban heat island effect in the built environment.
policy_statement: A8: Protect ventilation corridors via settlement structure and urban planning rules by not supporting new build-up areas or increased building heights in these corridors (2021–2030).
source_quote:
The Municipality of Budapest can provide for the ventilation corridors of significance for the settlement structure in its Settlement Structure Plan (TSZT) and the Rules of Urban Planning (FRSZ).

In these areas, the designation of new areas to be built up or the raising of the permitted building height may not be supported.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear land-use/planning restriction to preserve ventilation, directly tied to heat mitigation.

parent_statement: Aá-2: Mitigate the urban heat island effect in the built environment.
policy_statement: A9: Prioritize climate-friendly construction materials and technologies in municipal procurement and support schemes, including permeable/high-albedo pavements and green roofs/façades.
source_quote:
Climate  protection  has  to  be  a  priority  criterion  in  the  public  procurement  processes  and  the  tender-based  support schemes  of  the  Municipality  of  Budapest  (e.g.  Environmental  Protection  Fund,  Healthy  Streets  Program).

Instead  of  traditional asphalt,  'cooler'  and,  if  possible,  permeable  surfaces  of  higher  albedo  should  be applied.
extraction_rationale: This is an operational/procurement policy specifying technologies and implementation channels (procurement and tenders).

policy_statement: Aá-3: Develop the flood control system.
source_quote:
## Aá -3 Development of the flood control system

- A10 -Construction and development of flood control structures
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation objective with a defined sub-measure (A10).

parent_statement: Aá-3: Develop the flood control system.
policy_statement: A10: Construct and upgrade flood control structures to increase the length of flood protection lines meeting DFE + 1.3m safety level to 69 km by 2030.
source_quote:
Due to climate effects seen on the entire catchment area of the Danube, flood waves reaching or even exceeding a water level of 8 m by far may arise in the subsequent period as well just like in recent year, therefore the flood protection line needs to be developed urgently.

The development and further construction of existing flood control structures can provide for the regulated propagation of flood waves and the prevention of various kinds of flood damage.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete infrastructure adaptation policy with a quantified target (km of compliant flood line) and deadline.

policy_statement: Aá-4: Implement adaptive rainwater management.
source_quote:
## Aá -4 Adaptive rainwater management

- A11 -Surface runoff regulation and the system required for its safety
- A12 -Supporting the utilization and retention of rainwater
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation objective with enumerated sub-measures (A11-A12).

parent_statement: Aá-4: Implement adaptive rainwater management.
policy_statement: A11: Develop a hybrid rainwater drainage/runoff regulation system, including modelling, critical-point identification, and infrastructure upgrades on a continuous basis.
source_quote:
In the case of Budapest, we could aim at the creation of a hybrid system, so that the regulation and drainage of rainwater could be the most effective and most economical in the individual subareas, in accordance with the given circumstances.

The complete midand long-term rainwater drainage concept for Budapest is to be created with regard to all of these factors.
extraction_rationale: This is a defined planning and infrastructure program for stormwater management with explicit system approach and ongoing implementation.

parent_statement: Aá-4: Implement adaptive rainwater management.
policy_statement: A12: Support on-site rainwater retention and utilization (including regulatory incentives and support schemes) and require/compel major emitters to apply delayed runoff/retention/secondary use.
source_quote:
In order to  promote  the  application  and  spread  of  such  systems,  they  need  to  be  integrated  in  the  planning  of  municipal  or governmental  investment  projects  and,  for  private  investments,  the  appropriate  regulatory  instruments  (e.g.  building allowances (floor area, etc.)) and the related support system should be elaborated.

In  the  case  of  major  emitters  (industry, shopping malls, office blocks), users should be  made interested in applying or compelled to apply the delayed runoff, retention or secondary use of rainwater.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation policy combining incentives/regulation and targeted requirements for large sites.

policy_statement: Aá-5: Prepare for extreme weather conditions and health impacts of climate change.
source_quote:
## Aá -5 Preparation for extreme weather conditions and the health impacts of climate change

- A13 -Preparation of the transport system for extreme weather phenomena
- A14 -Controlling hazards caused by extreme weather phenomena
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation objective with enumerated sub-measures (A13-A16).

parent_statement: Aá-5: Prepare for extreme weather conditions and health impacts of climate change.
policy_statement: A13: Adapt transport infrastructure design and operations for heatwaves, storms, and flash floods, including emergency scenarios and resilient materials/pavements.
source_quote:
Transport  systems  and  public  utility  networks  should  be  designed  with  consideration  to  the  prognostications  that temperatures can be expected to increase and heatwaves, storms and flash floods will occur more frequently.

It  is  recommended to elaborate an emergency scenario for the resolution of operating disruptions caused by extreme weather  conditions (e.g. changing the route of services, commencing replacement services, providing information to travellers).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational and design adaptation commitment addressing identified hazards.

parent_statement: Aá-5: Prepare for extreme weather conditions and health impacts of climate change.
policy_statement: A14: Ensure hazard control and emergency plans cover climate-change-related extreme events and update public information materials accordingly.
source_quote:
It is necessary to examine and ensure that emergency plans manage extreme events which may occur due to climate change (drought,  flood,  flash  flood,  damage  to  critical  infrastructure,  etc.),  and  to  review  the  publication  prepared  to  inform  the citizens.

Hazard control plans include elements, e.g. the order of actions and measures, which support the decision-maker and facilitate the effective and successful implementation of control measures.
extraction_rationale: This is a governance/planning commitment to integrate climate extremes into emergency management.

parent_statement: Aá-5: Prepare for extreme weather conditions and health impacts of climate change.
policy_statement: A15: Assess climate vulnerability of drinking water bases and implement climate-adaptive development and operation of water supply, including well capacity enhancements and reconstruction by 2022.
source_quote:
Due to climate change affecting the catchment area of the Danube as well, extreme weather conditions are becoming more  and  more  frequent:  based  on  the  weather  trends  experienced  and  evaluated  in  recent  years,  there  is  a  justified demand for elaborating operational changes for periods hit by extreme drought.

Budapest Waterworks has started the development of 60 water production wells as part of a project.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation intervention in critical infrastructure (water supply) with concrete actions (well development) and timeframe.

parent_statement: Aá-5: Prepare for extreme weather conditions and health impacts of climate change.
policy_statement: A16: Integrate extreme-weather resilience into preservation and renovation of municipal buildings (windstorms, floods/flash floods/inundations) through 2030.
source_quote:
The foreseeable increase in the frequency of windstorms means a source of physical hazard for the building stock of the Municipality of Budapest, affecting primarily the structural boundaries of buildings, i.e. structures on the façade s and roofs.

For all these reasons, the Municipality has to pay priority attention concerning its own building stock to the proper sizing of support structures, basements, windows, sun shades and waterproofing sheets.
extraction_rationale: This is a defined adaptation requirement for municipal asset management, tied to specific hazards and building elements.

policy_statement: Aá-6: Mitigate vulnerability of natural and landscape values.
source_quote:
## Aá -6 Mitigation of the vulnerability of natural and landscape values

A17 -Preparation of the detailed climate change risk and vulnerability assessment for natural values

A18 -Continuing the expansion and extension of protected natural sites of local importance
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation/nature objective with enumerated sub-measures (A17-A19).

parent_statement: Aá-6: Mitigate vulnerability of natural and landscape values.
policy_statement: A17: Prepare a detailed climate change risk and vulnerability assessment for natural values by 2023.
source_quote:
Effective  nature  conservation  and  the  confining  of  invasive  animal  and  plant  species  requires  the  examination  of  the sensitivity  of  natural  values  to  climate  change  as  part  of  regular  status  assessment,  based  on  the  forecasts  of  a  precise climate model and the assessment and monitoring of risks and vulnerabilities.

Climate change intensifies the external effects on  natural  areas.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific, time-bound assessment action supporting adaptation of nature conservation management.

parent_statement: Aá-6: Mitigate vulnerability of natural and landscape values.
policy_statement: A18: Expand protected natural sites of local importance to 1,200 ha by 2026 (from 861 ha in 2019).
source_quote:
The primary objective is to protect the botanical, zoological, geological and landscape values of protected areas, to preserve biodiversity, to reduce conflicts concerning nature and the achieve that new areas are declared to  be  protected  sites  on  an  estimated  area  of  800  ha  based  on  preliminary  surveys.

The possibility of the extension  of protection is being examined continuously.
extraction_rationale: This is a land protection expansion policy with a quantified target in the measure table (1200 ha by 2026) and explicit intent to designate new protected areas.

parent_statement: Aá-6: Mitigate vulnerability of natural and landscape values.
policy_statement: A19: Implement nature conservation management to confine invasive plant and animal species, with continuous monitoring and a target to reduce invasive coverage by 2030.
source_quote:
One of the most important tasks of this management is to confine invasive species in the areas concerned, but nature conservation aspects need to be enforced not only in protected natural sites, but in the 'urban ecosystem' as well.

This requires the continuous collection of data by Hungarian Park Rangers ( Természetvédelmi Őrszolgálat ) and FŐKERT Nonprofit Zrt.
extraction_rationale: This is an ongoing management policy with a defined intervention (invasive species confinement) and monitoring system.

policy_statement: Aá0: Produce local climate forecasts and create city-level runoff/sewage models and a detailed vulnerability examination by 2022 to parameterize adaptation measures.
source_quote:
As  part  of  this  measure,  forecasts  need  to  be  generated  on  a  local  level  (cells  of  1-5  km),  based  on  a  scientifically substantiated  climate  model.

It is also necessary to conduct a detailed vulnerability examination for the territory of Budapest based on these models, based on which we can determine and parameterise the necessary adaptation measures.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific, funded modelling and assessment intervention with a stated timeframe and clear adaptation purpose.

policy_statement: SZ-1: Climate-conscious city management—lead by example and integrate climate protection into municipal operations.
source_quote:
## SZ-1  Climate  conscious  city  management:  cooperative  city  management  taking  the  lead  in  climate protection

SZ1 Climate conscious workplaces, climate conscious colleagues

SZ2  Enforcement  of  horizontal  climate  protection  principles  in  urban  development,  sectoral  and  urban planning
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella awareness/governance objective with enumerated sub-measures (SZ1-SZ4).

parent_statement: SZ-1: Climate-conscious city management—lead by example and integrate climate protection into municipal operations.
policy_statement: SZ1: Implement climate-conscious workplace initiatives and training within the Mayor's Office and municipal companies, targeting 1,500 trained participants by 2030.
source_quote:
The goal of the measure is to support and encourage initiatives promoting the climateconscious operation of the Mayor's Office and its companies and to introduce climate protection measures.

|                     | Target year value: 1,500 persons |
extraction_rationale: This is a specific internal capacity-building measure with a quantified target.

parent_statement: SZ-1: Climate-conscious city management—lead by example and integrate climate protection into municipal operations.
policy_statement: SZ2: Integrate climate protection principles into urban development and sectoral strategies, legal rules, tenders, and investments on a continuous basis.
source_quote:
This measure is intended to integrate climate protection measures and/or horizontal climate protection principles during the  preparation  and  review  of  urban  development  and  thematic  sectoral  strategies,  thus  establish  correlation  of  the documents with the Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan.

It is also necessary to integrate climate-related aspects in the due diligence and detailed planning of major investments from the point of view of climate protection, as well as to check whether they are duly realized.
extraction_rationale: This is a cross-cutting governance commitment to mainstream climate criteria into planning and investment decisions.

parent_statement: SZ-1: Climate-conscious city management—lead by example and integrate climate protection into municipal operations.
policy_statement: SZ3: Operate the Budapest Climate Change Platform and an online platform to share best practices, track measures, and build partnerships, targeting 20 sessions and 30,000 visitors by 2030.
source_quote:
The  purpose  of  the  measure  is  to  establish  long-term  cooperation  with  stakeholders  playing  a  strategic  role  in  the promotion of climate consciousness and the sharing of best practices.

One of the priority tasks of the Climate Change Platform is to realize cooperation with district municipalities, to promote district  climate  strategies  and  SECAPs.
extraction_rationale: This is a defined institutional program with explicit functions and quantified activity targets.

parent_statement: SZ-1: Climate-conscious city management—lead by example and integrate climate protection into municipal operations.
policy_statement: SZ4: Establish cooperation with the corporate sector to support and co-finance mitigation, adaptation, and awareness measures (e.g., green areas, solar investments, campaigns).
source_quote:
The purpose of the measure is to establish cooperation between the Municipality of Budapest and companies and to involve  companies  in  the  implementation  and  financing  of  the  mitigation,  adaptation  and  awareness-raising  measure  of Budapest, e.g. in the field of the expansion and development of green areas, solar panel investments and communication campaigns.

In order to reduce climate risks and reinforce climate consciousness in the corporate sector, it is necessary to establish cooperation and enter into thematic agreements with the interest groups and professional organisations of the corporate sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete partnership and implementation mechanism to mobilize private-sector action and resources.

policy_statement: SZ-2: Climate-conscious city dwellers—reinforce environmental culture and responsibility among residents and economic actors.
source_quote:
## SZ-2  Climate  conscious  city  dwellers:  reinforcement  of  the  environmental  culture  and  responsibility among the population and economic operators

SZ5 Thematic awareness-raising campa igns and informational activities

SZ6 Development of the adaptation knowledge and ability of the population
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella awareness objective with enumerated sub-measures (SZ5-SZ7).

parent_statement: SZ-2: Climate-conscious city dwellers—reinforce environmental culture and responsibility among residents and economic actors.
policy_statement: SZ5: Run thematic awareness campaigns to reduce household energy consumption and promote low-carbon behaviors, with quantified energy/CO2 savings targets by 2030.
source_quote:
Priority  issues  include  the  reduction  of  the  energy  consumption  of  households,  the  support  of  the  building  energy investments of the citizens, the promotion of public transport and cycling as opposed to the use of cars.

|                     | Target year value: 432,496 MWh; 85,744 tCO 2 /annum                                                                |
extraction_rationale: This is a funded programmatic intervention with explicit mitigation outcomes (energy and CO2 savings) and a target year.

parent_statement: SZ-2: Climate-conscious city dwellers—reinforce environmental culture and responsibility among residents and economic actors.
policy_statement: SZ6: Build public adaptation knowledge on heatwaves, rainwater management, property protection, and green infrastructure, targeting 100,000 people reached by 2030.
source_quote:
The Municipality of Budapest may also compile a heat plan document containing things to do concerning the provision of information, the communication panels which may be applied, as well as the tasks to be performed in connection with the events organised by the Municipality.

|                     | Target year value: 100 000                                                                                        |
extraction_rationale: This is a defined adaptation-awareness measure with a quantified outreach target.

parent_statement: SZ-2: Climate-conscious city dwellers—reinforce environmental culture and responsibility among residents and economic actors.
policy_statement: SZ7: Develop a sustainable/green public procurement strategy and enforce climate protection aspects in procurement by 2022.
source_quote:
For  this  reason,  the Municipality of Budapest wishes to create its sustainable, green and innovative procurement strategy as soon as possible.

| Timeframe           | 2022                                         |
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete governance commitment with a timeframe to change procurement practice as a delivery mechanism for climate objectives.

policy_statement: Review SECAP implementation every 2 years and require responsible departments to report progress every six months to the Chief Clerk for reporting to the Mayor.
source_quote:
It is to be reviewed every 2 years to what extent the measures and objectives of the SECAP have been realized.

It is recommended for the responsible  department s  of  the  Mayor's  Office  to  report  on  the  progress  achieved regarding the measures every six months to the Chief Clerk, who will then report to the Mayor directly.
extraction_rationale: This establishes a formal monitoring and reporting schedule (a governance mechanism) supporting implementation accountability.

policy_statement: Reduce California greenhouse gas emissions to 1990 levels by 2020 (AB 32 target).
source_quote: By requiring in law a reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions to 1990 levels by 2020, California set the stage for its transition to a sustainable, clean energy future.
extraction_rationale: This is a legally established, quantifiable statewide emissions target with a deadline (2020), meeting the criteria for a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Adopt and implement Scoping Plan measures by 2012 following Board approval (December 2008) and rulemaking over the next two years.
source_quote: It will be presented to the Board for approval at its meeting in December 2008. The measures in the Scoping Plan approved by the Board will be developed over the next two years and be in place by 2012.
extraction_rationale: Commits to a concrete implementation timeline for adopting measures (in place by 2012), which is an actionable program commitment.

policy_statement: Pursue long-term goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions 80% below 1990 levels by 2050 (Executive Order S-3-05).
source_quote: This long range goal is reflected in California Executive Order S-3-05 that requires an 80 percent reduction of greenhouse gases from 1990 levels by 2050.
extraction_rationale: A quantified long-term emissions reduction requirement with a deadline (2050).

policy_statement: Create targeted fees including a public goods charge on water use, fees on high-GWP gases, and a fee to fund AB 32 administrative costs.
source_quote: Creating targeted fees, including a public goods charge on water use, fees on high global warming potential gases, and a fee to fund the administrative costs of the State's long term commitment to AB 32 implementation.
extraction_rationale: Explicit commitment to establish fee-based instruments to support emissions reductions and program administration.

policy_statement: Establish a 'margin of safety' by recommending additional reductions in uncapped sectors to ensure the 2020 target is met.
source_quote: The plan provides a 'margin of safety,' that is, additional reductions beyond those in the draft plan to account for measures in uncapped sectors that do not, or may not, achieve the estimated reduction of greenhouse gas emissions in this plan. Along with the certainty provided by the cap, this will ensure that the 2020 target is met.
extraction_rationale: A program design commitment to add additional reductions as a backstop to meet the statutory target; concrete mechanism though not quantified here.

policy_statement: Support near-term development of carbon capture and sequestration technology and recognize terrestrial sequestration in land resources.
source_quote: In addition, the plan expresses support for near-term development of sequestration technology. This plan also acknowledges the important role of terrestrial sequestration in our forests, rangelands, wetlands, and other land resources.
extraction_rationale: States support for specific mitigation technology (sequestration) and land-based sinks; somewhat broad but still a named intervention area.

policy_statement: Recommend a greenhouse gas reduction goal for local governments of 15% below current levels by 2020 for municipal and community-wide emissions.
source_quote: ARB recommended a greenhouse gas reduction goal for local governments of 15 percent below today's levels by 2020 to ensure that their municipal and community-wide emissions match the State's reduction target.
section_header: Changes to Specific Measures and Programs
extraction_rationale: Quantified target (15% by 2020) directed at local governments; qualifies as a policy goal.

policy_statement: Implement Discrete Early Actions enforceable on or before January 1, 2010.
source_quote: Identify and adopt regulations for Discrete Early Actions that could be enforceable on or before January 1, 2010 (HSC §38560.5). The Board identified nine Discrete Early Action measures including potential regulations affecting landfills, motor vehicle fuels, refrigerants in cars, port operations and other sources in 2007.
section_header: 2. Assembly Bill 32: The Global Warming Solutions Act
extraction_rationale: A binding statutory requirement with a deadline and a defined program (Discrete Early Actions) that contains multiple sub-measures.

parent_statement: Implement Discrete Early Actions enforceable on or before January 1, 2010.
policy_statement: Adopt Discrete Early Action measure: ship electrification at ports.
source_quote: The Board identified nine Discrete Early Action measures including potential regulations affecting landfills, motor vehicle fuels, refrigerants in cars, port operations and other sources in 2007. The Board has already approved two Discrete Early Action measures (ship electrification at ports and reduction of high GWP gases in consumer products).
section_header: 2. Assembly Bill 32: The Global Warming Solutions Act
extraction_rationale: Specific named intervention already approved as an early action regulation.

parent_statement: Implement Discrete Early Actions enforceable on or before January 1, 2010.
policy_statement: Adopt Discrete Early Action measure: reduce high-GWP gases in consumer products.
source_quote: The Board identified nine Discrete Early Action measures including potential regulations affecting landfills, motor vehicle fuels, refrigerants in cars, port operations and other sources in 2007. The Board has already approved two Discrete Early Action measures (ship electrification at ports and reduction of high GWP gases in consumer products).
section_header: 2. Assembly Bill 32: The Global Warming Solutions Act
extraction_rationale: Specific named intervention already approved as an early action regulation.

policy_statement: Ensure early voluntary reductions receive appropriate credit under AB 32 implementation, including procedures for quantification methods.
source_quote: Ensure early voluntary reductions receive appropriate credit in the implementation of AB 32 (HSC §38562(b)(3)). In February 2008, the Board approved a policy statement encouraging voluntary early actions and establishing a procedure for project proponents to submit quantification methods to be evaluated by ARB.
section_header: 2. Assembly Bill 32: The Global Warming Solutions Act
extraction_rationale: A statutory and Board-approved policy framework to credit voluntary early reductions with a defined procedure.

policy_statement: Reduce State government greenhouse gas emissions by at least 30% below estimated business-as-usual by 2020 (about 15% below current levels).
source_quote: Therefore, California State government has established a target of reducing its greenhouse gas emissions by a minimum of 30 percent below its estimated business-as-usual emissions by 2020 - approximately a 15 percent reduction from current levels.
section_header: A. The Role of State Government: Setting an Example
extraction_rationale: Quantified target with deadline for State operations; clear policy commitment.

policy_statement: Adopt amended CEQA Guidelines to provide guidance on addressing greenhouse gases in CEQA documents by January 1, 2010 (SB 97).
source_quote: The Governor's Office of Planning and Research and the Resources Agency are developing proposed amendments to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines to provide guidance on how to address greenhouse gases in CEQA documents. As required by SB 97 (Chapter 185, Statutes of 2007), the amended CEQA guidelines will be adopted by January 1, 2010.
section_header: A. The Role of State Government: Setting an Example
extraction_rationale: Binding deadline and regulatory guidance instrument for integrating GHG analysis into environmental review.

policy_statement: Adopt Local Government Operations Protocol and develop a community emissions protocol to quantify and track local GHG emissions.
source_quote: To provide local governments guidance on how to inventory and report greenhouse gas emissions from government buildings, facilities, vehicles, wastewater and potable water treatment facilities, landfill and composting facilities, and other government operations, ARB recently adopted the Local Government Operations Protocol. ARB is also developing an additional protocol for community emissions.
section_header: B. The Role of Local Government: Essential Partners
extraction_rationale: Concrete guidance/protocol adoption and development commitment enabling measurement and tracking—an implementation policy tool.

policy_statement: Encourage local governments to adopt emissions reduction goals parallel to the State commitment (~15% below current levels by 2020) and provide tools/guidance.
source_quote: In addition to tracking emissions using these protocols, ARB encourages local governments to adopt a reduction goal for municipal operations emissions and move toward establishing similar goals for community emissions that parallel the State commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 15 percent from current levels by 2020. To consolidate climate action resources and aid local governments in their emission reduction efforts, the ARB is developing various tools and guidance for use by local governments, including the next generation of best practices, case studies, a calculator to help calculate local greenhouse gas emissions, and other decision support tools.
section_header: B. The Role of Local Government: Essential Partners
extraction_rationale: Policy guidance plus tool development to drive local adoption of quantified goals; partly voluntary but anchored by a numeric target and concrete support actions.

policy_statement: Emissions Reduction Measures (Scoping Plan recommended measures) to achieve the 2020 GHG limit.
source_quote: The following sections describe the recommended measures in this Proposed Scoping Plan. Additional information about these measures is provided in Appendix C.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella section introducing a structured set of specific measures; the measures themselves are extracted as individual/sub policies below.

policy_statement: Implement a broad-based California cap-and-trade program linked to Western Climate Initiative partners, with regulations developed by Jan 1, 2011 and program beginning in 2012.
source_quote: Implement a broad-based California cap-and-trade program to provide a firm limit on emissions. Link the California cap-and-trade program with other Western Climate Initiative Partner programs to create a regional market system to achieve greater environmental and economic benefits for California. Based on the requirements of AB 32, regulations to implement the cap-and-trade program need to be developed by January 1, 2011, with the program beginning in 2012.
section_header: 1. California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
extraction_rationale: Specific named regulatory program with deadlines and linkage design; core mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Phase cap-and-trade coverage: electricity generation and large industrial facilities starting 2012; upstream fuels and transportation fuels starting 2015.
source_quote: The proposed cap-and-trade measure phases in the following sectors: Starting in the first compliance period (2012): - Electricity generation, including imports not covered by a WCI Partner jurisdiction - Large industrial facilities that emit over 25,000 metric tons CO2E per year. Starting in the second compliance period (2015): - Upstream treatment of industrial fuel combustion at facilities with emissions at or below 25,000 metric tons CO2E, and all commercial and residential fuel combustion regulated where the fuel enters into commerce - Transportation fuel combustion regulated where the fuel enters into commerce.
section_header: 1. California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
extraction_rationale: Defines scope and timing of regulatory coverage—specific, enforceable design elements.

policy_statement: Limit offsets and non-WCI allowances to no more than 49% of required reductions under the cap-and-trade program.
source_quote: Consequently, the use of offsets and allowances from other systems are limited to no more than 49 percent of the required reduction of emissions. ARB will apply the limit on offsets that is within its jurisdiction, such that the allowable offsets in each compliance period is less than half of the emissions reductions expected from capped sectors in that compliance period.
extraction_rationale: A quantitative constraint on compliance instruments within cap-and-trade; clear rule commitment.

policy_statement: Implement Pavley light-duty vehicle GHG standards and adopt a second, more stringent phase (Pavley II).
source_quote: Implement adopted Pavley standards and planned second phase of the program. Align zero-emission vehicle, alternative and renewable fuel and vehicle technology programs with long-term climate change goals.
section_header: 2. California Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Standards
extraction_rationale: Specific regulatory standards program with planned expansion; direct mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Evaluate and potentially implement a feebate program as a backstop or supplement to Pavley standards to achieve equivalent or greater GHG reductions.
source_quote: ARB is evaluating the use of feebates as a measure to achieve additional reductions from the mobile source sector, either as a backstop to the Pavley regulation if the regulation cannot be implemented, or as a supplement to Pavley if the waiver is approved and the regulation takes effect. A feebate regulation would combine a rebate program for low-emitting vehicles with a fee program for high-emitting vehicles.
extraction_rationale: A proposed fiscal/regulatory instrument under evaluation with defined structure (fees + rebates) tied to achieving equivalent reductions.

policy_statement: Update and optimize the Zero Emission Vehicle (ZEV) program; Board to consider proposal in 2009 to align with 2020 and 2050 targets.
source_quote: In 2009, the Board will consider a proposal that is currently being developed to ensure that the ZEV program is optimally designed to help the State meet its 2020 target and put us on the path to meeting our 2050 target of an 80 percent reduction in greenhouse gas emissions.
extraction_rationale: Concrete commitment to Board consideration of a proposal to redesign a regulatory program; timing specified (2009).

policy_statement: Provide approximately $50 million per year in grants under the Air Quality Improvement Program for clean vehicle/equipment projects and research (AB 118).
source_quote: Under AB 118 (Núñez, Chapter 750, Statutes of 2007), ARB is administering the Air Quality Improvement Program, which provides approximately $50 million per year for grants to fund clean vehicle/equipment projects and research on the air quality impacts of alternative fuels and advanced technology vehicles.
section_header: Air Quality Improvement Program/Alternative and Renewable Fuel and Vehicle Technology Program
extraction_rationale: Ongoing funding commitment (grant program) with annual amount; supports low-carbon transport technologies.

policy_statement: Invest up to $120 million per year (2008–2015) via CEC Alternative and Renewable Fuel and Vehicle Technology Program to transform fuels/vehicles (AB 118).
source_quote: AB 118 also created the Alternative and Renewable Fuel and Vehicle Technology Program and authorized CEC to spend up to $120 million per year for over seven years (from 2008-2015) to develop, demonstrate, and deploy innovative technologies to transform California's fuel and vehicle types.
section_header: Air Quality Improvement Program/Alternative and Renewable Fuel and Vehicle Technology Program
extraction_rationale: Explicit multi-year public investment authorization with amounts and timeframe; supports low-carbon fuels/vehicles.

policy_statement: Set statewide energy efficiency targets: reduce annual electricity demand by 32,000 GWh and natural gas consumption by 800 million therms from business-as-usual.
source_quote: This measure would set new targets for statewide annual energy demand reductions of 32,000 gigawatt hours and 800 million therms from business as usual - enough to power more than 5 million homes, or replace the need to build about ten new large power plants (500 megawatts each).
extraction_rationale: Quantified statewide efficiency targets; clear resource-efficiency policy with major emissions implications.

policy_statement: Implement Solar Hot Water and Efficiency Act incentive program: $250 million over 10 years to install 200,000 solar water heating systems by 2017.
source_quote: The Solar Hot Water and Efficiency Act of 2007 (SHWEA) authorized a ten year, $250-million incentive program for solar water heaters with a goal of promoting the installation of 200,000 systems in California by 2017.
extraction_rationale: Specific incentive program with funding amount and deployment target; reduces fossil fuel use for water heating.

policy_statement: Increase combined heat and power (CHP) by an additional 4,000 MW installed capacity by 2020 (displacing ~30,000 GWh).
source_quote: This measure sets a target of an additional 4,000 MW of installed CHP capacity by 2020, enough to displace approximately 30,000 GWh of demand from other power generation sources.
extraction_rationale: Quantified capacity target with deadline; specific energy system intervention.

policy_statement: Achieve a statewide Renewables Portfolio Standard of 33% renewable electricity by 2020.
source_quote: Based on Governor Schwarzenegger's call for a statewide 33 percent RPS, the Plan anticipates that California will have 33 percent of its electricity provided by renewable resources by 2020, and includes the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions based on this level.
extraction_rationale: Quantified renewable energy target with deadline; core mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Adopt Low Carbon Fuel Standard to reduce carbon intensity of transportation fuels by at least 10% by 2020; develop regulation for Board consideration March 2009.
source_quote: ARB is developing a Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS), which would reduce the carbon intensity of California's transportation fuels by at least ten percent by 2020 as called for by Governor Schwarzenegger in Executive Order S-01-07. ARB identified the LCFS as a Discrete Early Action item, and is developing a regulation for Board consideration in March 2009.
extraction_rationale: Specific performance standard with quantified target and regulatory timeline; direct mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Develop regional passenger vehicle GHG reduction targets for 2020 and 2035 by September 30, 2010 under SB 375 in consultation with MPOs.
source_quote: SB 375 requires ARB to develop, in consultation with metropolitan planning organizations (MPOs), passenger vehicle greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets for 2020 and 2035 by September 30, 2010.
extraction_rationale: Binding statutory requirement with deadline to set regional targets; direct mitigation planning instrument.

policy_statement: Implement light-duty vehicle efficiency measures including tire inflation regulation and other efficiency actions to reduce GHGs.
source_quote: ARB is pursuing a regulation to ensure that tires are properly inflated when vehicles are serviced. ARB is also pursuing ways to reduce engine load via lower friction oil and reducing the need for air conditioner use.
extraction_rationale: Specific regulatory and program actions to improve vehicle efficiency; concrete interventions though not fully quantified here.

policy_statement: Require ship electrification at ports and implement additional goods movement efficiency measures to reduce GHGs.
source_quote: ARB has already adopted a regulation to require ship electrification at ports. ARB is proposing to develop and implement additional measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions due to goods movement from trucks, ports and other related facilities.
extraction_rationale: Adopted regulation plus commitment to develop additional measures; specific sector intervention.

policy_statement: Install 3,000 MW of new solar-electric capacity under the Million Solar Roofs Program by 2017 (SB 1).
source_quote: California has set a goal to install 3,000 megawatts (MW) of new solar capacity by 2017 - moving the state toward a cleaner energy future and helping lower the cost of solar systems for consumers. The Million Solar Roofs Initiative is a ratepayer-financed incentive program aimed at transforming the market for rooftop solar systems by driving down costs over time.
extraction_rationale: Quantified deployment goal and incentive program; direct mitigation via distributed solar.

policy_statement: Adopt medium- and heavy-duty vehicle efficiency measures including aerodynamic retrofits and hybridization.
source_quote: Requiring retrofits to improve the fuel efficiency of heavy-duty trucks could include a requirement for devices that reduce aerodynamic drag and rolling resistance. In addition, hybridization of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles would also reduce greenhouse gas emissions through increased fuel efficiency.
extraction_rationale: Specific regulatory measures proposed for HDV efficiency and hybridization; concrete interventions.

policy_statement: Industrial emissions measures including audits and controls on oil/gas and refinery methane/flaring.
source_quote: Require assessment of large industrial sources to determine whether individual sources within a facility can cost-effectively reduce greenhouse gas emissions and provide other pollution reduction co-benefits. Reduce greenhouse gas emissions from fugitive emissions from oil and gas extraction and gas transmission. Adopt and implement regulations to control fugitive methane emissions and reduce flaring at refineries.
extraction_rationale: Umbrella initiative with multiple distinct sub-actions described in the section.

parent_statement: Industrial emissions measures including audits and controls on oil/gas and refinery methane/flaring.
policy_statement: Require major industrial facilities to conduct energy efficiency and co-benefits audits via regulation.
source_quote: ARB would implement this measure through a regulation, requiring each facility to conduct an energy efficiency audit of individual combustion and other direct sources of greenhouse gases within the facility to determine the potential reduction opportunities, including criteria air pollutants and toxic air contaminants. The audit would include an assessment of the impacts of replacing or upgrading older, less efficient units such as boilers and heaters, or replacing the units with combined heat and power (CHP) units.
section_header: Energy Efficiency and Co-Benefits Audits for Large Industrial Sources
extraction_rationale: Specific regulatory requirement (audits) with defined scope and purpose; actionable policy.

parent_statement: Industrial emissions measures including audits and controls on oil/gas and refinery methane/flaring.
policy_statement: Develop measures to reduce methane emissions from oil and gas production via leak detection, retrofits, and best management practices.
source_quote: Two measures would be developed to reduce methane emissions in the oil and gas production and gas transmission processes from leaks and incomplete combustion of methane (used as fuel). These measures would include improved leak detection, process modifications, equipment retrofits, installation of new equipment, and best management practices.
section_header: Oil and Gas Recovery Operations and Transmission/Refineries
extraction_rationale: Specific planned measures with named interventions to reduce fugitive methane.

parent_statement: Industrial emissions measures including audits and controls on oil/gas and refinery methane/flaring.
policy_statement: Develop measures to reduce methane emissions from natural gas pipeline transmission systems.
source_quote: The first measure would affect oil and gas producers. The second would impact operators of natural gas pipeline systems.
section_header: Oil and Gas Recovery Operations and Transmission/Refineries
extraction_rationale: Specific measure targeting pipeline operators; though brief, it is a defined intervention area within the industrial measures.

parent_statement: Industrial emissions measures including audits and controls on oil/gas and refinery methane/flaring.
policy_statement: Develop refinery measures to limit GHG emissions from flaring while preserving safety flaring.
source_quote: Two measures would be developed for oil refineries. The first would limit the greenhouse gas emissions from refinery flares while preserving flaring as needed for safety reasons.
section_header: Oil and Gas Recovery Operations and Transmission/Refineries
extraction_rationale: Specific planned refinery control measure; clear intervention.

parent_statement: Industrial emissions measures including audits and controls on oil/gas and refinery methane/flaring.
policy_statement: Remove methane exemption from refinery VOC regulations to address methane's role in global warming.
source_quote: The second would remove the current fugitive methane exemption in most refinery Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) regulations. This exemption was established because methane does not appreciably contribute to urban smog, but is inappropriate given the role that methane plays in global warming.
section_header: Oil and Gas Recovery Operations and Transmission/Refineries
extraction_rationale: Specific regulatory change described and justified; direct mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Support implementation of a high-speed rail system between northern and southern California to reduce GHG emissions.
source_quote: A high speed rail (HSR) system is part of the statewide strategy to provide more mobility choice and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. This measure supports implementation of plans to construct and operate a HSR system between northern and southern California.
extraction_rationale: Explicit support for a major transportation infrastructure project framed as a GHG reduction measure; somewhat contingent on voter approval but still a policy commitment in the plan.

policy_statement: Expand green building practices and adopt/strengthen green building codes, including moving toward mandatory commercial green building code in 2011.
source_quote: In July 2008, the California Building Standards Commission (CBSC) adopted the Green Building Standards Code (GBSC) for all new construction in the state. While the current version of the commercial green building code is voluntary, CBSC anticipates adopting a mandatory code in 2011 which will institute minimum environmental performance standards for all occupancies.
extraction_rationale: Regulatory building code adoption and planned mandate with timeline; concrete policy lever for emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Require new State buildings to achieve LEED-NC Gold and retrofit existing State buildings to LEED-EB Silver equivalent; require CHPS 2009 criteria for new schools and modernization-funded schools.
source_quote: The State of California will set an example by requiring all new State buildings to exceed existing Green Building Initiative energy goals and achieve nationally-recognized building sustainability standards such as Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design - New Construction (LEED-NC) 'Gold' certification. Existing State buildings would also be retrofitted to achieve higher standards equivalent to LEED-EB for existing buildings (EB) 'Silver.'
extraction_rationale: Specific procurement/standards requirements for State facilities and schools; actionable and standards-based.

policy_statement: High Global Warming Potential (GWP) gases measures including direct regulations and an upstream mitigation fee.
source_quote: Recommended measures to address this growing problem take the form of direct regulations and use of mitigation fees. ARB is also proposing to establish an upstream mitigation fee on the use of high GWP gases.
extraction_rationale: Umbrella policy area with multiple discrete measures and a fee instrument; sub-measures are enumerated in Table 19.

parent_statement: High Global Warming Potential (GWP) gases measures including direct regulations and an upstream mitigation fee.
policy_statement: Establish an upstream mitigation fee on high-GWP gases to reflect climate impact in prices and encourage reduced use, reduced end-of-life losses, and alternatives.
source_quote: ARB is also proposing to establish an upstream mitigation fee on the use of high GWP gases. An upstream fee would ensure that the climate impact of these substances is reflected in the total cost of the product, encouraging reduced use and end-of-life losses, as well as the development of alternatives.
extraction_rationale: Clear financial instrument (fee) with stated behavioral objectives; direct climate policy.

policy_statement: Reduce methane emissions at landfills and move toward high recycling and zero-waste through diversion, composting, and commercial recycling.
source_quote: Reduce methane emissions at landfills. Increase waste diversion, composting, and commercial recycling. Move toward zero-waste.
extraction_rationale: Specific sector policy direction with named interventions; includes regulatory early action for landfill methane and broader waste diversion strategy.

policy_statement: Maintain 5 MMTCO2E of forest sequestration through sustainable management practices and avoiding/mitigating land-use changes that reduce carbon storage.
source_quote: The 2020 Proposed Scoping Plan target for California's forest sector is to maintain the current 5 MMTCO2E of sequestration through sustainable management practices, including reducing the risk of catastrophic wildfire, and the avoidance or mitigation of land-use changes that reduce carbon storage.
extraction_rationale: Quantified sequestration target with defined mechanisms (management, wildfire risk reduction, land-use change avoidance).

policy_statement: Implement Water sector measures to improve water and energy efficiency and reduce GHGs, including establishing a public goods charge on water to fund actions.
source_quote: ARB recommends a public goods charge for funding investments in water management actions that improve water and energy efficiency and reduce GHG emissions. As noted by the Economic and Technology Advancements Advisory Committee, a public goods charge on water can be collected on water bills and then used to fund end-use water efficiency improvements, system-wide efficiency projects, water recycling, and other actions that improve water and energy efficiency and reduce GHG emissions.
extraction_rationale: Defines a funding mechanism (public goods charge) and eligible investments; direct climate-related resource efficiency policy.

policy_statement: Encourage voluntary investment in manure digesters at dairies and reassess at five-year Scoping Plan update whether to make mandatory for large dairies by 2020.
source_quote: Encouraging the capture of methane through use of manure digester systems at dairies can provide emission reductions on a voluntary basis. The voluntary approach will be re-assessed at the five-year update of the Scoping Plan to determine if the program should become mandatory for large dairies by 2020.
extraction_rationale: Specific intervention (manure digesters) with a decision point to potentially mandate by 2020; somewhat conditional but includes a clear future regulatory consideration.

policy_statement: Set aside allowances in the first cap-and-trade compliance period to reward voluntary reductions occurring before 2012 and avoid disadvantaging early reducers (2007–2012).
source_quote: First, within the cap-and-trade program, ARB would set aside a certain number of allowances from the first compliance period to use to reward voluntary reductions that occur before 2012. In addition, ARB will assure that the allocation process in the first compliance period does not disadvantage facilities that have made reductions after AB 32 went into effect at the start of 2007 and before 2012.
extraction_rationale: Concrete cap-and-trade design commitment (allowance set-aside and allocation protection) to credit early action.

policy_statement: Adopt methodologies for quantifying voluntary reductions (offsets) under HSC §38571; Board has adopted several methodologies (forest, local government operations, urban forestry, manure digesters).
source_quote: ARB will adopt methodologies for quantifying voluntary reductions. (HSC §38571) The Board adopted a methodology for forest projects in October 2007, and for local government operations, urban forestry, and manure digesters in September 2008.
extraction_rationale: Commitment to adopt quantification methodologies with examples already adopted; enables offset integrity and potential compliance use.

policy_statement: Update the Scoping Plan at least once every five years to evaluate progress and adjust course (HSC §38561(h)).
source_quote: ARB will update the plan at least once every five years (HSC §38561(h)). These updates will allow ARB to evaluate the progress made toward the State's greenhouse gas emission reduction goals and correct the Plan's course where necessary.
extraction_rationale: Statutory planning/update requirement with defined frequency; governance policy for ongoing climate program management.

policy_statement: Implement annual State agency greenhouse gas 'Report Card' reporting and require outside audits every three years as funds are available (SB 85).
source_quote: SB 85 (Budget Committee, Chapter 178, Statutes of 2007) requires every State agency to prepare an annual 'Report Card,' detailing measures the agency has adopted and taken to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, including the actual emissions reduced as a result of those actions. Agencies are also required, as funds are available, to have an outside audit of greenhouse gas-related actions completed every three years to verify actual and projected reductions.
extraction_rationale: Binding reporting and audit requirements; supports accountability for climate actions.

policy_statement: Implement mandatory greenhouse gas reporting regulation for largest sources, with tracking starting 2008, reporting beginning 2009, and third-party verification beginning 2010.
source_quote: Affected facilities will begin tracking their greenhouse gas emissions in 2008, to be reported beginning in 2009 with a phase-in process to allow facilities to develop reporting systems and train personnel in data collection. Beginning in 2010, emissions reports will be more rigorous and will be subject to third-party verification.
extraction_rationale: Specific regulatory requirement with phased compliance dates and verification; foundational climate governance policy.

policy_statement: Develop a fee regulation to fund AB 32 program administration, aiming to begin collecting fees in FY 2009–2010; ~$55 million/year needed ongoing.
source_quote: This fall ARB will initiate a rulemaking for a fee program to fund administration of the program. ARB is moving on an expedited schedule to develop a fee regulation and expects to take a regulation to the Board in early 2009, with the aim of beginning to collect fees in the 2009-2010 fiscal year.
extraction_rationale: Concrete financial instrument (fees) with rulemaking and collection timeline; supports implementation capacity.

policy_statement: Develop climate change education components for California K–12 model curriculum by 2010 (Education and the Environment Initiative).
source_quote: By 2010, California will develop climate change education components to the State's new K-12 model school curriculum as part of the Education and the Environment Initiative (AB 1548, Pavley, Chapter 665, Statutes of 2003).
extraction_rationale: Time-bound curriculum development commitment; supports implementation through education/capacity building (indirect climate relevance).

policy_statement: Implement a robust statewide public outreach and education program coordinated by a Climate Action Team steering team.
source_quote: The Proposed Plan calls for a robust statewide program designed to generate awareness and involvement in California's climate change efforts. The Climate Action Team will convene a steering team that includes State agencies and other public agencies such as the state's air districts, and public and private utilities, which have a strong track record of successful efforts at public education to reduce driving (Spare the Air) or promote energy efficiency and reduce energy demand.
extraction_rationale: Specific program commitment (statewide outreach) with an implementation structure (steering team). Somewhat broad but clearly an implementation action.

policy_statement: Recommend a de minimis threshold of 0.1 MMTCO2E annual emissions per source category for regulatory applicability considerations.
source_quote: After this review and considering the level of emissions needed to meet the 1990 target established by AB 32, ARB recommends a de minimis level 0.1 MMTCO2E annual emissions per source category. Source categories whose total aggregated emissions are below this level are not proposed for emission reduction requirements in the Proposed Scoping Plan but may contribute toward the target via other means.
extraction_rationale: A concrete policy threshold guiding regulatory scope; directly tied to AB 32 implementation.

policy_statement: Invest $188 million in equity-focused climate interventions including building retrofits, air quality monitoring expansion, and planting over 75,000 trees.
source_quote: “To kickstart the implementation of my administration's climate strategy, we are investing $188 million in equity-focused interventions, spanning building retrofits, the expansion of the air quality monitoring network, to the planting of over 75,000 trees. The sum of these actions represents the beginning of our transition to a climate just society, the future of which is defined in this document.”
extraction_rationale: Contains a specific committed funding amount ($188 million) and named interventions (retrofits, air monitoring, tree planting), qualifying as a policy and a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Plant 75,000 trees by 2026 as part of Chicago's tree equity strategy.
source_quote: “A tree data tool that helps prioritize the planting of trees in areas of Chicago where the benefits of trees are most needed guides the initiative. Together with city departments and community partners, Chicago has the goal of planting 75,000 trees by 2026.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified target (75,000 trees) with a deadline (by 2026); clearly a nature-based climate action.

policy_statement: Establish community-led climate advisory boards and forums for regular community participation in implementing, reporting, and achieving 2022 CAP actions.
source_quote: “City departments and sister agencies will be key to executing many of the actions listed in the 2022 CAP. The City will also establish community-led climate advisory boards and forums for regular community participation in implementing, reporting, and achieving the actions related to the 2022 CAP.”
extraction_rationale: A specific governance intervention (“will establish” boards and forums) tied to implementation and accountability of climate actions.

policy_statement: Develop more City Council resolutions and ordinances to bolster 2022 CAP actions.
source_quote: “For example, the 2019 resolution-Support for Implementation of Clean Energy Transition Plan (R2019-157 )-established the City's goal to transition to citywide renewable energy by 2035. The City will develop more resolutions and ordinances to bolster the actions of the 2022 CAP.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit commitment to future legislation (“will develop more resolutions and ordinances”) to implement CAP actions; somewhat broad but still a policy lever commitment.

policy_statement: Reduce Chicago's GHG emissions by a minimum of 62% by 2040 (using 2017 inventory as baseline).
