(c) the mitigation of the potential contribution to Fiji's greenhouse gas emissions of the decision or action;”
section_header: Decision-makers must promote and ensure consistency with climate objectives (Section 19)
extraction_rationale: Creates a binding decision standard across a schedule of laws; directly climate-directed.

policy_statement: Issue and publish guidelines for decision-makers on the scope and application of climate factors required under Section 19.
source_quote:
“The Minister must issue guidelines for a person making a decision referred to in section 19(1) as to the scope and application of the factors that the person is required to consider under section 19(2) when making that decision or taking that action.

The Minister must publish guidelines issued in accordance with this section in the Gazette.”
section_header: Ministerial guidelines for actions and decisions (Section 20)
extraction_rationale: Mandatory guidance issuance and publication; operationalizes climate-informed decision-making.

policy_statement: Require ministries to report annually to the Director on implementation of the Act within their ministry.
source_quote: “Each ministry must report annually to the Director on the implementation of this Act within their ministry, including on the implementation of any duties, functions and obligations assigned to a minister or department under this Act or regulations made under this Act.”
section_header: Integration of this Act within ministries (Section 21)
extraction_rationale: Creates a recurring reporting obligation supporting accountability.

policy_statement: Require environmental impact assessments to assess material GHG emissions, climate vulnerability impacts, and climate risks to the activity, and include measures to address them.
source_quote: “Where an environmental impact assessment is required under the Environment Management Act 2005 for a proposed activity or undertaking, and that proposed activity or undertaking may result in material greenhouse gas emissions, increased climate vulnerability of the surrounding area including upstream or downstream impacts, or could be adversely affected by the impacts of climate change, the environmental impact assessment must include an assessment of those matters and measures to address them.”
extraction_rationale: Binding regulatory requirement integrating climate into EIA processes.

policy_statement: Align government procurement policies with climate objectives and key climate plans, including minimum standards for resilience and low/zero-emissions sourcing.
source_quote:
“The Fijian Procurement Office established by the Procurement Regulations 2010 must formulate procurement policies that are consistent with, or review and update existing procurement policies to ensure they are consistent with, the objectives and principles of this Act and the implementation of Fiji's NDC, NCCP, LEDS, NAP and National Ocean Policy and where possible, these procurement policies are to set minimum standards for-

(a) promoting adaptation and climate resilience; and (b) sourcing zero or low emissions products, vehicles or energy sources.”
extraction_rationale: Mandatory procurement policy alignment with explicit minimum standards; has clear mitigation and adaptation mechanisms.

policy_statement: Require ministers to annually review portfolios/functions for climate risks and adjust KPIs; and revise civil servant KPIs/job descriptions to build specialist skills for Act implementation.
source_quote:
“All ministers must, where relevant, annually review and assess ministerial portfolios and functions in relation to climate risks and make adjustments and changes to key performance indicators with the aim of ensuring climate change considerations are able to be adequately addressed.

All ministers must, where relevant, review and revise key performance indicators and job descriptions for civil servants within their ministry with the aim of ensuring that civil servants are increasingly equipped with relevant specialist skills to support the implementation of this Act.”
section_header: Ministerial portfolios, functions and human resourcing (Section 24)
extraction_rationale: Creates recurring administrative obligations to mainstream climate risk and build capacity.

policy_statement: Integrate evidence-based learning about climate change into the Fiji National Curriculum Framework at all levels.
source_quote: “In accordance with section 31(4) of the Constitution, the minister responsible for education must, in consultation with the Minister, integrate evidence-based learning about climate change into a variety of subjects of the Fiji National Curriculum Framework at all levels of the curriculum.”
section_header: Integration of climate change into curricula (Section 25)
extraction_rationale: Binding education-sector intervention with clear implementation requirement.

policy_statement: Require climate-related information in national budget supplement and require State entities to include climate-relevant expenditure and support needs in budget submissions; publish compliance guidelines.
source_quote:
“The minister responsible for finance must provide information on the economic implications of climate change in the supplement to the national budget.

All State entities must include in their budget submissions- (a) actual and estimated details of climate-relevant expenditure... and (b) information on support needed and received in relation to finance, technology transfer and capacity-building under Articles 9, 10 and 11 of the Paris Agreement.”
extraction_rationale: Creates mandatory budgeting and disclosure requirements; supports climate finance tracking and planning.

policy_statement: Develop and implement a National Climate Change Policy (NCCP) until 2030 and for successive 10-year periods; publish online before each period.
source_quote:
“The Minister must, with the assistance of the Committee, develop and implement a NCCP for the period until 2030 and for successive periods of 10 years.

The Minister must publish the NCCP online prior to the commencement of each successive period.”
section_header: PART 6-DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATION OF THE NATIONAL CLIMATE CHANGE POLICY
extraction_rationale: Legally mandated policy instrument with defined time horizons and publication requirement.

policy_statement: Develop and implement monitoring and evaluation frameworks to track NCCP delivery timeframes, institutional performance, and progress against development objectives.
source_quote:
“The Minister must develop and implement monitoring and evaluation frameworks and systems to monitor, in relation to the NCCP-

(a) delivery time-frames for results; (b) institutional performance and knowledge retention; and (c) progress made against development objectives.”
section_header: Development of the National Climate Change Policy (Section 27)
extraction_rationale: Specific required systems for M&E; concrete implementation mechanism.

policy_statement: Review and amend the NCCP for successive 10-year periods aligned with NDC review cycles; report to Parliament and publish online; Parliament must approve/amend/reject amendments.
source_quote:
“The Minister must, with the assistance of the Committee, review and amend the NCCP for successive 10-year periods in alignment with the review and enhancement of Fiji's successive NDCs under Part 3.

Parliament must consider the report and proposed amendments to the plan... and must either approve, amend or reject the Minister's proposed amendments to the NCCP.”
section_header: Review of the National Climate Change Policy (Section 28)
extraction_rationale: Creates a formal review/amendment cycle with legislative oversight—clear governance policy.

policy_statement: Develop a Fijian GHG Inventory and make it publicly available online on the Information Platform.
source_quote:
“The Minister must develop the Fijian GHG Inventory in accordance with the good practice guidelines and methodologies established under the Convention, accepted by the IPCC and agreed upon by the CMA.

The Minister must make the Fijian GHG Inventory publicly available online on the Information Platform.”
extraction_rationale: Binding MRV infrastructure requirement; directly supports mitigation accounting.

policy_statement: Require biennial sectoral emissions and emissions-reduction data estimation/compilation by specified permanent secretaries and compilation by the Director.
source_quote:
“The following permanent secretaries must biennially estimate and compile data related to emissions and emissions reductions activities from within their portfolio and submit it to the Committe- ...

The Director must compile the emissions and emissions reductions data reported in relation to each sector, take all reasonable steps to ensure the data is consistent and accurate, and submit the compiled emissions and emissions reduction data to the Committee.”
section_header: Sector-based collection of data and information needed to estimate emissions and emissions reduction data (Section 30)
extraction_rationale: Creates recurring MRV duties across sectors; concrete administrative requirement.

policy_statement: Mandate biennial reporting on bulk fuel sales by fuel importers and require guidelines on content and form of reporting.
source_quote:
“A person who imports fuels into Fiji for the purposes of distributing or selling fuel to companies or individuals must keep and biennially provide information to the permanent secretary responsible for transport on the amount of fuel sold for the financial year.

The Minister must develop and publish guidelines on the content and form of the information that is to be kept and provided...”
section_header: Mandatory reporting on bulk sale of fuels (Section 31)
extraction_rationale: Binding reporting requirement supporting emissions estimation for transport fuels.

policy_statement: Prepare a national inventory report biennially, submit it to the Minister ahead of Paris deadlines, and publish it online.
source_quote:
“The Director must prepare a national inventory report biennially and in accordance with the Paris Agreement, using the emissions data contained in the Fijian GHG Inventory.

The Director must make national inventory reports publicly available online as soon as practicable after they are submitted...”
extraction_rationale: Concrete, time-bound MRV deliverable required for Paris Agreement transparency.

policy_statement: Develop a publicly accessible online Information Platform within 12 months and maintain it with specified climate data, policies, and reports; ensure accessibility for people with disabilities.
source_quote:
“Within 12 months of the commencement of this section, the Director must develop a publicly accessible Information Platform online for the purpose of increasing the availability and accessibility of comprehensive data, information and government policies related to climate change.

The Director must take all reasonable steps to ensure that the Information Platform is accessible to people with disabilities.”
extraction_rationale: Time-bound creation of a named system with ongoing maintenance and accessibility requirements.

policy_statement: Set Fiji’s long-term emissions reduction target as net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050 and require steps to promote achievement via carbon budgets and key strategies.
source_quote:
“The long term emissions reduction target for Fiji is net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050.

The Minister must, with the assistance of the Committee, take all reasonable steps to promote the achievement of the long term emissions reduction target through the development and implementation of carbon budgets, the LEDS, NCCP and NDC.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit quantified mitigation target plus mandated implementation approach.

policy_statement: Publish every 5 years a statement on national emissions, progress toward NDC and long-term target, and recommendations for measures needed to meet targets.
source_quote:
“Every 5 years the Minister must, with the assistance of the Committee, publish a statement of-

(a) Fiji's greenhouse gas emissions over the 5-year period... (b) an assessment of the progress made towards Fiji's NDC and the long term emissions reduction target... and (c) recommendations on measures needed to meet the emissions reduction target in Fiji's NDC and the long-term emissions reduction target.”
extraction_rationale: Recurring transparency and planning requirement tied to mitigation targets.

policy_statement: Establish 5-year carbon budgets for 2026–2050 with specified determination deadlines, parliamentary tabling, online publication, and increasing ambition over time.
source_quote:
“The Minister, with the assistance of the Committee, must determine a carbon budget for Fiji in respect of each of the following periods- (a) 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2030; ... (e) 1 January 2046 to 31 December 2050.

The Minister must ensure that each carbon budget constitutes a greater reduction in greenhouse gas emissions than any previous carbon budget as part of the cumulative effort to achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions by the year 2050.”
extraction_rationale: Creates a binding carbon budgeting system with dates and ratcheting requirement.

policy_statement: Require carbon budgets to be expressed as reductions relative to 2013 emissions and require determination of the 2013 emissions figure using IPCC methodologies.
source_quote:
“Each carbon budget must be expressed as the extent to which the amount of Fiji's greenhouse gas emissions is to be reduced in relation to the amount of Fiji's greenhouse gas emissions for the year 2013.

For the purposes of this section, the Minister must determine a figure that represents the amount of Fiji's greenhouse gas emissions for the year 2013 in accordance with the IPCC methodologies.”
extraction_rationale: Defines binding accounting format for carbon budgets; supports enforceability and comparability.

policy_statement: Empower the Minister to introduce economy-wide mitigation regulations/measures/actions, including carbon pricing, fees, incentives/levies, sink protection, low-emissions building policies, and awareness programmes.
source_quote:
“The Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions with the purpose of limiting or reducing Fiji's greenhouse gas emissions across the economy...

Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may- (a) introduce and implement a carbon pricing mechanism, including an emissions trading scheme;”
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions (Section 43)
extraction_rationale: Umbrella mitigation authority with an enumerated list of specific instruments and interventions.

parent_statement: Empower the Minister to introduce economy-wide mitigation regulations/measures/actions, including carbon pricing, fees, incentives/levies, sink protection, low-emissions building policies, and awareness programmes.
policy_statement: Introduce and implement a carbon pricing mechanism, including an emissions trading scheme.
source_quote:
“Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may-

(a) introduce and implement a carbon pricing mechanism, including an emissions trading scheme;”
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions (Section 43)
extraction_rationale: Explicit financial instrument (carbon pricing/ETS) authorized by the Act.

parent_statement: Empower the Minister to introduce economy-wide mitigation regulations/measures/actions, including carbon pricing, fees, incentives/levies, sink protection, low-emissions building policies, and awareness programmes.
policy_statement: Prescribe fees and charges paid to the State on volumes of GHG emissions above a prescribed level.
source_quote:
“Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may-

(b) prescribe fees and other charges due to the State paid on the volume of greenhouse gas emissions above a prescribed level;”
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions (Section 43)
extraction_rationale: Explicit emissions fee instrument; clearly a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Empower the Minister to introduce economy-wide mitigation regulations/measures/actions, including carbon pricing, fees, incentives/levies, sink protection, low-emissions building policies, and awareness programmes.
policy_statement: Introduce fiscal incentives and national levies to reduce emissions, conserve natural sinks, and encourage investment in renewables, efficient cogeneration, energy-efficient infrastructure, and zero-waste infrastructure.
source_quote:
“Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may-

(c) introduce and implement fiscal incentives and national levies with the purpose of- (i) limiting or reducing Fiji's greenhouse gas emissions... (ii) enhancing the conservation of natural sinks... and (iii) encouraging public and private investment in renewable energy and efficient cogeneration technologies, energy efficient infrastructure and zero-waste infrastructure and processes;”
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions (Section 43)
extraction_rationale: Explicit fiscal/levy tools (financial instruments) with stated mitigation and sink objectives.

parent_statement: Empower the Minister to introduce economy-wide mitigation regulations/measures/actions, including carbon pricing, fees, incentives/levies, sink protection, low-emissions building policies, and awareness programmes.
policy_statement: Enhance protection of land and ocean carbon sinks, including halting/reversing deforestation, afforestation, REDD+, reef/fisheries conservation, mangrove protection/planting, nature-based coastal protection, and sustainable agriculture.
source_quote:
“Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may-

(d) enhance environmental protection of land and ocean carbon sinks... including with respect to halting and reversing deforestation and degradation of forests, afforestation initiatives, Fiji's REDD+ initiative, reef and fisheries conservation, mangrove protection and planting initiatives, nature-based coastal protection applications and sustainable agricultural practices;”
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions (Section 43)
extraction_rationale: Specific named interventions to protect/enhance sinks; primarily nature-based mechanisms explicitly tied to mitigation.

parent_statement: Empower the Minister to introduce economy-wide mitigation regulations/measures/actions, including carbon pricing, fees, incentives/levies, sink protection, low-emissions building policies, and awareness programmes.
policy_statement: Make regulations and develop policies for sustainable, low-emissions, energy-efficient, climate-resilient infrastructure and buildings.
source_quote:
“Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may-

(e) make regulations and develop policies for the construction of sustainable, low-emissions, energy efficient and climate resilient infrastructure and buildings;”
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions (Section 43)
extraction_rationale: Concrete regulatory authority for building/infrastructure standards combining efficiency and resilience.

policy_statement: Develop and implement a Transport Decarbonisation Implementation Strategy within 2 years to decarbonise the transport sector by 2050; review/update every 5 years.
source_quote:
“The Minister must, in consultation with the Minister responsible for transport, develop and implement a detailed Transport Decarbonisation Implementation Strategy within 2 years from the commencement of this section, that builds upon the LEDS to decarbonise the transport sector by 2050.

The Minister must review and update the Transport Decarbonisation Implementation Strategy every 5 years.”
extraction_rationale: Time-bound strategy requirement with a sectoral decarbonisation endpoint and periodic review.

policy_statement: Create and register carbon sequestration property rights as a distinct legal right to carbon sequestration and carbon stocks, enabling transfer and dealing as property.
source_quote:
“In this Act, carbon sequestration property right means the exclusive and distinct legal right to carbon sequestration and carbon stocks.

A carbon sequestration property right- (a) must be registered in accordance with this Part... and (f) when registered... entitles the right holder to deal with the right whether by sale, transfer, mortgage, charge or pledge.”
extraction_rationale: Establishes a legal framework enabling carbon rights and market transactions; foundational for mitigation projects.

policy_statement: Prohibit approval of mining/logging/extractive activities on land with registered carbon sequestration property rights where a REDD+ or specified emissions reduction project is approved.
source_quote:
“No mining, logging, exploration, exploitation or extractive activity is to be approved on lands over which-

(a) a carbon sequestration property right has been registered; and (b) an international REDD+ program or emissions reduction project, programme or activity involving forests, blue carbon or other project, programme or activity type prescribed by regulations made under this Act has been approved.”
section_header: Land over which a carbon sequestration property right is registered (Section 47)
extraction_rationale: Clear regulatory prohibition protecting carbon projects/sinks; enforceable land-use constraint.

policy_statement: Assign the Minister responsible for forests duties to develop/update REDD+ policy/strategy, reference level, safeguards, participation, and benefit-sharing arrangements.
source_quote:
“The Minister responsible for forests is responsible for-

(a) developing and updating Fiji's national REDD+ policy and strategy... (e) developing a benefit sharing arrangement for forest emission reduction projects, programmes and activities.”
extraction_rationale: Defines specific governmental responsibilities for a named mitigation policy framework (REDD+).

policy_statement: Create a process to declare and register Fijian Emissions Reduction Projects/Programmes/Activities, with Director determination within 60 days and registry registration.
source_quote:
“A person may apply to the Director for the declaration of an emissions reduction project, programme or activity as a Fijian Emissions Reduction Project, Programme or Activity.

The Director must determine, in writing, an application... within 60 days... and... must immediately register a Fijian Emissions Reduction Project, Programme or Activity in the Registry.”
section_header: Fijian Emissions Reduction Projects, Programmes or Activities (Section 50)
extraction_rationale: Creates an approval and registration system for mitigation projects with deadlines.

policy_statement: Issue Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units (FMOU) equal to verified emissions reductions after issuance of a Fijian Emissions Reduction Statement.
source_quote:
“If a Fijian Emissions Reduction Statement has been issued... the Director must... issue to the Registry account nominated on the statement a number of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units equal to the number specified in the statement as the unit entitlement for that statement.

Upon the issuance of a Fijian Mitigation Outcome Unit to a person, that person will be the legal owner of the Fijian Mitigation Outcome Unit.”
section_header: Issue of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units (Section 52)
extraction_rationale: Creates a statutory carbon credit issuance mechanism; central to mitigation market operations.

policy_statement: Require proponents to report reversals/loss of carbon stocks and remedy them or cancel equivalent units within 90 days; allow revocation for non-compliance.
source_quote:
“If Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units have been issued... and there has been a material reversal or loss of carbon stocks... the proponent must report the reversal or loss of carbon stocks to the Director...

A proponent may satisfy a requirement... by, within 90 days... (b) purchasing and cancelling a number of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units or other emissions reduction units approved by the Director as equivalent to the reversal or loss of carbon stocks.”
section_header: Requirement to cancel Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units where there has been a reversal of sequestration (Section 54)
extraction_rationale: Enforceable permanence/compliance mechanism for sequestration-based mitigation credits.

policy_statement: Require Director consent for international-standard emissions reduction projects and for use/sale/transfer of units; require existing projects to apply to continue; require registry tracking and inventory accounting.
source_quote:
“A person may apply to the Director for the Director's consent for the proponent to- (a) register or conduct an emissions reduction project... under an approved international emissions reduction standard... or (b) use, sell and transfer... emissions reduction units...

Emissions reduction projects... registered... prior to the date this section commences must apply for the Director's consent... to continue conducting the project...”
section_header: Registration and conduct under approved international emissions reduction standards (Section 55)
extraction_rationale: Creates a regulatory approval and tracking regime for international carbon standards operating in Fiji.

policy_statement: Allow conversion of international-standard emission reduction units to Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units subject to consent and anti-double-counting conditions.
source_quote:
“The proponent... may apply to the Director for the Director's consent... to convert... emission reduction units... to Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units.

The Director may only grant consent... if he or she is satisfied that- (a) there will be no double-counting of emissions reductions;”
section_header: Conversion of emission reduction units... to Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units (Section 56)
extraction_rationale: Defines a concrete market mechanism with integrity safeguards.

policy_statement: Require Director consent for Article 6 emissions reduction projects and require registry tracking with unique serial numbers; allow revocation for fraud/non-compliance.
source_quote:
“A person who registers, conducts or otherwise operates an emissions reduction project... in Fiji for the purposes of Article 6 of the Paris Agreement without the consent of the Director commits an offence...

The Director must record the approval of a project... in the Registry, and give emissions reduction units, including ITMOs... a unique serial number that allows them to be registered and tracked by the Registry.”
section_header: Emissions reduction projects... for the purposes of Article 6 (Section 57)
extraction_rationale: Creates enforceable authorization and accounting rules for Article 6 participation.

policy_statement: Require Director consent for international transfer of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units and require recording approvals in the Registry.
source_quote:
“A person who, without the consent of the Director- (a) transfers Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units to a foreign account; or (b) transfers Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units internationally and for the purposes of Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, commits an offence...

The Director must record the approval of an international transfer under this section in the Registry...”
section_header: International transfer of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units (Section 58)
extraction_rationale: Regulatory control over carbon credit exports with registry-based accounting.

policy_statement: Establish the Fijian Registry as an electronic, publicly accessible registry for emissions reduction projects and units (including ITMOs).
source_quote:
“This section establishes the Fijian Registry.

The Director must keep and maintain the Registry by electronic means. The Director must make the Registry publicly accessible online.”
extraction_rationale: Creates a named MRV/market infrastructure system with public accessibility requirement.

policy_statement: Establish the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) Steering Committee and require it to meet at least every 5 years to review the NAP.
source_quote:
“This section establishes the National Adaptation Plan Steering Committee.

The NAP Steering Committee must meet as and when instructed by the Minister or at least every 5 years for the purpose of reviewing the NAP...”
extraction_rationale: Creates an institutional adaptation governance mechanism with a minimum review frequency.

policy_statement: Require the NAP Steering Committee to prepare successive National Adaptation Plans and conduct public consultations.
source_quote:
“The NAP Steering Committee must prepare successive NAPs...

The NAP Steering Committee, when developing and reviewing successive NAPs, must conduct public consultations in a manner that encourages the participation of a diverse range of stakeholders...”
extraction_rationale: Binding requirement to produce and update a core adaptation planning instrument.

policy_statement: Empower the Minister to implement adaptation regulations/policies/measures/actions to increase resilience and require recording them on the Adaptation Registry.
source_quote:
“The Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, policies, measures, adaptation planning processes and actions with the purpose of increasing Fiji's resilience to climate change and ability to adapt to climate change.

The Director must record any regulations, policies, measures, adaptation planning processes and actions implemented in accordance with this section on the Adaptation Registry.”
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement... adaptation... (Section 68)
extraction_rationale: Creates adaptation implementation authority plus a transparency/recording requirement.

policy_statement: Develop integrated risk scenarios and publish them online on the Information Platform.
source_quote:
“These integrated risk scenarios must- (a) model the potential and projected physical impacts of climate change...

The Director must present any integrated risk scenarios to the Committee and make them publicly available online, including on the Information Platform.”
extraction_rationale: Defines a specific analytical product and mandates publication; supports adaptation decision-making.

policy_statement: Conduct an audit of public infrastructure and physical assets at risk from climate change and optionally maintain a register including repairs to increase resilience.
source_quote:
“The Minister may... conduct an audit of existing public infrastructure and physical assets that are at risk from climate change...

The Minister may maintain a register... and any repairs carried out... for the purpose of increasing resilience to the impacts of climate change.”
section_header: Audit of public infrastructure and physical assets (Section 70)
extraction_rationale: A defined adaptation intervention (risk audit/register). Some discretion (“may”), but concrete and operational.

policy_statement: Require climate risk and resilience assessments for proposals for new infrastructure and require guidelines on conducting such assessments.
source_quote:
“All ministers, State entities and other persons making decisions relating to proposals for new infrastructure must-- (a) direct that a climate risk and resilience assessment be conducted...

The Minister, in consultation with the Committee, must prepare and issue guidelines on how climate risk and resilience assessments are to be conducted...”
extraction_rationale: Binding requirement affecting infrastructure approvals; explicit adaptation/resilience mechanism.

policy_statement: Review and, if necessary, amend and scale up implementation/enforcement of the National Building Code immediately and every 5 years to increase climate resilience and align with the Act.
source_quote: “The Minister responsible for health... must review and if necessary amend the content, expand the scope and scale up the implementation and enforcement of the National Building Code immediately upon the commencement of this section and every 5 years thereafter for the purpose of increasing the climate resilience of Fiji's buildings...”
extraction_rationale: Time-bound and recurring regulatory update/enforcement commitment for resilience.

policy_statement: Establish the Fijian Adaptation Registry as a publicly accessible electronic registry for adaptation projects.
source_quote:
“This section establishes the Fijian Adaptation Registry.

The Adaptation Registry is to be maintained by electronic means and publicly accessible online.”
extraction_rationale: Creates a named transparency mechanism for adaptation actions.

policy_statement: Prepare and operationalise successive Fijian Planned Relocation Guidelines through standard operating procedures for proactive climate/disaster displacement risk management.
source_quote:
“The Minister, with the assistance of the Fijian Taskforce on Relocation and Displacement, must prepare successive Fijian Planned Relocation Guidelines.

The Minister... must operationalise the Fijian Planned Relocation Guidelines through developing standard operating procedures which enable pro-active processes for addressing the risk of climate and disaster driven displacement.”
extraction_rationale: Binding requirement to produce guidelines and SOPs for climate displacement—clear adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Assign responsibility to relocate and support at-risk communities under specified objectives and procedural safeguards (consultations, hearings, consent, exhaustion of other adaptation measures).
source_quote:
“The Minister, with the support of the Fijian Taskforce on Relocation and Displacement, is responsible for relocating and supporting at-risk communities...

(d) to relocate at-risk communities only when other adaptation measures as set out in the NAP have been exhausted; (e) to relocate at-risk communities only with the full free and prior informed consent of the communities...”
extraction_rationale: Creates a defined government responsibility with explicit conditions and rights-based safeguards.

policy_statement: Allow use of monies in the Climate Relocation of Communities Trust Fund for planned relocation purposes under Part 12.
source_quote: “The Minister may use monies in the Climate Relocation of Communities Trust Fund established under section 3 of the Climate Relocation of Communities Trust Fund Act 2019 for the purposes of this Part.”
section_header: Trust Fund for the Planned Relocation... (Section 78)
extraction_rationale: Explicit financing mechanism enabling adaptation/relocation expenditures.

policy_statement: Set long-term ocean sustainability target (100% sustainably and effectively managed waters) and 2030 marine protected area target (30% by 2030), and promote achievement through the National Ocean Policy.
source_quote:
“This section sets Fiji's long term ocean sustainability target... to be 100% sustainably and effectively managed.

This section sets Fiji's 2030 marine protected area target... for 30%... to be designated as a marine protected area by 2030.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified targets with deadline (2030) and defined management outcome; climate-relevant via ocean resilience/blue carbon framing.

policy_statement: Require preparation and periodic review/update (at least every 5 years) of successive National Ocean Policies with public consultations.
source_quote:
“The National Ocean Policy Steering Committee must prepare successive National Ocean Policies.

The National Ocean Policy Steering Committee must review and if necessary update the National Ocean Policy when instructed by the Minister or at least every 5 years.”
extraction_rationale: Creates a binding policy instrument and review cycle for ocean-climate governance.

policy_statement: Empower the Minister to implement science-based regulations/policies/measures/actions for conservation/restoration of coastal and marine environments, including protecting blue carbon and reducing anthropogenic stresses.
source_quote:
“The Minister may make and implement regulations, policies, measures and actions that promote an evidence-based approach to the conservation and restoration of Fiji's... coastal environments, including-

(a) protecting stores of blue carbon; (b) sustainable management of oceans and reducing anthropogenic stresses on marine and coastal ecosystems;”
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, policies, measures and actions (Section 84)
extraction_rationale: Concrete authority for ocean-related nature-based and pollution-reduction measures; explicitly evidence-based.

policy_statement: Enhance the mitigation potential of oceans through measures including blue carbon enhancement, offshore renewable energy generation, and energy efficiency in maritime services.
source_quote:
“The Minister may make regulations and policies and implement measures and actions to enhance the mitigation potential of oceans, including-

(a) enhancing blue carbon; (b) developing offshore renewable energy generation; and (c) increasing energy efficiency in maritime services.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit mitigation interventions with named mechanisms (blue carbon, offshore renewables, efficiency).

policy_statement: Direct Fiji Meteorological Service or State entities to prepare and regularly update studies on climate change impacts on oceans and ocean resource provision capacity.
source_quote: “The Minister may direct the Fiji Meteorological Service or any State entity to prepare and regularly update studies on the impact of climate change on oceans and the ability of oceans to sustainably provide resources for Fijians...”
section_header: Minister may direct Fiji Meteorological Service or any State entity to prepare studies (Section 86)
extraction_rationale: Defined research/study intervention supporting adaptation and ocean management; discretionary but concrete.

policy_statement: Authorize the finance minister to implement climate budget coding/tracking systems and publicly report on domestic climate finance sources and engagement with climate funds.
source_quote:
“The Minister responsible for finance may- ... (b) work closely with the national budget process... to implement climate budget coding and tracking systems...

(c) carry out the reporting, monitoring and evaluation of domestic climate finance sources including ECAL... and make any such reports publicly available on the Information Platform;”
section_header: Powers of the Minister responsible for finance (Section 87)
extraction_rationale: Creates concrete public financial management and transparency measures for climate finance.

policy_statement: Grant incentives (via regulations) for mitigation, renewable energy, energy efficiency, adaptation/resilience, and accredited climate training programmes; require incentives to be non-discretionary and rule-based.
source_quote:
“The Minister responsible for finance may... grant to persons that- (a) encourage and put in place measures for the mitigation of climate change including reduction of greenhouse emissions, use of renewable energy and energy efficiency; (b) put in place measures to adapt and improve Fiji's resilience to climate change; ... such incentives as may be necessary...

The Minister responsible for finance must... in regulations set out the nature of the incentives, the conditions for the grant or withdrawal of such incentives... including that such incentives are non-discretionary.”
section_header: Incentives for the promotion of climate change initiatives (Section 88)
extraction_rationale: Explicit subsidy/incentive instrument with regulatory design requirements.

policy_statement: Allow accredited entities to receive/administer climate finance with ministerial approval and require monitoring/evaluation/publication of results; allow guidelines for strategic use of climate finance.
source_quote:
“State entities or private organisations accredited to climate funds... can be recipients and administrators of public or private contributions... with the approval of the Minister.

Administrators... must monitor, evaluate, publish and communicate... the results of their actions to address climate change...”
extraction_rationale: Creates governance and accountability requirements for climate finance intermediaries.

policy_statement: Institute financial instruments and mechanisms to implement the Act and mitigation/adaptation actions.
source_quote: “The Minister responsible for finance, subject to and in accordance with all written laws, may institute financial instruments and mechanisms with the purpose of implementing this Act and climate change mitigation and adaptation actions pursuant to the objectives and principles of this Act.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit authorization for climate finance instruments; broad but clearly a financial policy tool.

policy_statement: Develop national climate finance strategies/frameworks/approaches (with the Reserve Bank) and review them every 5 years, addressing readiness, governance, accounting, and transparency.
source_quote:
“The Minister responsible for finance, in consultation with the Reserve Bank, must develop national climate finance strategies, frameworks and approaches to support and coordinate Fiji's ongoing access to climate finance.

The Minister, in consultation with the Reserve Bank, must review the national climate finance strategies and frameworks every 5 years.”
extraction_rationale: Mandatory strategy development and periodic review; clear means-of-implementation policy.

policy_statement: Develop and publish guidance materials within 12 months to help companies, investment schemes, FNPF, licensed financial institutions and the Reserve Bank meet climate-related obligations, referencing TCFD best practice.
source_quote:
“Within 12 months of the commencement of this section, the Minister must develop and publish guidance materials for the purpose of assisting directors... to fulfil their obligations under this Part.

In developing such guidance materials, the Minister must have regard to industry best practice including the recommendations of the Financial Stability Board's Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures.”
extraction_rationale: Time-bound requirement to publish guidance; supports implementation of mandatory climate risk governance/disclosure.

policy_statement: Require company directors to consider and evaluate foreseeable climate change risks and opportunities as part of their duty of care and diligence.
source_quote: “In exercising reasonable care and diligence under section 106(1) of the Companies Act 2015, directors or other officers of a company must consider and evaluate climate change risks and opportunities to the extent they are foreseeable and intersect with the interests of the company.”
section_header: Directors must consider and evaluate climate change risks and opportunities (Section 94)
extraction_rationale: Creates a binding corporate governance requirement explicitly tied to climate risk.

policy_statement: Require the Fiji National Provident Fund Board to consider and evaluate foreseeable climate change risks and opportunities.
source_quote: “In exercising its duties under section 9 of the Fiji National Provident Fund Act 2011, the Fiji National Provident Fund Board must consider and evaluate climate change risks and opportunities to the extent they are foreseeable and intersect with the interests of each fund and the Board.”
section_header: Fiji National Provident Fund Board must consider and evaluate climate change risks and opportunities (Section 95)
extraction_rationale: Binding climate risk governance requirement for a major institutional investor.

policy_statement: Mandate climate-related financial risk disclosures by companies and managed investment schemes, including risks, measures, integration into investment/risk policies, and alignment with Paris temperature goal.
source_quote:
“All companies and managed investment schemes... must disclose, in their financial statements and directors' report- (a) any material financial risks... arising from climate change risks and climate change opportunities; (b) measures adopted... to reduce its exposure...

(d) ... the extent to which the company or managed investment scheme complies with the long-term temperature goal in Article 2 of the Paris Agreement.”
section_header: Disclosure... by companies and managed investment schemes (Section 96)
extraction_rationale: Clear mandatory disclosure regime; directly climate-focused and enforceable.

policy_statement: Mandate climate-related financial risk disclosures by the Fiji National Provident Fund Board in its financial reports, including alignment with Paris temperature goal.
source_quote:
“The Fiji National Provident Fund Board... must disclose in their financial reports- (a) any material financial risks... arising from climate change risks and climate change opportunities; ...

(d) ... the extent to which each fund and the Board complies with the long-term temperature goal in Article 2 of the Paris Agreement.”
section_header: Disclosure... by the Fiji National Provident Fund Board (Section 97)
extraction_rationale: Mandatory disclosure requirement for a public pension/provident fund; directly climate-related.

policy_statement: Mandate climate-related financial risk disclosures by licensed financial institutions in Banking Act submissions, including measures and Paris temperature goal alignment.
source_quote:
“Every licensed financial institution... must disclose in their submission- (a) any material financial risks... arising from climate change risks and climate change opportunities; (b) measures adopted... to reduce its exposure...

(d) ... the extent to which the licensed financial institution complies with the long-term temperature goal in Article 2 of the Paris Agreement.”
extraction_rationale: Creates a binding climate disclosure obligation for regulated financial institutions.

policy_statement: Mandate climate-related financial risk disclosures by the Reserve Bank in annual accounts and operational reports, including Paris temperature goal alignment.
source_quote:
“The Reserve Bank must disclose in its annual accounts and reports of its operations... (a) any material financial risks... arising from climate change risks and climate change opportunities; ...

(d) ... the extent to which the Reserve Bank complies with the long-term temperature goal in Article 2 of the Paris Agreement.”
extraction_rationale: Binding disclosure requirement for the central bank; directly climate-related.

policy_statement: Make Helsinki carbon-neutral by 2035 by reducing greenhouse gas emissions 80% from 1990 levels and compensating the remaining 20% via emissions reductions outside the city.
source_quote: Helsinki is committed to doing its part in mitigating climate change. The objective of the Helsinki City Strategy 2017-2021 is to make Helsinki  carbon-neutral  by  2035.  This  goal will be achieved by reducing the greenhouse gas emissions in Helsinki by 80 per cent. The remaining  20  per  cent  will  be  compensated for by Helsinki taking care of implementing  emissions  reductions  outside  the  city.
extraction_rationale: Quantified citywide mitigation target with a deadline and a defined mechanism (80% reduction + 20% compensation).

policy_statement: Reduce Helsinki greenhouse gas emissions by 60% from 1990 to 2030 (intermediate target).
source_quote:
In addition to the objective of becoming carbon-neutral, the City  Strategy  2017-2021 also includes an intermediate goal: the greenhouse  gas  emissions  will  be  reduced by  60  per  cent  during  1990-2030. 

The objective for 2030 will be reached once the emissions are at 1.4 million tonnes.
section_header: Calculation of the required emissions reductions
extraction_rationale: Quantified interim mitigation target with timeframe.

policy_statement: Reduce traffic greenhouse gas emissions by 69% from 2005 levels by 2035.
source_quote: To  reach  the  goal  of  becoming carbon-neutral, the traffic emissions were set a separate goal: the objective is  to  reduce  greenhouse  gas  emissions  by 69 per cent from the level of 2005 by 2035 (this would mean a reduction of 60 per cent from the level of 2015: 363 kt CO2e).
extraction_rationale: Quantified sectoral mitigation target with baseline year and deadline.

policy_statement: Reduce emissions from energy use of buildings by 82% from 1990 to 2035.
source_quote: The emissions reduction goal for the energy use of buildings is 82 per cent during 19902035. The goal can be feasibly reached, but it  will  require  a  rapid  and  large-scale  start for  the  actions  (Table  2  and  Figure  8).
section_header: Emission reductions of construction and use of buildings
extraction_rationale: Quantified sectoral mitigation target with timeframe.

policy_statement: Implement key actions related to modes of transport to reduce emissions (action entity for sustainable transport modes).
source_quote:
## Key actions related to modes of transport (29 kt CO₂e).

(Includes the increase in the proportion of public transport (11 kt) and the increase in the proportion of cycling (18 kt) from Figure 11.)
extraction_rationale: Named action entity with quantified emissions impact and a list of specific sub-actions.

parent_statement: Key actions related to modes of transport (29 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Improve services at traffic nodes and smoothness of traffic connections, including implementing HSL Solmu action plan and park-and-ride action plan and improving wayfinding via signposts and mobile applications.
source_quote:
1. The services offered in traffic nodes and the smoothness of the traffic connections will be improved.
- The action plan devised in connection with HSL's Solmu project will be implemented.
- The regional action plan for park-and-ride services (HSL's publication 8/2017) in Helsinki will be implemented.
- The number of signposts and mobile applications will be increased to make the travel chain easy and quick to perceive in real time.
extraction_rationale: Specific operational commitments (implement named plans; increase wayfinding tools) under a defined action entity.

parent_statement: Key actions related to modes of transport (29 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Complete the target network for bicycle traffic in the inner city by 2025.
source_quote:
## 2. The target network for bicycle traffic in the inner city will be completed by 2025.

Parties responsible: Land Use and City Structure / Traffic and Street Planning.
extraction_rationale: Time-bound infrastructure completion commitment.

parent_statement: Key actions related to modes of transport (29 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Complete the Baana network for bicycle traffic by 2030.
source_quote:
## 3. The Baana network for bicycle traffic will be completed by 2030.

Parties responsible: Land Use and City Structure / Traffic and Street Planning.
extraction_rationale: Time-bound cycling infrastructure completion commitment.

parent_statement: Key actions related to modes of transport (29 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Expand the cycling lane network with high-level winter maintenance.
source_quote:
## 4. The cycling lane network with high-level winter maintenance will be expanded.

Parties responsible: Land Use and City Structure / Traffic and Street Planning, Buildings and Public Areas / Maintenance.
extraction_rationale: Specific service/infrastructure expansion commitment.

parent_statement: Key actions related to modes of transport (29 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Promote a pleasant and safe pedestrian environment, including implementing the traffic safety development programme.
source_quote:
5. A pleasant and safe environment for pedestrians will be promoted, for example by implementing the development programme for traffic safety.

Parties responsible: Land Use and City Structure / Detailed Planning, Land Use and City Structure / Traffic and Street Planning.
extraction_rationale: Concrete implementation commitment (implement a development programme) tied to walking.

parent_statement: Key actions related to modes of transport (29 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Develop bicycling services (city bikes, hubs, parking) and related communications; develop and increase capacity to carry bicycles on heavy train traffic.
source_quote: 6. Services for bicycling (city bikes, bike hubs, bike parking, etc.) and the related communications will be developed. The ability to carry bicycles in heavy train traffic will be developed and the capacity for this will be increased.
extraction_rationale: Specific service development commitments supporting modal shift.

parent_statement: Key actions related to modes of transport (29 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Implement the development programme for tram traffic in Helsinki to achieve objectives for speed, flow, reliability and disturbance level.
source_quote: 7. The development programme for tram traffic in Helsinki will be implemented. The objectives for the speed, flow, reliability and disturbance level of tram traffic will be achieved.
extraction_rationale: Implementation of a named programme with defined performance objectives.

parent_statement: Key actions related to modes of transport (29 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Improve public transport service level and rail network coverage by ensuring passenger demand through integrated land use and traffic investment planning and strengthening the trunk network.
source_quote:
## 8. The service level of public transport and the coverage of the rail network will be improved.

- By ensuring sufficient passenger demand through simultaneous planning of land use and traffic investments (such as complementary construction).
- By strengthening the efficient trunk network of public transport.
extraction_rationale: Specific improvement commitments for public transport service and network coverage.

parent_statement: Key actions related to modes of transport (29 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Implement the promotion programme for cycling and the development programme for bicycle parking.
source_quote:
9. The promotion programme for cycling and the development programme for bicycle parking will be implemented.

Parties responsible: Land Use and City Structure / Traffic and Street Planning, HSL, HKL.
extraction_rationale: Implementation commitment for named programmes.

policy_statement: Implement key actions related to the pricing of transport, including vehicle traffic pricing and parking fee measures, to reduce emissions.
source_quote:
Key actions related to the pricing of transport (35 kt CO₂e).

(Includes the pricing of vehicle traffic (26 kt) and the increase of parking fees (9 kt) from Figure 11.)
extraction_rationale: Named action entity with quantified emissions impact and multiple sub-actions; includes explicit pricing instruments.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the pricing of transport (35 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Prepare for a trial of a vehicle traffic pricing system (road toll/congestion tax) through additional surveys with the State and regional municipalities, including examining revenue allocation to transport system development.
source_quote:
## 10. A pricing system for vehicle traffic (a road toll or congestion tax):

- Necessary additional surveys conducted primarily together with the State and the municipalities in the region, helping the City prepare for the start of the trial. We will examine the allocation of road tolls for the development of the region's transport system as a part of the shared investment package of the State and the municipalities, which covers multiple terms of government. The requirement for the pricing is that the income from road tolls be allocated for the development of the region's transport system.
extraction_rationale: Concrete commitment to conduct surveys and prepare for a trial of a pricing instrument; explicitly climate-motivated in this section.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the pricing of transport (35 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Continue the current parking policy until 2021 and then raise parking fees further to reduce CO2 emissions, after studying business impacts.
source_quote: 11. The current parking policy will continue until 2021 and, afterwards, the parking fees will be raised further to reduce CO2 emissions. The impact on business will be studied before making the decision.
extraction_rationale: Explicit pricing measure with climate purpose and timing.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the pricing of transport (35 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Scale parking fees more heavily based on emissions and promotion of joint vehicle use.
source_quote:
12. Parking fees will be scaled more heavily from the perspective of emissions and the promotion of the joint use of vehicles.

Parties responsible: Land Use and City Structure / Traffic and Street Planning, Services and Permits / Environmental Services, Executive Office.
extraction_rationale: Explicit fee design change tied to emissions and shared mobility.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the pricing of transport (35 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Expand parking fee zones.
source_quote:
## 13. The parking fee zones will be expanded.

Parties responsible:

Land Use and City Structure /

Traffic and Street Planning.
extraction_rationale: Concrete pricing policy expansion; climate linkage established by being within pricing-for-emissions action entity.

policy_statement: Implement key actions related to a growing city structure to promote sustainable travel and reduce emissions.
source_quote:
Key actions related to the growing city structure (7 kt CO 2 e).

(Includes the more dense land use in 14 municipalities, also in Helsinki (7 kt), from Figure 11).
extraction_rationale: Named action entity with quantified emissions impact and multiple sub-actions.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the growing city structure (7 kt CO2e).
policy_statement: Promote public transport and other sustainable travel by complementing the community structure of the city.
source_quote:
14. The use of public transport and other sustainable means of travel will be promoted by complementing the community structure of the City.

Parties responsible: Land Use and City Structure / Traffic and Street Planning, Land Use and City Struc- ture / Detailed Planning.
extraction_rationale: Specific land-use planning intervention to shift travel modes.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the growing city structure (7 kt CO2e).
policy_statement: Update parking norms to better support sustainable transport in new areas and complementary construction.
source_quote:
15. The parking norms will be updated to better support sustainable transport both in the design of new areas and in the complementary construction of existing areas.

Parties responsible: Land Use and City Structure / Detailed Planning.
extraction_rationale: Regulatory/planning norm update affecting transport demand.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the growing city structure (7 kt CO2e).
policy_statement: Encourage creation of blocks and areas focused on bicycle and pedestrian traffic through land use planning.
source_quote:
16. The creation of blocks and areas that focus on bicycle and pedestrian traffic will be encouraged through land use planning.

Parties responsible: Land Use and City Structure / Detailed Planning, Land Use and City Structure / Traffic and Street Planning.
extraction_rationale: Specific planning commitment to prioritize active transport.

policy_statement: Implement key actions related to changes in vehicle technology, including environmental zones, charging infrastructure, procurement criteria, and low-emission public transport fuels.
source_quote:
Key actions related to the changes in vehicle technology (126 kt CO₂e).

(Includes the proportion of electric cars in Helsinki, 30% (86 kt), and the technology for heavy traffic (40 kt) from Figure 11)
extraction_rationale: Named action entity with quantified emissions impact and multiple sub-actions.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the changes in vehicle technology (126 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Develop and expand the environmental zone to include CO2 emissions criteria and prepare a CO2-based environmental zone for introduction.
source_quote:
## 17. The environmental zone will be developed:

- Assessments will be carried out for expanding the current environmental zone, including CO2 emissions in the criteria and applying the requirements to different types of vehicles (council term 20172021).
- A CO2 emissions based environmental zone will be ready for introduction based on the assessment. (council term 2021-2025).
extraction_rationale: Regulatory commitment with timeline and explicit CO2 criteria.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the changes in vehicle technology (126 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Enable market-based construction of public charging infrastructure for electric cars per electric traffic working group recommendations.
source_quote: 18. Market-based construction of public charging infrastructure for electric cars will be made possible. Implemented as per the recommendations of the electric traffic working group.
extraction_rationale: Specific enabling action for EV infrastructure deployment.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the changes in vehicle technology (126 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Tighten environmental criteria in competitive bidding for delivery, heavy delivery, utility vehicles and machinery services; monitor compliance; research an environmental bonus system.
source_quote: 19. The City of Helsinki will develop and tighten the environmental criteria (incl. alternative fuel sources, emission classes) in all competitive bidding processes for delivery services, heavy delivery services and utility vehicle and machinery services, as well as in competitive bidding processes for contract work including any of the above-mentioned services. Once the procurement process is completed, the client will monitor the environmental criteria. An environmental bonus system will be introduced into the competitive bidding processes for delivery and utility vehicle and machinery services as well as into competitive bidding processes for contract work including the above-mentioned services will be researched (cf. HSL).
extraction_rationale: Procurement policy change with monitoring and incentive design; concrete mechanism.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the changes in vehicle technology (126 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Apply environmental criteria to procurement of City-owned and leased vehicles; ensure Stara and HKL fleets use only biofuels or renewable electricity by 2020.
source_quote: 20. The environmental criteria will be applied to procurement of the City's own vehicles and leasing vehicles. The fleets of Stara and HKL will only use vehicles that run on biofuels or renewable electricity by 2020.
extraction_rationale: Binding operational/procurement commitment with deadline.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the changes in vehicle technology (126 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Develop city logistics and incentives for low-emissions delivery traffic, including researching a parking ID system with environmental price categories and expanding loading/unloading points.
source_quote:
21. The City of Helsinki will have an active role in developing city logistics and incentives to encourage low-emissions delivery traffic

- The introduction of a parking ID system for delivery traffic, implementing environmental criteria-based price categories for the parking ID system and expanding the network of loading and unloading points for delivery traffic will be researched.
extraction_rationale: Specific logistics policy and pricing-related research commitment to reduce delivery emissions.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the changes in vehicle technology (126 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: HSL targets: operate 10% of ordered bus traffic with electric buses by 2022 and 30% by 2025; run 90% of ordered traffic on biofuels by 2020.
source_quote: 22. HSL will continue to pursue its objectives; for example, 10 % of the bus traffic ordered by HSL will be operated using electric buses by 2022, with an increase to 30 % by 2025; and 90 % of the traffic ordered by HSL will be run on biofuels (renewable next-generation biodiesel and biogas) by 2020.
extraction_rationale: Quantified targets with deadlines for low-emission public transport operations.

parent_statement: Key actions related to the changes in vehicle technology (126 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Expand charging infrastructure for buses as part of the bus traffic competitive bidding programme.
source_quote:
23. The charging infrastructure for buses will be expanded as part of the bus traffic competitive bidding programme.

Parties responsible: HSL, HKL, Helen and Helen Electricity Networks.
extraction_rationale: Concrete infrastructure expansion commitment supporting electrification.

policy_statement: Implement key actions to reduce emissions from Port operations, including creating a Carbon-neutral Port by 2035 Action Plan and improving West Harbour traffic flow.
source_quote:
Key actions related to reducing the emissions from the Port operations (27 kt CO₂e).

(Includes the emissions from the harbours (27 kt) from Figure 11)
section_header: 4.1.5 Reducing the emissions from the harbours
extraction_rationale: Named action entity with quantified emissions impact and multiple sub-actions.

parent_statement: Key actions related to reducing the emissions from the Port operations (27 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Create the Carbon-neutral Port by 2035 Action Plan, including energy reviews every four years, advancing shore power, applying environmental criteria to machinery/vehicles, enabling low-emission fuel bunkering, and considering discounted port taxes and accommodating more energy-efficient ships.
source_quote:
24. The Port of Helsinki will create the Carbon-neutral Port by 2035 Action Plan which will include the following types of actions:

- Energy reviews performed every four years in accordance with the legislation on energy efficiency. In the reviews, the energy consumption profile of the company is examined in terms of electricity and heating, and new opportunities for saving energy are identified.
- Advancing the use of shore power with requirement outlines and increasing the number of shore power connections, if necessary.
- Using environmental criteria in the upgrading of the machinery and vehicle fleet of the Port. Enabling the bunkering of low-emission fuels (such as biogas and LNG) in various parts of the Port through surveys, negotiations with the authorities (Trafi) and instructions.
- Potential support for shipping companies taking environmental action, such as discounted port taxes. Enabling the visits and docking of more energyefficient and low-emission ships per freight unit in Vuosaari Harbour.
section_header: 4.1.5 Reducing the emissions from the harbours
extraction_rationale: Specific plan creation with enumerated interventions; includes pricing incentive (discounted port taxes).

parent_statement: Key actions related to reducing the emissions from the Port operations (27 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Make West Harbour traffic smoother between the harbour and Länsiväylä.
source_quote:
25. The traffic of the West Harbour will be made smoother between the Harbour and the Länsiväylä.

Parties responsible: Land Use and City Structure / Traffic and Street Planning, Executive Office / Area construction, Executive Office / Economic Development and The Port of Helsinki Ltd.
section_header: 4.1.5 Reducing the emissions from the harbours
extraction_rationale: Operational traffic-flow improvement action under port emissions reduction entity.

policy_statement: Implement key actions related to new mobility services and mobility steering, including pilots, open data, planning, communications, and mobility plans.
source_quote: Key actions related to new mobility services and the steering of mobility (11 kt CO₂e) (Includes ride-sharing services from Figure 11 (11 kt))
section_header: 4.1.6 New mobility services and steering of mobility
extraction_rationale: Named action entity with quantified emissions impact and multiple sub-actions.

parent_statement: Key actions related to new mobility services and the steering of mobility (11 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Act as a testing platform for smart mobility services and adopt more functional solutions.
source_quote:
26. The City will act as a testing platform for smart mobility services and adopt more functional solutions.

Parties responsible: Urban Environment Division + other divisions, Land Use and City Structure / Traffic and Street Planning, Executive Office / Economic Development, HSL, HKL, Forum Virium, Services and Permits / Environmental Services, S&C Foundation.
section_header: 4.1.6 New mobility services and steering of mobility
extraction_rationale: Concrete commitment to run pilots/testbeds and adopt solutions.

parent_statement: Key actions related to new mobility services and the steering of mobility (11 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Support introduction of mobility services by opening data, examining ride-sharing allocation to low-PT areas, identifying additional measures, and examining City-paid rides as part of ride-sharing services.
source_quote:
## 27. The City will support the introduction of different mobility services:

- Continuing to make data more open and developing the marketing of open data.
- Examining the allocation of ride-sharing services for areas with a low public transport service level.
- Examining the additional measures with which the City could help make new mobility services more common and prepare for their impact.
- Examining the development of rides paid for by the City as a part of ride-sharing services.
section_header: 4.1.6 New mobility services and steering of mobility
extraction_rationale: Specific enabling and planning actions; includes potential public spending on rides (edge case but explicit).

parent_statement: Key actions related to new mobility services and the steering of mobility (11 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Prepare the Smart Transport in Helsinki Action Plan (update to 2013 plan).
source_quote:
28. The Smart Transport in Helsinki Action Plan will be prepared (update to the Action Plan decided on in 2013).

Parties responsible: Land Use and City Structure / Traffic and Street Planning.
section_header: 4.1.6 New mobility services and steering of mobility
extraction_rationale: Plan preparation commitment (named action plan) with timeframe.

parent_statement: Key actions related to new mobility services and the steering of mobility (11 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Campaign and communicate to promote sustainable means of transport.
source_quote:
29. The City will campaign and communicate to promote sustainable means of transport.

Parties responsible: Urban Environment Division / communications, HSL.
section_header: 4.1.6 New mobility services and steering of mobility
extraction_rationale: Concrete communications action to influence transport behavior.

parent_statement: Key actions related to new mobility services and the steering of mobility (11 kt CO₂e).
policy_statement: Implement mobility plans and smart transport plans for City organisation and subsidiaries; survey company needs and opportunities to reduce and improve traffic efficiency with entrepreneurs.
source_quote: 30. Mobility plans and other smart transport plans will be implemented for the City organisation, subsidiary communities and companies. The City and HSL, together with entrepreneurs, will survey the needs of companies and the opportunities for reducing traffic and making it more efficient.
section_header: 4.1.6 New mobility services and steering of mobility
extraction_rationale: Implementation commitment for organisational mobility planning and business engagement.

policy_statement: Commit to planning and implementing new office buildings to near-zero-energy requirements stricter than national requirements, and apply near-zero-energy instructions to building modernisations where cost-efficient.
source_quote: Since  2018,  the  City  of  Helsinki  has  committed to  the  planning  and  implementation of new office buildings following its own near-zero-energy requirements that are stricter than the national requirements. Similarly,  the  City  is  committed  to  applying  the near-zero  energy  instructions  to  the  modernisation  of  buildings,  with  the  characteristics  and  cost  efficiency  of  each  buildings taken  into  consideration.
section_header: 4.2.1 Residential and service buildings and outdoor lighting owned by the City
extraction_rationale: Explicit commitment to higher-than-national building energy performance standards for City projects.

policy_statement: Upgrade street lighting to LED light sources and use smart lighting control.
source_quote:
54. The City will upgrade street lighting to use LED light sources, according to plan, and also use smart lighting control.

Parties responsible: Buildings and Public Areas / Maintenance, Built Assets Management.
section_header: Key actions related to outdoor lighting
extraction_rationale: Specific technology upgrade commitment for energy savings.

policy_statement: Use detailed planning to promote renewable energy production (property-specific, regional, centralised), account for wind power location principles, and pilot regional/plot-specific development projects with monitoring and scaling of best ideas.
source_quote: 55. Detailed planning will be used to promote the use of renewable energy and property-specific, regional and centralised production of renewable energy in a meaningful manner. Detailed planning will take the location principles for wind power into account. Detailed planning will be used to pilot regional or plot-specific development projects, the impacts of which will be assessed and monitored. The best ideas will be used in future locations.
section_header: Key actions related to detailed planning
extraction_rationale: Planning instrument commitment explicitly targeting renewable energy deployment and pilots.

policy_statement: Include stricter-than-national energy efficiency requirements in City plot conveyance conditions and continuously assess and develop requirements to promote energy conservation and renewable energy production.
source_quote: 59. The City's conditions for plot conveyance will include energy efficiency requirements that are stricter than the requirements at national level. The development needs and opportunities for the requirements will be actively assessed as the national requirements advance and as experience is gained from pilots and other projects. The requirements for energy efficiency will promote energy conservation and the production of renewable energy for buildings.
section_header: Key actions related to plot conveyance
extraction_rationale: Binding land/plot conveyance conditions (a steering mechanism) with explicit energy and renewables objectives.

policy_statement: Develop pre-emptive guidance for housing companies to promote energy-efficient renovations and renewable energy use, including adopting TOP11 geothermal implementation instructions and exploring fee exemptions for geothermal projects.
source_quote:
63. Pre-emptive guidance for housing companies (for example, in the project planning stage) will be developed to promote energy-efficient renovations and the use of renewable energy sources.

- The implementation instructions for the geothermal heating project, prepared jointly by the building control authorities of the TOP11 cities, will be taken into use (www.pksrava.fi, the instructions published in spring 2018). Additionally, the opportunity to exempt geothermal heating projects from building control licence fees will be explored.
section_header: Key actions related to building control
extraction_rationale: Concrete guidance and administrative fee policy exploration to accelerate low-carbon heating and renovations.

policy_statement: Prepare an energy renaissance programme to support energy-efficient renovation of neighbourhoods and existing private building stock (planning 2017-2021; implementation 2022-2035).
source_quote:
67. An energy renaissance programme will be prepared to support the renovation of neighbourhoods and the existing private building stock energyefficiently.

Parties responsible: Services and Permits / Environmental Services, Land Use and City Structure, Services and Permits / Building Control, Executive Office / neighbourhood construction, in collaboration with Helen.

Time span: Council terms of 2017-2021 (planning), 2022-2035 (implementation).
section_header: Key actions related to the energy renaissance
extraction_rationale: Named programme with defined planning and implementation periods; targets building energy efficiency improvements.

policy_statement: Investigate ending oil heating by 2035 and increasing renewable energy use and energy efficiency in electrically heated buildings, including selecting a pilot area.
source_quote:
68. The City will investigate ending oil heating by 2035 and increasing the use of renewable energy and the energy efficiency in electrically heated buildings.

- A pilot area will be selected. There, best options will be examined together with the residents.
section_header: Key actions related to the energy renaissance
extraction_rationale: Time-bound phase-out investigation with pilot; explicit oil heating end-date.

policy_statement: Acquire renewable district heating within the City organisation and create a plan for reaching 100% renewable district heating.
source_quote: 72. The opportunities to acquire renewable district heating will be identified in the City organisation, as will the cost effects thereof. The acquisition will be scheduled.
