policy_statement: Strive to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050.
source_quote: To stabilise the global temperature in the next 20 to 30 years, concerted and timely actions are needed worldwide to reduce carbon emissions. To this end, the Chief Executive announced in her 2020 Policy Address that Hong Kong would strive to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit government-wide climate target with a deadline (before 2050), qualifying as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Reduce Hong Kong's total carbon emissions by half from the 2005 level before 2035 (from about 40 million tonnes in 2005 to nearly 20 million tonnes in 2035).
source_quote: Adopting the prevailing technologies that are relatively mature and cost-effective, we aim to reduce the total carbon emissions by half before 2035 from the 2005 level, i.e. from about 40 million tonnes in 2005 to nearly 20 million tonnes in 2035.
extraction_rationale: Quantified emissions-reduction target with a clear baseline and deadline; a core mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Achieve net-zero carbon emissions in electricity generation before 2050 by progressively increasing the use of zero-carbon energy for electricity generation.
source_quote: At present, fossil fuels, including natural gas and coal, account for over 70% of Hong Kong's fuel mix for electricity generation. Under the overall strategy of achieving carbon neutrality, we must progressively increase the use of zero-carbon energy for electricity generation before 2050.
extraction_rationale: Long-term sectoral net-zero target with a stated mechanism (increase zero-carbon energy).

policy_statement: Increase the share of renewable energy (RE) in the fuel mix for electricity generation to 15% before 2050.
source_quote: Our goal is to increase the share of RE in the fuel mix for electricity generation from the existing less than 1% to 15% before 2050. Specifically, the Government can strive to develop more advanced waste-to-energy facilities to turn waste into electricity.
extraction_rationale: Quantified renewable energy target with a deadline; includes specific intervention (waste-to-energy).

policy_statement: Cease using coal for daily electricity generation by 2035, retaining coal only for backup support, replacing it with natural gas and zero-carbon energy (e.g., RE and nuclear).
source_quote: By 2035, we will cease using coal for daily electricity generation and will only keep it for providing backup support. Coal will be replaced by natural gas with lower carbon emissions and zero-carbon energy (e.g. RE and nuclear energy) by then.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: Clear phase-out commitment with a deadline and replacement pathway; a concrete mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Increase the share of renewable energy in the fuel mix for electricity generation to 7.5%–10% by 2035.
source_quote: To expedite transformation to low-carbon energy, we are committed to increasing the share of RE in the fuel mix for electricity generation from less than 1% at present to 7.5% to 10% by 2035.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: Quantified interim renewable energy target with a deadline; directly supports decarbonisation.

policy_statement: Incorporate renewable energy technologies in all capital works projects and raise requirements for applying RE technologies in new government buildings, increasing available roof space for RE installations from 10% to 25%.
source_quote: The Government will continue to take the lead in developing RE and strive to incorporate RE technologies in all capital works projects. We will update the Government circular on Green Government Buildings and raise the requirements of applying RE technologies in new government buildings. For instance, the proportion of available roof space for installing RE systems will be increased from the current 10% to 25%.
extraction_rationale: Specific operational/planning commitments with a quantified design requirement (roof space share).

policy_statement: Install larger floating solar systems (5–10 MW each) at multiple reservoirs and study a >100 MW floating solar system at Plover Cove Reservoir.
source_quote: Building on the success of the pilot projects of floating solar energy generation systems at Shek Pik Reservoir and Plover Cove Reservoir, the Water Supplies Department (WSD) plans to install larger floating solar energy generation systems with a generating capacity of 5-10 megawatts (MW) each at various reservoirs, including Plover Cove Reservoir, Shek Pik Reservoir and Tai Lam Chung Reservoir. In addition, WSD has embarked on a study on installing a floating solar energy generation system with a generating capacity of over 100 MW at Plover Cove Reservoir.
extraction_rationale: Concrete infrastructure deployment plan with specified capacities and locations; qualifies as a policy action.

policy_statement: Explore and facilitate private-sector installation of renewable energy systems on land and properties (e.g., solar in open car parks), coupled with the FiT Scheme.
source_quote: To assist the private sector in developing and applying RE, the Government will explore ways to facilitate the installation of RE systems by the private sector on their land and properties, such as measures to facilitate installation of solar energy generation systems by the private sector in open car parks. Coupled with the FiT Scheme, this can help foster the development of RE.
extraction_rationale: Specific enabling-policy commitment (facilitation measures) tied to a named instrument (FiT). Some details are to be explored, but the intervention is explicit.

policy_statement: Enhance regional cooperation to identify and develop zero-carbon energy sources in neighbouring regions, including joint investment and development to participate in and operate zero-carbon energy projects near Hong Kong.
source_quote: The Government, together with the power companies, will also explore ways to enhance regional cooperation on zero-carbon energy and identify sources of zero-carbon energy in neighbouring regions, including seeking joint investment and development opportunities for participating in and operating zero-carbon energy projects near Hong Kong.
extraction_rationale: Explicit commitment to pursue regional cooperation and joint investment for zero-carbon energy supply; a defined intervention though project specifics are not yet named.

policy_statement: Reduce electricity consumption of new and existing commercial buildings by 30%–40% and residential buildings by 20%–30% by 2050 (vs 2015 operational conditions).
source_quote: In this connection, we will strive to gradually reduce the electricity consumption of new and existing commercial buildings by 30% to 40%, and that of residential buildings by 20% to 30% by 2050, using the operational conditions of 2015 as the comparison basis.
extraction_rationale: Quantified long-term energy demand reduction targets for buildings with baseline year; a core resource-efficiency policy.

policy_statement: Reduce electricity consumption of new and existing commercial buildings by 15%–20% and residential buildings by 10%–15% by 2035 (vs 2015 operational conditions).
source_quote: To promote continuous decarbonisation in buildings, we have also set a medium-term target of reducing the electricity consumption of new and existing commercial buildings by 15% to 20%, and that of residential buildings by 10% to 15% by 2035, using the operational conditions of 2015 as the comparison basis.
extraction_rationale: Quantified medium-term building electricity reduction targets; directly supports decarbonisation.

policy_statement: Design new government buildings to achieve energy efficiency performance 10% better than statutory level.
source_quote: More green innovations and energy efficient elements will also be added to the design of new government buildings to achieve an energy efficiency performance of 10% better than statutory level, with a view to leading the trades to further optimise the energy efficiency performance of new buildings.
extraction_rationale: Specific government-building design requirement with a quantified performance margin; a concrete efficiency policy.

policy_statement: Tighten statutory OTTV standards by 2025 and complete RTTV reviews by 2023 and 2030; require OTTV of new government buildings to be at least 10% above statutory standards.
source_quote: The Government is conducting a review on the OTTV, and plans to complete the review for tightening up the statutory standards by 2025. The Government also plans to complete two reviews on the Residential Thermal Transfer Value (RTTV) by 2023 and 2030. To lead by example, the OTTV of new government buildings will be at least 10% above the statutory standards.
extraction_rationale: Time-bound regulatory review and tightening commitment with quantified government-leading requirement; qualifies as policy action.

policy_statement: Study feasibility of incorporating district cooling systems (DCS) in more new development areas (e.g., Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen NDA and artificial islands in Central Waters) to promote energy efficiency and mitigate the heat island effect.
source_quote: We will work on the infrastructure by integrating energy efficient facilities in development projects. We will study the feasibility of incorporating DCS in more new development areas, such as Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen New Development Area and the artificial islands in the Central Waters, so as to promote energy efficiency and mitigate the heat island effect in the areas.
extraction_rationale: Commitment to feasibility studies for specific infrastructure with stated objectives; somewhat exploratory but anchored to a named intervention (DCS).

policy_statement: Explore expanding the scope of building energy-efficiency regulation to cover all buildings with high energy consumption (e.g., data centres).
source_quote: We will actively explore the possibility of expanding the scope of regulation to cover all buildings with high energy consumption, such as data centres, so as to further enhance the overall energy efficiency performance of buildings in Hong Kong.
extraction_rationale: Regulatory expansion commitment (though details TBD) aimed at improving energy efficiency; qualifies as policy direction with a specific regulatory mechanism.

policy_statement: Consider conducting energy audits more frequently and mandating implementation of identified energy management opportunities; consider requiring large commercial buildings to carry out regular commissioning of air-conditioning and major building services installations.
source_quote: We will consider conducting energy audits more frequently and mandating the implementation of identified energy management opportunities. We will consider requiring large commercial buildings to carry out regular commissioning of air-conditioning systems and major building services installations to achieve optimal operational efficiency.
extraction_rationale: Proposed mandates and requirements are explicit regulatory mechanisms, even if framed as 'consider'; sufficiently specific to qualify as policy intent.

policy_statement: Release energy data and introduce energy benchmarking tools to facilitate comparison of building energy performance; support smart meters and demand-side management measures such as considering time-of-use tariffs.
source_quote: We plan to, through releasing energy data and introducing energy benchmarking tools, facilitate the comparison of building energy consumption performance and establish a two-way partnership in carbon reduction. Smart meters also provide the smart infrastructure required for introducing demand-side management measures, such as consideration of setting time-of-use tariffs as in some other economies to encourage users to change their habits and reduce electricity consumption during peak demand hours.
extraction_rationale: Concrete transparency/benchmarking action plus demand-side management pathway; time-of-use tariffs are a pricing instrument but only 'considered' here.

policy_statement: Keep MEELS under review, upgrade grading standards, consider minimum energy efficiency requirements for appliances before supply, and consider expanding MEELS to non-domestic/commercial appliances.
source_quote: We will keep the scheme under review. Apart from upgrading the grading standards, we will also consider setting a minimum energy efficiency requirement so that certain appliances must meet the minimum energy efficiency standards before they can be supplied in Hong Kong. Moreover, we will consider expanding the scope of the scheme to cover non-domestic or commercial appliances.
extraction_rationale: Regulatory strengthening and expansion of an existing mandatory labelling scheme; includes potential minimum standards (a binding mechanism).

policy_statement: Set a new Green Energy Target to improve the energy performance of the whole Government by 6% by 2024-25.
source_quote: We have also set a new Green Energy Target to further improve the energy performance of the whole Government by 6% by 2024-25.
extraction_rationale: Quantified government operational efficiency target with a deadline; clear policy commitment.

policy_statement: Achieve long-term target of zero carbon emissions from vehicles and the transport sector before 2050 through electrification, new energy transport, and traffic management measures.
source_quote: We expect to achieve the long-term target of zero carbon emissions from vehicles and the transport sector before 2050 through the electrification of vehicles and ferries, development of new energy transport and implementation of measures to improve traffic management.
extraction_rationale: Explicit sectoral net-zero target with stated mechanisms; core mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Cease new registration of fuel-propelled and hybrid private cars in 2035 or earlier.
source_quote: The measures outlined in the Hong Kong Roadmap on Popularisation of Electric Vehicles announced by the Government in 2021 cover various aspects, including ceasing the new registration of fuel-propelled and hybrid private cars in 2035 or earlier, as well as setting strategies and targets for providing charging facilities.
extraction_rationale: Clear regulatory/market access commitment with a deadline; directly reduces transport emissions.

policy_statement: Actively test viability of electric and new energy public transport and commercial vehicles to set a more concrete way forward and timetable around 2025; review charging-facility targets around 2025.
source_quote: The Government will play an active role in developing new energy transport, and will partner with different sectors in the coming years to actively test the technological and commercial viability of various electric and new energy public transport and commercial vehicles, with a view to setting a more concrete way forward and timetable in around 2025. In around 2025, we will review this year's target for the installation of charging facilities to keep up with the latest developments in EV.
extraction_rationale: Time-anchored commitment to trials and a review milestone; specific intervention though outcomes depend on results.

policy_statement: Collaborate with franchised bus companies and stakeholders in the next three years to test hydrogen fuel cell electric buses and heavy vehicles.
source_quote: Following the release of the Plan, the Government has set up an Interdepartmental Working Group on the application of hydrogen energy in Hong Kong. We plan to collaborate with the franchised bus companies and other stakeholders in the next three years to test out hydrogen fuel cell electric buses and heavy vehicles.
extraction_rationale: Specific trial programme with a defined timeframe and technology focus; mitigation-oriented.

policy_statement: Subsidise ferry operators to conduct trials for electric and hybrid ferries and explore progressively replacing traditional ferries with new energy ferries before 2035 (subject to trial results).
source_quote: As regards ferries, the Government will subsidise ferry operators to conduct trials for electric and hybrid ferries. Subject to the trial results and relevant technological developments, the Government will explore with the ferry operators the possibility of progressively replacing traditional ferries with new energy ferries before 2035.
extraction_rationale: Contains a subsidy (financial instrument) and a time-bound transition exploration (before 2035); sufficiently specific.

policy_statement: Roll out Free-flow Tolling System at government tolled tunnels and the Tsing Sha Control Area and press ahead with congestion charging; draw up preliminary proposals for congestion charging in 2022.
source_quote: For instance, the Free-flow Tolling System will be rolled out at government tolled tunnels and the Tsing Sha Control Area, while 'congestion charging' will be pressed ahead actively, with a view to charging different toll levels according to the traffic condition of the tunnels and the Control Area during different time periods. We commenced a traffic survey in September 2021 to collect the latest data and draw up preliminary proposals for 'congestion charging' in 2022.
extraction_rationale: Concrete transport-demand management measures with an implementation step and a dated proposal milestone; congestion charging is a pricing instrument.

policy_statement: Move away from reliance on landfills for municipal waste disposal by 2035 by developing adequate waste-to-energy facilities and advancing waste reduction, separation and recycling.
source_quote: The Government promulgated the Waste Blueprint for Hong Kong 2035 (the Waste Blueprint) early this year, advocating the vision of 'Waste Reduction · Resources Circulation · Zero Landfill'. The Waste Blueprint sets out targets for per capita MSW disposal and recovery rate, and the goal of developing adequate waste-to-energy facilities, with the aim to move away from the reliance on landfills for municipal waste disposal by 2035 as planned.
extraction_rationale: Clear goal with a deadline and named mechanisms (waste-to-energy, waste reduction/recycling); directly linked to emissions from landfills.

policy_statement: Achieve carbon neutrality in waste management before 2050 by eliminating municipal waste disposal at landfills (via moving away from landfills by 2035 and subsequent decomposition by 2050).
source_quote: If we can develop adequate waste-to-energy facilities so as to move away from over-reliance on landfills for municipal waste disposal by 2035 as planned, there will be no more municipal waste disposal at landfills. By 2050, most of the landfilled waste will have been decomposed, which will significantly reduce GHG emissions, thus helping us achieve the target of carbon neutrality before 2050.
extraction_rationale: Explicit sectoral carbon-neutrality target with a pathway and timeline; mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Reduce per capita MSW disposal by 40%–45% and raise recovery rate to about 55%.
source_quote: Through implementing MSW charging and other waste reduction and recycling initiatives, and encouraging the whole community to work together, we aim to progressively reduce the per capita MSW disposal by 40% to 45% and raise the recovery rate to about 55%.
extraction_rationale: Quantified waste reduction and recycling targets; climate-relevant due to landfill methane and lifecycle emissions.

policy_statement: Expand and enhance central collection services for food waste, waste plastics and waste paper and enhance the community recycling network across all districts to improve recycling effectiveness.
source_quote: We will continue to expand and enhance the central collection services for food waste, waste plastics and waste paper. The community recycling network covering all districts in Hong Kong will be enhanced to cover more areas and target participants, thereby raising the effectiveness of recycling.
extraction_rationale: Specific service expansion commitments; concrete interventions supporting waste diversion and emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Enhance recovery of landfill gases from the three operating landfills to provide thermal energy and electricity for landfill operation and export to the gas company and power grids.
source_quote: In the meantime, we will enhance the recovery of landfill gases from the three landfills currently in operation for providing thermal energy and electricity to support landfill operation and export to the gas company and power grids to provide energy for the public.
extraction_rationale: Specific operational measure to capture and use landfill gas; direct mitigation action.

policy_statement: Adopt a multi-pronged approach to go 'plastic-free' by formulating policies and regulations, stepping up publicity, expanding waste plastics recycling facilities, and encouraging replacement of single-use plastics with reusable/alternative materials.
source_quote: We will map out a long-term solution and go 'plastic-free' by adopting a multi-pronged approach, which includes formulating suitable policies and regulations, stepping up publicity, and expanding waste plastics recycling supporting facilities for turning waste into resources, as well as encouraging the public to replace single-use plastics with reusable or alternative materials.
extraction_rationale: Policy package with explicit regulatory and infrastructure components; somewhat broad but anchored to concrete levers.

policy_statement: Allocate about HK$240 billion over the next 15 to 20 years to implement mitigation and adaptation measures to combat climate change.
source_quote: The Government plans to allocate about $240 billion in the next 15 to 20 years to implement mitigation and adaptation measures to combat climate change, including the four main actions mentioned in this Chapter, covering energy saving and green buildings, RE, green transport and waste management, etc.
extraction_rationale: Explicit budget allocation over a defined period for climate actions; qualifies as a financial policy commitment.

policy_statement: Use the Government Green Bond Programme (established 2018) to fund green public works projects; issue green bonds totalling about HK$175.5 billion within five years (2021-22 onward) and plan retail green bonds.
source_quote: We plan to issue green bonds further, totalling some HK$175.5 billion within the next five years from 2021-22, having regard to the market situation. In view of the growing interest of the general public in green and sustainable development, the Government is also planning to issue retail green bonds to provide opportunities for members of the public to take part in green finance, thereby raising public awareness of and interest in green and sustainable finance.
extraction_rationale: Concrete financing instrument with quantified issuance plan and timeframe; directly supports funding for green projects.

policy_statement: Establish the Steering Committee on Climate Change and Carbon Neutrality (mid-2021) to formulate overall strategy and oversee implementation and coordination using a whole-government approach.
source_quote: The Steering Committee on Climate Change and Carbon Neutrality under the chairmanship of the Chief Executive was established in mid-2021 to formulate the overall strategy at the highest level and oversee implementation and coordination. We will adopt a whole-government approach to formulate more holistic and proactive decarbonisation measures, and implement decarbonisation action plans in our pursuit of the carbon neutrality target.
extraction_rationale: Institutional governance mechanism established to steer and coordinate climate policy implementation; a concrete administrative policy.

policy_statement: Set up the Office of Climate Change and Carbon Neutrality to strengthen coordination and promote deep decarbonisation.
source_quote: To ensure effective implementation of the measures and follow-up actions, ENB will set up the Office of Climate Change and Carbon Neutrality to strengthen coordination and promote deep decarbonisation, etc.
extraction_rationale: Concrete institutional setup to implement climate actions; supports delivery of mitigation policies.

policy_statement: Review Hong Kong's Climate Action Plan about every five years to update strategies and targets for decarbonisation and other actions to combat climate change.
source_quote: We will, in line with the spirit of the Paris Agreement, review Hong Kong's Climate Action Plan about every five years to update the strategies and targets for decarbonisation and other actions to combat climate change.
extraction_rationale: Defined periodic review cycle for updating climate strategies; a governance/process policy with a clear cadence.

policy_statement: Explore establishing a dedicated advisory committee on climate change by integrating existing advisory platforms to encourage community participation in climate actions.
source_quote: We will explore ways to establish a dedicated advisory committee on climate change through the integration of the existing advisory platforms, with the aim to encourage different sectors in the community, including our young generation, to actively participate in climate actions.
extraction_rationale: Institutional participation mechanism; exploratory but specific (dedicated advisory committee) and tied to climate governance.

policy_statement: Broaden teachers' knowledge and strengthen school learning materials and experiences on climate change to enhance student awareness and promote low-carbon transformation.
source_quote: We will broaden school teachers' knowledge about climate change. Schools may strengthen the relevant learning materials in different subjects and provide diversified learning experiences, so as to enhance students' awareness of climate change and its impacts, encourage the students to practise what they have learned, and promote low-carbon transformation.
extraction_rationale: Concrete capacity-building commitments in education; not quantified but includes specific interventions (curriculum/material strengthening).

policy_statement: Update infrastructure design standards and manuals to incorporate climate change parameters and review/update them with reference to IPCC Sixth Assessment Report as necessary.
source_quote: The CCWGI updates the design standards for various types of infrastructure in a timely manner, taking into account the relevant climate change parameters. With the progressive release of the Sixth Assessment Report by the IPCC since August 2021, the CCWGI will take into account the relevant assessment reports to review and update the relevant design standards for infrastructure in a timely manner as and when necessary.
extraction_rationale: Explicit adaptation governance/engineering standard-setting commitment tied to climate science updates.

policy_statement: Implement suitable improvement works and formulate management measures for low-lying coastal or windy locations in priority order based on a consultancy study assessing storm surges and waves.
source_quote: CEDD commenced a consultancy study in 2019 to comprehensively review the low-lying coastal or windy locations in Hong Kong, and to carry out investigations of related storm surges and waves in order to assess the impacts of extreme weather and climate change at those locations. The Government plans to implement suitable improvement works and formulate management measures for some of the concerned low-lying coastal or windy locations in order of priority.
section_header: Combating Sea Level Rise and Marine Protection
extraction_rationale: Adaptation commitment to implement works/management measures informed by a study; specific to sea level rise and storm surge risk.

policy_statement: Commence a strategic shoreline management study to formulate long-term strategies and protection measures for coastal areas under climate change.
source_quote: CEDD also plans to commence a strategic study on shoreline management to analyse the impacts of climate change on the development of coastal areas, so as to formulate suitable long-term strategies and protection measures, and to strengthen the capabilities of the Government and relevant stakeholders in coping with climate change.
section_header: Combating Sea Level Rise and Marine Protection
extraction_rationale: Planned strategic study with explicit purpose of developing long-term protection measures; adaptation policy action.

policy_statement: Continue reviewing Drainage Master Plans and allocate resources for drainage improvement works to address increased rainfall intensity and flood risk under climate change.
source_quote: DSD will continue to review the Drainage Master Plan of various districts in Hong Kong to assess the flood risk, and allocate resources for implementing drainage improvement works.
section_header: Combating Extreme Rainstorms and Tropical Cyclones
extraction_rationale: Ongoing planning and resourcing commitment for flood-risk reduction; adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Complete drainage improvement works at Pokfulam Village by 2024 and carry out improvement works at remaining flooding blackspots once planning/design are completed.
source_quote: For the remaining four flooding blackspots, the drainage improvement works at Pokfulam Village in Southern District have commenced and are expected to complete in 2024. The remaining three flooding blackspots are located at Shek Wu Wai in San Tin, Yuen Long, Lam Tsuen Valley Basin in Tai Po and on Chatham Road South in Tsim Sha Tsui. Improvement works will be carried out as soon as the planning and design works are completed.
section_header: Combating Extreme Rainstorms and Tropical Cyclones
extraction_rationale: Specific infrastructure works with a completion date and commitment to proceed at other sites; adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Continue implementing the Landslip Prevention and Mitigation Programme and enhance slope drainage design standards to strengthen slope resilience against extreme rainstorms.
source_quote: CEDD will continue to implement the Landslip Prevention and Mitigation Programme to upgrade government man-made slopes and to mitigate natural terrain landslide risk. CEDD also endeavours to enhance the slope drainage design standard to improve the slope surface drainage system with the aim of strengthening the resilience of the slopes against extreme rainstorms.
section_header: New technologies to cope with extreme rainstorm events
extraction_rationale: Named programme with explicit continuation and design-standard enhancement for climate-driven landslide risk; adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Reduce average fresh water per capita consumption by 10% by 2030 (vs 2016) and contain fresh water demand at around 1 billion m³ per annum before 2040 through water conservation, water loss management, and expanded use of lower grade water for non-potable purposes.
source_quote: To achieve the goal of reducing the average fresh water per capita consumption by 10% in 2030, using 2016 as the base year, and containing the fresh water demand at the level of around 1 billion m³ per annum before 2040, WSD is taking forward three major water demand management initiatives, namely water conservation, water loss management and expansion of the use of lower grade water (viz. seawater and recycled water) for non-potable purposes.
section_header: Combating Extreme Droughts and Safeguarding Water Supply
extraction_rationale: Quantified water-demand targets with deadlines and named initiatives; adaptation to drought risk and resource efficiency.

policy_statement: Supply recycled water to the public in phases starting from 2024 via reclaimed water supply in Sheung Shui/Fanling and grey water recycling at Anderson Road Quarry Development; expand recycled water use where feasible.
source_quote: Construction of the relevant infrastructure for expanding the use of lower grade water for non-potable purposes, including the reclaimed water supply system in Sheung Shui and Fanling and the grey water recycling supply system at the Anderson Road Quarry Development site, is in progress for supplying recycled water to the public in phases starting from 2024. WSD will continue to expand the use of recycled water to other new development areas and areas where fresh water is supplied for flushing wherever it is technically feasible and cost-effective.
section_header: Combating Extreme Droughts and Safeguarding Water Supply
extraction_rationale: Concrete infrastructure rollout with a start date and expansion commitment; adaptation and water efficiency.

policy_statement: Commission the first stage of the Tseung Kwan O Desalination Plant in 2023 with daily capacity ~135,000 m³ (expandable to 270,000 m³) to enhance water supply resilience under extreme dry weather.
source_quote: To cope with the possible extreme dry weather, WSD is constructing the first stage of Tseung Kwan O Desalination Plant to exploit alternative water resources other than rainfall. The plant, targeted to be commissioned in 2023, will have a daily capacity of about 135 000 m³ that will meet around 5% of the overall fresh water demand in Hong Kong, with provision for future expansion to a daily capacity of up to 270 000 m³.
extraction_rationale: Specific adaptation infrastructure project with commissioning year and capacity figures.

policy_statement: Enhance building design and promote urban forestry to alleviate temperature rise; complete review of design standards for public infrastructure and government buildings under extreme temperatures largely by 2023.
source_quote: We will continue to enhance building design and promote urban forestry with a view to alleviating and coping with temperature rise. ArchSD is coordinating with relevant departments to follow up and review the design standards relating to public infrastructure and government buildings. The work is expected to be largely completed in 2023.
extraction_rationale: Adaptation measures addressing extreme heat with a time-bound standards review milestone; includes NBS element (urban forestry).

policy_statement: Launch a new gross floor area (GFA) concession mechanism for green and amenity features in new private development projects in 2022.
source_quote: BD is working closely with stakeholders to formulate the implementation details of the new GFA concession mechanism which is targeted to be launched in 2022.
extraction_rationale: Time-bound policy mechanism (development incentive) to promote green building features; climate link is indirect but relevant to heat/urban environment.

policy_statement: Continue to promote active planting, proper maintenance and preservation practices to achieve a sustainable and healthy urban forest, including improving tree growing environments via smart technologies and soil improvements.
source_quote: The Development Bureau is studying and exploring feasible measures to improve the growing environment of urban trees, which include the application of smart technologies in tree management, review of soil volume for new roadside trees and improvement of soil quality for existing planting areas. The Government will continue to promote active planting, proper maintenance and preservation practices with a view to achieving a sustainable and healthy urban forest.
extraction_rationale: Concrete nature-based adaptation actions (urban forestry) with specified measures; addresses heat island explicitly.

policy_statement: Continue strengthening preparation for and response to natural disasters and enhance post-disaster recovery; enhance information dissemination arrangements for public preparedness and recovery.
source_quote: The Government will continue to strengthen preparation for and response to natural disasters, and to enhance capabilities in post-disaster recovery. Relevant departments will enhance arrangements on the dissemination of information so that the public can make preparation for appropriate response to, and recovery from, natural disasters, with a view to mitigating the potential threats.
extraction_rationale: Explicit resilience commitment for emergency preparedness and recovery under more frequent extreme weather.

policy_statement: Conduct regular exercises to enhance preparedness and collaboration among units to cope with natural disasters.
source_quote: In order to safeguard the life and property of the public, relevant bureaux and departments will conduct regular exercises of various forms to enhance preparedness and collaboration among the units concerned to cope with natural disasters.
extraction_rationale: Operational preparedness commitment; concrete action (regular exercises) supporting climate resilience.

policy_statement: Maintain Indonesia's First NDC targets of 29% (unconditional) and up to 41% (conditional) GHG reduction below BAU by 2030.
source_quote: In the First NDC, Indonesia has unconditional target of 29% and conditional target up to 41% compared to business as usual in 2030.
extraction_rationale: Quantified national mitigation targets with a deadline (2030) constitute a formal climate policy commitment.

policy_statement: Peak national GHG emissions in 2030 with a net sink in the forest and land-use sector (FOLU).
source_quote: Through LTS-LCCR 2050, Indonesia will increase ambition on GHG reduction by achieving the peaking of national GHG emissions in 2030 with net- sink of forest and land-use sector, reaching 540 Mton CO2e by 2050, and with further exploring opportunity to rapidly progress towards net-zero emission in 2060 or sooner.
extraction_rationale: Contains a time-bound national emissions milestone (peaking in 2030) and specifies the mechanism (net sink in FOLU).

policy_statement: Reach national emissions of 540 MtCO2e by 2050 under the long-term strategy.
source_quote: Through LTS-LCCR 2050, Indonesia will increase ambition on GHG reduction by achieving the peaking of national GHG emissions in 2030 with net- sink of forest and land-use sector, reaching 540 Mton CO2e by 2050, and with further exploring opportunity to rapidly progress towards net-zero emission in 2060 or sooner.
extraction_rationale: Quantified long-term emissions level (540 MtCO2e) with a target year (2050).

policy_statement: Explore opportunities to rapidly progress toward net-zero emissions in 2060 or sooner.
source_quote: Through LTS-LCCR 2050, Indonesia will increase ambition on GHG reduction by achieving the peaking of national GHG emissions in 2030 with net- sink of forest and land-use sector, reaching 540 Mton CO2e by 2050, and with further exploring opportunity to rapidly progress towards net-zero emission in 2060 or sooner.
extraction_rationale: States a national net-zero timeframe; wording is exploratory but anchored to a specific year and framed as ambition under the strategy.

policy_statement: Maintain an increasing trend of net-sink in the forestry sector after 2030.
source_quote: In order to achieve this target, forestry sector will share considerable efforts to maintain increasing trend of net-sink after 2030, significant transition of energy sector by raising the proportion of renewable energy in energy mix, increasing energy eff.shorticiency, reducing substantial amount of coal consumption and implementing CCS/ CCUS and BECCS.
extraction_rationale: Sectoral mitigation commitment tied to the national target; although not quantified, it specifies a concrete outcome (net-sink trend) and timeframe (after 2030).

policy_statement: Raise the proportion of renewable energy in the national energy mix as part of the energy transition.
source_quote: In order to achieve this target, forestry sector will share considerable efforts to maintain increasing trend of net-sink after 2030, significant transition of energy sector by raising the proportion of renewable energy in energy mix, increasing energy eff.shorticiency, reducing substantial amount of coal consumption and implementing CCS/ CCUS and BECCS.
extraction_rationale: Named intervention (increase renewables share) as part of a national mitigation strategy; lacks a numeric target here but is a concrete policy direction.

policy_statement: Increase energy efficiency as part of the long-term energy transition.
source_quote: In order to achieve this target, forestry sector will share considerable efforts to maintain increasing trend of net-sink after 2030, significant transition of energy sector by raising the proportion of renewable energy in energy mix, increasing energy eff.shorticiency, reducing substantial amount of coal consumption and implementing CCS/ CCUS and BECCS.
extraction_rationale: Specific intervention (energy efficiency) stated as a required effort to achieve mitigation targets.

policy_statement: Reduce coal consumption substantially as part of the long-term energy transition.
source_quote: In order to achieve this target, forestry sector will share considerable efforts to maintain increasing trend of net-sink after 2030, significant transition of energy sector by raising the proportion of renewable energy in energy mix, increasing energy eff.shorticiency, reducing substantial amount of coal consumption and implementing CCS/ CCUS and BECCS.
extraction_rationale: Clear mitigation action (coal reduction) even though not quantified in this passage.

policy_statement: Implement CCS/CCUS and BECCS as part of the long-term mitigation strategy.
source_quote: In order to achieve this target, forestry sector will share considerable efforts to maintain increasing trend of net-sink after 2030, significant transition of energy sector by raising the proportion of renewable energy in energy mix, increasing energy eff.shorticiency, reducing substantial amount of coal consumption and implementing CCS/ CCUS and BECCS.
extraction_rationale: Named technologies (CCS/CCUS, BECCS) constitute specific mitigation interventions.

policy_statement: Reduce climate change impacts so that national GDP loss is limited by 3.45% in 2050 by increasing resilience in food, water, energy, and environmental health.
source_quote: The LTS-LCCR 2050 sets the goal of adaptation pathways to reduce the impact of climate change on national GDP loss by 3.45% in 2050, through increasing resilience in four basic necessities (food, water, energy, and environmental health), with three target areas of resilience (economy, social and livelihood, ecosystem and landscape).
extraction_rationale: Quantified adaptation outcome (GDP loss by 2050) and specified resilience domains; this is a clear adaptation target.

policy_statement: Under the LCCP pathway, reach 540 MtCO2e by 2050 (about 1.61 tCO2e per capita).
source_quote: Under LCCP, rapid decrease in emissions will occur after 2030, reaching 540 Mton CO2e by 2050 or equivalent to about 1.61 ton CO2e per capita.
extraction_rationale: Quantified emissions level and per-capita metric with a target year; constitutes a mitigation target.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, peak national GHG emissions in 2030 with net sink in forestry and land uses and explore net-zero by 2060 or sooner.
source_quote: Through low carbon scenario compatible with the Paris Agreement target (LCCP), Indonesia foresees to reach the peaking of national GHGs emissions in 2030 with net sink in forestry and land uses (FOLU), and with further exploring opportunity to rapidly progress towards net-zero emission in 2060 or sooner.
extraction_rationale: Time-bound national mitigation milestones; includes land-sector sink as explicit mechanism.

policy_statement: Implement policies and measures to make the AFOLU sector a net sink by 2030 with effective implementation and adequate international support.
source_quote: These PaMs provide a good foundation for implementing low carbon development compatible with the Paris Agreement target. Effective implementation of these PaMs and adequate international support (investment, technology, and capacity building) could bring AFOLU sector become net sink in 2030.
extraction_rationale: Defines a sectoral outcome (AFOLU net sink) with a year (2030), conditional on implementation/support; still a policy target.

policy_statement: Implement forest governance policies and measures supporting REDD+ and low-carbon development (including peat/forest licensing controls, certification, SEAs, environmental economic instruments, and an environmental fund agency).
source_quote: This successful endeavour has been supported by a number of PaMs including: (i) Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 on termination of new license issuance on peatland, (ii) implementation of mandatory certification for sustainable forest management, (iii) Government Regulation No. 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs) through landscape approach aiming at securing food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management, (iv) Government Regulation No. 46/2017 on Environmental Economic Instrument, and (v) Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018 on the establishment of Environmental Fund Management Agency (BPDLH).
extraction_rationale: Named umbrella set of enacted policies (laws/regulations) with explicit climate/forest governance relevance and listed sub-measures.

parent_statement: Implement forest governance policies and measures supporting REDD+ and low-carbon development (including peat/forest licensing controls, certification, SEAs, environmental economic instruments, and an environmental fund agency).
policy_statement: Terminate issuance of new licenses on peatland (Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019).
source_quote: This successful endeavour has been supported by a number of PaMs including: (i) Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 on termination of new license issuance on peatland, (ii) implementation of mandatory certification for sustainable forest management, (iii) Government Regulation No. 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs) through landscape approach aiming at securing food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management, (iv) Government Regulation No. 46/2017 on Environmental Economic Instrument, and (v) Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018 on the establishment of Environmental Fund Management Agency (BPDLH).
extraction_rationale: Binding mechanism via a named Presidential Instruction restricting peatland licensing; directly affects land-use emissions.

parent_statement: Implement forest governance policies and measures supporting REDD+ and low-carbon development (including peat/forest licensing controls, certification, SEAs, environmental economic instruments, and an environmental fund agency).
policy_statement: Implement mandatory certification for sustainable forest management.

extraction_rationale: Regulatory/standards-based intervention (mandatory certification) to improve forest management and reduce degradation emissions.

parent_statement: Implement forest governance policies and measures supporting REDD+ and low-carbon development (including peat/forest licensing controls, certification, SEAs, environmental economic instruments, and an environmental fund agency).
policy_statement: Apply Government Regulation No. 46/2016 on Strategic Environmental Assessments (SEAs) using a landscape approach to secure food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management.
source_quote: This successful endeavour has been supported by a number of PaMs including: (i) Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 on termination of new license issuance on peatland, (ii) implementation of mandatory certification for sustainable forest management, (iii) Government Regulation No. 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs) through landscape approach aiming at securing food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management, (iv) Government Regulation No. 46/2017 on Environmental Economic Instrument, and (v) Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018 on the establishment of Environmental Fund Management Agency (BPDLH).
extraction_rationale: Binding planning instrument (SEA regulation) guiding land-use decisions; explicitly tied to ecosystem management and security objectives.

parent_statement: Implement forest governance policies and measures supporting REDD+ and low-carbon development (including peat/forest licensing controls, certification, SEAs, environmental economic instruments, and an environmental fund agency).
policy_statement: Implement Government Regulation No. 46/2017 on Environmental Economic Instruments.
source_quote: This successful endeavour has been supported by a number of PaMs including: (i) Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 on termination of new license issuance on peatland, (ii) implementation of mandatory certification for sustainable forest management, (iii) Government Regulation No. 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs) through landscape approach aiming at securing food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management, (iv) Government Regulation No. 46/2017 on Environmental Economic Instrument, and (v) Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018 on the establishment of Environmental Fund Management Agency (BPDLH).
extraction_rationale: Establishes economic instruments for environmental management; qualifies as a broad financial/economic policy tool.

parent_statement: Implement forest governance policies and measures supporting REDD+ and low-carbon development (including peat/forest licensing controls, certification, SEAs, environmental economic instruments, and an environmental fund agency).
policy_statement: Establish the Environmental Fund Management Agency (BPDLH) (Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018).
source_quote: This successful endeavour has been supported by a number of PaMs including: (i) Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 on termination of new license issuance on peatland, (ii) implementation of mandatory certification for sustainable forest management, (iii) Government Regulation No. 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs) through landscape approach aiming at securing food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management, (iv) Government Regulation No. 46/2017 on Environmental Economic Instrument, and (v) Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018 on the establishment of Environmental Fund Management Agency (BPDLH).
extraction_rationale: Creates a dedicated environmental fund management institution; functions as a financing mechanism for environmental/climate actions.

policy_statement: Develop the long-term low-carbon energy strategy using four guiding pillars: energy efficiency; decarbonized electricity in transport/buildings; fuel shift from coal to gas/renewables in industry; and renewable energy enhancement in power, transport, and industry.
source_quote: Four following guiding pillars were used to develop long-term low carbon strategy in energy sector taking into account past development and future projection of energy demand and supply : (i) implementation of energy eff.shorticiency measures; (ii) use of decarbonized electricity in transport and buildings; (iii) fuel shift from coal to gas and renewables in industry; and (iv) enhancement of renewable energy in power, transport and industry.
extraction_rationale: Defines a structured policy framework (pillars) with specific interventions across sectors; sufficiently concrete to qualify as policy direction.

policy_statement: Reduce the impact of climate change on national GDP loss by 3.45% in 2050 by increasing resilience in food, water, energy, and environmental health.
source_quote: By extending adaptation strategy in Updated NDC, the adaptation pathways set the goal to reduce the impact of climate change on national GDP loss by 3.45% in 2050, through increasing resilience in four basic necessities (food, water, energy, and environmental health), with three target areas of resilience (economy, social and livelihood, ecosystem and landscape)
extraction_rationale: Restates a quantified adaptation goal and specifies resilience domains; clear policy target.

policy_statement: Include ocean in the NDC adaptation component and implement coastal protection programmes for coastal and fishery adaptation under RPJMN 2020-2024.
source_quote: This climate-related evidence suggested the important role of ocean in adaptation to climate change and Indonesia has included ocean in adaptation component of the NDC. The National Medium-Term Plan (RPJMN) 20202024 has put adaptation in coastal and fishery through coastal protection programmes, which is in-line with NDC.
section_header: 3.3. Role of Ocean and Integrated Terrestrial and Marine Ecosystem Management and Conservation
extraction_rationale: Explicit commitment to ocean-based adaptation and a named programme type (coastal protection) embedded in national planning.

policy_statement: Implement COVID-19 recovery ocean/coastal ecosystem actions including 15,000 hectares of mangrove planting and 50 hectares of coral reef restoration in Bali (2020).
source_quote: Coastal and marine based activities have also been part of COVID-19 recovery programme, including 15 thousands hectare mangrove planting and 50 hectare coral reef restoration in marine tourism area in Bali in 2020.
section_header: 3.3. Role of Ocean and Integrated Terrestrial and Marine Ecosystem Management and Conservation
extraction_rationale: Quantified ecosystem restoration actions with location and year; qualifies as a concrete nature-based intervention with climate relevance.

policy_statement: Continuously improve and transform PROKLIM into a national movement on joint adaptation and mitigation through Minister Regulation No. 84/2016.
source_quote: Climate Village Programme (PROKLIM) has been continuously improved, including by transforming the PROKLIM become national movement on joint adaptation and mitigation which aims at increasing understanding on climate change and its impacts and to encourage the implementation of adaptation and mitigation actions at the local level through Minister Regulation (Minister of Environment and Forestry) No. 84/2016.
section_header: 3.4. Framework on Climate Change Actions in Indonesia
extraction_rationale: Named program with an implementing regulation and explicit adaptation/mitigation objectives; qualifies as a policy/program commitment.

policy_statement: Reduce risks and vulnerability to climate change in all development sectors by 2030 through climate literacy, local capacity, knowledge management, policy convergence with disaster risk reduction, and adaptive technology.
source_quote: Therefore, the objectives of Indonesia's climate change adaptation strategy are directed at reducing risks, increasing adaptive capacity, strengthening resilience, and reducing vulnerability to climate change in all development sectors by 2030 through increasing climate literacy, strengthening local capacity, improving knowledge management, policies convergence on climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction, and the application of adaptive technology.
section_header: 3.4. Framework on Climate Change Actions in Indonesia
extraction_rationale: Time-bound (by 2030) adaptation objectives with specific mechanisms; although broad, it lists concrete intervention types.

policy_statement: Actions to turn Forestry and Other Land Uses into a net sink by 2050 (CPOS) and by 2030 (LCCP) through a defined set of measures.
source_quote: Efforts to significantly reduce the emission of this sector and turn it into net sink by 2050 under CPOS and by 2030 under LCCP depends primarily on the success of the following actions: (i) reducing emission from deforestation and peatland (peat decomposition and peat fire); (ii) increasing the capacity of natural forest in sequestering carbon (by reducing degradation and enhancing the regeneration); (iii) restoring peatland, (iv) implementing forest restoration (enrichment planting/sink enhancement), (v) adopting sustainable forest management practices; and (vi) maximizing the use of unproductive lands (idle lands) for the establishment of forest and agriculture plantations (see Figure 6).
extraction_rationale: Umbrella initiative with explicit net-sink outcomes and a numbered list of sub-actions; extract as parent plus sub-items.

parent_statement: Actions to turn Forestry and Other Land Uses into a net sink by 2050 (CPOS) and by 2030 (LCCP) through a defined set of measures.
policy_statement: Reduce emissions from deforestation and peatland (peat decomposition and peat fire).
source_quote: Efforts to significantly reduce the emission of this sector and turn it into net sink by 2050 under CPOS and by 2030 under LCCP depends primarily on the success of the following actions: (i) reducing emission from deforestation and peatland (peat decomposition and peat fire); (ii) increasing the capacity of natural forest in sequestering carbon (by reducing degradation and enhancing the regeneration); (iii) restoring peatland, (iv) implementing forest restoration (enrichment planting/sink enhancement), (v) adopting sustainable forest management practices; and (vi) maximizing the use of unproductive lands (idle lands) for the establishment of forest and agriculture plantations (see Figure 6).
extraction_rationale: Specific mitigation action targeting key land-sector emission sources.

source_quote: Efforts to significantly reduce the emission of this sector and turn it into net sink by 2050 under CPOS and by 2030 under LCCP depends primarily on the success of the following actions: (i) reducing emission from deforestation and peatland (peat decomposition and peat fire); (ii) increasing the capacity of natural forest in sequestering carbon (by reducing degradation and enhancing the regeneration); (iii) restoring peatland, (iv) implementing forest restoration (enrichment planting/sink enhancement), (v) adopting sustainable forest management practices; and (vi) maximizing the use of unproductive lands (idle lands) for the establishment of forest and agriculture plantations (see Figure 6).
extraction_rationale: Named restoration intervention to enhance sinks.

parent_statement: Actions to turn Forestry and Other Land Uses into a net sink by 2050 (CPOS) and by 2030 (LCCP) through a defined set of measures.
policy_statement: Adopt sustainable forest management practices.
source_quote: Efforts to significantly reduce the emission of this sector and turn it into net sink by 2050 under CPOS and by 2030 under LCCP depends primarily on the success of the following actions: (i) reducing emission from deforestation and peatland (peat decomposition and peat fire); (ii) increasing the capacity of natural forest in sequestering carbon (by reducing degradation and enhancing the regeneration); (iii) restoring peatland, (iv) implementing forest restoration (enrichment planting/sink enhancement), (v) adopting sustainable forest management practices; and (vi) maximizing the use of unproductive lands (idle lands) for the establishment of forest and agriculture plantations (see Figure 6).
extraction_rationale: Specific management practice adoption to reduce degradation and emissions.

parent_statement: Actions to turn Forestry and Other Land Uses into a net sink by 2050 (CPOS) and by 2030 (LCCP) through a defined set of measures.
policy_statement: Maximize use of unproductive (idle) lands for establishing forest and agriculture plantations.
source_quote: Efforts to significantly reduce the emission of this sector and turn it into net sink by 2050 under CPOS and by 2030 under LCCP depends primarily on the success of the following actions: (i) reducing emission from deforestation and peatland (peat decomposition and peat fire); (ii) increasing the capacity of natural forest in sequestering carbon (by reducing degradation and enhancing the regeneration); (iii) restoring peatland, (iv) implementing forest restoration (enrichment planting/sink enhancement), (v) adopting sustainable forest management practices; and (vi) maximizing the use of unproductive lands (idle lands) for the establishment of forest and agriculture plantations (see Figure 6).
extraction_rationale: Land-use planning intervention to reduce pressure on forests and enable plantations on degraded lands.

policy_statement: Ban conversion of forested productive production forest to APL except where non-forested production forest lands are unavailable (Government Regulation No. 104/2015).
source_quote: Government Regulation No.104/2015 on the changes of forest land use and function, which ban the conversion of forested land (productive production forest) in forest area for APL, except in the province where the non-forested lands in the production forest are not available;
extraction_rationale: Binding regulatory ban on forest conversion; directly mitigates deforestation emissions.

policy_statement: Expand protected forest area from 51.8 Mha to 65.3 Mha under RPJMN 2020-2024.
source_quote: In the National Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMN) 2020-2024, forest area that need to be protected based on the value of ecosystem services of the forest, are expanded from 51.8 Mha to 65.3 Mha, which are located inside and outside forest area.
extraction_rationale: Quantified land protection expansion target embedded in national development planning; supports conservation and emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Limit cumulative deforestation to 6.8 Mha under LCCP (vs 14.6 Mha under CPOS).
source_quote: The CPOS and LCCP indicate that expected cumulative area to be deforested in the future are about 14.6 Mha and 6.8 Mha respectively (see Figure 7).
extraction_rationale: Quantified deforestation constraint under a scenario; functions as a mitigation target for land-use change.

policy_statement: Provide Result-based Payment eligibility for local governments and concessions conserving forests beyond regulation under Ministerial Regulation No. 70/2017.
source_quote: Under the implementation of REDD+, the local governments and concessions who can conserved the forest beyond the existing regulation, are eligible for receiving Result-based Payment (RBP) under the Ministerial Regulation (Minister for Environment and Forestry) No. 70/2017.
extraction_rationale: Creates a performance-based finance mechanism (RBP) tied to forest conservation outcomes.

policy_statement: Require all forest concession companies to implement sustainable harvesting practices by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Under LCCP, by 2050 all forest concession companies have implement sustainable harvesting practices. At present, the forest concessions that have received the good forest certification reach about 76%.
section_header: b. Conservation and Sustainable Forest Management
extraction_rationale: Time-bound requirement for concession practices; concrete management commitment.

policy_statement: Restore production forests through enhanced natural regeneration (ENR) to reach 1.70 Mha after 2030 and 8.8 Mha by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: It is expected that under LCCP, area of production forest that being restored through the ENR programme after 2030 should reach about 1.70 Mha, about 2 times of the CPOS, and by 2050 it will reach 8.8 Mha or about 6 times of the CPOS.
section_header: b. Conservation and Sustainable Forest Management
extraction_rationale: Quantified restoration targets with timeframe; clear nature-based mitigation action.

policy_statement: Prohibit new permits for peatland use under Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019.
source_quote: Under Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019, there will not be any new permit for the use of peatland. In addition, the Ministerial Regulation No. 15/2017 (Minister for Environment and Forestry) mandates private sector and local governments to improve the use of peatland and water management.
section_header: c. Protection and Restoration of Peatland
extraction_rationale: Binding restriction on peatland permitting; directly targets peat emissions.

policy_statement: Mandate private sector and local governments to improve peatland use and water management (Ministerial Regulation No. 15/2017).
source_quote: Under Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019, there will not be any new permit for the use of peatland. In addition, the Ministerial Regulation No. 15/2017 (Minister for Environment and Forestry) mandates private sector and local governments to improve the use of peatland and water management.
section_header: c. Protection and Restoration of Peatland
extraction_rationale: Regulatory mandate specifying responsible actors and required management improvements.

policy_statement: Restore degraded peatland to 2.7 Mha by 2030 and 4.2 Mha by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: For peatland restoration, CPOS figures the area of degraded peatland being restored should reach 1.03 Mha by 2030 and 1.7 Mha by 2050. While under LCCP, the target will be increased to 2.7 Mha by 2030 and 4.2 Mha by 2050.
section_header: c. Protection and Restoration of Peatland
extraction_rationale: Quantified restoration targets with years; clear peatland restoration policy.

policy_statement: Accelerate afforestation/reforestation and rehabilitate unproductive lands: 5.3 Mha by 2030 and 10.6 Mha by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Under CPOS, Indonesia aims to rehabilitate the unproductive lands with priority in critical and very critical lands about 4.32 Mha by 2030 and 8.6 Mha by 2050. Under the LCCP, this target is increased to 5.3 Mha by 2030 and 10.6 Mha by 2050.
extraction_rationale: Quantified land rehabilitation targets with deadlines; constitutes a concrete sink-enhancement policy.

policy_statement: Scale adoption of low-emission rice varieties to 0.97 Mha by 2030 and 2.07 Mha by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Under CPOS, the adoption of low emission variety is expected to be 0.93 Mha by 2030 and 1.96 Mha by 2050. Under LCCP, an ambitious target is set to 0.97 Mha by 2030 and 2.07 Mha by 2050.
extraction_rationale: Quantified technology adoption targets in agriculture mitigation.

policy_statement: Scale SPR/STT water-saving paddy cultivation to 1.31 Mha by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: By 2050, the technology programme is expected to be scaled up to 1.18 M ha and 1.31 M ha under CPOS and LCCP, respectively.
extraction_rationale: Quantified scale-up target for a specific mitigation technology in rice cultivation.

policy_statement: Implement biogas from livestock waste for 41,000 head by 2030 and 94,000 head by 2050 (CPOS and LCCP).
source_quote: The CPOS and LCCP are setting a similar target for biogas implementation, accounted for 41,000 head in 2030 and 94,000 head in 2050.
extraction_rationale: Quantified deployment targets for livestock biogas; concrete mitigation action.

policy_statement: Increase livestock feed supplement adoption to 6.58 million head by 2050 under LCCP to reduce methane from enteric fermentation.
source_quote: The target in CPOS and LCCP scenarios in 2050 is 3.42 million head and 6.58 million head, respectively.
extraction_rationale: Quantified target for a methane-reduction practice in livestock management.

policy_statement: Reduce synthetic fertilizer use by substituting organic fertilizer, reducing total urea use by 5,374 tons (2030) and 65,697 tons (2050) under LCCP.
source_quote: Under CPOS, the adoption of this mitigation action in 2030 and 2050 are expected to reduce the use of urea amounted to 3,089 ton and 58,513 ton, respectively. Under LCCP, the reduction of total urea used in 2030 and 2050 is expected to be 5,374 ton and 65,697 ton, respectively.
extraction_rationale: Quantified reductions in fertilizer use with years; concrete mitigation measure.

policy_statement: Increase integrated oil palm–livestock farming to 21.11% (3.02 Mha) by 2030 and 34.33% (4.91 Mha) by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Under CPOS, integrated farming of oil palm-livestock is targeted to reach 11.70% (1.68 Mha) in 2030 and 22.72% (3.25 Mha) in 2050. Under LCCP, the target is increased to 21.11% (3.02 Mha) in 2030 and to 34.33% (  4.91 Mha) in 2050.
extraction_rationale: Quantified adoption targets for an integrated farming system framed under low-carbon objectives.

policy_statement: Examine incentives to encourage climate-friendly integrated farming practices for large-scale plantations.
source_quote: To increase the adoption of the integrated farming practices, particularly for large scale plantations, Government will examine possible incentive for encouraging climate-friendly farming practices.
extraction_rationale: Commits to developing incentives; somewhat vague ("examine") but still a stated government action toward adoption of climate-friendly practices.

policy_statement: Enforce restrictions on conversion of agricultural lands as mandated by Law No. 41/2009 on sustainable agriculture land.
source_quote: Restriction of conversion of agriculture lands as mandated by the Law No. 41/2009 on sustainable agriculture land is enforced.
section_header: c. Optimizing Use of Unproductive Land
extraction_rationale: Binding legal enforcement affecting land-use change; relevant to avoiding deforestation and maintaining agricultural land.

policy_statement: Reduce food loss to 34 kg per capita by 2050 under LCCP through improved harvest/post-harvest technology (cold storage and packaging).
source_quote: Improvements in harvest and post-harvest technology are expected to reduce food loss from 71 Kg per capita in 2010 to 40 Kg per capita in 2050 under CPOS and to 34 Kg per capita under LCCP.
section_header: d. Reducing Food Loss and Food Waste
extraction_rationale: Quantified per-capita food loss reduction target with a year and specified mechanisms.

policy_statement: Reduce avoidable food waste through household campaigns and green certification for large-scale consumers (restaurants and hotels).
source_quote: The fraction of avoidable food waste could be reduced through campaign (private household) and applying green certification for large scale consumers (e.g. restaurants and hotels).
section_header: d. Reducing Food Loss and Food Waste
extraction_rationale: Specific interventions (campaigns, certification) to reduce food waste; lacks numeric target but is a concrete policy approach.

policy_statement: Energy sector mitigation options: energy efficiency, renewable substitution, and electrification of end uses with decarbonized electricity.
source_quote: The mitigation options in energy sector includes: (i) energy eff.shorticiency measures in all subsectors; (ii) substitution of fossil fuel by renewable in power generation and transport; and (iii) electrification of end use in building and in transportation (must be accompanied by decarbonisation of electricity).
extraction_rationale: Umbrella set of mitigation options presented as a structured list; extract as parent with sub-actions.

parent_statement: Energy sector mitigation options: energy efficiency, renewable substitution, and electrification of end uses with decarbonized electricity.
policy_statement: Implement energy efficiency measures in all energy subsectors.
source_quote: The mitigation options in energy sector includes: (i) energy eff.shorticiency measures in all subsectors; (ii) substitution of fossil fuel by renewable in power generation and transport; and (iii) electrification of end use in building and in transportation (must be accompanied by decarbonisation of electricity).
extraction_rationale: Specific intervention (efficiency) explicitly listed as a mitigation option.

parent_statement: Energy sector mitigation options: energy efficiency, renewable substitution, and electrification of end uses with decarbonized electricity.
policy_statement: Substitute fossil fuels with renewables in power generation and transport.
source_quote: The mitigation options in energy sector includes: (i) energy eff.shorticiency measures in all subsectors; (ii) substitution of fossil fuel by renewable in power generation and transport; and (iii) electrification of end use in building and in transportation (must be accompanied by decarbonisation of electricity).
extraction_rationale: Explicit fuel substitution action for mitigation.

parent_statement: Energy sector mitigation options: energy efficiency, renewable substitution, and electrification of end uses with decarbonized electricity.
policy_statement: Electrify end uses in buildings and transportation, accompanied by decarbonization of electricity.
source_quote: The mitigation options in energy sector includes: (i) energy eff.shorticiency measures in all subsectors; (ii) substitution of fossil fuel by renewable in power generation and transport; and (iii) electrification of end use in building and in transportation (must be accompanied by decarbonisation of electricity).
extraction_rationale: Specific mitigation pathway combining electrification with power decarbonization.

policy_statement: Target universal household electricity access through grid/non-grid and rooftop solar PV.
source_quote: It is targeted that in the future all household will have electricity access through grid and non-grid as well as roof-top solar PV.
extraction_rationale: Explicit access target with specified delivery modes including rooftop solar; climate relevance is indirect but significant due to renewable component.

policy_statement: Nearly decarbonize the power sector by 2050 through massive renewables, CCS/CCUS on coal plants, and BECCS.
source_quote: It is expected that in 2050 the power sector will nearly decarbonised, through: (i) utilization of renewables (hydro, geothermal, solar, wind, biomass) in massive scale; (ii) most coal powerplants are equipped with CCS/CCUS; and (iii) biomass-coal cofiring power plants are connected to CCS (Biomass Energy with Carbon Capture and Storage or BECCS).
extraction_rationale: Clear long-term decarbonization objective with specified technology pathways and year.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, achieve a 2050 power generation mix of renewables 43%, coal 38%, natural gas 10%, and BECCS 8%.
source_quote: Power generation mix are: renewables (43%), coal (38%), natural gas (10%) and BECCS (8%). The renewables include hydro, geothermal, solar PV, biomass, biofuel and wind.
extraction_rationale: Quantified generation mix target for 2050 under a scenario; constitutes a planning target.

policy_statement: Equip around 76% of coal power plants with CCS to achieve zero emissions in coal power plants by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Around 76% of the coal power plant are equipped with CCS to achieve zero emissions in coal power plants.
extraction_rationale: Quantified CCS deployment share tied to an emissions outcome; concrete mitigation measure.

policy_statement: Deploy specified renewable and BECCS capacities by 2050 under LCCP (e.g., solar PV 113 GW, hydro 68 GW, geothermal 23 GW, wind 17 GW, biomass 13 GW, biofuel 14 GW, BECCS 23 GW).
source_quote: Installed capacity of renewable power generation mix are: solar PV 113 GW, hydro 68 GW, geothermal 23 GW, wind power 17 GW, biomass 13 GW, biofuel 14 GW and BECCS 23 GW with negative emissions.
extraction_rationale: Quantified capacity targets by technology; clear mitigation investment direction.

policy_statement: Develop off-grid and micro-grid power systems and smart grids to manage intermittent renewables, including smart micro-grids for 100% renewable remote areas.
source_quote: Increasing development of 'off-grid' and 'micro-grid'. Due to significant portion of intermittent renewable (solar and wind) will be deployed in the future, it will require development of smart grid that can handle large supply intermittency.
extraction_rationale: Specific infrastructure/technology measures enabling renewable integration; concrete implementation direction.

policy_statement: Achieve transport mitigation by electrifying transport and increasing biofuel supply for diesel and gasoline substitution, continuing higher biodiesel blends (B30-B50) from sustainable sources to 2050.
source_quote: Mitigation target in transport will be achieved by: (i) electrification of transport; (ii) supplying more biofuels for diesel substitute (fatty acid methyl-esther and bio-hydrocarbon or green diesel); and (iii) gasoline substitute (bioethanol and CPO-based gasoline). The biofuel (CPO-based) programme is considered successful and will be continued to 2050 by supplying biofuel with higher biodiesel proportions (B30, B40, B50), which will be produced from sustainable sources.
extraction_rationale: Explicit mitigation mechanisms for transport and continuation of a biofuel blending policy through 2050.

policy_statement: Build 3,200 km of train tracks to serve transport in Sumatra, Java, Kalimantan, and Sulawesi.
source_quote: Existing plan shows that 3,200 km of train tracks will be built to serve transport in Sumatra, Java, Kalimantan, and Sulawesi.
extraction_rationale: Quantified transport infrastructure expansion; climate relevance is indirect (modal shift potential) but the commitment is concrete.

policy_statement: General guidelines for the LTS-LCCR energy mitigation strategy (focus on power, efficiency, transport system changes, biofuels, industrial fuel shift, renewables, and CCS/BECCS).
source_quote: Based on the understanding of type of fuels and energy-consuming sectors, taking into account past development and future projection of energy demand and supply, the LTS-LCCR was developed using the following general guidelines: 1. Focussing on power sector. 2. Minimize energy demand without sacrificing people welfare and economic development (energy eff.shorticiency measure), 3. Develop more eff.shorticient transport system (promote mass public transport), electrification of vehicles and other equipment at end-users (residential and commercial) with decarbonized electricity.
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: Umbrella guideline list with numbered items; extract as parent and capture remaining items as subs where explicitly listed.

parent_statement: General guidelines for the LTS-LCCR energy mitigation strategy (focus on power, efficiency, transport system changes, biofuels, industrial fuel shift, renewables, and CCS/BECCS).
policy_statement: Focus mitigation efforts on the power sector.
source_quote: Based on the understanding of type of fuels and energy-consuming sectors, taking into account past development and future projection of energy demand and supply, the LTS-LCCR was developed using the following general guidelines: 1. Focussing on power sector. 2. Minimize energy demand without sacrificing people welfare and economic development (energy eff.shorticiency measure), 3. Develop more eff.shorticient transport system (promote mass public transport), electrification of vehicles and other equipment at end-users (residential and commercial) with decarbonized electricity.
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: Specific strategic focus area for mitigation implementation.

parent_statement: General guidelines for the LTS-LCCR energy mitigation strategy (focus on power, efficiency, transport system changes, biofuels, industrial fuel shift, renewables, and CCS/BECCS).
policy_statement: Minimize energy demand through energy efficiency measures without sacrificing welfare and economic development.
source_quote: Based on the understanding of type of fuels and energy-consuming sectors, taking into account past development and future projection of energy demand and supply, the LTS-LCCR was developed using the following general guidelines: 1.
