Focussing on power sector. 2. Minimize energy demand without sacrificing people welfare and economic development (energy eff.shorticiency measure), 3. Develop more eff.shorticient transport system (promote mass public transport), electrification of vehicles and other equipment at end-users (residential and commercial) with decarbonized electricity.
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: Explicit efficiency-based demand reduction guideline.

parent_statement: General guidelines for the LTS-LCCR energy mitigation strategy (focus on power, efficiency, transport system changes, biofuels, industrial fuel shift, renewables, and CCS/BECCS).
policy_statement: Develop more efficient transport systems by promoting mass public transport and electrifying vehicles/end-user equipment with decarbonized electricity.
source_quote: Based on the understanding of type of fuels and energy-consuming sectors, taking into account past development and future projection of energy demand and supply, the LTS-LCCR was developed using the following general guidelines: 1. Focussing on power sector. 2. Minimize energy demand without sacrificing people welfare and economic development (energy eff.shorticiency measure), 3. Develop more eff.shorticient transport system (promote mass public transport), electrification of vehicles and other equipment at end-users (residential and commercial) with decarbonized electricity.
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: Concrete transport mitigation guideline combining modal shift and electrification.

policy_statement: Oblige local governments to manage municipal solid waste under Law No. 18/2008.
source_quote: Law No. 18/2008 regarding MSW management obliges local governments to manage MSW.
extraction_rationale: Binding legal obligation on waste management; climate relevance is indirect but waste methane mitigation is significant in this document.

policy_statement: Implement Presidential Regulation No. 35/2018 to support MSW utilization for electricity generation via PLTSa or RDF.
source_quote: In addition, there are National Policy and Strategy (Jakstranas) and Provincial Policy and Strategy (Jakstrada) in waste management as well as Presidential Regulation No. 35/2018 concerning MSW utilization for electricity generation in PLTSa or RDF (refuse-derived fuels) that support GHG emission reduction.
extraction_rationale: Named regulation enabling waste-to-energy pathways explicitly linked to GHG reduction.

policy_statement: Under CPOS, manage MSW through 30% source reduction (3R) and 70% treatment via landfilling, composting, and waste-to-energy.
source_quote: Under CPOS, the MSW will be managed through waste reduction at sources (30%) by 3R (reduce-reuse-recycle) and waste treatment (70%) through landfilling, composting, and converting waste to energy.
extraction_rationale: Quantified waste management shares under a scenario; constitutes a policy pathway for waste sector mitigation.

policy_statement: Increase septic tank access targets: rural from 71% (2020) to 85% (2050) and urban from 88% (2020) to 99% (2050).
source_quote: Government programs to increase the number of septic-tank from 71% in 2020 to 85% in 2050 for people live in rural and from 88% in 2020 to 99% in 2050 for people live in urban are implemented in order to increase the access of people to the toilet (individual and communal) could be implemented as mitigation measures by introducing technologies that reduces or lower the GHG emissions.
extraction_rationale: Quantified sanitation infrastructure targets with years; framed as mitigation via lower-emission technologies.

policy_statement: Increase centralized aerobic wastewater treatment share in urban areas to 36% by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Under TRNS, it is assumed that the use of aerobic centralised will increase from 1% of people live in urban in 2020 to 14% in 2050 while under LCCP it will increase to 36% in 2050.
extraction_rationale: Quantified technology shift target with year; supports methane reduction from wastewater.

policy_statement: Implement blended cement targets: CPOS 50% of cement production at clinker/cement ratio 0.75 to 2050; LCCP increase to ratio 0.70 for most production (2030-2050).
source_quote: Blended cement mitigation under CPOS are the extend of clinker to cement ratio in 50% of cement production capacities at the level of clinker to cement ratio of 0.75 to 2050. Under LCPP, blended cement mitigation are increased by implementing clinker to cement ratio up to 0.70 for most cement productions in 2030 to 2050.
section_header: a. Blended Cement in Cement Industry
extraction_rationale: Quantified industrial process mitigation parameters with time horizon; concrete IPPU mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Improve ammonia-urea plant technology so most plants reach at least 36.6 GJ/ton NH3 natural gas consumption (BPT) by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Under LCCP, the natural gas consumption in the most plant should at least have natural gas consumption rate of 36.6 GJ natural gas /ton NH3 or at least Best Practice Technology (BPT) in 2050.
section_header: b. Technology Improvement of New Ammonia Urea Plants
extraction_rationale: Quantified efficiency/technology benchmark with year; clear industrial mitigation measure.

policy_statement: Deploy secondary catalyst reduction for N2O destruction in nitric acid production under LCCP due to high cost.
source_quote: Other selective catalytic process, e.g. secondary catalyst reduction (SCR) will also be applied as secondary mitigation for the N2O emissions destruction in nitric acids productions in 2022, with the EF decreased to 2.5 Kg N2O per ton HNO3. The deployment potential for future mitigation is relatively small due to high cost, therefore, this mitigation will be deployed under the LCCP.
section_header: c. Secondary Catalyst for N2O Destruction in Nitric Acid Industry
extraction_rationale: Specific mitigation technology commitment (SCR) with performance metric; tied to scenario deployment.

policy_statement: Deploy advanced aluminium processing technology to reduce PFC emissions under TRNS and LCCP, reducing 2050 PFC emissions from 577 ktCO2e (CPOS) to 462 ktCO2e.
source_quote: This mitigation is planned to be deployed in the aluminium industry for additional mitigation potential in 2050 under TRNS and LCCP. By maintaining this mitigation technology, in 2050, PFC emissions level under TRNS and LCCP can be reduced from 577 Kton CO2e (CPOS) to 462 Kton CO2e.
section_header: d. Improvement of Aluminium Processing Technology
extraction_rationale: Quantified emissions reduction outcome and deployment timeframe; concrete IPPU mitigation action.

policy_statement: Continue monitoring, reviewing, and updating Indonesia's LTS-LCCR 2050 as necessary considering national circumstances and Paris Agreement provisions.
source_quote: In this regard, the Indonesia's LTS-LCCR 2050 will be monitored, reviewed and updated, as necessary, taking into consideration national circumstances, capacity and capability, and the provision under the Paris Agreement.
extraction_rationale: Commits to an ongoing governance mechanism (MRU) for the long-term strategy; while procedural, it is a stated implementation commitment.

policy_statement: Accelerate decarbonisation by setting 2030 as an interim milestone for full decarbonisation of the energy sector by 2050 and integrating environmental factors in other public policies.
source_quote: “Accelerate the decarbonisation process by setting 2030 as an interim milestone for achieving full decarbonisation of the energy sector by 2050 and integrating environmental factors in other public policies.”
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This is a stated national objective with a clear timeframe (2030 milestone; 2050 full decarbonisation) guiding policy action across sectors.

policy_statement: Promote self-consumption and renewable energy communities to make citizens and businesses key players in the energy transition.
source_quote: “This requires the promotion of self-consumption and renewable energy communities, but also the greatest possible degree of regulation and transparency of the sales segment, so that consumers may reap the benefits of a competitive market.”
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This commits to specific interventions (self-consumption and energy communities) rather than background context.

policy_statement: Promote energy efficiency across all sectors as an instrument for environmental protection, energy security and reducing energy costs.
source_quote: “Promote energy efficiency across all sectors as an instrument for protecting the environment, improving energy security and reducing energy costs for families and businesses.”
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: A cross-sector policy commitment; somewhat broad but anchored as a stated objective and instrument choice.

policy_statement: Promote electrification of consumption, particularly in civil and transport sectors, to improve air and environmental quality.
source_quote: “Promote electrification of consumption, in particular in the civil and transport sectors, as an instrument for additionally improving air and environmental quality.”
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: Specific intervention direction (electrification) with sectoral focus; climate relevance is indirect but substantial.

policy_statement: Consider additional instruments if necessary, including reviewing energy taxation diversified by polluting and climate-changing emissions.
source_quote: “A willingness to consider additional instruments if necessary, such as, for example, a review of energy taxation, diversified on the basis of polluting and climate-changing emissions, and in any case in line with the Community approach to this issue.”
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This signals potential fiscal reform but is conditional ('willingness to consider'); extracted as an edge-case policy direction.

policy_statement: Phase out coal for electricity generation by the end of 2025, conditional on timely construction of replacement plants and necessary infrastructure.
source_quote: “the phasing out of coal, scheduled by the end of 2025, as mentioned within the limits of, and as long as the replacement plants and necessary infrastructure are constructed in good time;”
extraction_rationale: Clear, time-bound commitment (end of 2025) with implementation condition; core mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Implement policies and measures needed to achieve greenhouse gas reduction objectives agreed at European and international level.
source_quote: “Italy will implement the policies and measures needed to achieve the objectives of reducing greenhouse gases agreed at European and international level.”
extraction_rationale: High-level commitment; somewhat generic but explicitly commits to implementing measures to meet agreed GHG objectives.

policy_statement: Exceed, if possible, the 30% renewable energy share target by 2030 using calibrated instruments while limiting soil consumption and landscape/environment impacts.
source_quote: “Italy will promote the further development of renewables while also protecting and enhancing pre-existing products, by exceeding, if possible, the 30% target set, which must, in any event, be assumed to be a contribution towards meeting the EU target.” “This will be achieved through the use of instruments calibrated on the basis of the sectors of use, types of measures and size of the plants, with an approach aimed at limiting soil consumption and the impact on the landscape and environment, including requirements on air quality.”
extraction_rationale: Contains a quantified target (30% by 2030) and implementation approach; includes explicit land/impact constraints.

policy_statement: Adopt the Plan for the Sustainable Energy Transition of Suitable Areas (PSETSA) by the end of 2020 to frame where hydrocarbon exploration, research and production would be planned to improve sustainability.
source_quote: “In addition, by the end of 2020 the Plan for the Sustainable Energy Transition of Suitable Areas (PSETSA) will be adopted.” “This document will make it possible to establish a framework of reference of those areas in Italy in which hydrocarbon exploration, research and production activities would be planned, with the aim of improving their environmental, social and economic sustainability.”
extraction_rationale: Time-bound adoption of a named plan; climate relevance is peripheral/indirect (hydrocarbon planning with sustainability framing).

policy_statement: Adopt preventive measures and operational rules to improve resilience of transmission and distribution networks to expected increases in extreme events and heavy load periods.
source_quote: “Particular attention will be paid to the resilience of the systems, in particular of transmission and distribution networks, through preventive measures proportionate to the expected increase in extreme events and periods of heavy load, and operational rules that enable the systems to be quickly restored to normal functioning levels.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit adaptation/resilience commitment tied to climate-driven extreme events.

policy_statement: Enhance electricity interconnections and market coupling with other Member States and study/develop interconnections with third countries.
source_quote: “the electricity interconnections and market coupling with other Member States will be enhanced; however, given Italy's geographical position, the interconnections with third countries will also be studied and developed, in order to facilitate efficient trade.”
extraction_rationale: Infrastructure/market integration commitment; climate relevance indirect (enables renewables integration and system efficiency).

policy_statement: Adopt the INECP Observatory as a permanent technical office to support implementation and monitoring of the Plan.
source_quote: “a permanent technical office will be set up (INECP Observatory, which will absorb the existing Renewables Observatory). The role of the office will be to discuss, share and agree and cooperate on topics regarding the implementation of the Plan”
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: Institutional implementation mechanism; not a climate outcome itself but a concrete governance policy enabling delivery.

policy_statement: INECP Observatory will draw up an annual implementation report to be sent to national institutions and parliamentary committees.
source_quote: “Each year the Observatory will draw up an implementation report that will be sent to the State-Regions Conference, the Prime Minister's Office and Parliamentary Committees 8 (environment) and10 (productive activities) and to the ANCI.”
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: Concrete monitoring/reporting commitment; supports accountability for climate/energy policies.

policy_statement: Set up a Plan-monitoring platform by GSE to channel data and support INECP monitoring and reporting.
source_quote: “To this end, for the purposes of the INECP Observatory and to provide timely, up-to-date information to citizens and central and local government bodies, GSE will set up a Plan-monitoring platform to which data and information from different sources will be channelled.”
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: Specific operational commitment to build monitoring infrastructure; enables tracking of climate/energy targets.

policy_statement: Propose extending the burden-sharing approach beyond 2020 to share RES objectives with Regions and call on regional governments to contribute coherently.
source_quote: “This approach, based on a distribution of effort between the various Regions, will also be proposed beyond 2020, in order to ensure sharing of objectives and to call on regional governments to contribute in a coherent manner to their attainment.”
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: Forward-looking policy commitment on governance of RES targets; somewhat general but anchored to an existing decree model.

policy_statement: Adopt pathways to achieve climate neutrality by 2050 in the Long-Term Strategy, aligned with EU approach.
source_quote: “To quantify the effort required, the Strategy identifies possible pathways to achieve 'climate neutrality' by 2050, in line with EU and Italian policy approaches.”
extraction_rationale: Long-term target-setting (climate neutrality by 2050) guiding policy; not detailed measures but a defined outcome.

policy_statement: Create Green Bonds ('green' government securities) with issuances proportionate to state-budget interventions to combat climate change and promote energy conversion and circular economy.
source_quote: “it is worth noting in this section the creation of 'green' government securities. Issuances of Green Bonds will be proportionate to interventions funded from the State budget to combat climate change, promote energy conversion and the circular economy, protect the environment and foster social and territorial cohesion.”
extraction_rationale: A financial instrument commitment (sovereign green bonds) explicitly tied to climate and energy conversion spending.

policy_statement: Achieve a 30% share of renewable energy in gross final energy consumption by 2030 (about 33 Mtoe RES out of 111 Mtoe).
source_quote: “Italy plans to pursue the target of obtaining 30% of gross final consumption of energy from renewable sources in 2030” “the target for 2030 projects a gross final consumption of energy of 111 Mtoe, with approximately 33 Mtoe of that coming from renewable sources.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified national RES target with year and energy quantities.

policy_statement: Achieve by 2030 sectoral renewable shares of 55.0% in electricity, 33.9% in heating and cooling, and 22.0% in transport (RED II accounting).
source_quote: “the contribution of renewables to meet total gross final consumption by 2030 (30%) is expected to have the following distribution between the different sectors: - -55.0% renewables share in the electricity sector; - -33.9% renewables share in the heating sector (for heating and cooling); - -22.0% with regard to the incorporation of renewables in the transport sector (calculated using the target accounting criteria established by RED II).”
extraction_rationale: Quantified sectoral targets for 2030; clear policy targets.

policy_statement: Reach 52,000 MW solar PV and 19,300 MW wind capacity by 2030 (including 900 MW offshore wind and 880 MW CSP).
source_quote: “Table 10 - Growth targets for power (MW) from renewable sources for 2030” “Solar ... 52,000 ... Wind ... 19,300 ... of which off-shore ... 900 ... of which concentrated solar power (CSP) ... 880”
extraction_rationale: Quantified installed-capacity targets by technology for 2030.

policy_statement: Promote revamping and repowering of existing wind plants to increase output while limiting soil consumption.
source_quote: “it will not only be necessary to stimulate new production, but also to preserve existing production and, if possible, actually increase it, by promoting the revamping and repowering of installations.” “the opportunity to promote investments in the revamping and repowering of existing wind power plants ... will also help to limit the impact on soil consumption.”
extraction_rationale: Specific intervention (repowering/repowering) with stated purpose; not quantified but concrete.

policy_statement: Prioritise PV installation on buildings and already-used/compromised areas; allow ground-mounted PV with priority to unproductive/contaminated sites and areas along infrastructure.
source_quote: “a reduction in soil consumption, will be followed ... by promoting their installation primarily on buildings, roofs, car parks, service areas, etc.” “it is nevertheless still vital to promote large ground-mounted photovoltaic installations, with priority being given, however, to unproductive areas ... preference should be given to contaminated sites, waste disposal sites and areas along the infrastructure system.”
extraction_rationale: Siting policy guidance for PV expansion; concrete planning constraint linked to environmental impacts.

policy_statement: Introduce more stringent performance requirements for incentives for biomass heat generators and encourage replacement of old wood-fired systems with higher-class low-emission systems.
source_quote: “In order to stimulate the renewal of old systems using efficient, low-emission technologies, more stringent performance requirements on accessing incentives for biomass-fired heat generators will be introduced in the short term.” “the replacement of domestic wood-fired systems with more efficient, lower-emission systems that meet the highest environmental classification standards ... will be encouraged.”
extraction_rationale: Concrete regulatory/incentive tightening for biomass heating; addresses air quality and efficiency.

policy_statement: Confirm target of at least 1.1 billion m³ of advanced biomethane by 2030 for transport (from agricultural waste and OFMSW).
source_quote: “For advanced biomethane originating from agricultural waste and the organic fraction of municipal solid waste (OFMSW), the target of at least 1.1 billion m 3 by 2030 is confirmed.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified target with deadline; specific fuel pathway.

policy_statement: Reach almost 6 million electrically powered vehicles by 2030 (about 4 million all-electric) and introduce compulsory quotas of electric vehicles for public transport.
source_quote: “almost 6 million electrically powered vehicles in overall circulation by 2030, approximately 4 million of which will be all-electric vehicles.” “The aim is to introduce compulsory quotas of electric vehicles specifically for public transport.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified deployment target plus regulatory intent (compulsory quotas) for public transport electrification.

policy_statement: Promote production and use of hydrogen produced by renewable electricity (R&D and demonstration) to reduce emissions and store excess renewable electricity.
source_quote: “The plan is also to promote - starting with research, development and demonstration activities - the production and use of hydrogen produced by renewable electricity.” “This offers the double advantage of reducing emissions ... while at the same time making it possible to store excess renewable electricity generated when supply exceeds demand.”
extraction_rationale: Specific technology policy with explicit climate mechanism; includes implementation pathway (R&D/demonstration).

policy_statement: Reduce primary energy consumption by 43% and final energy consumption by 39.7% by 2030 versus PRIMES 2007; target absolute levels of 125.1 Mtoe primary and 103.8 Mtoe final in 2030.
source_quote: “Italy intends to pursue an indicative reduction target for 2030 of 43% for primary energy consumption and of 39.7% for final energy consumption, with respect to the reference PRIMES 2007 scenario.” “Italy is pursuing a target of 125.1 Mtoe of primary energy and 103.8 Mtoe of final energy”
extraction_rationale: Quantified efficiency targets and absolute consumption levels for 2030.

policy_statement: Achieve cumulative end-use energy savings of about 51.4 Mtoe over 2021-2030 under Article 7 EED (0.8% per year obligation).
source_quote: “the energy savings targets set for each Member State to be attained between 1 January 2021 and 31 December 2030 are equivalent to a minimum of 0.8% per year” “the target already set out in the draft INECP, of about 51.4 Mtoe ... is confirmed.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified cumulative savings obligation with timeframe; clear policy target.

policy_statement: Renovate 3% annually of central public administration building floor area; plan to renovate 3.2 million m² during 2021-2030 and continue PREPAC with additional funding.
source_quote: “With regard to the energy renovation each year of 3% of the floor area of properties of the central public administration ...” “during the period 2021-2030, 3.2 million m 2 of floor area of buildings associated with the central public administration will be subjected to energy renovation.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified public-sector renovation commitment with timeframe; clear compliance mechanism.

policy_statement: Earmark additional resources for PREPAC: €25 million for 2019 and €40 million per year for 2020-2022.
source_quote: “The existing measure was also reinforced by the 2019 Budget Law, which earmarked further resources for the programme, totalling €25 million for 2019 and €40 million each year from 2020 to 2022.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit budget allocation (financial instrument) supporting energy renovation programme.

policy_statement: Expand efficient district heating and cooling networks by about 900 km to deliver about 4,000 GWh additional energy, based on GSE economic potential assessment.
source_quote: “the economically sustainable growth potential for energy provided by district heating is approximately 4,000 GWh, to be attained by extending national district heating and district cooling networks by approximately 900 km”
extraction_rationale: Quantified infrastructure expansion objective; supports efficiency and system optimisation.

policy_statement: Reduce energy dependence from 77.7% (2016) to about 68% by 2030.
source_quote: “On the basis of the scenario with targets, energy dependence should decrease from 77.7% in 2016 to approximately 68% in 2030.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified national energy security target; achieved via renewables/efficiency and diversification.

policy_statement: Develop new storage capacity: install at least 6 GW of new storage systems by 2030 and about 4.5 GW of distributed storage coupled with distributed systems.
source_quote: “Installation of new storage systems amounting to at least 6 GW by 2030” “A high penetration of storage systems coupled with distributed systems (about 4.5 GW) is envisaged”
extraction_rationale: Quantified infrastructure target for flexibility and renewables integration.

policy_statement: Reduce renewable over-generation to around 1 TWh by 2030 through network upgrades, new dispatching resources and storage.
source_quote: “Reduction of over-generation to values of around 1 TWh by 2030, by upgrading the network, introducing new dispatching resources and storage systems and making more use of existing storage systems.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified operational target tied to storage/network measures; supports renewables integration.

policy_statement: Increase resilience of electricity networks against extreme weather events by adopting and implementing specific action plans starting with higher-risk areas.
source_quote: “Increased network resilience, including against extreme weather events, by adopting and implementing specific action plans, starting with higher risk areas, in order to protect continuity of supply and the safety of individuals and property.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit adaptation/resilience policy responding to extreme weather risk.

policy_statement: Aim for 2030 electricity interconnectivity level of 10% (Italy INECP) and implement planned interconnection projects subject to cost-benefit analysis.
source_quote: “Level of electricity interconnectedness ... 2030 objectives ... ITALY (INECP) ... 10%” “in order for a new interconnector to be constructed, it is an absolute prerequisite that its socio-economic and environmental costs and benefits are analysed beforehand, to ensure that the benefits outweigh the costs.”
section_header: iii. Overview table with key objectives, policies and measures of the plan / 2.4.1 Electrical interconnectivity
extraction_rationale: Quantified interconnectivity objective plus implementation condition; climate relevance indirect.

policy_statement: Implement electricity network upgrades by 2023: Colunga-Calenzano, Foggia-Villanova, and Bisaccia-Deliceto 380 kV lines.
source_quote: “The following cross-zonal measures are scheduled to be implemented by 2023: - -380 kV Colunga-Calenzano electricity line - -380 kV Foggia-Villanova electricity line - -380 kV Bisaccia-Deliceto electricity line”
extraction_rationale: Specific named infrastructure projects with deadline; enables renewables integration and system efficiency.

policy_statement: Invest an estimated €21.4 billion in electricity distribution networks (including resilience measures and 2G meters) under the evolution scenario.
source_quote: “In any event, the spatial coherence between generation and load does not guarantee ... In the scenario involving an evolution trend, the estimated investment costs in the distribution network stand at €21.4 billion, which includes planned measures to increase resilience ... and the roll-out of 2G meters (€4.8 billion).”
extraction_rationale: Quantified investment commitment/need; supports grid modernisation for renewables and electrification.

policy_statement: Abolish regulated retail electricity prices ('Enhanced Protection') by 1 January 2022, with accompanying consumer-awareness and market-qualification measures.
source_quote: “prerequisites for the abolition of price protection schemes, which the Italian authorities recently established should take place on 1 January 2022 (Article 12 of Decree-Law No 162/2019).”
extraction_rationale: Time-bound regulatory reform; climate relevance peripheral but affects energy market functioning.

policy_statement: Remove the €0/MWh price floor and allow negative price bids on day-ahead and intraday electricity markets to align with EU rules.
source_quote: “Italy plans to remove the floor, thus allowing negative price bids on the day-ahead and intraday markets.”
extraction_rationale: Concrete market rule change; supports integration of variable renewables and flexibility.

policy_statement: Set up a National Observatory of Energy Poverty at the beginning of 2020 coordinated operationally by GSE.
source_quote: “an Observatory of Energy Poverty is scheduled to be set up by the Ministry of Economic Development at the beginning of 2020. Although the Observatory will be coordinated by GSE at operational level”
extraction_rationale: Specific institutional measure with timeframe to address energy poverty.

policy_statement: Create an 'energy income' rotation fund to cover 100% of investment costs for domestic PV installations up to 20 kW for low-income households.
source_quote: “a provision entitled 'energy income' is being created. This involves setting up a rotation fund for granting capital contributions covering 100% of the cost of investment in photovoltaic installations for domestic use (up to 20 KW).”
extraction_rationale: Clear financial instrument (rotation fund) with defined coverage and size limit; supports equitable access to renewables.

policy_statement: Adopt automatic access to electricity and gas social bonuses for recipients of citizenship income and move toward automated identification of eligible households.
source_quote: “those who benefit from the 'citizenship income' ... have automatic access to the social bonuses for electricity and gas.” “plans are in place to introduce an automated mechanism for identifying those entitled to the relief schemes”
extraction_rationale: Concrete policy change to expand uptake of existing support; climate relevance indirect.

policy_statement: Allocate €15 million per year for 2020 and 2021 for an experimental programme for tree planting and creation of urban and suburban forests in metropolitan cities.
source_quote: “reforestation measures, with a grant of €15 million for each of the years 2020 and 2021 for an experimental programme for tree planting, replanting and forestry and the creation of urban and suburban forests in metropolitan cities;”
extraction_rationale: Budgeted nature-based programme with explicit funding and timeframe.

policy_statement: Implement the Experimental Mobility Voucher Programme with specified multi-year funding (2019-2024) to incentivise sustainable mobility in metropolitan areas.
source_quote: “Incentives for sustainable mobility in metropolitan areas, setting up a special fund called the 'Experimental Mobility Voucher Programme', with an allocation of €5 million for 2019, €70 million for 2020, €70 million for 2021, €55 million for 2022, €45 million for 2023 and €10 million for 2024.”
extraction_rationale: Clearly funded programme with multi-year allocations; supports modal shift and emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Provide Mobility Vouchers (€1,500 per car and €500 per motorcycle) for scrappage of older vehicles in infringement municipalities, usable for public transport season tickets or bicycles within three years.
source_quote: “establishing, within the above-mentioned spending limits and until resources have been used up, a 'Mobility Voucher' of €1,500 per passenger vehicle and €500 per motorcycle scrapped. The voucher is to be used, within the following three years, to buy season tickets for local and regional public transport or bicycles, including e-bikes;”
extraction_rationale: Specific incentive design with amounts and eligible uses; mitigation via transport demand shift.

policy_statement: Allocate €20 million in 2020 and €20 million in 2021 for projects creating/modernising preferential lanes for local public transport.
source_quote: “funding for projects creating, extending, modernising or bringing up to standard preferential lanes for local public transport 9LPT), with an allocation of €20 million to be authorised for each of the years 2020 and 2021;”
extraction_rationale: Budgeted transport infrastructure measure; supports modal shift and emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Set up Economic Environmental Zones (ZEAs) in national parks with support for businesses reducing GHG emissions and promoting renewables and efficiency; allocate €20 million per year (2020-2022) for ZEA initiatives.
source_quote: “establishing Economic Environmental Zones (ZEAs) in areas within national parks.” “From the fund, €20 million for 2020, 2021 and 2022 is destined for initiatives in the ZEAs.”
extraction_rationale: Named policy instrument with earmarked funding; supports mitigation via business investment.

policy_statement: Allocate at least €150 million per year (2020-2022) from a state fund for initiatives to reduce GHG emissions, develop renewables and energy efficiency, combat deforestation, promote geological CO2 capture and sustainable mobility.
source_quote: “of which a quota of at least €150 million for each of the years 2020, 2021 and 2022 is intended for initiatives to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, develop renewable energy and energy efficiency, combat deforestation, and promote the geological capture of CO2 and sustainable mobility.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit budget earmark for climate actions; broad but financially anchored.

policy_statement: Allocate €40 million (2019-2024) for trial 'green corners' selling loose/on-draught products to reduce waste and GHGs.
source_quote: “in order to reduce the production of waste and GHGs, a non-repayable economic contribution of €40 million for 2019-2024 has been allocated for the trial of 'green corners' in city shops”
extraction_rationale: Funded waste-prevention measure with explicit climate linkage.

policy_statement: Allocate €27 million (2019-2024) for the 'mangiaplastica' programme to deploy plastic-eating machines exchanging bottles for vouchers.
source_quote: “an experimental programme called ' mangiaplastica ' is planned. A total of €27 million has been allocated for 2019-2024 to provide municipalities and supermarkets, on demand, with 'plastic-eating' machines”
extraction_rationale: Funded circular economy intervention; climate relevance indirect via waste/emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Set up the 'Io sono Ambiente' fund with €6 million (2020-2022) for environmental information/training campaigns in schools.
source_quote: “a specific fund named 'Io sono Ambiente' (I am the environment) has been set up, with €6 million allocated for 2020-2022.”
extraction_rationale: Budgeted education/awareness measure; climate relevance indirect.

policy_statement: Provide a tax credit (up to €10,000 per beneficiary; €10 million total for 2020) for sellers reusing/recycling returned packaging under the Growth Decree-Law voucher scheme.
source_quote: “The seller re-using the packaging, or sorting it to be sent for recycling, receives a tax credit equal to double the amount granted to the purchaser as a voucher. This credit is granted up to a maximum amount of €10,000 per beneficiary, for a total limit of €10 million for 2020.”
extraction_rationale: Concrete fiscal incentive for circular economy; climate relevance indirect but material.

policy_statement: Provide a 25% contribution (tax credit/discount) for purchases of products made 75% from recycled waste/scrap and quality compost, capped per beneficiary with €10 million total for 2020.
source_quote: “for 2020 the Growth Decree-Law provides for a contribution equal to 25% of the purchase cost of: a) semi-finished and finished products which are 75% made up of recycled waste and scrap; b) quality compost derived from the processing of sorted organic waste.” “the contribution due to them is granted in the form of a tax credit up to a yearly maximum of €10,000 per beneficiary for a total yearly limit of €10 million for 2020.”
extraction_rationale: Specific fiscal incentive with rates and caps; supports resource efficiency and emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Implement coal phase-out by 2025 supported by infrastructure changes (flexible generation, networks, storage) and specific works during 2020-2025 including ~3 GW new gas capacity and 3 GW new storage in centre-south/south and Sicily.
source_quote: “Italy has planned gradual termination of production of electricity with carbon by 2025, with the first significant step by 2023, compensated ... by a plan for changing infrastructures (to flexible generation, networks and storage systems) to be carried out in the coming years.” “some infrastructure changes are linked in particular to the phasing out of carbon and, in particular, are to be launched in the period 2020-2025: - -new gas capacity for around 3 GW ... and new storage systems for 3 GW in the centre south and south zones, and in Sicily;”
extraction_rationale: Time-bound mitigation policy with quantified supporting infrastructure; includes fossil-to-gas transition element.

policy_statement: Install at least 3000 MVAR of new synchronous condensers (especially south and centre-south) to address voltage regulation needs from coal phase-out and renewables growth.
source_quote: “the installation of at least 3000 MVAR of new synchronous condensers, in particular in the south and centre-south zones, to tackle the consequent requirements arising from voltage regulation;”
extraction_rationale: Specific grid-stability infrastructure commitment enabling renewables integration.

policy_statement: For Sardinia coal phase-out, evaluate a new Sardinia-Sicily-continent interconnection plus 400 MW gas generation or storage on the island and at least 250 MVAR condensers.
source_quote: “for the phasing-out of coal in Sardinia, a new electricity interconnection between Sardinia, Sicily and the continent is being looked into, along with new capacity for gas generation or storage capacity of 400 MW located on the island and the installation of condensers for at least 250 MVAR.”
extraction_rationale: Specific quantified measures tied to coal phase-out; supports system adequacy and renewables integration.

policy_statement: Establish a first verification step by end of 2020 to ensure authorisation proceedings for principal coal phase-out works are concluded.
source_quote: “A first verification step may be in place at the end of 2020, the date on which the authorisation proceedings, for the principal works at least, will need to have been concluded.”
extraction_rationale: Implementation milestone for coal phase-out enabling infrastructure; time-bound administrative commitment.

policy_statement: Implement Po Basin Agreement 2017 measures in regional air quality plans to reduce agricultural emissions via covered manure storage, correct spreading methods and soil burial of fertilisers where feasible.
source_quote: “the Italian Regions must, as part of the air quality plans, apply practices aimed at the reduction of emissions produced by agricultural activity, including coverage of structures for storing sewage, using the correct methods for spreading of manure and the burial of soil surfaces used to apply fertilisers”
extraction_rationale: Specific mandated practices for regions; adaptation is not primary—this is mitigation/air pollutant reduction.

policy_statement: Adopt a national code of good agricultural practices for controlling ammonia emissions with mandatory measures and optional measures financed via rural development funds.
source_quote: “The code provides mandatory measures for mitigating and reducing ammonia by means of: different use of fertilisers; techniques for spreading manure and storage. The optional mitigation measures are to be financed using European funding attributable to rural development policies.”
extraction_rationale: Regulatory/planning instrument with mandatory measures and financing pathway.

policy_statement: Assess measures to promote CO2 sequestration in agricultural soils and forest systems, including potential payments for ecosystem services.
source_quote: “an assessment will be made of potential measures to promote initiatives aimed at CO2 sequestration in agricultural soils and forest systems” “This will also take into account potential payment measures for ecosystem services for forestry and those linked to agricultural soils”
extraction_rationale: Policy intent but not yet adopted; extracted as an edge-case because it commits to assessment rather than implementation.

policy_statement: Increase forest utilisation rates from current 30-33% to 40-45% over ten years under the Consolidated Law on Forests and Forest Supply Chains (TUFF) to support sustainable forest management and carbon absorption.
source_quote: “With this measure, the goal is to recognise Sustainable Forestry Management as a tool aimed at ensuring an increase in carbon absorption” “over a period of ten years, a progressive change of the utilisation rates recorded thus far is envisaged, increasing from the current 30-33% to a possible 40-45%.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified forestry management change with timeframe; nature-based mitigation.

policy_statement: Establish the Fund for energy transition in the industrial sector using EU ETS auction revenues above €1,000 million, up to €100 million/year (2020) and €150 million/year (from 2021) for industrial decarbonisation and efficiency measures.
source_quote: “Decree-Law No 101 of 3 September 2019 established the 'Fund for energy transition in the industrial sector'” “This excess amount, up to a maximum of €100 million per year for 2020 and €150 million as of 2021, will be used to fund decarbonisation and energy efficiency measures in the industrial sector.”
extraction_rationale: Clear financial instrument with funding caps and purpose; direct mitigation.

policy_statement: Phase out environmentally damaging subsidies by establishing an interministerial working group within 90 days and drafting legislative proposals by 31 December 2019.
source_quote: “Action 1 of the cross-cutting measures contained in the memorandum provides for environmentally damaging subsidies to be cut back, by: - setting up, within 90 days, an interministerial working group” “- drawing up, by 31 December 2019, and presenting to stakeholders legislative proposals for cutting back on environmentally damaging subsidies”
extraction_rationale: Time-bound governance steps toward subsidy reform; policy is procedural but includes deadlines and legislative output.

policy_statement: Budget Law 2020 revises and increases excise duties on fossil fuels used for electricity generation based on GHG and fine particle emissions, with particularly high increases for coal, coke and lignite.
source_quote: “the Budget Law for 2020 revises and increases the levies on energy products used to produce electricity. The sole aim of this measure is to introduce specific rates of excise duties determined on the basis of levels of emissions of greenhouse gases and fine particles.” “The increase, which applies to all fossil fuels, is particularly high for coal, coke and lignite.”
extraction_rationale: Concrete fiscal instrument explicitly linked to emissions; direct mitigation incentive.

policy_statement: Implement RES1 (Ministerial Decree 4 July 2019) to incentivise almost 8 GW of mature renewable plants via competitive procedures in six rounds up to 2021.
source_quote: “in 2019 Ministerial Decree 4/7/2019 (RES1) was published, providing an incentive for almost 8GW (of which 7.4GW new) for renewable energy plants with a high level of technological maturity.” “The quotas are allocated by means of competitive procedures ... in six rounds up until 2021.”
extraction_rationale: Named policy instrument with quantified capacity and implementation schedule; financial support mechanism.

policy_statement: Set up a market platform for long-term trading (PPAs) within 180 days of RES1 entry into force to promote PPAs for new renewable plants without charges for the State or consumers.
source_quote: “The Ministerial Decree of 4 July 2019 provides that a regulatory framework for the creation of a market platform for long-term trading be set up within 180 days of its entry into force.” “The ultimate aim is to promote the use of these contractual schemes without them resulting in charges for the State or for consumers.”
extraction_rationale: Time-bound regulatory commitment enabling PPAs; supports renewables financing.

policy_statement: Carry out an interactive mapping/survey with Regions to identify suitable and unsuitable areas for renewable plants and coordinate plant, grid and storage development with simplified authorisations.
source_quote: “national objectives will be shared and agreed with the Regions under a national regulatory framework ... will set out criteria ... on the basis of which the Regions themselves will be able to identify the areas that are suitable for installing renewable energy plants and those which are not.” “To achieve these aims, a computerised and interactive survey will be carried out”
extraction_rationale: Concrete planning/governance measure to enable RES deployment and reduce conflicts; not quantified but specific.

policy_statement: Promote smaller islands as laboratories for renewables and electrification via incentives and pilot projects under Ministerial Decree 14 July 2017.
source_quote: “the Ministerial Decree of 14 July 2017 sets out specific targets for covering consumption with renewable energy sources” “-implementation of pilot projects designed to increase the use of renewables by using storage systems, developing electric transport, integrating the electricity system with the island water systems”
extraction_rationale: Named decree and pilot programme; supports mitigation and system innovation.

policy_statement: Promote renewable energy communities with direct support for production and locally consumed energy and privileged access to support mechanisms, exploring support for energy-poor households.
source_quote: “Renewable energy communities will be promoted in economic terms by means of direct support mechanisms for production ... and for locally consumed energy.” “ways in which those communities can also provide support to families in conditions of energy poverty ... will be explored.”
extraction_rationale: Specific policy instrument (energy communities) with economic support; includes equity dimension though partly exploratory.

policy_statement: Extend and refine obligations to integrate renewables into buildings, including progressive extension to existing buildings and simplifying the obligations system.
source_quote: “progressive and gradual extension of the minimum quota obligation for renewable energy sources ... to existing buildings” “there are plans to update the obligations system, making it simpler and immediately applicable”
extraction_rationale: Regulatory expansion of building RES obligations; concrete though details pending.

policy_statement: Introduce rewards for PV installations replacing asbestos-containing roofing.
source_quote: “introduce rewards for construction of photovoltaic plants where the modules are installed as replacements for roofing containing asbestos.”
extraction_rationale: Specific incentive design; climate relevance indirect but supports PV deployment.

policy_statement: Issue a decree to incentivise existing agricultural biogas plants (operational before 31 Dec 2017) meeting sustainability criteria and operating programmably from 30 June 2020 onwards.
source_quote: “the Budget Law for 2020 envisages the right to use an incentive on electricity produced. This applies to existing biogas-powered plants that started operating before 31 December 2017” “To benefit from the incentive ... reconvert daily production in accordance with a programmable system ... from 30 June 2020 onwards.”
extraction_rationale: Specific eligibility and date; incentive-based policy to maintain renewable generation and system flexibility.

policy_statement: Update mandatory biofuel quotas and introduce differentiated targets through RED II transposition for 2022-2030, including adding renewable hydrogen and possibly recycled carbon fuels.
source_quote: “Obligation to use biofuels and other renewables in transposing RED II: 2022-2030” “The main objectives are: updating the mandatory quotas ... adding hydrogen from renewable sources and possibly fuels from recycled carbon”
extraction_rationale: Time-bound legislative commitment with specific content elements; mitigation in transport.

policy_statement: Maintain incentives for biomethane and advanced biofuels (2018-2022) via certificates for ten years, covering about 1.1 billion m³/year biomethane demand for road transport.
source_quote: “Incentives to use biomethane and advanced biofuels ... with issuing of certificates of release for consumption for a duration of ten years.” “It is envisaged that this incentivisation system will cover ... biomethane, corresponding to around 1.1 billion cubic metres a year.”
extraction_rationale: Specific incentive mechanism with duration and quantified expected coverage.

policy_statement: Accelerate public fleet procurement requirements: 30% (2022), 50% (2025), 85% (2030) of new vehicles purchased by public bodies in high-PM10 provinces to be electric/plug-in hybrid/methane/hydrogen (and buses electric/methane).
source_quote: “must ensure that at least 30% (by 2022), 50% (by 2025) and 85% (by 2030) of the vehicles purchased must be electric and hybrid with off-vehicle charging, powered by methane and hydrogen, and electricity and methane in the case of buses.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified regulatory procurement mandate with deadlines; mitigation via fleet transition.

policy_statement: Update PNIRE targets for 2020: up to 13,000 slow/accelerated and 6,000 fast charging stations and 130,000 EVs; provide €72.2 million total budget including €28.7 million government co-financing.
source_quote: “The targets of the Plan to be achieved by 2020 are to create up to 13,000 slow/accelerated charging stations and 6,000 fast charging stations” “Provision is made for a total budget of €72.2 million, in respect of government co-financing totalling €28.7 million.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified infrastructure and deployment targets with budget; supports transport electrification.

policy_statement: Mandate SUMPs by 2021 for metropolitan cities and municipalities >100,000 and polluted cities; require SUMPs for access to funding by 2025 for municipalities >50,000 (simplified guidelines).
source_quote: “it will be mandatory to prepare a SUMP ... by 2021” “municipalities with a population of more than 50,000 inhabitants, using simplified guidelines, will have to prepare a SUMP as a mandatory requirement for access to funding by 2025.”
extraction_rationale: Regulatory planning requirement with deadlines; supports transport efficiency and emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Oblige public bodies to redevelop public lighting systems by 31 December 2023 to reduce electricity consumption by at least 50% versus 2015-2016 average.
source_quote: “the Budget Law for 2018 established that public bodies are obliged to redevelop public lighting systems by 31 December 2023, guaranteeing a reduction in electricity consumption of at least 50% in relation to the average consumption 2015-2016.”
extraction_rationale: Binding requirement with deadline and quantified savings; clear efficiency policy.

policy_statement: Continue and strengthen White Certificates scheme for 2021-2030, including simplifying and potentially radically reforming the scheme.
source_quote: “The process for updating and reinforcing the White Certificates will be continued with a view to simplifying the scheme” “The possibility of implementing a radical reform of the scheme is being examined.”
extraction_rationale: Commitment to maintain and reform a core efficiency obligation instrument; details partly pending.

policy_statement: Assess a three-year tax deduction scheme for energy-efficient retrofitting and integrate Ecobonus, Sismabonus and Bonus Casa into a single mechanism rewarding deep renovation.
source_quote: “A tax deduction scheme for the energy-efficient retrofitting and restoration of existing buildings, to run for three years, is currently being assessed.” “the plan is to integrate the Ecobonus, Sismabonus and Bonus Casa schemes into a single mechanism.”
extraction_rationale: Policy under assessment; extracted as edge-case because it signals planned reform but not yet adopted.

policy_statement: Increase National Energy Efficiency Fund allocation by €733 million for 2021-2030 and create a new fund section to provide guarantees for loans for energy-efficient retrofits.
source_quote: “For 2021-2030 the additional funding mentioned above will be €733 million.” “a new section of the fund is being created that will be used to offer guarantees for financial institutions funding energy-efficient retrofitting.”
extraction_rationale: Financial instrument expansion with quantified additional funding and guarantee mechanism.

policy_statement: Focus Conto Termico on energy retrofits of non-residential buildings in public and private tertiary sector and simplify access for public bodies.
source_quote: “the plan is to focus the Conto Termico scheme on energy-efficient retrofitting and restoration of non-residential buildings, in the public and private tertiary sector.” “The intention is to continue the task of simplifying access to the scheme for public bodies”
extraction_rationale: Specific reform direction for an existing incentive; supports efficiency and thermal renewables.

policy_statement: Introduce EPC definition for buildings into the Public Contracts Code and create a new PPP contract type for EPCs to remove barriers to energy performance contracting.
source_quote: “the plan is to introduce into the Italian Code of Public Contracts ... the definition of the EPC for buildings as a special contract, and a new type of PPP contract for EPCs for buildings”
extraction_rationale: Regulatory reform to enable energy efficiency service models; concrete legal change.

policy_statement: Carry out periodic energy audits for large companies and energy-intensive companies and extend audits to gas-sector energy-intensive companies, linking benefits to implementation of efficiency measures.
source_quote: “in the period 2021-2030, the plan is to carry out the energy audit preparation programme in large companies and in energy-intensive companies, extending it also to energy-intensive companies in the gas sector and correlating the benefit perceived by the energy-intensive companies with carrying out energy efficiency measures”
extraction_rationale: Specific extension and conditionality for audits; supports industrial efficiency.

policy_statement: Update heating/cooling provisions to replace high-emission systems (diesel boilers and inefficient biomass) and assess new limits on cooling system use by climate zone.
source_quote: “provisions relating to air conditioning installations will be updated, with the specific intention of gradually replacing installations with high emissions (including diesel boilers and non-efficient biomass installations) with low-emission, highly efficient technology.” “The introduction of new limits on the use of cooling installations will then be assessed”
extraction_rationale: Regulatory update commitment; partly assessed but includes clear intent and examples.

policy_statement: Update and facilitate district heating/district cooling development via implementing decree under Law 172/2017 to support cogeneration capacity increases and network expansion.
source_quote: “this has already been provided by an implementing provision of Italian Law 172/2017, which establishes subsidies for cogeneration installations ... and which is combined with an extension of the network in terms of increasing transport capacity.”
extraction_rationale: Specific enabling measure for district heating; financial support implied via subsidies.

policy_statement: Budget Law 2020 assigns up to €500 million per year to municipalities for public works increasing energy efficiency and renewables installations, and for sustainable local development including sustainable mobility.
source_quote: “The Budget Law for 2020 assigns contributions of up to €500 million per year in total to the municipalities for investment in public works for increasing energy efficiency.” “The subsidies can also be used by the municipalities for projects in the areas of sustainable local development, sustainable mobility”
extraction_rationale: Large budget allocation with eligible uses; financial instrument supporting efficiency and renewables.

policy_statement: Update gas Preventive Action Plan and Emergency Plan under Regulation (EU) 2017/1938.
source_quote: “Revision of the Preventive Action Plan for the Italian natural gas system, in accordance with the new Security Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2017/1938)” “Update of the Emergency Plan for the Italian natural gas system, in coordination with the Emergency Plans of the other Countries”
extraction_rationale: Specific regulatory planning updates required for security; climate relevance indirect.

policy_statement: Diversify gas supply sources by increasing LNG supplies and developing LNG market to support security and maritime fuel sulphur limits.
source_quote: “Italy is actively pursuing a strategy for diversifying and increasing LNG supplies” “with the aim of also supporting the measure of gradually introducing a limit of 0.1% of sulphur content in fuels used by ships at berth in ports and passenger vessels”
extraction_rationale: Energy security policy; climate relevance indirect/peripheral (LNG is fossil but may reduce local pollutants).

policy_statement: Update Emergency Plan for the Security of the Electricity System and integrate measures into EU Risk Preparation Plans.
source_quote: “Update of the Emergency Plan for the Security of the Electricity System (EPSES)” “The measures set out in the EPSES will form part of future Risk Preparation Plans”
extraction_rationale: Operational security planning; climate relevance indirect but includes resilience to system stress.

policy_statement: Implement capacity market via annual auctions to ensure adequacy and promote low-emission investments; auctions launched for 2022 and 2023 delivery years.
source_quote: “The system was launched with the auctions for 2022 and 2023.” “the rules governing the capacity market have been integrated with the projected emissions limits for CO2 per unit of energy delivered ... excluding coal-fired installations.”
extraction_rationale: Concrete market mechanism with timeline and emissions eligibility; supports reliability and coal phase-out.

policy_statement: Double public clean energy R&D funding under Mission Innovation from €222 million (2013) to €444 million from 2021.
source_quote: “Italy has undertaken to double the value of the resources portfolio for public research in the field of clean energy, from around €222 million in 2013 ... to around €444 million from 2021”
extraction_rationale: Quantified funding target with year; direct means-of-implementation policy.

policy_statement: Adopt a long-term energy R&I strategy to 2030 (and possibly 2050) with objectives to monitor/develop key technologies and promote deployment models for energy transition and safety.
source_quote: “determine a long-term strategy (at least until 2030 and possibly to 2050) that indicates the objectives and priorities” “The principal objectives aim to: 1. monitor and develop product and process technologies vital to the energy transition; 2. promote the introduction of technologies, organisational and operational models and systems used for the energy transition and for safety.”
extraction_rationale: Strategic policy commitment with defined objectives; not fully quantified but concrete scope.

policy_statement: Maintain Electricity System Research Fund at €210 million for 2019-2021 under the new Three-Year Plan approved 9 August 2019.
source_quote: “A new Three-Year Plan for 2019-2021 has been approved by Decree of the Ministry of Economic Development of 9 August 2019” “The allocation provided for the three-year period amounts to €210 million”
extraction_rationale: Specific funding allocation and plan adoption; supports clean energy R&D.

policy_statement: Authorize Mission Innovation-related expenditure of €10 million (2019), €10 million (2020) and €20 million (2021) under the Fund for investments and infrastructural development.
source_quote: “for interventions undertaken to meet the commitments made by the Italian government via the Mission Innovation partnership ... expenditure of €10 million is authorised for each of the years 2019 and 2020 and €20 million for 2021.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit budget authorisation for clean energy innovation; financial instrument.

policy_statement: Accelerate decarbonisation by setting 2030 as an interim milestone for full decarbonisation of the energy sector by 2050 and integrating environmental factors in other public policies.
source_quote: “Accelerate the decarbonisation process by setting 2030 as an interim milestone for achieving full decarbonisation of the energy sector by 2050 and integrating environmental factors in other public policies.”
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This is a stated national objective with a clear timeframe (2030 milestone; 2050 full decarbonisation) guiding policy action across sectors.

policy_statement: Promote self-consumption and renewable energy communities to make citizens and businesses key players in the energy transition.
source_quote: “This requires the promotion of self-consumption and renewable energy communities, but also the greatest possible degree of regulation and transparency of the sales segment, so that consumers may reap the benefits of a competitive market.”
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This commits to specific interventions (self-consumption and energy communities) rather than background context.

policy_statement: Promote energy efficiency across all sectors as an instrument for environmental protection, energy security and reducing energy costs.
source_quote: “Promote energy efficiency across all sectors as an instrument for protecting the environment, improving energy security and reducing energy costs for families and businesses.”
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: A cross-sector policy commitment; somewhat broad but anchored as a stated objective and instrument choice.

policy_statement: Promote electrification of consumption, particularly in civil and transport sectors, to improve air and environmental quality.
source_quote: “Promote electrification of consumption, in particular in the civil and transport sectors, as an instrument for additionally improving air and environmental quality.”
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: Specific intervention direction (electrification) with sectoral focus; climate relevance is indirect but substantial.

policy_statement: Consider additional instruments if necessary, including reviewing energy taxation diversified by polluting and climate-changing emissions.
source_quote: “A willingness to consider additional instruments if necessary, such as, for example, a review of energy taxation, diversified on the basis of polluting and climate-changing emissions, and in any case in line with the Community approach to this issue.”
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This signals potential fiscal reform but is conditional ('willingness to consider'); extracted as an edge-case policy direction.

policy_statement: Phase out coal for electricity generation by the end of 2025, conditional on timely construction of replacement plants and necessary infrastructure.
source_quote: “the phasing out of coal, scheduled by the end of 2025, as mentioned within the limits of, and as long as the replacement plants and necessary infrastructure are constructed in good time;”
extraction_rationale: Clear, time-bound commitment (end of 2025) with implementation condition; core mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Implement policies and measures needed to achieve greenhouse gas reduction objectives agreed at European and international level.
source_quote: “Italy will implement the policies and measures needed to achieve the objectives of reducing greenhouse gases agreed at European and international level.”
extraction_rationale: High-level commitment; somewhat generic but explicitly commits to implementing measures to meet agreed GHG objectives.

policy_statement: Exceed, if possible, the 30% renewable energy share target by 2030 using calibrated instruments while limiting soil consumption and landscape/environment impacts.
source_quote: “Italy will promote the further development of renewables while also protecting and enhancing pre-existing products, by exceeding, if possible, the 30% target set, which must, in any event, be assumed to be a contribution towards meeting the EU target.” “This will be achieved through the use of instruments calibrated on the basis of the sectors of use, types of measures and size of the plants, with an approach aimed at limiting soil consumption and the impact on the landscape and environment, including requirements on air quality.”
extraction_rationale: Contains a quantified target (30% by 2030) and implementation approach; includes explicit land/impact constraints.

policy_statement: Adopt preventive measures and operational rules to improve resilience of transmission and distribution networks to expected increases in extreme events and heavy load periods.
source_quote: “Particular attention will be paid to the resilience of the systems, in particular of transmission and distribution networks, through preventive measures proportionate to the expected increase in extreme events and periods of heavy load, and operational rules that enable the systems to be quickly restored to normal functioning levels.”
extraction_rationale: Explicit adaptation/resilience commitment tied to climate-driven extreme events.

policy_statement: Create Green Bonds ('green' government securities) with issuances proportionate to state-budget interventions to combat climate change and promote energy conversion and circular economy.
source_quote: “it is worth noting in this section the creation of 'green' government securities. Issuances of Green Bonds will be proportionate to interventions funded from the State budget to combat climate change, promote energy conversion and the circular economy, protect the environment and foster social and territorial cohesion.”
extraction_rationale: A financial instrument commitment (sovereign green bonds) explicitly tied to climate and energy conversion spending.

policy_statement: Achieve a 30% share of renewable energy in gross final energy consumption by 2030 (about 33 Mtoe RES out of 111 Mtoe).
source_quote: “Italy plans to pursue the target of obtaining 30% of gross final consumption of energy from renewable sources in 2030” “the target for 2030 projects a gross final consumption of energy of 111 Mtoe, with approximately 33 Mtoe of that coming from renewable sources.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified national RES target with year and energy quantities.

policy_statement: Reduce primary energy consumption by 43% and final energy consumption by 39.7% by 2030 versus PRIMES 2007; target absolute levels of 125.1 Mtoe primary and 103.8 Mtoe final in 2030.
source_quote: “Italy intends to pursue an indicative reduction target for 2030 of 43% for primary energy consumption and of 39.7% for final energy consumption, with respect to the reference PRIMES 2007 scenario.” “Italy is pursuing a target of 125.1 Mtoe of primary energy and 103.8 Mtoe of final energy”
extraction_rationale: Quantified efficiency targets and absolute consumption levels for 2030.

policy_statement: Achieve cumulative end-use energy savings of about 51.4 Mtoe over 2021-2030 under Article 7 EED (0.8% per year obligation).
source_quote: “the energy savings targets set for each Member State to be attained between 1 January 2021 and 31 December 2030 are equivalent to a minimum of 0.8% per year” “the target already set out in the draft INECP, of about 51.4 Mtoe ... is confirmed.”
extraction_rationale: Quantified cumulative savings obligation with timeframe; clear policy target.

policy_statement: Allocate €15 million per year for 2020 and 2021 for an experimental programme for tree planting and creation of urban and suburban forests in metropolitan cities.
source_quote: “reforestation measures, with a grant of €15 million for each of the years 2020 and 2021 for an experimental programme for tree planting, replanting and forestry and the creation of urban and suburban forests in metropolitan cities;”
extraction_rationale: Budgeted nature-based programme with explicit funding and timeframe.

policy_statement: Reduce economy-wide greenhouse gas emissions by 46% in fiscal year 2030 from fiscal year 2013 levels (to 760 million t-CO2e).
source_quote: Japan aims to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 46 percent in fiscal year 2030 from its fiscal year 2013 levels, setting an ambitious target which is aligned with the longterm goal of achieving net-zero by 2050. Furthermore, Japan will continue strenuous efforts in its challenge to meet the lofty goal of cutting its emission by 50 percent.
section_header: Japan's Greenhouse Gas Emission Reduction Target
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified, time-bound national mitigation target (46% by FY2030 from FY2013), which qualifies as a core climate policy commitment under the NDC.

policy_statement: Pursue efforts to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 50% in fiscal year 2030 from fiscal year 2013 levels.
source_quote: Japan aims to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 46 percent in fiscal year 2030 from its fiscal year 2013 levels, setting an ambitious target which is aligned with the longterm goal of achieving net-zero by 2050. Furthermore, Japan will continue strenuous efforts in its challenge to meet the lofty goal of cutting its emission by 50 percent.
section_header: Japan's Greenhouse Gas Emission Reduction Target
extraction_rationale: This is an additional quantified ambition (50% by FY2030). While phrased as continued efforts rather than a binding target, it is still a concrete numeric commitment stated in the NDC.

policy_statement: Achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions (carbon neutrality) by 2050.
source_quote: Japan aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to net-zero, that is, to realize carbon neutrality by 2050, based on the idea that addressing climate change is no longer a constraint on economic growth and that proactive climate change measures bring transformation of industrial structures as well as its economy and society, leading to dynamic economic growth. By the Act Partially Amending the Act on Promotion of Global Warming Countermeasures (Act No. 54 of 2021) which was enacted in 204th session of the Diet, net-zero by 2050 became a Basic Principle of the Act.
extraction_rationale: This is a long-term quantified mitigation goal (net-zero by 2050) and is further anchored by a legislative change making it a basic principle, meeting the protocol’s criteria for a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Legislate net-zero by 2050 as a Basic Principle via the Act Partially Amending the Act on Promotion of Global Warming Countermeasures (Act No. 54 of 2021).
source_quote: By the Act Partially Amending the Act on Promotion of Global Warming Countermeasures (Act No. 54 of 2021) which was enacted in 204th session of the Diet, net-zero by 2050 became a Basic Principle of the Act. The legislative amendment will enhance the continuity and predictability of policies and accelerate efforts and investments as well as innovation for decarbonization towards not only the achievement of the mid-term target, but also the realization of a decarbonized society.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding mechanism (legislative amendment) that institutionalizes the net-zero objective, qualifying as a regulatory/legislative climate policy.

policy_statement: Establish and implement the Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) to evaluate and use international emission reductions/removals toward achieving Japan’s NDC, aiming to secure ~100 million t-CO2 cumulative reductions/removals by fiscal year 2030 and count acquired credits.
source_quote: Japan will establish and implement the Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) in order to quantitatively evaluate contributions of Japan to greenhouse gas emission reductions and removals which are achieved through the diffusion of, among others, leading decarbonizing technologies, products, systems, services, and infrastructures as well as through the implementation of measures in developing countries and others, and in order to use such contributions to achieve Japan's NDC. By doing so, through public-private collaborations, Japan aims to secure accumulated emission reductions and removals at the level of approximately 100 million t-CO2 by fiscal year 2030. Japan will appropriately count the acquired credits to achieve its NDC.
section_header: 5. Assumptions and methodological approaches, including those for estimating and accounting for anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and, as appropriate, removals:
extraction_rationale: This is a specific named intervention (market mechanism under Article 6) with a quantified target (~100 million t-CO2 by FY2030) and an explicit accounting/use commitment for NDC achievement.

policy_statement: Ensure environmental integrity and avoid double counting for the JCM in line with international rules including the Paris Agreement.
source_quote: With regards to the JCM which Japan has initiated to establish, Japan secures environmental integrity and the avoidance of double-counting in line with the international rules including the Paris Agreement. Also, based on its experience in the JCM, Japan intends to lead international discussions, thereby contributing to the development of appropriate international rules for the use of market mechanisms.
section_header: 5. Assumptions and methodological approaches, including those for estimating and accounting for anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and, as appropriate, removals:
extraction_rationale: This is an operational/implementation rule commitment governing how the market mechanism will function (integrity and double-counting avoidance), which is a concrete policy condition for Article 6 cooperation.

policy_statement: Make proactive international cooperation efforts to promote decarbonization and improve resilience in developing countries, including developing policies and institutional platforms, promoting sector- and city-level efforts, and facilitating technology diffusion.
source_quote: Furthermore, Japan will also make proactive efforts in the area of international cooperation to promote decarbonization and to improve resilience in developing countries and others, including from developing policies and institutional platforms to promoting sector- and city-level efforts as well as facilitating technology diffusion.
section_header: 5. Assumptions and methodological approaches, including those for estimating and accounting for anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and, as appropriate, removals:
extraction_rationale: This is a stated commitment to undertake specific categories of international cooperation actions (policy/platform development, sector/city efforts, technology diffusion) with explicit mitigation and adaptation/resilience objectives; however, it is somewhat broad and not quantified.

policy_statement: Continue annual rigorous reviews and examinations of progress in government countermeasures under the Plan for Global Warming Countermeasures, and continue similar progress management for the new fiscal year 2030 target.
source_quote: Every year since the formulation of the plan, the Global Warming Prevention Headquarters, led by the Prime Minister with all Cabinet Ministers as its members, has made rigorous reviews and examinations on, among others, the state of progress in each countermeasure taken by the Government, by using the outcome in emission reductions including figures by greenhouse gases and other classifications, and indicators to evaluate the progress in implementing countermeasures. Also, with regard to the new target for fiscal year 2030, the Government will continue progress management in a similar manner as mentioned in the above.
extraction_rationale: This is a governance/implementation commitment (ongoing monitoring and progress management) tied to emissions outcomes and the FY2030 target; it is a concrete institutional action though not a direct emissions-reduction measure itself.

policy_statement: Ensure implementation of Kuwait's National Adaptation Plan (NAP) through a national coordination mechanism and partnerships with governmental and non-governmental institutions.
