source_quote: The Government of Kuwait, represented by the Environment Public Authority (EPA), has committed itself to ensure the implementation of its National Adaptation Plan (NAP), in partnership with other governmental and non-governmental institutions, furthermore A national coordination mechanism has been identified to implement a range of national initiatives to protect the various vital sectors from the Negative impacts of climate change. Therefore, future programs have been developed to deal with the various risks face the sectors and across time periods.
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit governmental commitment to implement the NAP, including an identified coordination mechanism and partnership approach (a concrete governance/implementation commitment rather than background).

policy_statement: Establish a comprehensive ongoing monitoring program using environmental data and information to monitor climate change and assess its impacts in Kuwait, in partnership with stakeholders.
source_quote: One of the expected results is a comprehensive ongoing monitoring program through the necessary environmental data and information to monitor climate change and assess its impact on the State of Kuwait on an ongoing basis, In partnership with all stakeholders such as the academia, private sector and nongovernmental actors in the areas of adaptation to climate change.
extraction_rationale: Commits to an ongoing monitoring program with specified means (environmental data/information) and stakeholder partnership; this is a concrete intervention supporting adaptation planning.

policy_statement: Seek technical assistance from international organizations and other stakeholders to implement adaptation programs and reduce socio-economic side effects.
source_quote: Therefore, EPA will seek technical assistance from international organizations, industrial community and other stakeholders to implement the proposed programs to adapt to climate change and reduce the side effects associated with socio-economic problems. This will be achieved in the manner of implementing the national plan which is based on participation, while maintaining the coordination and oversight role of the EPA in the various activities and initiatives that aim to reach the desired goal to reduce the Negative impacts of climate change and adopt with it.
extraction_rationale: A stated implementation commitment (technical assistance-seeking) tied to executing adaptation programs; somewhat procedural but includes a clear action to enable implementation.

policy_statement: Integrate climate change adaptation into relevant new and existing policies, programmes and activities across all relevant sectors and levels.
section_header: 1.3. The need for National Adaptation Plan (NAP)
extraction_rationale: Although framed as UNFCCC objectives, the document uses these as the basis for Kuwait’s NAP purpose; it is a concrete mainstreaming commitment (policy integration) rather than background.

policy_statement: Enhance national climatological, meteorological and hydrological capabilities and contribute to early warning for climate change-induced disasters.
source_quote: It is also expected that NAP should enhance national climatological, meteorological and hydrological capabilities and the  means  to  contribute  to  climate  change-induced  disasters  early  warning.  It  should promote policies and strengthen institutional frameworks which develop cooperation and coordination, in a spirit of partnership between the government, local populations, and community groups and facilitate access by local populations to appropriate information and  technology.
section_header: 1.3. The need for National Adaptation Plan (NAP)
extraction_rationale: Defines a concrete capability-building and early warning objective within the NAP expectations; qualifies as a policy direction with specific intervention areas (capabilities/early warning).

policy_statement: Implement the UNFCCC-defined National Adaptation Plan (NAP) process elements (A-D) as Kuwait’s NAP framework.

policy_statement: Implement green belts and increase protected areas to adapt to dust storms, with planted belts of 50–180 km length and 5–20 km width over a 5-year duration starting in 2015.
source_quote: In response, Kuwait has undertaken some adaptation projects such as implementing green belts project and increasing the protected areas to adapt to a dust storm. The green belt projects consist of planted areas with trees and shrubs of 50-180 Km in  length  and  5-20  Km  in  width.  These  projects  have  started  in  2015  for  5-year duration time.
extraction_rationale: Concrete adaptation intervention with quantified dimensions and timeframe; clearly aimed at dust-storm adaptation.

policy_statement: Projects and National Initiatives (listed climate change adaptation projects and initiatives).
source_quote:
Many  initiatives  and  campaigns  were  taken  to  increase  public awareness  about  the  adaptation  to  climate  change.  The  following  points  provide  a comprehensive summary of ongoing and past climate change adaptation projects and initiatives.

1. Implementing green belts project and increasing the protected areas to adapt to dust storms.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella heading introducing a numbered list of specific initiatives; extract as parent to attach sub-items.

policy_statement: Implement the Kuwait Green Wall Project to increase protected areas by planting 315,000 trees for a 420 km wall along the borderline to hold back moving sand (started 2015; ongoing).
source_quote: Meanwhile, Kuwait has implemented a project called 'Kuwait Green Wall Project. This project aims to increase the protected areas by planting 315,000 trees for 420 Km wall along the borderline to hold back the moving sand. The adaptation sector is the Public Health/ Dust Control, and the responsible parties are the governments and NGOs. This project started in 2015 and still ongoing.

policy_statement: Introduce more than 50 types of trees for greenery/landscape and develop crop varieties adapted to high temperatures and resistant to salinity and drought under the Agriculture Master Plan.
source_quote: More than 50 types of trees for greenery and landscape that can reduce climate change effect, were introduced under the Agriculture Master Plan by Kuwait Institute for Scientific  Research  (KISR)  and  the  Public  Authority  for  Agricultural  Affairs  and  Fish Resources  (PAAFR).  Development  of  new  varieties  of  crops  that  can  adapt  to  high temperatures  and  have  high  resistance  to  salinity  and  drought  such  as  Conocarpus, Ficus,  Prosopis,  and  date  palm  trees,  were  implemented  in  Kuwait  (Al  Dosery  et  al., 2012).
extraction_rationale: Concrete intervention (tree introductions and crop variety development) explicitly linked to climate change effects and heat/salinity/drought tolerance.

source_quote: Medium-term actions   ▪ Incorporate measures for adaptation to climate change into actions carried out by the Ministry of Electricity and Water. ▪ Invest in high end and accurate programs to refer to information about water level based on hydraulic models. ▪ Control water prices such as water consumption are fair and reasonable by all consumers. ▪ Increase water block-tariff to control unnecessary water consumption.
section_header: 5.3.2 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Water Resources
extraction_rationale: Specific economic instrument (tariff) explicitly stated; qualifies as a financial instrument policy.

policy_statement: Reduce physical leakages in water systems (recommended measure under water sector plan).
source_quote: The SNC highlighted some recommendations to reduce water consumption, including employing new water a block-tariff, and reducing physical leakages.    Applying  these recommendations was estimated based on the three scenarios as well as the cost in US dollars of the increasing demand for water resources under the three scenarios.
extraction_rationale: Specific intervention (reduce leakages) explicitly recommended as part of adaptation to water demand under climate scenarios; concrete action though implementation details are limited.

policy_statement: Adopt reverse osmosis as a more energy-sustainable water treatment method (long-term action under water sector plan).
source_quote:
Long-term actions     ▪ Design effective policies to preserve and protect water resources. ▪ Support research and development to model the impact of climate change on water resources.

|                | ▪ Involve more environmentally sustainable methods of water treatment like Reverse osmosis, where the net energy consumption is lower than other methods. ▪ Invest in the installment of water-efficient devices in homes, where the consumption of water is better regulated and limited. ▪ Develop integrated climatic and hydrological models and assess climate change impacts on water resources management.   |
section_header: 5.3.2 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Water Resources
extraction_rationale: Specific technology shift explicitly justified by lower net energy consumption; concrete long-term action.

policy_statement: Enhance resilience of coastal zones to face sea level rise (SLR) risks through a package of short-, medium-, and long-term actions (budget: USD 7.8 million).
source_quote: Designing  adaptive  long-term  coastal  plans  to  restrict  establishing  major projects on vulnerable coasts is very urgent action that must be taken. to establish such adaptive plans, more researches assessing the impacts of SLR on the coastal zone of Kuwait  are  needed.  Also,  raising  awareness  among  decision-makers  in  Kuwait  to incorporate SLR scenarios into upcoming development plans is an important adaptation step.
section_header: 5.3.3 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Coastal Zone
extraction_rationale: Programmatic coastal adaptation plan with specific measures named; budget exists in plan table though not quoted here.

policy_statement: Restrict establishing major projects on vulnerable coasts through adaptive long-term coastal plans (urgent action).

section_header: 5.3.3 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Coastal Zone
extraction_rationale: Specific land-use planning restriction explicitly stated as urgent; qualifies as a policy intervention.

policy_statement: Legislate laws restricting negative anthropogenic activities in coastal zones to maintain coastal wildlife (medium-term action under coastal plan).
source_quote: Medium-term actions   ▪ Provide financial aid for preventative and protective actions for coastal damage. ▪ Make sure that the required resources to undergo projects and initiatives concerning the construction, research or communication are available. ▪ Raising awareness among decision-makers in Kuwait to incorporate SLR scenarios into development plans ▪ Legislating laws to restrict negative anthropogenic activities in the coastal zones to maintain the coastal wildlife
section_header: 5.3.3 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Coastal Zone
extraction_rationale: Explicit legislative action to restrict harmful activities; concrete regulatory mechanism.

policy_statement: Enhance and build capacity of the health sector to prepare for increased health risks due to climate change through short-, medium-, and long-term actions (budget: USD 4.1 million).
source_quote: Enhancing the building capacity of the health sector to be prepared for increased risks due to climate change must be set as an objective of climate change adaptation for this sector. Immediate adaptation actions should be taken to  ensure the achievement of this objective. These adaptation actions include but not limited to initiating researches to investigate the risks of climate change induced diseases, adjusting the office working hours to avoid working during maximum temperature in the day,  raising  the  awareness  of  how  to  respond  to  dust  and  heat  waves  events  and establishing national health alerts for dust and heat wave events.
section_header: 5.3.4 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Human Health Sector
extraction_rationale: Programmatic sector plan with explicit objective and named actions; budget is provided in plan table.

policy_statement: Establish national health alerts for dust storms and heat waves (short-term action under health plan).
source_quote:
Short term actions                ▪ Increase public awareness of climate changes effects and impacts on general health. ▪ Conduct risk assessments and vulnerability to Climate Change on the general public. ▪ Involve the media in carrying the message of issues of Health, as people get more influenced and receive the message more directly and subconsciously through advertisement and social media sites.

|                     | ▪ Adjust the official working hours to avoid working during maximum temperatures in the day (study and issue a new threshold). ▪ Raising awareness of how to respond to dust and heat waves events. ▪ Establishing national health alerts for dust storms and heat waves.   |
section_header: 5.3.4 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Human Health Sector
extraction_rationale: Specific intervention (national alerts) explicitly stated; concrete adaptation measure for extreme events.

policy_statement: Intentionally incorporate resiliency and climate action/adaptation into all land-use planning, policies, and standards.
source_quote: Intentionally incorporate key issues of resiliency and climate action/adaptation into all land-use planning, policies, and standards. Consider energy and water related goals to reduce demand such as human-scaled interventions, building scale incentive programs, deep energy retrofits, building code provisions, and partnerships at the City scale.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete governance commitment to mainstream climate resilience/adaptation into planning and standards (a binding mechanism pathway via policies/standards), even though it lacks a numeric target.

policy_statement: Use land use planning to reduce water demand and urban heat island impacts.
source_quote: Emphasize land use planning can reduce water demand and heat island impacts. Protect  the  environment  for  future  generations  and  mitigate  urban  heat  island  by  using  smart  growth development practices to protect and maintain limited resources.
extraction_rationale: This states a deliberate planning approach (land use planning/smart growth) to achieve specific climate-relevant outcomes (reduced water demand and heat island mitigation), though it is somewhat high-level.

policy_statement: Plan for uncertainty by considering multiple scenarios for future risk and vulnerability.
source_quote: Plan for uncertainty by considering multiple scenarios for future risk and vulnerability. Understand the anticipated context of a hotter, drier future in Las Vegas and how limited and shrinking water resources and climate change will affect the region.
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit commitment to scenario-based risk planning for climate-related uncertainty; it is a planning policy rather than a quantified target.

policy_statement: Increase density in key parts of the city to improve access to efficient energy, transportation, and community resources.
source_quote: Increase density. Density will occur in key parts of the city based on analysis which shows the biggest increases in access to efficient energy, transportation, and community resources.
extraction_rationale: This is a land-use policy direction (densification) explicitly tied to efficiency in energy/transport/resource access; it is not quantified but is a specific intervention.

policy_statement: Prioritize and incentivize construction of 'Missing Middle' housing to create more affordable housing that efficiently uses natural resources.
source_quote: Increase access to housing. Prioritizing and incentivize construction of 'Missing Middle' housing will create more affordable housing which efficiently uses natural resources and matches the character of Las Vegas neighborhoods.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific policy intervention (prioritize and incentivize Missing Middle housing) with an explicit resource-efficiency rationale; climate benefit is indirect.

policy_statement: Optimize efficient use of limited resources (land and water) by promoting enhanced infrastructure, increased tree shade, and strategic density along transportation corridors.
source_quote: Efficiently  use  resources. Optimize  the  efficient  use  of limited  resources  such  as  land  and  water  by  promoting practices such as enhanced city infrastructure, increased tree  shade,  and  strategic  density  along  transportation corridors.
extraction_rationale: This is a defined package of interventions (infrastructure, tree shade, corridor density) aimed at conserving land and water; it is actionable though not quantified.

policy_statement: Prioritize mixed-use transit-oriented development corridors for higher density development integrating diverse affordable housing types, supported by zoning typologies and modest amendments to Title 19.
source_quote: To accomplish an infill strategy that ties with many additional goals throughout the plan, the plan links identified regional centers with mixed-use transit-oriented development (TOD) corridors, accented at key nodes. These corridors must be prioritized for higher density development that integrates a diverse range of affordable housing types. A number of new place types are recommended, as well as a corresponding land use tool-box, zoning typology, and modest amendments to Title 19, including:
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete land-use and regulatory commitment (TOD prioritization plus zoning/code amendments) that strongly affects transport/energy use; climate relevance is indirect but substantial.

policy_statement: Urban Forestry: reduce heat hazards with green infrastructure, including code/zoning amendments for trees and planting at least 100,000 trees to increase canopy to 20%.
source_quote:
Due to notable increases in the urban heat island effect, steps must be taken to reduce heat hazards with appropriate green infrastructure, including:

- LVMC and zoning amendments for trees
- At least 100,000 public and private high quality, native and adaptive trees that increase the canopy are planted to increase the canopy to 20%
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella initiative with explicit sub-actions (code amendments and quantified tree/canopy targets) addressing extreme heat risk via green infrastructure.

policy_statement: Parks and Connectivity: develop a Parks System Plan, increase park acreage, and ensure most residents live within walking distance of parks/trails.
source_quote:
Because parks and recreational facilities are an important quality of life component, park facilities, amenities, connections, and safety were frequently noted throughout public outreach. As a result, the City will

- Develop  a  Parks  System  Plan  and  achieve  CAPRA certification
- Increase park acreage to 7 acres per 1,000 residents, specifically in noted areas of need
- Ensure 85% of dwelling units are within a short walk of a park or trail
extraction_rationale: This is a named initiative with multiple concrete sub-commitments including quantified access/acreage targets; climate relevance is indirect (urban cooling/health) unless hazards are named (not here).

policy_statement: Food and Urban Agriculture: eliminate food deserts, reduce food swamps, and expand community gardens/small agricultural uses to improve supply chain security and redundancy.
source_quote:
Given  the  lack  of  regional  agriculture,  it  is  necessary to ensure supply chain security and redundancy. To supplement these efforts, the City must ensure:

- No food deserts and reduce food swamps by increasing healthy food access
- Provide accessibility to community gardens and increase allowable small agricultural uses
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella policy area with specific sub-actions; climate relevance is peripheral-to-indirect (resilience framing via supply chain redundancy, but not explicitly climate).

policy_statement: Environmental Justice: reduce exposure and risk in low-income and minority communities through air quality, brownfield redevelopment, stormwater pollution prevention, and inclusive planning/transportation decision-making.
source_quote:
Reducing  exposure  and  risk  to  low-income  and  minority communities must be prioritized, especially for new transportation and infrastructure projects. The City must:

- Ensure an air quality index of 100 or better
- Eliminate brownfields within the City by redevelopment
- Improve stormwater pollution prevention efforts
- Engage residents of all races, ethnicities, abilities and means  in  the  planning  and  transportation  decisionmaking process
extraction_rationale: This is a named policy package with multiple specific commitments including a quantified air quality target; climate relevance is indirect (pollution and redevelopment) with some adaptation relevance via stormwater quality but not hazard-focused.

policy_statement: Implement a layered Complete Street network and coordinate/completion of major regional transportation projects to improve modal split and jobs-housing balance.
source_quote: The plan recommends a new layered Complete Street network to improve the City's overall modal split and jobs-housing balance. In  addition  to  complete  streets  and  bicycle  and trail  improvements  identified  in  the  Mobility  Master  Plan, this plan also recommends coordination and completion of major projects with state and regional partners, including:
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transportation system intervention (complete streets network) that can materially reduce vehicle dependence; climate relevance is indirect because emissions are not explicitly stated here.

policy_statement: Develop and implement RTC's On Board Mobility Plan recommendations to enable high-capacity transit on key TOD corridors.
source_quote: Tied  closely  to  the  2050  General  Plan  for  future  land use,  the  City  and  RTC  must  develop  and  implement  the recommendations  from  RTC's  On  Board  Mobility  Plan that  will  enable  high  capacity  transit  to  be  built  on  key TOD corridors, including Maryland Pkwy, Charleston Blvd, Decatur Blvd, Sahara Ave, and Las Vegas Blvd.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete commitment to implement a transit plan enabling high-capacity transit on specified corridors; climate relevance is indirect (transport emissions not explicitly mentioned).

policy_statement: Implement the Smarter Vegas plan, a citywide fiber network, and transportation electrification to enable connected/autonomous vehicles and other options.
source_quote: Implementing  the  Smarter  Vegas  plan,  a  citywide  fiber network,  and  transportation  electrification  will  enable  a range of new options, including connected and autonomous vehicles.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific set of interventions including transportation electrification; climate relevance is indirect because GHG reduction is not explicitly stated in this sentence.

policy_statement: Reduce water consumption to 90 gallons per person per day through code changes, pricing, incentives, and education aligned with SNWA's Water Resources Plan.
source_quote: In the face of a changing climate, this plan is closely linked to  Southern  Nevada  Water  Authority's  Water  Resources Plan  and  aligns  a  target  to  reduce  water  consumption  to 90 gallons per person per day. This can be done by making corresponding code changes, pricing, incentives, and education efforts   to meet regional water resources and conservation goals.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified conservation target with explicit implementation mechanisms (code changes, pricing, incentives, education) and explicit climate framing.

policy_statement: Increase the share of renewable energy in municipal operations and the community in line with the state's renewable portfolio standard while reducing energy consumption.
source_quote: The City has been known for its efforts in renewable energy and energy efficiency. This plan will enable both municipal operations and the community to increase its overall share of  renewable  energy  in  line  with  the  state's  renewable portfolio standard while reducing energy consumption.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear energy policy direction (renewables plus reduced consumption) tied to an external standard (state RPS), though it lacks a numeric local target.

policy_statement: Improve municipal and community recycling rates and reduce municipal solid waste through work with the City's franchisee and new waste management opportunities.
source_quote: Through close work with the City's franchisee and exploring new waste management opportunities, the City can continue  to  improve  both  its  municipal  and  community recycling rates and reduce municipal solid waste.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational commitment in waste management (recycling and waste reduction), though phrased somewhat conditionally ('can continue').

policy_statement: Attain municipal and community carbon neutrality through reductions from stationary and mobile emission sources.
source_quote: Because of the City's leadership in sustainability, the City will boldly work to attain municipal and community carbon neutrality  through  reductions  from  stationary  and  mobile sources of emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit climate mitigation target (carbon neutrality) covering both municipal and community emissions, with a stated mechanism (reductions from stationary and mobile sources) though no deadline is provided here.

policy_statement: Complete a vulnerability assessment and establish a framework for mitigation, adaptation, response, and recovery for hazards including drought, extreme heat, and flooding.
source_quote:
As  a  part  of  this  Master  Plan,  the  City  completed  a  vulnerability assessment  factoring  adaptive  capacity  and  sensitivity for a variety of hazards, as well as recommendations and a  framework  for  mitigation,  adaptation,  response,  and recovery, including:

- Drought, Extreme Heat, Flooding
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete resilience planning action (vulnerability assessment and framework) explicitly covering climate hazards (drought, extreme heat, flooding).

policy_statement: Include specific recommendations and projects from the Regional Flood Control District to address flooding risk expected to increase in intensity and frequency.
source_quote: As a specific disruptive hazard  that has  potential to increase  in  intensity  and  frequency  over  time,  specific recommendations  and  projects  from  the  Regional  Flood Control District are included.
extraction_rationale: This is an adaptation commitment to incorporate flood control projects in response to increasing flood hazard; it is specific but does not list project names in this excerpt.

policy_statement: Publish an annual report evaluating progress and implementation of plan outcomes including the 'Fifty by '50' outcomes.
source_quote:
For  transparent  communication  of  the  plan's  outcomes and performance, the City will publish a prepared annual report to  evaluate  and  discuss  annual  progress  and implementation of the plan, progress of the 'Fifty by '50'

outcomes  and  others  highlighted  for each  goal,  and  recommendations  for plan improvement.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete accountability/monitoring commitment (annual reporting). Climate relevance is indirect because it covers the whole plan, including climate-related outcomes.

policy_statement: Adopt 2-year strategic action plans to implement strategies and achieve outcomes, aligned with budgeting and the CIP.
source_quote: The  plan  recommends  that  the  City  Council  and  city management adopt 2-year strategic action plans to implement  various  strategies  and  to  achieve  outcomes. For  each  strategic  action  plan,  the  priorities  of  the  City Council  and  department  level  strategic  business  plans are  all  aligned  with  the  plan's  outcomes,  as  well  as  the budget process and CIP.
extraction_rationale: This is a governance mechanism commitment (recurring 2-year action plans tied to budget/CIP) that enables implementation of climate-related measures; climate relevance is indirect.

policy_statement: Implement the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) Process for a ten-year period (2020–2030), with monitoring and evaluation and a review around 2029 to develop a new framework for 2031–2040.
source_quote: “This NAP Process will be in effect for ten years (2020-2030), during which time there will be ongoing monitoring and evaluation, in approximately 2029, this first period of implementation will be reviewed, and a new framework will be developed to guide the period from 2031-2040.”
extraction_rationale: Contains a defined implementation period and a scheduled review/update cycle, which is a concrete planning commitment rather than background.

policy_statement: Pursue NAP objectives to reduce vulnerability to climate change by building adaptive capacity and resilience, and to integrate climate change adaptation into fiscal, regulatory, and development policies, programs, and activities.
source_quote: “The objectives of the NAP process are: - i. to reduce vulnerability to the adverse impacts of climate change by building adaptive capacity and resilience; and, - ii. to facilitate the integration of climate change adaptation into fiscal, regulatory, and development policies, programs, and activities (UNFCCC, 2012).”
extraction_rationale: States explicit government objectives that guide policy integration and resilience-building; while broad, it is a formal commitment with defined mechanisms (integration into fiscal/regulatory/development policies).

The  City  of  Luxor  would  gain  from  developing  a street  lighting  strategic  plan, identifying  areas  of differentiated usage, where lighting would be then adapted to the actual needs per specific area.

Such an improvement in urban planning and street infrastructures, linked with a tighter management of public demands, should lead to designing a lighting system combining qualitative lighting and reduced energy consumption.
section_header: 4.1.2. Street lighting — Street lighting strategic plan
extraction_rationale: Concrete planning intervention with described technical measures; budget is also provided in the subsection.

policy_statement: Upgrade water distribution and wastewater processes by assessing the system and installing variable-speed/high-efficiency pumps and SCADA to reduce electricity consumption.
source_quote:
The  Governorate  services  should  conduct  a  detailed  assessment  of  the  current  status  of  the  water distribution network and the wastewater treatment process.

For example, switching from classical pumps to variable speed devices and high efficiency equipment might result in cutting electricity consumption by 30% or more. Likewise establishing a SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) system for monitoring and control could help identifying where the main problems are and how the water distribution could be optimized while reducing energy consumption.
extraction_rationale: Specific operational/technology interventions (variable speed pumps, SCADA) explicitly aimed at energy savings; quantified savings assumptions and budgets are provided.

policy_statement: Conduct a comprehensive waste management assessment to enable separate collection, recycling chains, biodigesters, and landfill methane recovery.
source_quote:
The  Governorate  would  gain  realising  a  comprehensive  assessment  of  its  waste  management,  with  the following objectives:

- -Get a good understanding of the breakdown in different type of waste as a basis to design the most appropriate model of separate waste collection...
- -Specifically explore the benefit of installing bio-digesters units around the City of Luxor.
- -Explore the benefit or recovering methane form the landfill to capture it, hence significantly reducing GHG from the City of Luxor.
extraction_rationale: A defined intervention (comprehensive assessment) with specified follow-on actions (separate collection, biodigesters, methane capture) that would change waste system operations and emissions.

policy_statement: Implement a fleet plan to reduce fuel use through improved fleet management and awareness, and progressively replace old vehicles (potentially via leasing).
source_quote:
The City of Luxor could engage in a comprehensive plan to:

- -Continue  upgrading  the  fleet  management  tool  and  invest  more  in  people  awareness  in  order  to reduce energy consumption of the fleet as its actually stands, and
- -Replace old vehicles with new ones, looking for progressive replacement through leasing to avoid too heavy investments.
extraction_rationale: Specific operational and investment actions for municipal fleet with quantified reduction assumptions later in the section.

policy_statement: Develop a Sustainable, Clean and Green Urban Mobility Master Plan (SCGUMMP) for Luxor to reduce transport energy use and emissions.
source_quote:
Hence, a Master Plan for a Sustainable and Green Mobility is urgently required to reduce the high level of energy consumption and all nuisances attached to road traffic (noise, jam, air pollution).

Ideally, a city committed to reduced energy consumption and GHG emission such as Luxor would implement a Sustainable, Clean and Green Urban Mobility Master Plan (SCGUMMP) that could entail the following:
extraction_rationale: Named master plan with a clear purpose (reduce energy consumption and GHG emissions) and a list of specific components; further detailed as Priority Action #1 in project fiches.

parent_statement: Develop a Sustainable, Clean and Green Urban Mobility Master Plan (SCGUMMP) for Luxor to reduce transport energy use and emissions.
policy_statement: Negotiate a common charter with transport providers to improve routes, stops, and timing to reduce energy consumption in the short term.
source_quote: It seems that the only option would be to promote a negotiation process with all transport providers to adopt a common charter for global improvement of transport services aiming  at  clarifying routes, stops, timing, in order to promote synergies and avoid competition that will hamper the development of an efficient system.
extraction_rationale: Specific governance intervention (common charter) intended to improve efficiency and reduce energy use; budget is provided later.

policy_statement: Tourism sector greening programme covering hotels/resorts, cruise fleet, land transport, and heritage-site lighting, supported by awareness and technical support units/funds.
source_quote:
There are naturally four areas that would require action to improve the sustainability profile of the tourism sector in Luxor: hotel and resorts; cruise fleet; land transportation; heritage sites.

However, any action should start with a significant effort in raising awareness among tourism operators to highlight the potential benefits of green practices for their business (cost cutting from efficiency gains) and the improved attractiveness for visitors.
extraction_rationale: Defines a multi-component programme with specific intervention areas and later quantified expected results and budgets; constitutes a policy package.

parent_statement: Tourism sector greening programme covering hotels/resorts, cruise fleet, land transport, and heritage-site lighting, supported by awareness and technical support units/funds.
policy_statement: Establish a 'Green tourism support unit' to provide advice and audits to hotels/resorts investing in energy efficiency and renewable energy.
source_quote:
To shift behaviour and speed up the shift, the Governorate should establish a ' Green tourism support unit ' providing advices to tourism operators willing to invest in energy efficiency and renewable energy.

This technical unit will ensure audits to any resort and hotel willing to make necessary investments to contribute to the SECAP adopted in the City of Luxor - Governorate of Luxor.
extraction_rationale: Creates a named institutional intervention (support unit) with defined services (advice, audits) to enable mitigation actions.

parent_statement: Tourism sector greening programme covering hotels/resorts, cruise fleet, land transport, and heritage-site lighting, supported by awareness and technical support units/funds.
policy_statement: Create an investment fund offering attractive-rate loans to hotels/resorts for efficiency and renewable investments, replenished by contributions linked to savings.
source_quote:
The technical unit could also set up an investment fund that would help resorts and hotels doing the right

choice, providing loans at an attractive rate as an incentive to support the transition. Hotels and resorts having  benefited  from  subsidies  or  loans  from  the  fund  would  be  invited  to  replenish  this  fund  with  a contribution proportionate to the saving obtained through refurbishment operations.
extraction_rationale: Explicit financial instrument (investment fund providing loans) with a replenishment mechanism.

parent_statement: Tourism sector greening programme covering hotels/resorts, cruise fleet, land transport, and heritage-site lighting, supported by awareness and technical support units/funds.
policy_statement: Establish a 'Green boat refurbishment fund' to support upgrading cruise boats, potentially replenished by loans/subsidies recipients.
source_quote:
The Governorate of Luxor could facilitate the establishment of ' Green boat refurbishment fund ' that could be replenished by tourist operators benefiting from loans or subsidies to upgrade their boat.

Note that modern engines could dramatically reduce energy consumption.
extraction_rationale: Explicit financial mechanism (fund) tied to boat upgrades for energy savings/emissions reduction.

parent_statement: Tourism sector greening programme covering hotels/resorts, cruise fleet, land transport, and heritage-site lighting, supported by awareness and technical support units/funds.
policy_statement: Develop a 'Green dock programme' including solar PV at docks to supply docking boats and reduce diesel use when boats are not sailing.
source_quote:
The fleet improvement programme should extend to redesigning the docks to make them a demonstrative example of what a 'green harbour' on river Nile could be.

Obviously the new plans should promote solar PV equipment as a major source of renewable energy supply for all activities along the docks. Hence, renewable energy will supply docking boats avoiding unnecessary use of diesel motors when cruise boats and dhows are not sailing.
extraction_rationale: Specific infrastructure/renewable energy intervention explicitly aimed at reducing diesel use and improving sustainability.

policy_statement: Residential buildings programme combining awareness, solar water heating deployment, and building retrofitting to reduce energy use and emissions by 2030.
source_quote:
There  is  a  lot  to  do  to raise  public  awareness on  energy  issues,  inviting  inhabitants  to  reduce  their consumption and, as a consequence, cut their energy bill.

The most obvious plan to develop on the medium term is the promotion of Solar Heating System to produce hot sanitary water and avoid unnecessary electricity consumption.
extraction_rationale: A structured action package with defined measures and quantified assumptions/budgets later in the section.

parent_statement: Residential buildings programme combining awareness, solar water heating deployment, and building retrofitting to reduce energy use and emissions by 2030.
policy_statement: Run a residential energy awareness campaign promoting thermostat settings, efficient behaviours, and efficient appliances to reduce household electricity use.
source_quote:
Such awareness campaign to promote efficient behaviour should focus on few measures:

- -Promoting the proper temperature at home... Adjusting air conditioning systems' thermostats to be always at 24 degrees Celsius in summer would save up to 25 per cent of the energy consumption,
- -Promoting behavioural changes at home... and emphasises on buying green label appliances,
extraction_rationale: Specific behavioural intervention with concrete measures and quantified savings potential (up to 25%).

parent_statement: Residential buildings programme combining awareness, solar water heating deployment, and building retrofitting to reduce energy use and emissions by 2030.
policy_statement: Promote solar water heating (SWH) systems to replace electric water heating in households.
source_quote:
- -Promote the use of solar water heating (SWH) system instead of the current electric water heating (EWH) systems.

Currently, there is almost no use of solar water heating system in the city of Luxor and this action could tremendously reduce the electricity consumption for the specific need of hot sanitary water.
extraction_rationale: Specific technology substitution programme explicitly aimed at reducing electricity consumption.

parent_statement: Residential buildings programme combining awareness, solar water heating deployment, and building retrofitting to reduce energy use and emissions by 2030.
policy_statement: Develop a residential building renovation/retrofitting programme supported by third-party financing via a bank repaid from energy savings.
source_quote:
Develop a partnership with a bank acting as a 'third party investor' that will support the necessary investment to cover the cost of building' retrofitting.

The bank will recover the cost of the loan from a part of the savings allowed by the retrofitting programme, and
extraction_rationale: Defines a financing-enabled retrofit programme (third-party investor model) to deliver energy reductions; constitutes a concrete policy mechanism.

policy_statement: Implement tertiary-building actions including mapping energy use, awareness/training for entrepreneurs, and partnerships for showcases in schools, hospitals, mosques and churches.
source_quote:
It is necessary to add a first step to properly assess the need through a detailed mapping of tertiary buildings, (schools  and  religious  buildings),  registering  average  energy  consumption  per  square  meter,  date  of construction, location.

The Governorate should develop partnerships with some of these  'service  providers'  to  develop showcases of efficient building also using renewable energy,
extraction_rationale: Specific planned interventions (mapping, partnerships, showcases) to reduce energy use in tertiary buildings; quantified expected results and budgets are provided.

policy_statement: Industry actions: conduct energy audits and establish a 'Green Industry Unit' to support process efficiency, rooftop renewables, and waste reduction/recycling.
source_quote:
One practical option would be to develop energy audits for companies willing to address energy issues.

The 'Green Industry Unit' initially set up to offer services to Industry' operators could progressively expend its support to the service sector (tertiary buildings) and the industry.
extraction_rationale: Specific interventions (audits, creation of a technical unit) to drive energy efficiency and renewables in industry; constitutes a concrete policy approach.

policy_statement: Renewable energy development programme for Luxor including solar PV (public buildings and households), solar heating, biogas studies, and hydro prefeasibility along the Nile.
source_quote:
Following this route, the Governorate of Luxor will reduce its dependency on 'imported energy' and spark a new economy that will create jobs and generate revenues for local industries and people.

The plan would be to develop solar PV units in every possible place invited inhabitants to contribute to this development.
extraction_rationale: Defines a renewable energy development plan with multiple specific technologies and implementation mechanisms; includes budgets and studies.

parent_statement: Renewable energy development programme for Luxor including solar PV (public buildings and households), solar heating, biogas studies, and hydro prefeasibility along the Nile.
policy_statement: Partner with Terra Sola to deploy solar PV on Governorate buildings, symbolic buildings, parking lots/bus stations, and small-scale household units.
source_quote:
As Terra Sola also plans to establish a dedicated fund to developing and supporting small and medium-sized renewable  energy  projects  in  Luxor,  the  Governorate  of  Luxor  should  develop  a  partnership  with  this company targeting different objectives:

- -Develop solar PV units on all Governorate buildings...
- -Implement solar 'umbrella' on parking lots and bus stations...
- -Promote small scale units for households.
extraction_rationale: Specific partnership-based deployment actions for solar PV across multiple asset types; explicit renewable energy expansion.

parent_statement: Renewable energy development programme for Luxor including solar PV (public buildings and households), solar heating, biogas studies, and hydro prefeasibility along the Nile.
policy_statement: Create a revolving fund to support household and private-owner solar PV deployment.
source_quote:
The plan would be to develop solar PV units in every possible place invited inhabitants to contribute to this development.

The City of Luxor could set up a revolving fund to support this development.
section_header: 4.3. Renewable energy development — Solar PV for residents and private owners
extraction_rationale: Explicit financial instrument (revolving fund) to accelerate distributed solar PV adoption.

parent_statement: Renewable energy development programme for Luxor including solar PV (public buildings and households), solar heating, biogas studies, and hydro prefeasibility along the Nile.
policy_statement: Promote solar heating across sectors through awareness, needs identification, pilot projects, and local technician development.
extraction_rationale: Specific renewable heat programme with defined steps and pilots; supports decarbonisation of heat demand.

parent_statement: Renewable energy development programme for Luxor including solar PV (public buildings and households), solar heating, biogas studies, and hydro prefeasibility along the Nile.
policy_statement: Commission a comprehensive study on biogas potential from agricultural by-products and organic waste to design biodigester deployment and energy uses.
source_quote:
The Governorate of Luxor should command a comprehensive study to explore the benefit of such a technology in the surrounding of the City.

Such a pre-study would require an investment of 20.000 Euro that would be necessary before entering the detailed conception phase.
extraction_rationale: Specific commitment to commission a study with a stated budget to enable biogas deployment; concrete preparatory action.

parent_statement: Renewable energy development programme for Luxor including solar PV (public buildings and households), solar heating, biogas studies, and hydro prefeasibility along the Nile.
policy_statement: Conduct a 20,000 Euro prefeasibility study for hydro turbines along the Nile to assess applicability in Luxor.
source_quote:
It would be very interesting to check if this technology could be adapted in Luxor, for example with a barge equipped with such hydro turbine close to the bridge connecting Western and Eastern banks.

A  20.000  Euro  prefeasibility  study  could  give  enough  information  to  decide  if  the  Governorate of  Luxor should proceed with this technology or not.
section_header: 4.3. Renewable energy development — Hydro along the Nile River
extraction_rationale: Specific funded prefeasibility study commitment to evaluate renewable generation option.

policy_statement: Achieve a 26% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 compared to BAU through the SECAP action plan.
source_quote:
The current action plan will result in achieving a 26% reduction in GHG emission compared to the business as usual scenario in 2030, where emission would reach 2,270 ktCO2eq/ year.

Note that this plan reaches a reduction of 600 ktCO2eq/year in 2030 representing a reduction of 33% compare to the level of 2015 GHG emissions.
extraction_rationale: Quantified overall mitigation outcome for the plan with a deadline (2030) and BAU comparator; functions as the plan’s headline target.

policy_statement: Develop an early warning system to alert citizens in case of extreme weather events or natural disasters (heat waves, fires, floods).
source_quote:
Developing an early warning system, to alert citizens in the case of extreme weather events or natural disasters such as heat waves, fires, floods, etc. is vital.

This system needs to be set up as early as possible connecting with national monitoring centres to be able to transmit appropriate information as early as possible to citizen of Luxor.
section_header: 7.1. Public health and quality of life — Alert / Communication / Education
extraction_rationale: Specific adaptation measure (early warning system) explicitly tied to climate hazards; includes urgency and system design elements.

policy_statement: Improve sheltering capacities by improving air conditioning in public services to provide extreme heat protection and shelters during extreme events.
source_quote:
Improve sheltering capacities :  Improve air conditioning in public services (hospitals, city hall, etc.) using climate friendly options to offer appropriate extreme heat protection to those citizens that lack the infrastructure to protect themselves.

Such sites should also be considered as potential shelters when other type of extreme weather events will affect the more vulnerable groups (storms, floods).
section_header: 7.1. Public health and quality of life — Strategic actions
extraction_rationale: Concrete adaptation action focused on heat protection and sheltering during extreme events.

policy_statement: Establish underground water reservoirs and a flood control system to retain water during heavy rains and monitor Nile level and heavy rain occurrence.
source_quote:
Establish underground water reservoirs and develop a flood control system . Reservoirs are necessary to retain water in case of heavy rains.

Such reservoirs should be part of a flood control system that will monitor the Nile river level and occurrence of heavy rain.
extraction_rationale: Specific infrastructure adaptation measure addressing flood/heavy rain risks with defined functions.

policy_statement: Modify building codes to promote more energy efficient and heat tolerant structures (including demonstration of Nubian Vault techniques).
source_quote:
Modify the building codes to promote more energy efficient and heat tolerant structures.

The Nubian Vault is one these techniques only requiring mud and clay (no cement, no wood, and no iron) to elaborate on buildings that are particularly well adapted to hot regions.
section_header: 7.3. Land planning and building management — Strategic
extraction_rationale: Regulatory/planning commitment (modify building codes) explicitly linked to heat tolerance and energy efficiency; includes a concrete technique example.

policy_statement: Develop greening infrastructure (green roofs/walls, tree planting, fountains) to increase shade and reduce the heat island effect.
source_quote:
Develop greening infrastructure such as buildings' roofs and walls covered with greenery to increase the amount of shade and refresh the environment.

Likewise, developing green areas in the city by planting trees and building fountains will help reduce the heat island effect.
section_header: 7.3. Land planning and building management — Technical measures
extraction_rationale: Specific adaptation measures to address heat stress/urban heat island through urban greening.

policy_statement: Protect biodiversity by planting native species along the Nile, establishing/restoring riparian buffers, and preserving desert biodiversity.
source_quote:
Protect the biodiversity . This programme should include tree planning (using native species) alongside the  Nile  River  and  riverside  biodiversity  protection.

It  should  aim  to  establish  and  restore  riparian buffers.
section_header: 7.3. Land planning and building management — Technical measures
extraction_rationale: Concrete nature-based adaptation programme with specified actions (native species planting, riparian buffers).

policy_statement: Priority Action #1: Urban Sustainable Mobility Master Plan for Luxor (project fiche) to reduce transport energy use and GHG emissions.
source_quote:
The 'Urban Sustainable Mobility Master Plan' will be Luxor' strategic roadmap to improve mobility, while reducing energy consumption and GHG emissions from the highest emitting sector.

The aim of this master plan is to switch to green transport and mobility, including tourists' transports that currently use fossil fuel .
section_header: SECTION V: PROJECT FICHES — 1. Urban Sustainable Mobility Master Plan
extraction_rationale: Named priority action with defined objectives and implementation process; clearly mitigation-focused.

policy_statement: Priority Action #2: Sustainable and Green Boats—convert cruise boats and small passenger boats from diesel to CNG/LPG and add solar PV for onboard electricity.
source_quote:
The Sustainable and Green Boats (SGB) priority action, which is one component of the SGTP, consists mainly in converting all these boats using fossil fuel to operate with LPG (Liquid Petroleum Gaz) or CNG (Compressed natural gas) which are far cleaner than diesel and generate lessCO 2 emissions.

The ambition is to convert 110 cruise boats and 155 small passengers boats.
section_header: SECTION V: PROJECT FICHES — 2. Sustainable and Green Boats
extraction_rationale: Specific conversion programme with quantified targets (110 cruise boats, 155 small boats) and defined technology pathway; direct mitigation.

parent_statement: Priority Action #2: Sustainable and Green Boats—convert cruise boats and small passenger boats from diesel to CNG/LPG and add solar PV for onboard electricity.
policy_statement: Convert 110 cruise boats and 155 small passenger boats to operate with CNG.
source_quote:
The planned action is set through the following assessments and development:

- Implementing the plan to convert cruise boats and small passenger boats to operate with CNG, and

The ambition is to convert 110 cruise boats and 155 small passengers boats.
section_header: SECTION V: PROJECT FICHES — 2. Sustainable and Green Boats
extraction_rationale: Quantified conversion target and specific action (CNG conversion).

policy_statement: Priority Action #3: Green Residential Buildings Plan (GRP) combining LED replacement, solar water heating, solar PV, and retrofitting with revolving funds and awareness programmes.
source_quote:
The City of Luxor wants to move forward to holistically solve the challenges to be faced in the residential sector by adopting the 'Green Residential Plan' (GRP) promoting a sustainable approach in residential buildings combining energy efficiency and renewable energy development - solar PV and SWH systems.

The Green Residential Plan aims to reduce energy consumption and GHG emissions through an awareness programme to enhance users' behaviours on the saving toolsand methods and a major investment plan to improve building energy efficiency.
section_header: SECTION V: PROJECT FICHES — 3. Green Residential Buildings Plan
extraction_rationale: Named plan with defined measures and financing approach (revolving funds) and quantified deliverables/targets; direct relevance to mitigation via efficiency and renewables.

policy_statement: Priority Action #4: Greening Hotels and Resorts (Sustainable and Green Tourism Plan) including awareness, a management unit, and a revolving fund for solar water heating in hotels.
source_quote:
The Sustainable and Green Tourism Plan (SGTP) will focus on hotels and resorts to promote energy conservation, energy efficiency and develop renewable solutions to cover energy needs.

| Sustainable and Green Tourism Plan management unit (50 K€ /year)                     | 250,000 €   |
| Revolving fund for investment on SWH in hotels and resorts (on land) (20 hotels)     | 1,000,000 € |
section_header: SECTION V: PROJECT FICHES — 4. Greening Hotels and Resorts
extraction_rationale: Named priority action with explicit budget lines including a revolving fund (financial instrument) and management unit; targets energy efficiency and renewables in tourism.

policy_statement: Priority Action #5: Green Governorate Buildings Plan to reduce municipal building energy use and deploy solar PV and solar water heating.
source_quote:
The City of Luxor - Governorate of Luxor has the desire to move forward to holistically solve these challenges by promoting sustainable energy in Governorate (municipal) buildings in the city of Luxor through the development of a comprehensive plan to reduce energy consumption and consequently GHG emissions.

Also, the Governorate plan is to enhance energy efficiency in these municipal buildings by promoting renewable energy and incorporate SWH systems utilising solar energy and apply green measures such as LED lamps and sensors - 'Green Municipal Buildings Plan - GMBP.''
section_header: SECTION V: PROJECT FICHES — 5. Green Governorate Buildings Plan
extraction_rationale: Named plan with specific measures (LED/sensors, efficient AC, solar PV, SWH) and large investment budget; direct mitigation and efficiency.

policy_statement: Al-Qurna Priority Action #3: Install off-grid solar PV with batteries (starting with 40 kW) to replace diesel generators used for lighting heritage sites and reduce emissions/vibrations.
source_quote:
The main problem is in the redundant system to light the Kings Valley's tombs and the lower part of the mountain using two fossil fuel generators, of 150 kW and 160 kW respectively.

The project proposes a solar off-grid PV to allow for the usage of lithium batteries system to offer in its first phase 40 kW.
section_header: Annex 1. Al-Qurna, Governorate of Luxor, Study Report — 5.1.3. Solar PV for Heritage Sites
extraction_rationale: Specific renewable energy intervention with a defined initial capacity (40 kW) and clear mitigation purpose (replace diesel generators).

policy_statement: Al-Qurna Priority Action #4: Provide agricultural machinery (tractors, shredders, trailers) to stop burning sugarcane/banana residues and manage agricultural waste.
source_quote:
The problem is that instead of managing agricultural waste, farmers usually burn the pre-harvest sugarcane because it costs less than compiling and transporting.

To provide the department of agriculture in Luxor Governorate, MoAgr., with:
- 20 agricultural tractor,
- 20 shredder, and
section_header: Annex 1. Al-Qurna, Governorate of Luxor, Study Report — 5.1.4 Management of Agriculture waste
extraction_rationale: Specific equipment provision programme with clear objective (replace burning) and quantified inputs; direct mitigation via avoided burning emissions.

policy_statement: Al-Qurna Priority Action #2: Convert West Bank microbuses to natural gas and build parking lots with PV sheds to reduce emissions from tourist vehicles idling near heritage sites.
source_quote:
The project proposes the conversion of all the microbuses' engines on the West Bank, from diesel and gasoline into natural gas.

The proposed project suggests 2 parking lots (to be divided into 4 stages)... The parking will be designed with waiting areas for drivers to serve as a safe spot for parking, hence protecting the site and decreasing emissions.
section_header: Annex 1. Al-Qurna, Governorate of Luxor, Study Report — 5.1.2 Clear transportation on the west bank
extraction_rationale: Specific transport interventions (fuel switching and parking/management infrastructure) aimed at reducing emissions and protecting heritage sites.

policy_statement: Al-Qurna Priority Action #5: Establish an Environmental Public Awareness Unit to mobilize staff and the public on energy conservation/efficiency and environmental/heritage protection.
source_quote:
As municipality staff, population and local stakeholders lack information and need to be mobilised to act on energy conservation / efficiency, environmental protection and protection of Heritage and archaeological sites.

Luxor Governorate will set up a dedicated unit, focusing on raising awareness in different public audiences to optimise the impact of the measures proposed to reduce energy consumption and improve the quality of life and the protection of heritage and monuments in the city.
section_header: Annex 1. Al-Qurna, Governorate of Luxor, Study Report — 5.1.5. Environmental public awareness unit
extraction_rationale: Institutional commitment to create a dedicated awareness unit with defined objectives and target audiences; supports mitigation and adaptation behaviours.

policy_statement: Reduce Memphis-area greenhouse gas emissions below 2016 levels by 15% by 2020, 51% by 2035, and 71% by 2050.
source_quote: The Memphis area's greenhouse gas emissions for the baseline year of 2016 totaled 17,191,915 metric tons (MT) CO 2 e/year. The Climate Action Plan outlines how the Memphis area could reduce greenhouse gas emissions below 2016 levels 15% by 2020, 51% by 2035, and 71% by 2050.
extraction_rationale: Quantified, time-bound emissions-reduction targets (numbers + deadlines) constitute a clear mitigation policy commitment.

policy_statement: Set local government operations GHG reduction targets for buildings (20% by 2020, 55% by 2035, 80% by 2050) and fleet vehicles (15% by 2020, 45% by 2035, 80% by 2050).

section_header: LEADING BY EXAMPLE: LOCAL GOVERNMENT INVENTORY, REDUCTION TARGETS AND RECOMMENDATIONS
extraction_rationale: Explicit quantified targets for government operations emissions reductions; qualifies as a target-setting policy.

policy_statement: Achieve economywide greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reductions of 40% by 2030 and 85% by 2050 from 1990 levels, putting New York on a path toward carbon neutrality.
source_quote: This Scoping Plan includes recommendations to meet the Climate Act's nation-leading goals and requirements, including actions to achieve a reduction in economywide greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions of 40% by 2030 and 85% by 2050 from 1990 levels, which will put New York on a path toward carbon neutrality while ensuring equity, system reliability, and a just transition from a fossil fuel economy to a robust clean energy economy.
extraction_rationale: Quantified, time-bound statewide emissions targets established as requirements/goals under the Climate Act and reiterated as Scoping Plan commitments.

policy_statement: Achieve 70% renewable electricity by 2030 and 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040.
source_quote: It identifies actions needed for New York to achieve 70% renewable electricity by 2030, 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040, a 40% reduction in statewide GHG emissions from 1990 levels by 2030, an 85% reduction in statewide GHG emissions from 1990 levels by 2050, and net zero emissions statewide by 2050.
extraction_rationale: Explicit, time-bound clean electricity targets; core mitigation policy directives.

policy_statement: Achieve net zero emissions statewide by 2050.
source_quote: It identifies actions needed for New York to achieve 70% renewable electricity by 2030, 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040, a 40% reduction in statewide GHG emissions from 1990 levels by 2030, an 85% reduction in statewide GHG emissions from 1990 levels by 2050, and net zero emissions statewide by 2050.
extraction_rationale: Explicit statewide net-zero target with deadline; direct mitigation commitment.

policy_statement: Ensure Disadvantaged Communities receive at least 35% (goal 40%) of benefits of spending on clean energy and energy efficiency programs, projects, or investments.
source_quote: The Climate Act requires that Disadvantaged Communities receive a minimum of 35%, with a goal of 40%, of the benefits of spending on clean energy and energy efficiency programs, projects, or investments in the areas of housing, workforce development, pollution reduction, low-income energy assistance, energy, transportation, and economic development.
extraction_rationale: Binding distributional requirement for program benefits; climate-justice implementation rule tied to climate spending.

policy_statement: DEC will draft and promulgate enforceable regulations by January 1, 2024 to ensure the State meets statewide GHG emission limits (40% by 2030; 85% by 2050).
source_quote: DEC will have until January 1, 2024, to draft and promulgate enforceable regulations to ensure that the State meets the Climate Act's statewide GHG emission limits (i.e., 40% reduction in Statewide GHG emissions by 2030 and 85% reduction by 2050, both from 1990 levels) as outlined in the Scoping Plan.
extraction_rationale: Time-bound regulatory mandate to implement emissions limits; binding mechanism.

policy_statement: PSC will issue a comprehensive review of the renewable energy program by July 1, 2024 and every two years thereafter, including progress toward 70% renewable electricity by 2030 and 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040 and related procurement targets.
source_quote: By July 1, 2024, and every two years thereafter, the PSC will issue a comprehensive review of the renewable energy program, including progress in meeting the overall targets for 70% renewable electricity by 2030 and 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040. This review will also include a progress update on the programs the PSC has established to require procurement of 9 GW of offshore wind by 2035, 6 GW of solar PV by 2025, and 3 GW of energy storage by 2030.
extraction_rationale: Recurring reporting/review requirement with specified scope and deadlines; governance mechanism supporting mitigation targets.

policy_statement: Adopt regulations requiring all new passenger cars, pickup trucks, and SUVs sold in New York State be zero-emission by 2035.
source_quote: Governor Hochul directed DEC to adopt regulations that will require all new passenger cars, pickup trucks, and SUVs sold in New York State be zero-emission by 2035 and be modeled on California's Advanced Clean Cars II regulation finalized in 2022.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies — Regulatory Action
extraction_rationale: Binding regulatory requirement with deadline; direct transportation mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Implement Advanced Clean Trucks regulation incorporating California's zero-emission standards for medium- and heavy-duty trucks and large entity reporting requirements.
source_quote: Advanced Clean Trucks (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 218 Regulation), adopted in 2021, incorporated California's Advanced Clean Truck zero-emission vehicle standards for MHD trucks as well as large entity reporting requirements for owners and operators of MHD trucks as part of New York's existing low emission vehicle program.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies — Regulatory Action
extraction_rationale: Adopted regulation mandating ZEV standards and reporting; direct mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Adopt oil and natural gas sector regulations to lower methane and VOC emissions from sources in New York's oil and natural gas sector.
source_quote: Oil and Natural Gas Sector regulations (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 203 Regulations), adopted and effective in 2022 to support the goals and requirements of the Climate Act, lowers methane and volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions for sources in New York's oil and natural gas sector.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies — Regulatory Action
extraction_rationale: Binding regulation targeting methane reductions; direct mitigation.

policy_statement: Prohibit specific hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) in certain end uses and require standards and reporting under DEC Part 494.
source_quote: Hydrofluorocarbon Standards and Reporting (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 494 Regulations) prohibits specific HFCs, potent GHGs in certain refrigerants, aerosol propellants, and foam-blowing agent end uses that represent avoidable HFC emissions where safer alternatives are available.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies — Regulatory Action
extraction_rationale: Regulatory prohibition of high-GWP gases; direct mitigation.

policy_statement: Require large generators of food scraps to donate excess edible food and recycle remaining food scraps if within 25 miles of an organics recycler.
source_quote: Food Donation and Food Scraps Recycling (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 350 Regulations), adopted in 2022 pursuant to ECL Article 27, Title 22, requires large generators of food scraps to donate excess edible food and to recycle all remaining food scraps if they are located within 25 miles of an organics recycler, which will reduce methane and VOC emissions in support of the goals and requirements of the Climate Act.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies — Regulatory Action
extraction_rationale: Binding regulation with specific requirements; direct methane mitigation from waste.

policy_statement: Establish statewide GHG emission limits for 2030 and 2050 under 6 NYCRR Part 496 (2030 limit equals 60% of 1990 levels; 2050 equals 15% of 1990 levels).
source_quote: DEC promulgated 6 NYCRR Part 496 that established the two statewide GHG emission limits called for in the Climate Act: a limit for 2030 that is equal to 60% of 1990 GHG emission levels and a limit for 2050 that is equal to 15% of 1990 emission levels.
section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation — Key Milestones and Implementation Steps To-Date
extraction_rationale: Promulgated regulation establishing enforceable statewide limits; direct mitigation.

policy_statement: Publish an annual statewide GHG emissions report as DEC and NYSERDA update the inventory.

section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation — Key Milestones and Implementation Steps To-Date
extraction_rationale: Ongoing reporting commitment required for tracking compliance; governance mechanism supporting climate policy.

policy_statement: Use Value of Carbon guidance to incorporate a monetary value for avoided GHG emissions in State agency decision-making.
source_quote: Further, DEC, in consultation with NYSERDA, established the Value of Carbon guidance to help State agency decision-making by placing a monetary value for the avoided emissions of GHGs. The Value of Carbon guidance provides metrics that may be broadly applicable to actions by all State agencies and authorities-such as benefit-cost analyses, rulemaking processes, environmental assessments, and demonstrations of the benefits of climate change policies-to demonstrate the global societal value of actions to reduce GHG emissions.
section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation — Key Milestones and Implementation Steps To-Date
extraction_rationale: Formal guidance instrument directing how agencies evaluate climate impacts; direct climate relevance though not a spending line itself.

policy_statement: Implement a two-year moratorium on certain permits for cryptocurrency mining operations using behind-the-meter electricity and proof-of-work methods, and prepare a GEIS on this mining type.

This law directs DEC, in consultation with the New York State Department of Public Service (DPS), to prepare a generic environmental impact statement on this type of cryptocurrency mining operation.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies — Legislation
extraction_rationale: Binding legislative moratorium and required environmental review; indirect climate mitigation via limiting high-emissions electricity use.

policy_statement: Require PSC to develop a regulatory structure for utility thermal energy networks and direct utilities to launch pilot projects.

section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies — Legislation
extraction_rationale: Legislated regulatory mandate and pilots enabling building decarbonization; direct climate relevance.

policy_statement: Commit to a statewide dashboard of community GHG emission inventories to promote local planning, monitor equity, measure progress, and ensure data consistency.
source_quote: Establish Statewide Dashboard of Community GHG Emission Inventories: This strategy calls for a dashboard that would promote local climate action planning, monitor equity considerations, measure progress, and ensure data consistency at the county and municipal levels.
extraction_rationale: Specific named intervention (dashboard) to support climate action measurement; not emissions-reducing itself but enables implementation.

policy_statement: Develop model above-minimum energy conservation codes and construction policies to accelerate local energy efficiency with a focus on equity.

extraction_rationale: Concrete policy tool (model codes/policies) aimed at accelerating efficiency; indirect climate relevance but substantial.

policy_statement: Implement statewide community air monitoring in Disadvantaged Communities and develop strategies by June 1, 2024 to reduce toxic and criteria air pollutants in Disadvantaged Communities.

section_header: Buildings — Adopt Zero-Emission Codes and Standards and Require Energy Benchmarking for Buildings:

extraction_rationale: Clear commitment to regulatory action plus supporting programs; direct mitigation of high-GWP gases.

policy_statement: Meet Climate Act electricity build targets: 6,000 MW distributed solar by 2025, 3,000 MW energy storage by 2030, and 9,000 MW offshore wind by 2035.

extraction_rationale: Quantified deployment targets tied to achieving emission limits; direct mitigation and efficiency pathway.

This will give New Zealanders the regional and local climate projections data they need to assess future climate risk and make adaptation decisions.

By January 2023, national climate projection datasets for Aotearoa are being produced.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.1: Provide access to the latest climate projections data
extraction_rationale: This is a specific, time-bound government-led intervention (producing and providing datasets by a stated date) to enable adaptation decision-making; it is not merely descriptive background.

policy_statement: Establish a platform for Māori climate action to resource Tiriti partnership, support a national Māori climate strategy/action plan, and fund kaupapa Māori climate solutions.
source_quote:
“The platform will build on three focus areas:
- embed partnership and representation - to uphold Te Tiriti principles, processes and mechanisms will be resourced and designed alongside Māori to help tangata whenua to actively participate in the climate response
- support Māori-led strategy and alignment - to elevate te ao Māori within the climate response, Māori will be supported to define, measure and implement a national Māori climate strategy and action plan
- activate kaupapa Māori, tangata Māori solutions - to enable community action, kaupapa Māori, tangata Māori actions and solutions for the climate emergency will be funded.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.3: Establish a platform for Māori climate action
