source_quote:
“3.7.2: Produce adaptation guidance for central government policy makers

A methodology for central government to ensure it considers adaptation in new policy and services. This will avoid increased exposure or vulnerability to climate impacts.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.7.2
extraction_rationale: A concrete deliverable (methodology) intended to change government policy practice to reduce climate vulnerability.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance for decision makers to assess and manage climate risks.
policy_statement: Produce guidance for dynamic adaptive pathways planning (DAPP) for central and local government to plan under uncertain climate futures.
source_quote:
“3.7.3: Produce guidance for dynamic adaptive pathways planning (DAPP)

A guide for central and local government on how to plan for adaptation in a context of uncertain climate futures.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.7.3
extraction_rationale: Specific guidance to operationalise an adaptation planning method under uncertainty.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance for decision makers to assess and manage climate risks.
policy_statement: Produce guidance on using socio-economic scenarios in adaptation planning for government and businesses.
source_quote:
“3.7.4: Produce guidance on using different socio-economic scenarios for adaptation planning

Assists central and local government and businesses to consider future socio-economic scenarios when assessing climate risks, and planning how to manage them.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.7.4
extraction_rationale: A defined guidance output to improve climate risk assessment and planning.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance for decision makers to assess and manage climate risks.
policy_statement: Regularly update adaptation guidance for local government, including guidance on communicating technical information and making climate decisions.
source_quote:
“3.7.5: Regularly update adaptation guidance for local government

Supports local government to consider adaptation in planning and decisions. This will include guidance on communicating scientific and technical information to communities, and on making climate decisions.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.7.5
extraction_rationale: Ongoing guidance updates are a concrete government support intervention for local adaptation decision-making.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance for decision makers to assess and manage climate risks.
policy_statement: Produce guidance on integrating mātauranga Māori into adaptive planning and working with mana whenua.
source_quote:
“3.7.6: Produce guidance on integrating mātauranga Māori into adaptive planning and working with mana whenua

Helps central and local government effectively engage with hapū, iwi and Māori when managing risk and planning for adaptation.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.7.6
extraction_rationale: A specific guidance deliverable to improve adaptation planning processes with Māori partnership.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance for decision makers to assess and manage climate risks.
policy_statement: Produce guidance for preparing adaptation plans using a standard approach under uncertainty.
source_quote:
“3.7.7: Produce guidance for preparing adaptation plans

Enables communities and different audiences, sectors and levels of government to produce their own adaptation plans, using a standard approach under conditions of uncertainty in climate projections.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.7.7
extraction_rationale: Concrete guidance product enabling adaptation planning across audiences.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance for decision makers to assess and manage climate risks.
policy_statement: Regularly update the guide to local climate change risk assessments on a six-yearly cycle after each national risk assessment.
source_quote:
“3.7.8: Regularly update the guide to local climate change risk assessments

Sets out a step-by-step process for local risk assessments. It will be updated on a six-yearly cycle after the release of each national climate change risk assessment.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.7.8
extraction_rationale: A defined recurring update commitment tied to the national risk assessment cycle.

policy_statement: Develop and publish guidance for infrastructure asset owners to assess climate risks and impacts on physical assets and services by 2026.
source_quote:
“Te Waihanga will scope and deliver guidance for asset owners to evaluate risks to their physical assets and the services they provide. This will help them understand, and subsequently manage, the impacts of climate change on existing and new assets.

By 2026, the guidance will be published.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.8: Develop guidance for assessing risk and impact on physical assets and the services they provide
extraction_rationale: This is a specific deliverable (published guidance by a date) intended to change infrastructure risk management practice for climate impacts.

policy_statement: Assess socioeconomic and climate vulnerability for Māori by collecting and analysing social data against climate data to target resilience support.
source_quote: “This action will collect and analyse social data against climate data to determine where support for resilience is most needed. This will enable the Government to better understand what support is needed to strengthen resilience for Māori communities.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.10: Assess socioeconomic and climate vulnerability for Māori
extraction_rationale: A defined analytical programme to inform targeted adaptation support; it is an actionable commitment rather than general intent.

policy_statement: Implement the National Disaster Resilience Strategy by designing a pathway to give effect to its vision, goals and objectives.
source_quote: “The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) will design a pathway to give effect to the National Disaster Resilience Strategy's vision, goals and objectives. The vision is for a disaster-resilient nation that acts proactively to manage risks and to build resilience in a way that contributes to the wellbeing and prosperity of all.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.11: Implement the National Disaster Resilience Strategy
extraction_rationale: This is a government implementation commitment for a named strategy focused on proactive risk management and resilience, relevant to climate-exacerbated hazards.

policy_statement: Improve how science, data, mātauranga Māori and knowledge inform emergency management decisions via NEMA’s Science Strategy framework.
source_quote: “The National Emergency Management Agency 's 2021 Science Strategy will be used to create a framework for scientific engagement, promotion and influence for risk reduction, readiness, response and recovery. Research, data, mātauranga Māori, local knowledge and technical expertise will inform strategic decisions on emergency management, and explore practical interventions to improve disaster resilience.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.12: Improve how science, data and knowledge are used to inform emergency management
extraction_rationale: A concrete institutional framework commitment to improve risk reduction and resilience decision-making, including climate-related hazards.

policy_statement: Provide a forestry planning and advisory service offering data-informed tools and advice, including where land may need restoration/regeneration or retirement from forestry.
source_quote: “The forestry planning and advisory service will help to reduce climate risks by providing data-informed advice and planning tools. Advice will be on both harvest and non-harvest forestry for example, to help decision makers consider where land is available for new forestry; where restoration, regeneration and reversion may be needed; and where unsuitable land may need to be retired from forestry, including conversion from plantation to indigenous forestry.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.13: Provide a forestry planning and advisory service
extraction_rationale: A specific service intervention with defined advisory functions to reduce climate risks in land/forestry management.

policy_statement: Deliver the Integrated Farm Planning Programme to provide a framework enabling farmers/growers to meet regulatory and business needs (including greenhouse gases) within a single planning framework.
source_quote: “The Integrated Farm Planning Programme will provide a framework for farmers and growers to incorporate all their key farming areas, including greenhouse gases, into their farm planning. The goal is to enable a farmer or grower, using their preferred data-collection tool, platform or system, to meet all regulatory and business needs within a single framework.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.14: Deliver the Integrated Farm Planning Programme
extraction_rationale: A defined programme with a clear intervention (integrated planning framework) that explicitly includes climate considerations and supports adaptation planning in primary industries.

policy_statement: Improve consumer understanding of property insurance pricing and climate risks through information sheets linked to hazard disclosure work.
source_quote: “Information sheets will help consumers identify, manage or even reduce their climate risks. This links to the work on Land Information Memoranda (LIMs), as greater disclosure can help people make better decisions on where to buy and build property.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.16: Improve consumer understanding of property insurance pricing and risks
extraction_rationale: A specific informational intervention aimed at enabling climate risk management decisions in housing/insurance.

policy_statement: Support integration of climate adaptation and mitigation considerations in new and revised standards commissioned by third parties.
source_quote: “At the beginning of each relevant project, Standards NZ may bring adaptation and mitigation to the attention of the committee members of a standard it has commissioned. This may help improve resilience in existing and new assets, by guiding industry practice in asset design and operation.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.17: Support and promote the integration of climate adaptation and mitigation in new and revised standards commissioned by third parties
extraction_rationale: A defined institutional practice to influence standards-setting toward adaptation/mitigation outcomes; somewhat discretionary (“may”) but still a stated action programme.

policy_statement: Review electricity and gas networks’ management of climate risk and resilience by amending asset management plan requirements and publishing reviews.
source_quote: “The Commission is currently consulting on amending the asset management plan requirements for electricity distributors so that sector stakeholders can better understand distributors' risk management, including managing network resilience challenges posed by climate change. From time to time, the Commission will publish reviews of aspects of regulated networks' plans, to support them to improve their approach to managing risk and building adaptive capacity, and to provide more confidence that their related expenditure forecasts are robust.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.18: Review electricity and gas networks' management of climate risk and resilience
extraction_rationale: A regulatory oversight action with concrete mechanisms (amending requirements; publishing reviews) to improve climate resilience of networks.

policy_statement: Develop mātauranga Māori indicators of climate impacts on the natural environment to support monitoring, baselines and environmental assessments.
source_quote: “Mātauranga Māori indicators will enable monitoring and evaluation of impacts on biodiversity, mahinga kai, flora, fauna and human health. This will create data baselines that centralise indigenous knowledge and values, and can be used in environmental assessments.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.21: Develop mātauranga Māori indicators of climate impacts on the natural environment
extraction_rationale: A proposed but specific programme deliverable (indicators/baselines) to monitor climate impacts, supporting adaptation decisions.

policy_statement: Work with community housing providers to improve data on climate risk exposure and implement an action programme to increase community housing resilience.
source_quote:
“This will provide better data and information on the exposure of community housing providers to climate risks. An action programme will increase the resilience of community housing by supporting strategies for emergency management and long-term adaptation.

In turn, this will reduce exposure of community housing tenants to climate risks.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.22: Work with community housing providers to enable effective climate hazard response
extraction_rationale: A defined proposed programme with clear outputs (data, action programme) to reduce housing exposure to climate hazards.

policy_statement: Develop 3D coastal mapping to assess sea-level rise impacts and model tsunami and storm surge impacts on communities, infrastructure and biodiversity.
source_quote: “Coastal mapping comprises detailed 3D mapping of the coastal zone and the upgrade and addition of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) sites in the coastal zone. The purpose is to assess the impacts of sea-level rise and model the impacts of tsunami and storm surges on communities, infrastructure and biodiversity.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.23: Develop 3D coastal mapping
extraction_rationale: A specific proposed data/mapping intervention to support hazard modelling and adaptation planning.

policy_statement: Design a methodology for climate risk assessments of public buildings to support owners’ adaptation strategies.
source_quote:
“Developing a methodology for risk assessment based on the property resilience research (see action 5.7: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings), to address matters such as cultural and heritage values and seismic hazard risks, will support decision-making.

This will help owners of public buildings assess and understand climate risks and implement adaptation strategies.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.25: Design methodology for risk assessments of public buildings
extraction_rationale: A concrete proposed methodological tool to enable adaptation decisions for public buildings.

policy_statement: Produce guidance for disaster risk management for cultural heritage to reduce risks before, during and after disasters.
source_quote: “This action will improve disaster risk management for cultural heritage through guidance on reducing risks before, during and after disasters.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.26: Produce guidance for disaster risk management for cultural heritage
extraction_rationale: A specific guidance commitment for protecting cultural heritage from climate-exacerbated disasters.

policy_statement: Develop a framework to assess exposure and vulnerability of taonga/cultural assets to climate change.
source_quote: “It will develop a framework to identify valued cultural heritage and the actual and potential exposure and vulnerability of cultural heritage to climate change. The framework will take a broad and inclusive approach, recognising the ways in which different communities identify, access and participate in what is culturally important to them.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.27: Develop a framework for assessing exposure and vulnerability of taonga/cultural assets to climate change
extraction_rationale: A defined proposed framework to assess climate vulnerability of cultural assets, enabling adaptation planning.

policy_statement: Assess healthcare service resilience to climate events to ensure continued access to healthcare services under climate adversity.
source_quote: “The aim of this action is to understand the healthcare service's vulnerability to climate events, and consider physical risks to infrastructure, and changes in illness patterns and vulnerability. This will help to ensure communities can continue to access the healthcare services they need, even in the face of climate change adversity.”
section_header: Chapter 3: Enabling better risk-informed decisions — Action 3.28: Assess healthcare service resilience
extraction_rationale: A concrete assessment action to support health-sector adaptation and continuity of services.

policy_statement: Repeal and replace the Resource Management Act with new legislation (Natural and Built Environments Act, Spatial Planning Act, Climate Adaptation Act) to better prepare for climate adaptation and natural hazard risk, with Acts expected to pass in 2023.
source_quote:
“In early 2021, the Government announced its intention to repeal the Resource Management Act 1991 and replace it with a Natural and Built Environments Act, a Spatial Planning Act and a Climate Adaptation Act.

In 2023, the Natural and Built Environments Act and the Spatial Planning Act are expected to be passed.”
section_header: Chapter 4: Driving climate-resilient development in the right locations — Action 4.1: Reform the resource management system
extraction_rationale: This is a major legislative reform programme with explicit climate adaptation objectives and a stated legislative timeline.

policy_statement: Set national direction on natural hazard risk management and climate adaptation through the National Planning Framework, including hazard risk assessment methodologies, with draft released after the Natural and Built Environments Act is passed.
source_quote:
“The National Planning Framework will set clear direction for local authorities on how to achieve the climate resilience outcomes in the Natural and Built Environments Act. It will set out methods and requirements for planning for natural hazards and considering future climate risks.

The draft National Planning Framework will be released for consultation shortly after the Natural and Built Environments Act is passed.”
section_header: Chapter 4: Driving climate-resilient development in the right locations — Action 4.2: Set national direction on natural hazard risk management and climate adaptation through the National Planning Framework
extraction_rationale: A concrete national planning instrument with defined content and process milestone, intended to guide local adaptation decisions.

policy_statement: Establish an initiative for resilient public housing by developing and using a decision-making framework by 2024 to determine adaptation actions for new and existing public housing assets.
source_quote:
“A framework for public housing assets will be developed to determine the actions to adapt new and existing assets. This will help reduce exposure of public housing tenants to climate hazards.

By 2024, a decision-making framework will be in use to determine adaptation actions for both new and existing assets.”
section_header: Chapter 4: Driving climate-resilient development in the right locations — Action 4.3: Establish an initiative for resilient public housing
extraction_rationale: A specific programme with a defined tool (framework) and deadline for operational use, targeting reduced hazard exposure.

policy_statement: Embed adaptation in housing and urban development funding models (including Māori housing) by updating programmes to consider climate hazard costs and reviewing/amending programmes by 2024.
source_quote:
“Existing funding programmes for urban development and housing, including Māori housing, will be updated to consider the costs of existing and future climate hazards. New funding programmes may be created if there are gaps.

By 2024, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) will have begun reviewing funding programmes it administers and amending them to appropriately consider climate-related risk.”
section_header: Chapter 4: Driving climate-resilient development in the right locations — Action 4.4: Embed adaptation in funding models for housing and urban development, including Māori housing
extraction_rationale: This is a funding-model reform commitment (resource allocation mechanism) with a timeline, directly aimed at integrating climate risk into investment decisions.

policy_statement: Reform institutional arrangements for water services by creating new water entities with statutory objectives including sustainable and resilient delivery that seeks to mitigate effects of climate change and natural hazards, with legislation enacted by 2024.
source_quote:
“By 2024, legislation to establish water services entities will be enacted (to enable them to become operational from 1 July 2024).

If the Bill is enacted in its current form, one of the statutory objectives of the new entities will be to 'deliver water services in a sustainable and resilient manner that seeks to mitigate the effects of climate change and natural hazards'.”
section_header: Chapter 4: Driving climate-resilient development in the right locations — Action 4.5: Reform institutional arrangements for water services
extraction_rationale: A legislative/institutional reform with explicit statutory climate resilience objective and a clear enactment timeline.

policy_statement: Integrate climate risk and adaptation into Treasury investment guidance for infrastructure, including full lifecycle adaptation costs and options to build adaptive capacity, with advice and decisions completed by 2024.
source_quote:
“The Treasury publishes a range of guidance for central government departments and other entities on investment management and state sector performance. It will integrate consideration of climate risks and future adaptation into this guidance.

By 2024, advice on the best way forward, and any associated budget bid or Cabinet decisions, will be complete and future implementation measures defined.”
section_header: Chapter 4: Driving climate-resilient development in the right locations — Action 4.6: Integrate adaptation into Treasury decisions on infrastructure
extraction_rationale: A concrete change to central government investment decision frameworks with a defined completion date for advice/decisions.

policy_statement: Integrate adaptation into Waka Kotahi’s investment decision-making and the National Land Transport Programme by 2024.
source_quote:
“Waka Kotahi will incorporate adaptation in the Investment Decision Making Framework, its structured approach to decisions on investment in land transport. This will include business case development and risk assessment.

By 2024, Waka Kotahi will integrate adaptation into planning, investment and decision-making for the National Land Transport Programme.”
section_header: Chapter 4: Driving climate-resilient development in the right locations — Action 4.7: Integrate adaptation into Waka Kotahi decision-making
extraction_rationale: A specific operational/planning change with a deadline, embedding climate adaptation into transport investment decisions.

policy_statement: Pass legislation to support managed retreat by introducing a Climate Adaptation Bill with a managed retreat framework by end of 2023.
source_quote:
“The Government will develop legislation to address the complex technical, legal and financial issues associated with managed retreat as described by the Resource Management Review Panel. This legislation is being progressed through the development of the Climate Adaptation Act.

By the end of 2023, the Government is expecting to introduce the Climate Adaptation Bill, setting out the managed retreat framework.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.1: Pass legislation to support managed retreat
extraction_rationale: A binding legislative commitment with a clear deadline to establish a managed retreat framework—core adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Conduct the Future for Local Government review to recommend changes to local government roles and funding/financing to support agile, sustainable, proactive adaptation decision-making, with final report mid-2023.
source_quote:
“Adaptation will bring new challenges and opportunities to local governance. The system must be equipped for agile, sustainable and proactive decision-making and implementation.

In mid-2023, the Local Government Review Panel will provide the Minister of Local Government with its final report and recommendations for improving the local governance system.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.2: The Future for Local Government review
extraction_rationale: A formal review process with a defined output and date, explicitly framed as necessary for adaptation governance and financing.

policy_statement: Complete a case study exploring co-investment models for flood resilience in Westport, including receiving a strategic business case on flood resilience options.
source_quote:
“The Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) is working with the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), the West Coast Regional Council, the Buller District Council and local iwi to explore options to increase flood resilience in Westport.

In June 2022, ministers will receive a strategic business case from the Buller District Council and West Coast Regional Council on a package of flood resilience options to reduce flood risk in Westport.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.3: Complete case study to explore co-investment for flood resilience
extraction_rationale: A specific, time-bound government-led analytical/pilot action to develop adaptation investment approaches for flooding.

policy_statement: Develop options to support access and affordability of home flood insurance, with advice and next steps agreed by end of 2022.
source_quote:
“This work includes exploring options to support access and affordability of flood insurance. The Government intends to develop options that ensure home flood insurance continues to play an appropriate role in supporting community resilience.

By the end of 2022, the Government will have received advice on flood insurance options and agreed to next steps.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.4: Develop options for home flood insurance
extraction_rationale: A concrete policy development commitment with a deadline, aimed at maintaining insurance as an adaptation/resilience mechanism.

policy_statement: Publish a programme of work (via a dedicated webpage) on how Aotearoa meets climate change costs and invests in resilience by end of 2022.
source_quote:
“It will communicate how this range of work is progressing across government in one place. A dedicated webpage will be kept up to date as work evolves and new actions are developed.

By the end of 2022, a dedicated webpage will be established to provide an update in one place on the range of work progressing across government.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.5: Publish the programme of work on how Aotearoa meets the costs of climate change and invests in resilience
extraction_rationale: A specific transparency/coordination deliverable with a deadline, tied to adaptation financing and investment in resilience.

policy_statement: Scope a resilience standard or code for infrastructure, including assessing costs/benefits and whether it should be mandatory or voluntary, with stakeholder feedback received by 2024.
source_quote:
“Te Waihanga will scope the impact (including of costs, benefits and regulations) of a standard or code for resilient infrastructure.

By 2024, stakeholder feedback on a resilience standard or code will have been received.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.6: Scope a resilience standard or code for infrastructure
extraction_rationale: A defined standards-development scoping action with a timeline, aimed at risk reduction and resilience planning in infrastructure.

policy_statement: Reduce and manage climate hazard impacts on homes and buildings through research, guidance, assessment frameworks, and investigating incentives, with data available by August 2024 to inform frameworks and regulatory updates.
source_quote:
“This action includes five components that build off one another and are necessary to inform regulatory change and other actions in this chapter. These five components are:
- collate existing information to help people adapt their homes and buildings
- carry out research to understand the impacts of climate hazards on various housing typologies, and the costs and benefits of adaptation at the property level
- develop property-level guidance based on updated climate data to inform homeowners and renters about climate impacts and their options to respond to risks
- develop an assessment framework to help building owners, developers and new home builders identify relevant climate hazards and understand their building's adaptation requirements
- investigate incentives that could help building owners to increase their building's resilience.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.7: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings
extraction_rationale: A multi-component, specific intervention programme explicitly intended to inform regulatory change and incentives; it is more than aspirational.

policy_statement: Support kaitiaki communities (hapū, iwi and Māori) to adapt and conserve taonga/cultural assets through advice, wānanga, expert assistance, information sharing and funding advice, beginning improvements by 2024.
source_quote:
“Support includes advice, wānanga (conferences, forums, seminars), expert assistance, information sharing and funding advice for kaitiaki to self-determine adaptation pathways.

By 2024, the Ministry for Culture and Heritage (MCH) will have started working with relevant partners on how improvements can be made to support and access to information on cultural assets to assist kaitiaki to self-determine adaptation pathways.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.8: Support kaitiaki communities to adapt and conserve taonga/cultural assets
extraction_rationale: A defined support programme with a timeline for initiating improvements, aimed at adaptation of cultural assets.

policy_statement: Prioritise nature-based solutions in planning and regulations for carbon removals and climate adaptation, with a framework developed by 2024.
source_quote:
“To address the climate and biodiversity crises together, the Government will prioritise nature-based solutions in planning and regulations, where possible, for both carbon removals and climate change adaptation. It will also investigate how to best ensure that climate change policy and planning use a biodiversity lens to prioritise nature-based solutions.

By 2024, a framework will be developed, and prioritising of nature-based solutions in regulations and planning will be underway and future implementation measures confirmed.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.9: Prioritise nature-based solutions
extraction_rationale: A clear government commitment with a deliverable (framework) and implementation pathway (planning/regulatory prioritisation).

policy_statement: Develop and implement the Transpower Adaptation Plan for the national grid, addressing exposed assets and new investment and considering multiple climate hazards.
source_quote:
“The Transpower Adaptation Plan will outline how Transpower will adapt to climate change through the design, delivery and operation of the national grid. It will address exposed assets and new investment in infrastructure, and consider adaptation in maintenance and development programmes.

Transpower will consider multiple risks to the national grid from climate hazards, including coastal inundation, increased frequency of high-impact flood and wind events, and accelerated erosion.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.10: Develop and implement the Transpower Adaptation Plan
extraction_rationale: A named plan with defined scope and mechanisms for adapting critical infrastructure to climate hazards.

policy_statement: Encourage and support evaluation of climate risks to landfills and contaminated sites using a council tool.
source_quote:
“Coastal inundation and flooding could be a significant risk to existing and closed landfills and contaminated sites across the country. At least 110 closed landfills are vulnerable to sea-level rise.

The Ministry for the Environment (MfE) has helped councils develop a tool to evaluate climate risks for landfills and contaminated sites.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.11: Encourage and support the evaluation of climate risks to landfills and contaminated sites
extraction_rationale: A concrete tool-based intervention to enable risk assessment and planning for climate impacts on waste infrastructure.

policy_statement: Explore funding options to support investigation and remediation of contaminated sites and landfills vulnerable to climate change impacts.
source_quote:
“Considering this, the Government has agreed to consider how best to support the funding of remediation.

Access to funding will help to turn risk assessment into risk reduction, and ensure remediation occurs before inundation risks become a reality.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.12: Explore funding options to support the investigation and remediation of contaminated sites and landfills vulnerable to the effects of climate change
extraction_rationale: A funding-policy exploration commitment explicitly tied to climate risk reduction; while options are not specified, it is a deliberate resource-allocation mechanism under consideration.

policy_statement: Connect communities to integrated disaster response and recovery support through locally led, regionally coordinated, nationally supported networks.
source_quote: “This action will continue work with central and local government, communities (including rural communities), iwi, organisations and others to support effective, integrated disaster response and recovery. Communities affected by disasters will be assisted by networks that are locally led, regionally coordinated and nationally supported.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.13: Connect communities to wider response and recovery support
extraction_rationale: A defined operational commitment to strengthen response/recovery systems relevant to climate-driven disasters.

policy_statement: Support development of a green taxonomy/definitional tools to encourage investment in climate- and nature-positive projects and reduce greenwashing.
source_quote: “This will support the development of a 'green' taxonomy to identify a common definition of climate and naturepositive investments. This could help guide businesses that are investing in both adaptation and mitigation to protect against greenwashing.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.14: Support the development of definitional tools to encourage greater investment in 'green' projects
extraction_rationale: A specific policy tool development (taxonomy) intended to steer investment toward resilient/low-emissions projects.

policy_statement: Use public finance instruments (CERF and Sovereign Green Bonds) to support climate objectives, including considering extending CERF to adaptation in future Budgets and issuing Green Bonds from 2022 onwards.
source_quote:
“This includes the establishment of the Climate Emergency Response Fund (CERF) and the Sovereign Green Bond (Green Bond) programme.

In Budget 2022, the CERF was focused on the emissions reduction plan. However, for future Budgets the Government will consider extending the scope of the CERF to fund measures to support climate change adaptation.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.15: Public investment in climate change initiatives
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit public investment/financing policy instrument (fund and bonds) with stated intent to potentially fund adaptation measures.

policy_statement: Identify options to integrate nature-based solutions into urban form (eg, street trees, green roofs, waterways) to reduce flooding and heatwave impacts and address equity.
source_quote:
“This work will build on indigenous knowledge and new research to produce new data and insights on nature-based solutions such as vegetation (eg, street trees and green roofs) and water elements (eg, open canals and waterways). This includes understanding barriers and identifying ways to accelerate nature-based solutions through changes to urban form and development.

This action will help reduce the impact of climate events, such as flooding and heatwaves, in our urban areas to improve outcomes for people, communities and biodiversity.”
section_header: Chapter 5: Adaptation options including managed retreat — Action 5.16: Identify options to increase the integration of nature-based solutions into urban form
extraction_rationale: A proposed but specific work programme to accelerate NBS in urban development explicitly for hazard impact reduction (flooding/heatwaves).

policy_statement: Implement the Department of Conservation Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan to assess ecosystem/species vulnerability and undertake actions (eg, translocation, pest control), with reporting framework by 2024.
source_quote:
“The plan aims to assess ecosystem and species vulnerability to climate impacts, and the adaptation actions to enhance their resilience. Possible actions include translocating climatevulnerable species, and pest control to improve the resilience of native ecosystems.

By 2024, a reporting framework on the implementation of the CCAAP will be in place.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.1: Implement the Department of Conservation Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan
extraction_rationale: A named plan with concrete adaptation measures and a reporting framework deadline.

policy_statement: Engage with councils to implement the New Zealand Coastal Policy Statement and review progress by 2024.
source_quote:
“The NZCPS provides the policy mechanism for protecting indigenous biodiversity in the coastal environment, and for managing risks to coastal ecosystems (policies 11, and 24-27 NZCPS). The NZCPS's coastal hazard management mechanisms include managed retreat and nature-based solutions.

By 2024, DOC will review progress on NZCPS implementation by councils.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.2: Engage with councils to implement the New Zealand Coastal Policy Statement
extraction_rationale: A concrete engagement and review commitment tied to implementing an existing policy instrument that includes adaptation mechanisms.

policy_statement: Implement Te Mana o te Taiao – Aotearoa New Zealand Biodiversity Strategy 2020, including establishing collaborative structures and launching a second implementation plan by 2024.
source_quote:
“Te Mana o te Taiao - Aotearoa New Zealand Biodiversity Strategy 2020 (ANZBS) is a strategic document for the protection, restoration and sustainable use of biodiversity in Aotearoa from 2020 to 2050.

By 2024, the collaborative structures and channels into the biodiversity sector will be established and the second implementation plan will be launched.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.3: Implement Te Mana o te Taiao - Aotearoa New Zealand Biodiversity Strategy 2020
extraction_rationale: A named strategy implementation commitment with a time-bound milestone; biodiversity resilience is explicitly linked to climate in the strategy description.

policy_statement: Implement the proposed National Policy Statement on Indigenous Biodiversity, with NPS-IB in force by 2024 and implementation begun.
source_quote:
“The objective of the NPS-IB is to protect, maintain and restore indigenous biodiversity.

By 2024, the NPS-IB will be in force and implementation will have begun.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.4: Implement the proposed National Policy Statement on Indigenous Biodiversity
extraction_rationale: A regulatory instrument commitment with a clear in-force date; explicitly framed as contributing to biodiversity resilience to climate change.

policy_statement: Implement the Water Availability and Security programme to help food and fibre businesses and rural communities adapt to variable water availability through demand reduction and best use of water, partnering with Māori and rural communities.
source_quote:
“The Water Availability and Security programme will help food and fibre businesses and rural communities adapt to increasingly variable natural water availability through a range of complementary activities to both reduce demand and make best use of available water.

By 2024, the Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) will form a permanent team to address water availability and security in the food and fibre sectors and rural communities.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.6: Implement the Water Availability and Security programme
extraction_rationale: A defined programme with a structural commitment (permanent team by 2024) and explicit adaptation mechanism for water variability.

policy_statement: Implement the National Policy Statement on Freshwater Management 2020, requiring councils to notify plans by 2024 to ensure healthy freshwater ecosystems and mitigate negative land-use impacts.
source_quote:
“The National Policy Statement on Freshwater Management 2020 (NPS-FM 2020) applies to all freshwater, including groundwater, and will require management of freshwater in both rural and urban areas.

By 2024, regional councils will notify plans implementing the NPS-FM 2020.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.7: Implement the National Policy Statement on Freshwater Management 2020
extraction_rationale: A regulatory implementation commitment with a deadline for council plans; supports freshwater resilience under climate change.

policy_statement: Deliver a collection of Biosecurity New Zealand actions to protect indigenous ecosystems and economy from invasive species under climate change.
source_quote: “The following actions address risks to indigenous ecosystems and species that result from the greater spread, survival and establishment of invasive species. They also help build climate resilience of ecosystems generally.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.8: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella initiative explicitly followed by numbered sub-actions (6.8.1–6.8.8), so it is extracted as a parent policy.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of Biosecurity New Zealand actions to protect indigenous ecosystems and economy from invasive species under climate change.
policy_statement: Implement an on-farm biosecurity programme to improve voluntary biosecurity practices on dairy and sheep/beef farms, measuring behaviour changes by mid-2023.
source_quote:
“This programme aims to improve biosecurity on dairy and sheep and beef farms and create a more resilient biosecurity system. It is responsible for developing and implementing an action plan to overcome barriers and increase voluntary on-farm biosecurity practices.

By mid-2023, changes will have been measured in the four core behaviours (talk about biosecurity, show leadership, be curious to understand the risks, and make choices recognition and reinforcement) to track programme impact against objectives.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.8.1: Implement an on-farm biosecurity programme
extraction_rationale: A specific programme with measurable milestone to strengthen resilience to climate-driven pest/disease risks.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of Biosecurity New Zealand actions to protect indigenous ecosystems and economy from invasive species under climate change.
policy_statement: Invest in strengthening border biosecurity via Sea Cargo and Mail Pathways projects to identify pest species arriving at international borders.
source_quote: “Two significant projects (Sea Cargo Programme and Mail Pathways Project) delivered by Biosecurity New Zealand will improve how we address the biosecurity risk from mail and sea cargo pathways. They will also protect biodiversity by identifying pest species that arrive through our international borders.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.8.2: Invest in strengthening border biosecurity
extraction_rationale: A specific investment/project commitment to reduce invasive species risks exacerbated by climate change.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of Biosecurity New Zealand actions to protect indigenous ecosystems and economy from invasive species under climate change.
policy_statement: Continue the Freshwater Biosecurity Partnership Programme, including updated strategy by 2024 and improved detection/control tools and targeted campaigns.
source_quote:
“The programme will include a focus on supporting the development of effective early-detection and control tools. It will also improve access to information about the distribution of freshwater pests, enabling the Check Clean Dry campaign to be targeted to the highest-risk locations, activities and distribution pathways.

By 2024, development and implementation of an updated Freshwater Biosecurity Partnership Programme strategy will be completed, which includes more support for collaboration on developing new or improved detection and control tools.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.8.3: Continue the Freshwater Biosecurity Partnership Programme
extraction_rationale: A defined programme continuation with a time-bound strategy update and explicit climate-related vulnerability rationale.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of Biosecurity New Zealand actions to protect indigenous ecosystems and economy from invasive species under climate change.
policy_statement: Implement the Clean Hull programme to reduce spread and impacts of marine pests via domestic vessel movements, with design and baseline by 2024.
source_quote:
“This involves implementing a behaviour change programme to address the risks of marine pest spread via domestic vessel movements.

By 2024, the Clean Hull programme will be designed, and a baseline established of awareness of risks from vessel movements and current behaviours of vessel owners.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.8.4: Reduce the spread and impacts of marine pest species through the Clean Hull programme
extraction_rationale: A specific programme with a design/baseline milestone to address climate-amplified marine pest risks.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of Biosecurity New Zealand actions to protect indigenous ecosystems and economy from invasive species under climate change.
policy_statement: Prevent spread of wilding conifers and contain/eradicate established areas by 2030, protecting 4 million hectares by 2024 through control efforts.
source_quote:
“Established in 2016, this programme ensures a collaborative, coordinated and effective national approach to wilding conifer control.

By 2024, the programme will protect 4 million hectares of land that is significantly vulnerable to invasion by controlling wilding conifer infestations.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.8.5: Prevent the spread of wilding conifers, and contain or eradicate established areas of wilding conifers by 2030
extraction_rationale: A quantified target and timeline for invasive species control with explicit resilience co-benefits (fire risk, water availability, biodiversity).

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of Biosecurity New Zealand actions to protect indigenous ecosystems and economy from invasive species under climate change.
policy_statement: Continue the National Interest Pest Responses programme and complete technical reviews of each species control programme by 2024.
source_quote:
“Nine harmful weeds are managed under the National Interest Pest Responses (NIPR) programme, with the aim of eradicating them or significantly reducing infestations.

By 2024, a technical review of each of the National Interest Pest Responses species control programmes will be completed.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.8.6: Continue the National Interest Pest Responses programme
extraction_rationale: A defined programme with a time-bound review deliverable supporting ecosystem resilience under changing climate conditions.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of Biosecurity New Zealand actions to protect indigenous ecosystems and economy from invasive species under climate change.
policy_statement: Invest in a plant health and environmental capability facility, submitting a detailed business case for Cabinet approval in November 2022.
source_quote:
“Significant investment in Ministry for Primary Industry (MPI) plant health and environment work (currently in Tāmaki, Auckland) will support growth and development in the arable, forestry and horticulture sectors.

In November 2022, a detailed business case is submitted for Cabinet approval.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.8.7: Invest in plant health and environmental capability facility
extraction_rationale: A specific investment initiative with a concrete milestone (business case submission) to improve resilience to pests/diseases under climate change.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of Biosecurity New Zealand actions to protect indigenous ecosystems and economy from invasive species under climate change.
policy_statement: Enhance diagnostic capabilities of national reference laboratories for new/suspected pests and diseases by January 2024 through operational research and collaboration.
source_quote:
“They bring a better understanding of new and emerging pests and diseases that are likely to establish in a changing climate.

By January 2024, the diagnostic capabilities to manage new and suspected exotic pests and diseases through an operational research programme and collaboration with internal and international organisations will be enhanced.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.8.8: Use the Animal Health Laboratory and Plant Health and Environment Laboratory
extraction_rationale: A time-bound capability enhancement commitment supporting early detection/response to climate-driven biosecurity risks.

policy_statement: Implement the Sustainable Land Management Hill Country Erosion Programme to support regional planning and treatment of erosion-prone land and contribute to afforestation.
source_quote:
“The Sustainable Land Management Hill Country Erosion Programme will support regional planning for, and treatment of, erosion-prone land and, in turn, contribute to afforestation.

Afforestation can reduce soil loss and other effects from the increasing scale and magnitude of storms.”
section_header: Chapter 6: Natural environment — Action 6.12: Implement the Sustainable Land Management Hill Country Erosion Programme
extraction_rationale: A defined programme linking land treatment/afforestation to reduced storm/erosion impacts; qualifies as adaptation with explicit intervention.

policy_statement: Partner with Māori landowners to develop resources/tools to understand climate risks and increase resilience of housing on Māori land and cultural sites.
source_quote: “This work will be progressed in partnership with Māori landowners to produce resources and tools to improve understanding of climate-related risks and increase the resilience of housing on Māori land. It will promote mātauranga Māori and increase the resilience of Māori-owned land, homes and cultural sites.”
section_header: Chapter 7: Homes, buildings and places — Action 7.2: Partner with Māori landowners to increase the resilience of Māori-owned land, homes and cultural sites
extraction_rationale: A proposed but specific partnership programme with defined outputs (resources/tools) to increase resilience of Māori housing and sites.

policy_statement: Update Building Code and related requirements using forward-looking climate data to ensure buildings withstand more extreme climate hazards, including adding hazards not currently covered.
source_quote:
“Updated forward-looking climate data and modelling (action 3.2: Design and develop risk and resilience and climate adaptation information portals) will be used to:
- update Building Code performance requirements
- identify and add climate hazards not currently in the Building Code
- produce guidance and tools to help people meet new performance requirements.”
section_header: Chapter 7: Homes, buildings and places — Action 7.4: Update regulatory requirements to ensure buildings are designed and constructed to withstand more extreme climate hazards
extraction_rationale: A concrete regulatory update programme specifying mechanisms (Building Code updates; adding hazards; guidance/tools).

policy_statement: Review and update housing and urban strategies/programmes/regulations to ensure they are fit for a changing climate and consider extreme events and tenancy/housing quality rules.
source_quote:
“Current strategies, programmes and regulations will be reviewed to ensure housing and urban environments are fit for the changing climate. For example, this could lead to updated requirements for homeowners and landlords, or for public and community housing.

This action will help ensure the built environment is designed and planned to cope with extreme events and the changing climate.”
section_header: Chapter 7: Homes, buildings and places — Action 7.5: Update housing and urban settings
extraction_rationale: A proposed but specific regulatory/programmatic review commitment aimed at climate resilience of housing and urban environments.

policy_statement: Develop and implement the Waka Kotahi Climate Adaptation Plan for land transport, including a reporting framework by 2024.
source_quote:
“In 2022, Waka Kotahi will publish and begin applying an adaptation plan. This will outline how Waka Kotahi will adapt to climate change through the design, delivery, operation and use of the land transport system.

By 2024, a reporting framework on the implementation of the adaptation plan will be developed.”
section_header: Chapter 8: Infrastructure — Action 8.1: Develop and implement the Waka Kotahi Climate Adaptation Plan
extraction_rationale: A named plan with implementation and reporting commitments to adapt transport infrastructure to climate hazards.

policy_statement: Develop a National Energy Strategy by end of 2024, with a vision for a net-zero economy in 2050 and pathways away from fossil fuels.
source_quote:
“The Government has committed to developing an energy strategy by the end of 2024, fully collaborating and engaging with Māori and working with energy system stakeholders. The vision is for a net-zero economy in 2050, where energy is accessible and affordable, secure and reliable, and supports New Zealanders' wellbeing.

The strategy addresses challenges in the energy sector and signals pathways away from fossil fuels.”
section_header: Chapter 8: Infrastructure — Action 8.2: Develop the National Energy Strategy
extraction_rationale: A time-bound strategy commitment with explicit net-zero and fossil-fuel transition elements (mitigation) and energy security framing.

policy_statement: Manage dry-year risk through the New Zealand Battery Project, completing feasibility study by end of 2022 to increase electricity system resilience in low inflow periods.
source_quote:
“The New Zealand Battery Project will assess the options for managing dry-year risk in a highly renewable electricity system. The current focus is on the feasibility of pumped hydroelectricity at Lake Onslow. The feasibility study will be completed by the end of 2022.

The aim is to increase the resilience of the electricity system when hydro lakes have low inflows for long periods.”
section_header: Chapter 8: Infrastructure — Action 8.3: Manage dry-year risk through the New Zealand Battery Project
extraction_rationale: A specific project with a clear deliverable date (feasibility study) and explicit resilience objective.

policy_statement: Adjust regulated electricity and gas network revenue settings to reflect prudent and efficient resilience costs to climate change in upcoming price-quality path reviews.
source_quote: “In the Commerce Commission's next reviews of regulated price-quality paths - from 2025 for electricity networks and from 2026 for gas networks - it will consider the extent to which revenue limits should provide for different expenditure levels from the current period. This will include if expenditure levels need to change due to any increased costs of resilience to climate change, where these are based on robust forecasts.”
section_header: Chapter 8: Infrastructure — Action 8.4: Provide for regulated network revenues to reflect the prudent and efficient costs of resilience
extraction_rationale: A regulatory financial mechanism (revenue limits) explicitly incorporating climate resilience costs with specified review years.

policy_statement: Progress the Rail Network Investment Programme to restore the rail network to a resilient and reliable state, with climate change mitigation a key focus in resilience investments.
source_quote:
“KiwiRail's Rail Network Investment Programme (RNIP) is a 10-year programme of investment in Aotearoa New Zealand's rail network, to restore it to a resilient and reliable state. Mitigating climate change is a key focus within the RNIP when considering resilience projects for investment.

Restoration of the national rail network to a reliable and resilient state will also reduce its vulnerability to climate hazards and provide a platform for future investment to support growth.”
section_header: Chapter 8: Infrastructure — Action 8.5: Progress the Rail Network Investment Programme
extraction_rationale: A defined investment programme with explicit resilience and mitigation focus; qualifies as policy due to named programme and investment framing.

policy_statement: Invest in public transport and active transport to increase transport system resilience, improve equity, support sustainable growth, and reduce emissions.
source_quote:
“Investment in multi-modal infrastructure can increase the resilience of the transport system and help manage the vulnerability of existing assets. More use of public transport and active modes will help reduce reliance on private vehicles.

Safe and attractive alternatives to driving create a more resilient transport system, support sustainable growth and reduce emissions.”
section_header: Chapter 8: Infrastructure — Action 8.6: Invest in public transport and active transport
extraction_rationale: A stated investment commitment with explicit adaptation (resilience) and mitigation (reduce emissions) outcomes.

policy_statement: Embed nature-based solutions in transport policy and investment to reduce transport emissions and improve climate adaptation and biodiversity outcomes, including protecting carbon sinks and supporting sequestration opportunities.
source_quote:
“At a local, regional and national scale these measures can reduce transport emissions and improve climate adaptation as well as biodiversity. Key initiatives include:
- considering the role of nature-based solutions in reducing transport emissions and contributing to other benefits
- ensuring transport policy and investment encourage nature-based solutions, including protecting existing carbon sinks and supporting new long-term carbon sequestration opportunities.”
section_header: Chapter 8: Infrastructure — Action 8.7: Embed nature-based solutions as part of the response to reducing transport emissions and improving climate adaptation and biodiversity outcomes
extraction_rationale: A concrete policy direction to integrate NBS into transport decisions with explicit emissions and adaptation outcomes.

policy_statement: Modernise the emergency management system through legislative reforms and improved guidance, adopting new legislation and a national emergency management plan by 2024.
source_quote:
“The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) plans to modernise emergency management, including through legislative reforms, working with communities and organisations, clearer roles and responsibilities, and a strengthened partnership with Māori.

By 2024, new emergency management legislation will be adopted, and a national emergency management plan and improved guidance will be provided across the emergency management system.”
section_header: Chapter 9: Communities — Action 9.1: Modernise the emergency management system
extraction_rationale: A concrete legislative and system reform commitment with a deadline, relevant to climate-driven hazard frequency/severity.

policy_statement: Develop the Health National Adaptation Plan by end of 2022 and develop regional climate health action plans from 2023.
source_quote:
“The aim of the HNAP is to prepare the health sector to meet the needs of communities in terms of the effects of climate change, including physical, mental and cultural health and wellbeing.

By the end of 2022, the HNAP is expected to be completed. From 2023, regional climate health action plans will be developed.”
section_header: Chapter 9: Communities — Action 9.2: Develop the Health National Adaptation Plan
extraction_rationale: A named plan with explicit climate-health adaptation purpose and clear deadlines for completion and follow-on regional plans.

policy_statement: Implement the Climate Migration Action Plan, including commissioning research on Pacific climate migration trends and using development cooperation funds to support a Pacific regional approach to climate mobility.
source_quote:
“One of the key actions is commissioning research to improve understanding of Pacific climate migration trends and the impact on communities in the Pacific and Aotearoa. The other main actions focus on using international development cooperation funds for Pacific Island countries.

This will support a Pacific regional approach to climate mobility, and advance Aotearoa and Pacific interests in the international context.”
section_header: Chapter 9: Communities — Action 9.4: Implement the Climate Migration Action Plan
extraction_rationale: A defined plan implementation with specific actions (research; funding use) addressing climate displacement impacts.

policy_statement: Strengthen teaching and learning related to climate change by supporting schools and kura to include climate understanding and responses in local curricula.
source_quote:
“It will support early learning services, schools and kura to include understanding of, and responses to, climate change in their local curricula and marau ā-kura (living, breathing curriculum), as well as learning that is important for social cohesion.

The aim is to support all children and young people to grow as lifelong learners who are connected to the environment and their communities, and actively involved in a sustainable future.”
section_header: Chapter 9: Communities — Action 9.7: Strengthen teaching and learning related to climate change
extraction_rationale: A concrete education-sector action to embed climate understanding and responses, supporting adaptive capacity.

policy_statement: Expand funding for proactive community resilience via decentralised Whānau Ora funding to support long-term resilience plans.
source_quote:
“This will seek to expand funding for Māori to build their community resilience through the COVID-19 pandemic, and plug funding gaps for communities to carry out their long-term resilience plans.

Funding would be decentralised by expanding the scope of funds provided through Whānau Ora.”
section_header: Chapter 9: Communities — Action 9.9: Expand current funding for proactive community resilience
extraction_rationale: A proposed funding expansion (financial instrument) explicitly aimed at building community resilience/adaptive capacity.

policy_statement: Implement an income insurance scheme proposal to support workers’ adaptive capacity, with potential legislation in 2022 and operation in 2024/25 if adopted.
source_quote:
“If a decision is made to introduce the proposed scheme, the Government would introduce legislation in 2022 and the scheme would start operating in 2024/25.

This policy would reduce the economic impacts of a changing climate on workers and communities by, for example, cushioning the impact of a large employer closing or resizing in a small town or region, and enabling workers to transition to new job opportunities afforded by changes in the economy.”
section_header: Chapter 9: Communities — Action 9.10: Implement an income insurance scheme to support adaptive capacity of communities and the economy
extraction_rationale: A proposed but specific social insurance policy with legislative/operational timelines and explicit climate-related rationale.

policy_statement: Deliver the New Zealand Freight and Supply Chain Strategy, launching by mid-2023, incorporating climate adaptation through a resilience outcome.
source_quote:
“This strategy will present a long-term and system-wide view of the freight system. Climate adaptation is being considered through the resilience outcome, to ensure Aotearoa New Zealand's freight and supply chain system is resilient, reliable and prepared for disruption.

By the middle of 2023, the Government will have launched the New Zealand Freight and Supply Chain strategy.”
section_header: Chapter 10: Economy and financial system — Action 10.1: Deliver the New Zealand Freight and Supply Chain strategy
extraction_rationale: A named strategy with a launch deadline and explicit climate adaptation integration for system resilience.

policy_statement: Pass the Fisheries Amendment Bill to strengthen and modernise fisheries management, enabling agile catch limit adjustments responsive to climate-driven stock changes by late 2022.
source_quote:
“The Bill also allows for more agile and streamlined decisions in response to changes in fish stock abundance, by enabling development of the pre-set decision rules.

By late 2022, the Fisheries Amendment Bill will be passed.”
section_header: Chapter 10: Economy and financial system — Action 10.2: Strengthen fisheries rules
extraction_rationale: A legislative reform with a deadline and explicit mechanism to respond to climate impacts on fish stocks.

policy_statement: Deliver the Aquaculture Strategy to support sustainable, innovative aquaculture and adaptation to climate change, including forecasting effects and resilience actions, with ongoing implementation plans and annual reporting by 2024.
source_quote:
“The Government's Aquaculture Strategy sets objectives and actions to support Aotearoa in becoming a world leader in sustainable and innovative aquaculture. One of the strategy's objectives is to support the industry to adapt to climate change.

By 2024, the Government will continue releasing implementation plans for the Aquaculture Strategy and reporting each year on the environmental effects of aquaculture.”
section_header: Chapter 10: Economy and financial system — Action 10.3: Deliver the Aquaculture Strategy
extraction_rationale: A named strategy with explicit climate adaptation objective and defined reporting/implementation commitments.

policy_statement: RBNZ to introduce climate-related stress tests, integrate climate into supervision, and develop risk management guidance, with increased integration by March 2024.
source_quote:
“The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) is taking action to help regulated financial entities identify and manage climate risks better. This includes:
- introducing climate-related stress tests that model the effect of severe but plausible scenarios on the balance sheets of regulated financial institutions
- incorporating climate change in scheduled supervisor engagements with the management and boards of regulated entities
- developing guidance on managing risk for the entities the RBNZ regulates.

By March 2024, the RBNZ will have climate change considerations increasingly integrated into its supervisory, stress-testing and policy work.”
section_header: Chapter 10: Economy and financial system — Action 10.4: Reserve Bank of New Zealand supports the stability of the financial system
extraction_rationale: A concrete set of supervisory and analytical interventions with a timeline, directly targeting climate-related financial stability risks.

policy_statement: Deliver the Sustainable Food and Fibre Futures Fund by co-investing in innovative primary-sector projects addressing climate change risks.
source_quote: “The Sustainable Food and Fibre (SFF) Futures Fund supports innovative projects that design and test new approaches and solutions to risks such as climate change in the primary sector. The fund supports innovation in Aotearoa New Zealand's food and fibre sector by co-investing in initiatives that bring economic, environmental and social benefits for all New Zealanders.”
section_header: Chapter 10: Economy and financial system — Action 10.7: Continue delivering the Sustainable Food and Fibre Futures Fund
extraction_rationale: A co-investment fund is a financial instrument with explicit climate-risk focus in the primary sector.

policy_statement: Establish innovation grants to boost private-sector R&D and accelerate climate-focused innovation for adaptation and low-emissions transition.
source_quote:
“These grants will boost investment in private sector research and development and support innovation. They will share the risk with Aotearoa companies.

This means more climatefocused innovation should happen faster, to better enable adaptation action and the transition to a low-emissions economy.”
section_header: Chapter 10: Economy and financial system — Action 10.8: Establish innovation grants
extraction_rationale: A grant programme (financial instrument) explicitly intended to accelerate climate-focused innovation for adaptation and mitigation.

policy_statement: Monitor residential insurance premiums and insurance uptake to understand shifts in availability and affordability.
source_quote: “Monitoring residential premiums and uptake of insurance gives a better understanding of the scale of shifts in insurance availability and affordability.”
section_header: Chapter 10: Economy and financial system — Action 10.10: Monitor residential insurance premiums
extraction_rationale: A specific monitoring commitment supporting adaptation policy on insurance retreat/affordability; somewhat narrow but still a defined government action.

policy_statement: Review the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy settings to ensure visitors contribute to resilient, adaptable infrastructure and the natural environment.
source_quote:
“The Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), directed by the Minister of Tourism, is reviewing the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL). This includes ensuring international visitors contribute to resilient, adaptable infrastructure and the natural environment they use during their visit.

This action will support a focus on the spending priorities of the IVL, as well as any further work across the life of the national adaptation plan (eg, other tools) to support adaptation and climate resilience in tourism.”
section_header: Chapter 10: Economy and financial system — Action 10.15: Review the settings for the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy
extraction_rationale: A levy review is a fiscal instrument affecting funding priorities for resilience; explicit adaptation rationale is stated.

policy_statement: Leverage government procurement policy to enable mitigation and adaptation in government investments, including resilient buildings/infrastructure and reduced emissions and waste.
source_quote: “This action will check the current government's procurement policy framework enables mitigation and adaptation in government investments. The greatest opportunity will likely be in construction contracts, making buildings and infrastructure resilient to a changing climate, and reducing carbon emissions and waste.”
section_header: Chapter 10: Economy and financial system — Action 10.16: Leverage government procurement for climate outcomes
extraction_rationale: A concrete policy review/action to align procurement with climate outcomes; includes explicit mitigation and adaptation mechanisms.

policy_statement: Establish central government oversight and coordination for implementing the national adaptation plan, including annual agency reporting commencing in 2023.
source_quote:
“This will provide transparency of implementation of the plan across government, improve coordination within central government and enable accountability.

Annual reporting requirements by agencies will be completed each year, commencing in 2023.”
section_header: Chapter 11: Implementing the plan — Action 11.1: Establish central government oversight and coordination for implementing the national adaptation plan
extraction_rationale: A governance/implementation policy with defined accountability mechanism (annual reporting) and start date.

policy_statement: Reduce Italy's greenhouse gas emissions by 6.5% compared to 1990 levels under the EU burden-sharing agreement.
source_quote:
The ratification law prescribes that:

1. Italy's greenhouse gas emissions should be reduced by 6.5%, compared to 1990 levels, as agreed under the European 'burden sharing' adopted by the European Union on 4 th March 2002;
extraction_rationale: Quantified national mitigation target anchored in ratification law and EU burden-sharing; clear baseline and percentage reduction.

policy_statement: Allocate 25 million Euro per year (2002–2004) to support pilot projects for energy efficiency, clean fuels/engines, and increasing carbon sinks.

policy_statement: Allocate 68 million Euro per year by 2003 to support developing-country projects that reduce GHG emissions and promote adaptation to climate change impacts.

extraction_rationale: Explicit international climate finance allocation; includes both mitigation and adaptation objectives.

policy_statement: Adopt and implement a National Action Plan to reduce greenhouse gas emissions (CIPE, 19 December 2002) to implement Kyoto ratification law guidelines.
source_quote: The third National Communication of Italy to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change is based on the National Action Plan to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, adopted by the Interministerial Committee for Economic Planning on 19 th December 2002. The National Action Plan is directed to implement the guidelines included in the Kyoto Protocol ratification law.
extraction_rationale: Named plan adopted by CIPE with explicit purpose to implement Kyoto law; constitutes a policy framework commitment though details are elsewhere.

policy_statement: Agreement Protocol (Turin, 5 June 2001) by Regions and Autonomous Provinces to coordinate policies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

that their various policies shall be oriented, to the greatest extent possible, towards the reduction of greenhouse gases;

that initiatives and financing, both Central-State and local, shall be coordinated for the priority objective of sustainability;

that optimal strategies for the reduction of greenhouse gases shall be formulated as part of the Plans for the Safeguarding and Reclamation of Air Quality;

extraction_rationale: Time-bound planning deliverable with specified priorities; includes explicit efficiency mechanism and renewables.

extraction_rationale: Binding structural reform and fuel-switch mandate with quantified capacities; mitigation via lower-carbon generation.

policy_statement: Implement Ministry of Industry decrees (24 April 2001) to increase end-use energy efficiency.
source_quote: Decrees  of  the  Ministry  of  Industry  of  24  April 2001 to increase end-use energy efficiency;

policy_statement: Provide 41% tax deductibility for building retrofitting expenses, including renewable-energy-based plants (Law 449/97).

policy_statement: Exempt 300,000 tonnes/year of biodiesel from excise duties (Law 388/2000, art. 21).

extraction_rationale: Explicit fiscal exemption with quantity cap; supports low-carbon fuels.

policy_statement: Increase renewable electricity use to a total of 75 TWh by 2010 (reference scenario).

the 'reference scenario' includes the implementation  of  programmes...

policy_statement: Adopt a National Climate Research Plan as a component of the National Research Plan.
source_quote: Italy has adopted a National Climate Research Plan through the joint efforts of the Ministry for the Environment  and  Territory  and  the  Ministry  for Education, University and Research, which is a component of the National Research Plan.
extraction_rationale: Named plan adopted by ministries; policy commitment to organize climate research (capacity-building).
