extraction_rationale: Formal deliberation establishing an action plan; although informational, it specifies concrete program elements and governance intent.

policy_statement: Introduce a carbon tax (Law 448/98) with revenues usable for subsidies supporting emissions reductions, energy efficiency, and renewable energy; planned increases 1999–2005 were frozen at 1999 levels.
source_quote:
Law  448/98 ,  which  introduced  the  carbon  tax, mentioned that the Government would be able to draw on a portion of the resulting revenues for use as compensation for the measures taken in the different sectors and as subsidies for the reduction of emissions, for the promotion of energy efficiency and for the development of renewable sources.

The carbon-tax, for that matter, was supposed to have been gradually increased between 1999 and 2005;  instead, on account of the high price of oil, it was frozen at the 1999 levels.
extraction_rationale: Explicit fiscal instrument (carbon tax) with stated use of revenues for climate-related subsidies; includes implementation detail (freeze).

policy_statement: Law 120/2002 requires the Ministry for the Environment and Territory to present by 30 September 2002 a national action plan to reduce GHG emissions and increase removals.
source_quote: Law no. 120 of 1 June 2002, passed in ratification of the Kyoto Protocol... establishes  that  the  Ministry  for  the Environment  and  Territoryshall  present  within  30 September 2002 to the Interministerial Committee for Economic  Planning,  a  national  action  plan  for  the reduction  of  greenhouse  gas  emission  levels  and increase of their removals.
section_header: 4.1 Summary of planned aimed measures almed at  of  achieving  the  objectives  of  the  Kyoto Protocol
extraction_rationale: Binding legal requirement with deadline and deliverable (national action plan) covering mitigation and sinks.

policy_statement: Voluntary agreement with ENEL commits to reduce CO2 emissions by 20% by 2006.
source_quote: The most important step has been the signing of a voluntary agreement on 20 July 2000 by the Ministry of the Environment, the Ministry of Production Activities and ENEL, with the latter, Italy's leading producer of electricity, voluntarily  committing  itself  to  reduce  its  emissions  of CO2 (by  -20%  within  2006).
section_header: 2.5.4.5 Indicators for the generation of electricity
extraction_rationale: Specific voluntary agreement with quantified target and deadline; clear mitigation commitment.

policy_statement: Implement a 2% renewable electricity obligation starting in 2002, with compliance via green certificates issued by GRTN (Legislative Decree 79/1999, art. 11).
source_quote: Article 11 of Legislative Decree no. 79 of 16 March 1999 on the liberalisation  of  the  electricity  industry  stipulates that,  starting  in  2002,  producers  and  importers  are required  to  supply  to  the  national  electricity  system quantities of energy produced by new plants operated with renewable sources and equal to at least 2% of the thermoelectricity produced or imported in the course of the previous year. This requirement... can  also  be  met  by  purchasing from  other  operators  the  'green  certificates' issued by the Manager of the National Transmission  Network  (GRTN).
section_header: 2.5.4.5 Indicators for the generation of electricity
extraction_rationale: Regulatory obligation with start date and compliance mechanism (tradable certificates).

policy_statement: Increase CO2 removals from land use, land-use change and forestry under Kyoto Protocol Article 3.3 and 3.4.

section_header: 4.1.1 General guidelines on policies and measures

policy_statement: Promote R&D and deployment for hydrogen, biomass CHP, solar thermal power, wind and photovoltaic, and waste/biogas power plants.
source_quote: - promotion of research and development aiming at introducing hydrogen as a main fuel in energy systems and in  the transport sector; promotion of biomass based combined heat and power plants   and solar thermal power plants; promotion of wind and photovoltaic  power  plants  and  waste  and  biogas based power plants.
section_header: 4.1.1 General guidelines on policies and measures

policy_statement: Voluntary agreement with ENEL aims to reduce emissions by 22 MtCO2 by 2006 compared to 1990, including efficiency improvements and conversion of 15,000 MW to combined-cycle plants.
source_quote:
The voluntary agreement with Enel has the objective  of  reducing  emissions  of  22  MtCO 2 by  2006, compared to the emissions of 1990, by:
- increasing the efficiency of existing plants and converting 15.000 MW to combined-cycle plants;
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: Quantified emissions reduction objective with deadline and specific actions/capacity; direct mitigation policy.

source_quote: Legislative Decrees of 24 April 2001 provide for the  reduction  of  electricity  and  gas  consumptions through the implementation of measures adopted by distribution companies; these measures are expected to  be  fully  adopted  since  non-compliance    would incur  financial  penalties.  The  overall  effect  of  such Decrees is expected to entail a reduction from 7 to 8 MtCO2.
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: Binding obligation with enforcement (penalties) and quantified expected emissions impact.

policy_statement: Implement the '10,000 photovoltaic roofs' programme (2000–2002) with estimated emissions reduction of ~0.12 MtCO2/year.
source_quote: The  programme  of 10,000  photovoltaic  roofs is expected to be partially implemented and, according to  rough  estimates,  emission  reduction  should  be around 0.12 MtCO2 year.
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: Named programme with quantified expected emissions reduction; implementation commitment though noted as partial.

policy_statement: Increase waste incinerator burning capacity by 220,000 tonnes per year by 2010 to reduce 1.6 MtCO2.

section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources

The  policy  aiming  at  spurring  the  expansion  of renewable sources still further indicates as feasible an additional expansion by 2010,  of 11 TWh...

This    additional  expansion requires    an  increase  of  0.3%  each  year  of  the mandatory  2%  obligation,  from  2005  to  2012..
extraction_rationale: Specific quantified policy adjustment (annual increase) tied to renewable generation outcome; direct mitigation.

policy_statement: Increase photovoltaic capacity by about 150 MW via R&D and niche uses, requiring investment and incentives (negative NPV).

This is a more expensive option than other renewable sources since it entails higher investment costs... The possibility of an additional expansion of about 150 MW with an investment of 1.125 million Euros and a  negative  NPV  of  220  million  Euros  is  identified.
section_header: 4.2.4 Additional measures for the electric energy sector
extraction_rationale: Specific capacity expansion option with investment figures; framed as additional measure (not yet established).

section_header: 4.3.3.2 Increase in the efficiency of the transformers stock

Incentives to cogeneration shoud be  actuated  through  the  following  alternative options:
extraction_rationale: Quantified expansion and emissions reduction; includes explicit incentive mechanisms (though options).

This    measure does not require additional incentives.
extraction_rationale: Regulatory authorization commitment for alternative fuels in cement sector; concrete intervention though phrased as 'should be established'.

policy_statement: Voluntary agreement with FIAT targets reducing specific car emissions from 164 gCO2/km to 145 gCO2/km, enabling 6.8 MtCO2 reduction by 2010.

By the end of 2004 the Ministry of Finance should reformulate the excise taxes on fuels in such a way that,  with  the  revenue  flow  remaining  equal,  fuels that cause less damage to human health and to the environment, as well as lower emissions of CO2, are promoted.
