policy_statement: Extend subsidies for replacing existing cars with low-consumption vehicles (≤120 gCO2/km) to reduce 3.5–6 Mt CO2.
source_quote: incentives in the form of subsidies for the replacement of existing automobiles with new vehicles providing consumption rates lower than 5 lt/100 km (average CO2 emissions equal to or lower than 120 g/Km); it is expected that a directive on the subject  will  be  issued  before  the  end  of  this  year. Estimates  show  that  this  measure,    should  lead  to reductions in CO 2 from 3.5 to 6 Mt,
section_header: 4.4.4 Additional initiatives planned for the transport sector
extraction_rationale: Specific subsidy programme with quantified emissions reduction; directive expected (some uncertainty).

policy_statement: Blend biodiesel into transport diesel up to 5%, with expected CO2 reduction of 4 Mt and cost of 15 million Euro.
source_quote:
Bio-fuels. There  are  plans  for  the  blending  of diesel  fuel  used  in  engines  with  bio-diesel... up to a level of 5%.

It is  estimated  that  the  measure  in  question  would reduce CO2 by 4 Mt... with  an  overall  cost  of  15  million  euro.
section_header: 4.4.4 Additional initiatives planned for the transport sector
extraction_rationale: Quantified blending target and emissions reduction with cost; clear mitigation measure.

policy_statement: Increase natural gas use in residential and service sectors as an implemented measure with estimated 8.0 MtCO2 reduction by 2010.
source_quote:
The use of natural gas in residential units registered significant increases in the years following 1990 and is  expected  to  continue  growing  in  the  years  to come; this remains the most economical measure for reducing  emissions.

Table 4.9... Various decrees  | Increase in the use of natural gas in the residential and service-industry sectors | 8.0
section_header: 4.5.1 Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector
extraction_rationale: Implemented measure with quantified estimated reduction (via table reference embedded in text); policy lever is decrees promoting gas switching.

policy_statement: Apply Law 10/91 to reduce heat consumption in new buildings (estimated 3.7 MtCO2 reduction by 2010).
source_quote:
The legislation  developed  for  the implementation of Law 10/91 ... has reduced energy consumption in new buildings by 10% within the last two years, compared to the 1990 levels.

Table 4.9 - List of measures implemented... Implementation of Law 10/91 | Reduction in heat consumption of new residential and service-industry buildings | 3.7
section_header: 4.5.1 Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector
extraction_rationale: Named law implementation with quantified estimated reduction; building efficiency policy.

policy_statement: Extend Ministerial Decrees on end-use efficiency beyond 2006 to achieve additional 3.8–6.5 Mt CO2 reductions by 2010.
source_quote: There are plans for the ministerial decrees of April 2001 to remain in effect beyond 2006, with the same annual increases as those set for the period 2002-2006: the result would be a further reduction... of from 3.8 to 6.5 Mt CO2
section_header: 4.5.4 Additional initiatives planned for the residential and tertiary sector
extraction_rationale: Explicit plan to extend decrees with quantified emissions reduction range; policy continuation commitment.

policy_statement: Expand thermal solar energy use to save 70,000 toe and reduce ~0.2 Mt CO2 with investments estimated at 800 million Euro.
source_quote: It  is  predicted  that  investments  can  be  made  for potential  energy  savings  of  70,000  t.o.e.,  which would result in reductions of approximately 0.2 Mt in  CO 2 investments.  Overall  investments  are  estimated at 800 million euro,
section_header: 4.5.4.2 More extensive use of thermal solar energy
extraction_rationale: Quantified energy savings, emissions reduction, and investment; concrete renewable heat policy option.

policy_statement: Reduce N2O emissions from adipic and nitric acid production via voluntary agreements and installation of abatement technologies (thermal/catalytic; SCR).
source_quote:
## Reduction of N2O emissions from the production of adipic acid and nitric acid

In  the  case  of  adipic  acid,  the  planned  course  of action calls for the adoption in Italy of the devices (thermal  or  catalytic)  already  used  in  the  other European countries for the treatment of effluent gases. The measure referred to consists of a voluntary agreement with the only enterprise involved.
extraction_rationale: Specific industrial abatement interventions with named technologies and voluntary agreement mechanism; direct mitigation of non-CO2 GHG.

policy_statement: Reduce N2O emissions from agricultural soils by rationalising fertiliser use through awareness efforts and codes of good agricultural practice; estimated decrease 0.46 Mt CO2e by 2010.
source_quote:
The emission reductions in question can result from a rationalisation of the use of fertilisers...

By combining these recommendations with others... additional,  limited  reductions could be achieved... resulting in an estimated decrease of 0.46 CO2 equivalent Mt.
extraction_rationale: Specific intervention mechanism (codes of practice and rationalisation) with quantified estimated reduction.

policy_statement: Reduce methane emissions from manure management by covering liquid waste tanks and using biogas for combustion/cogeneration; costs 6.2–33.2 million Euro/year.
source_quote:
The proposed initiative involves covering the holding  tanks  used  to  store  liquid  animal  waste  and then conveying the resulting biogas to combustion or  cogeneration plants.

...with  a  reduction  in  methane  emissions  of between 7 and 39 kt of methane per year, at an overall  cost  of  from  6.2  to  33.2  million  Euro  per year.
extraction_rationale: Concrete technical intervention with quantified emissions reduction range and annual cost; direct mitigation.

policy_statement: Meet Directive 99/31/EC deadline to reduce biodegradable municipal waste landfilled by 50% by 2010 vs 1995, reducing 0.64 Mt CO2e.
source_quote: fulfilment of the deadlines set for the reduction of  the  biodegradable  fraction  of  the  municipal waste  in  landfills,  as  stipulated  under  Directive 99/31/EC, which calls for a reduction of 50% as early as 2010, compared to the 1995 level... making for a forecast decrease of 0,64 Mt;
section_header: 4.7.3 Waste: Stabilisation of the organic fraction and energy recovery
extraction_rationale: Binding EU directive target with quantified reduction and year; direct waste-sector mitigation.

policy_statement: Achieve 30% of municipal waste sent to energy-recovery treatments by 2010, adding 500 MWe capacity and reducing 0.33 Mt CO2e.
source_quote: it is assumed that, by 2010, the  portion  of  municipal  waste  sent  to  energyrecovery treatments shall be 30%... making  for  an  additional  increase  of  500 MWe  municipal  electrical  capacity  from  waste... with a decrease in equivalent CO2 of 0.33 Mt.
section_header: 4.7.3 Waste: Stabilisation of the organic fraction and energy recovery
extraction_rationale: Quantified waste-to-energy share and capacity increase with emissions reduction; concrete mitigation measure.

policy_statement: Forestry-sector carbon removal measures under Kyoto Articles 3.3 and 3.4 with maximum national potential of 10.2 Mt CO2 removals and investments of 526.7 million Euro.
source_quote:
The  measures  contemplated  in  the  sector  'land use, land use change and forestry' for the generation and certification of carbon credits during the period 2008-2012 are summarised on table 4.14.

Table 4.14 - Maximum national potential for carbon removal

Total  | 10.2 | 526.7
extraction_rationale: Umbrella sink programme with quantified removal potential and investment; includes multiple sub-activities in table.

policy_statement: Create the National Forestry Inventory of Carbon (INFOCARB) by 2005 and update every 5 years.
source_quote: From a technical perspective, the National Forestry Inventory of Carbon (INFOCARB) should be created by 2005. This inventory must then be updated every  5  years,  corresponding  to  the  end  of  the period  of  commitment  under  the  Kyoto  Protocol
extraction_rationale: Time-bound institutional measure to enable sink accounting and cap revision; concrete deliverable and schedule.

policy_statement: Undertake new afforestation/reforestation plantings during 2003–2008 (40,000 ha) to remove ~1 Mt CO2 in 2008–2012 and ~20 Mt CO2 at maturity.
source_quote: c) the new plantings to be made during the period 2003-2008,  forecast  at  40,000  hectares,  for  an average  removal  of  1  Mt  CO 2 during  the  period 2008-2012 and of 20 Mt CO2 at the maturity.
extraction_rationale: Quantified area and removals with time windows; direct sink creation policy.

policy_statement: Carry out reforestation in hydrogeologically unstable areas at ~6,000 ha/year (2003–2012) totaling 60,000 ha, removing ~1 Mt CO2 in 2008–2012.
source_quote: The operating capacity of the Basin Authorities is approximately 6,000 hectares of reforestation per year for the period of 2003-2012, making for a total of 60,000 hectares. Average removal for this type of planting  is  estimated  at  1  Mt  CO 2 for  the  period 2008-2012
extraction_rationale: Quantified annual rate and total hectares with estimated removals; also explicitly tied to hydrogeological risk reduction.

policy_statement: Establish the National Register of Agro-Forestry Carbon Storage Pools to certify carbon removals from agricultural and forestry systems.
source_quote:
4.8.4  National  Register  of  Agro-Forestry  Carbon Storage Pools

The  National  Register  of  Agro-Forestry  Carbon Storage Pools  is the tool for certifying the quantities  of  carbon  removed  by  Italian  agricultural  and forestry system.
section_header: 4.8.4 National Register of Agro-Forestry Carbon Storage Pools
extraction_rationale: Institutional mechanism for MRV/certification of sinks; necessary for Kyoto accounting and crediting.

policy_statement: Use flexible mechanisms (Emissions Trading, CDM, JI) to complement domestic policies due to lower unit costs.
source_quote: The  present  section  addresses  the  use  of  flexible mechanisms: Emissions Trading, Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) and Joint Implementation (JI) project. These mechanisms complement internal policies, often  on  account  of  their  greater  convenience  in terms of the unit cost for reducing emissions.
extraction_rationale: Explicit policy choice to use Kyoto mechanisms; not quantified here but clearly a mitigation instrument strategy.

policy_statement: Adopt a National Action Plan to combat desertification (CIPE deliberation 21.12.1999) to guide regions and basin authorities in prevention, mitigation and adaptation strategies.
source_quote: the Italian Government  has  arranged  a  National  Action  Plan (MATT, 1999). The Plan, approved upon deliberation of the Interministerial Committee for Economic Planning of 21.12.1999, outlines  an  information and awareness path  addressed to the Regions and the  Basin  Authorities  to  spot  the  most  vulnerable areas and define prevention, mitigation and adaptation  strategies.
extraction_rationale: Named plan approved by CIPE with explicit adaptation/mitigation/prevention objectives; climate-relevant via desertification linkage.

policy_statement: Adopt a National Research Programme (CIPE 21 Dec 2000) establishing a Strategic Programme for Sustainable Development and Climate Change and creating a Euro-Mediterranean Centre for Climate Change Research.
source_quote:
On 21 December 2000, the Interministerial Committee  for  Economic  Planning  approved  the National Research Programme (MIUR, 2000) which set up the features for  the Strategic Programme for Sustainable Development and Climate Change.

In order to meet the above-mentioned requirements, the  Plan  foresees  the  creation  of  a  research  infrastructure, acting as a EuroMediterranean Centre for the  Research  on  Climate  Change
section_header: 6.5.5 Deliberation of the Interministerial Committee for Economic Planning for the National Research Programme, 21 December 2000
extraction_rationale: Formal programme approval with explicit institutional creation; supports climate knowledge and response strategies.

policy_statement: Law 36/1994 governs water use to promote saving and renewal of resources and avoid jeopardising water stocks and hydro-geological balance; assigns regions to define ATOs for efficient water services.
source_quote: Governs the utilisation of water stipulating that the use of water geared towards saving and renewing resources, in order to avoid jeopardising water stocks... and the hydro-geological balance. Devolves to the regions identification the Optimal Territorial Settings (ATO) the management of water services accord - ing to criteria of operating and economic efficiency.
section_header: Annex 2: Mitiligation and adaptation adopted in Italy since 1998
extraction_rationale: Regulatory framework for water conservation and management efficiency; adaptation-relevant for drought/water stress though not explicitly climate-labeled in quote.

policy_statement: Law 183/1989 establishes basin authorities and basin plans for land protection and proper water use to preserve and protect territory.
source_quote: Framework measure on the subject of land protection, the management water resources and the protection environmental... basin authorities must draw up the plan, an informative, regulatory technical tool used to plan and program initiative and norms of use to preserve, protect and upgrade he land as well the proper use of water, based on physical and environmental characteris - tics of the territory.
section_header: Annex 2: Mitiligation and adaptation adopted in Italy since 1998
extraction_rationale: Binding institutional and planning mechanism for hydrogeological risk and water management; adaptation-relevant.

policy_statement: Legislative Decree 79/1999 establishes renewable obligation (2%), cogeneration exemptions, and dispatch priority for renewables and cogeneration.
source_quote:
The decree contemplates mechanisms and provisions which can favour - grams and initiatives for the reduction of greenhouse gases, including: art. 11, paragraphs 1, 2 and 3: obligation of producers and importers of renewable energy to include in the supplies... a share of 2% produced by renewable sources...

art. 11, paragraph 4... dispatching priority given to energy renewable sources and cogeneration;
section_header: Annex 2: Mitiligation and adaptation adopted in Italy since 1998
extraction_rationale: Regulatory package with explicit obligations and priority dispatch; direct mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Implement the National Energy and Climate Plan 2021-2030 (PNEC 2030) as Portugal’s primary national energy and climate policy instrument for the decade, under political coordination of the Ministerial Commission for Climate Action (CAC).
source_quote: “The National Energy and Climate Plan 2021-2030 (PNEC 2030) is this decade's primary national energy and climate policy instrument and it was approved through the Council of Ministers Resolution n.º 53/2020, of 10 th of July. The Ministerial Commission for Climate Action (CAC) is responsible for the political coordination of PNEC 2030, in charge of supervising and monitoring its implementation and the achievement of the established targets.”
section_header: 1.2. Legal and policy frameworks and institutional arrangements
extraction_rationale: This is a formally approved national policy instrument with an assigned governance body responsible for implementation and target achievement (binding institutional mechanism).

policy_statement: Pursue Portugal’s long-term mitigation vision through the Carbon Neutrality Roadmap 2050 (RNC2050) as the national long-term strategy submitted to the European Commission and UNFCCC.
source_quote: “The Portuguese long-term vision for mitigation has been set in the Carbon Neutrality Roadmap 2050  (RNC2050),  approved  by  the  Council  of  Ministers  nº.  107/2019,  of  1 st of  July,  which constituted the Portuguese Long-Term Strategy submitted to the European Commission and to United Nations Framework Convention for Climate Change (UNFCCC).”
section_header: 1.2. Legal and policy frameworks and institutional arrangements
extraction_rationale: A formally approved long-term mitigation strategy (named roadmap) adopted by Council of Ministers resolution.

policy_statement: Implement the revised National Adaptation Strategy (ENAAC 2020) to improve cross-domain articulation, integrate adaptation into sectoral policies, and implement adaptation measures.
source_quote: “Portugal also has a revised NAS - National Adaptation Strategy (ENAAC 2020, approved by the Council of Ministers Resolution n.º 56/2015, of 30 th of July) (English version in Annex 1), focusing on improving the articulation between domains (particularly those of transversal nature), on the integration in sectoral policies, and the implementation of adaptation measures.”
section_header: 1.2. Legal and policy frameworks and institutional arrangements
extraction_rationale: A formally approved national adaptation strategy with explicit focus areas and implementation intent.

policy_statement: Implement the Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC / NAP) to complement ENAAC 2020 and focus on implementing adaptation measures.
source_quote: “The Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme, approved by the Resolution of the Council of  Ministers  Nº.  130/2019,  of  2 nd of  August  (English  version  in  Annex  2),  complements  and systematises  the  work  carried  out  in  the  context  of  ENAAC  2020,  focusing  on  its  second objective: to implement adaptation measures.”
section_header: 1.2. Legal and policy frameworks and institutional arrangements
extraction_rationale: A formally approved national programme with a defined purpose (implementation of adaptation measures).

policy_statement: Use environmental assessment procedures to integrate current and future climatic vulnerabilities, climate scenarios, and adaptation measures into project and plan assessments.
source_quote: “The Environmental Assessment procedures consider national and territorial adaptation planning instruments; current and future climatic vulnerabilities through historical data on the climate and the occurrences of extreme weather events; environmental, social and economic impacts and consequences, considering CC scenarios; key risks/impacts of CC in the project; assessment if  pre-existing vulnerabilities to CC will be exacerbated; alternatives more resilient to climate pressures and/or allowing a more significant climate vulnerability reduction; critical thresholds that compromise the project or the environment, forcing the adoption of adaptation measures; minimisation measures based on NAP for the relevant vulnerabilities or impacts.”
section_header: Integration of climate change impacts and resilience into environmental assessment procedures
extraction_rationale: Sets an operational requirement for assessment procedures to account for climate vulnerabilities and adaptation measures (a planning/regulatory integration mechanism).

policy_statement: Strengthen Portugal–Spain cooperation between national adaptation units to exchange information and identify priorities and common actions on shared climate risks.
source_quote: “Since 2016 Portugal and Spain has strengthened relations between the national adaptation units improving the exchange of information and identification of priorities and common actions in the field of shared risks associated with the impacts of climate change.”
section_header: Networks or other collaborations on adaptation across national authorities
extraction_rationale: A stated cross-border cooperation action with a defined purpose (shared climate risk priorities and actions).

policy_statement: Maintain and develop adapt.local, a municipal partnership network for local climate adaptation, and develop intermunicipal climate change adaptation plans promoted by subregional structures.
source_quote: “Created  in  December  2016,  adapt.local  -  Network  of  Municipalities  for  Local  Adaptation  to Climate Change constitutes a partnership led by municipalities but involving higher education institutions,  research  centres,  non-governmental  organisations,  and  companies.  Recently, Intermunicipal  Climate  Change  Adaptation  Plans  have  been  developed,  promoted  by  subregional  structures.”
section_header: Good practice examples of networks or other collaborations on adaptation across local and regional authorities
extraction_rationale: Named network and associated planning outputs (intermunicipal plans) constitute concrete adaptation governance and planning interventions.

policy_statement: Financially support adaptation activities in Portugal through the AdaPT Programme under the EEA Grants mechanism, including projects such as the Climate Portal.
source_quote: “The  development  of  the  Climate  Portal  was  one  of  the  projects  resulting  from  the  AdaPT Programme's  activities.  This  programme  was  designed  to  financially  support  activities  on "Adaptation to Climate Change"  in Portugal guided by the terms established in the Memorandum of Understanding between Portugal, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein, under the European Economic Area Financial Mechanism (EEA Grants).”
extraction_rationale: Explicitly describes a programme designed to provide financial support for adaptation activities (a funding instrument/program).

policy_statement: Extend the validity of the National Adaptation Strategy (NAS) until 31 December 2025 through PNEC 2030.
source_quote: “The National Energy and Climate Plan 2020-2030 (PNEC 2030) is the main instrument of national energy and climate policy for the next decade towards carbon neutrality in 2050. PNEC 2030 also has extended the validity of the NAS until 31 st of December 2025.”
section_header: Summaries of national strategies, policies, plans and efforts
extraction_rationale: A time-bound extension of a national strategy’s validity is a concrete policy decision with a clear deadline.

policy_statement: Develop the National Adaptation Roadmap 2100 (RNA 2100) to update climate projections and impacts, produce regional adaptation narratives, establish spatial-planning adaptation guidelines, and identify investment needs and costs including costs of inaction, with completion expected in 2023.
source_quote: “Following a similar approach, the National Adaptation Roadmap 2100 (RNA 2100) is being drawn up and is expected to be completed in 2023. The RNA 2100 will update the knowledge of climate projections for Portugal and respective impacts in key sectors, for different Greenhouse Gases (GHG) concentration scenarios.”
section_header: Summaries of national strategies, policies, plans and efforts
extraction_rationale: A named roadmap under development with a stated completion date and defined outputs (guidelines, narratives, investment needs).

policy_statement: Commit to mobilise 0.15% to 0.20% of Portugal’s GNI as ODA allocated to Least Developed Countries by 2030.
source_quote: “As an EU Member State, Portugal made the commitment to mobilise 0.15% to 0.20% of its GNI as ODA allocated to Least Developed Countries (LDC) by 2030.”
section_header: 4.5. Provision of new and additional resources
extraction_rationale: Quantified financial commitment with a deadline (2030), constituting a financial instrument/commitment for international support.

policy_statement: Operate the Portuguese Environmental Fund (established 2017) to support national environmental policies and objectives, including climate change, and include international cooperation on climate change as an identified action domain.
source_quote:
“The Portuguese Environmental Fund was established in 2017. The purpose of this instrument is to support national environmental policies for the pursuit of Sustainable Development Objectives, contributing to the achievement of national and international objectives and commitments, in particular those related to climate change, water resources, waste and nature conservation and biodiversity.

One of  the  domains  that  is  clearly  identified  as  action  domain  of  this  Fund  is  international cooperation in the field of climate change, in accordance with the compliance of international commitments.”
section_header: 4.5. Provision of new and additional resources
extraction_rationale: Creates/uses a dedicated fund (financial instrument) with explicit climate-change purpose and an international cooperation domain.

policy_statement: Implement the Regional Programme for Climate Change (PRAC) in the Autonomous Region of the Azores, encompassing mitigation and adaptation, including studies of vulnerabilities and definition of adaptation measures for relevant sectors.
source_quote: “The Autonomous Region of the Azores proceeded with the Regional Programme for Climate Change  (PRAC -Portuguese  acronym),  approved  by  the  Regional  Legislative  Decree  Nº. 30/2019/A, 28 th of  November, which encompasses mitigation and adaptation. PRAC allowed improving the level of knowledge on climate change in the Region through the studies of current and  future  vulnerabilities  and  the  definition  of  adaptation  measures  for  the  most  relevant sectors.”
extraction_rationale: A legally approved regional programme with explicit mitigation/adaptation scope and defined actions (studies and measures).

policy_statement: Use POSEUR Priority Axis 2 to fund adaptation to climate change and risk prevention/management, including investment priorities for adaptation and for disaster resilience and disaster management systems.
source_quote: “The Operational Programme for Sustainability and Efficiency in the Use of Resources (POSEUR) was partially funded by the EU Structural and Cohesion Funds and its Thematic Objective 5 aims to strengthen national adaptive capacity. Its Priority Axis 2 - Adaptation to climate change and risk  prevention  and  management,  includes  two  investment  priorities  (IP):  5.1.  Support  for investment for adaptation to climate change; 5.2. Promoting investments to address specific risks, ensure disaster resilience and develop disaster management systems.”
section_header: 5.1.2. State of play of the implementation of measures planned under 'Strategies and Plans': spending earmarked for climate adaptation including in disaster risk management
extraction_rationale: A defined funding programme axis with explicit adaptation objective and investment priorities (financial instrument).

policy_statement: Create and implement the support programme “More Sustainable Buildings” (2020) to rehabilitate and improve buildings’ energy and water performance.
source_quote: “With the specific objective  of  rehabilitating  and  improving  buildings'  concerning  energy  and water  performance  it  was  created  the  support  programme  "More  Sustainable  Buildings",  in 2020, and it has been financing 890 applications, amounting to €1.75 million.”
section_header: 5.1.3. State of play of the implementation of measures planned under 'Strategies and Plans': the share of spending used to support climate adaptation in each sector
extraction_rationale: A named support programme with financing provided (grant-like instrument) and explicit performance objectives (energy and water).

policy_statement: Implement the “Village Condominium” integrated support programme to manage fuels around settlements in forest territories with high forest density and dispersed rural settlements.
source_quote: “In  2020,  the  Environmental  Fund  financed  applications  with  the  objective  to  implement adaptation measures that guarantee the improvement of the adaptive capacity and increase the territory's resilience to the impacts of climate change and applications made under the "Village Condominium", the Integrated Support Programme for Villages located in forest territories, to ensure  the  management  of  fuels  around  settlements  in  areas  of  high  forest  density  and increased number and dispersion of small rural settlements.”
section_header: 5.1.3. State of play of the implementation of measures planned under 'Strategies and Plans': the share of spending used to support climate adaptation in each sector
extraction_rationale: A named programme with funded applications and a specific intervention (fuel management) to reduce wildfire risk and improve resilience.

policy_statement: Target 100% municipal coverage by climate change adaptation plans or strategies by 2030 under P-3AC (NAP) result indicators.
source_quote:
“Table 1. Result indicators and targets defined under the NAP (Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme - P-3AC).

Municipalities covered by adaptation plans (municipal, inter-municipal or regional) — Target 2030: 100%”
extraction_rationale: A quantified national target (100% by 2030) embedded in the NAP monitoring framework.

policy_statement: Implement the Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC) through nine lines of action addressing key climate impacts and vulnerabilities.
source_quote:
“This Programme complements and systematizes the work carried out in the context of the ENAAC 2020 with a view to the second objective - to implement adaptation measures, grouped into 8 concrete lines of action of direct intervention in the territory and infrastructures, complemented by a transversal line of action) which aim to respond to the significant impacts and vulnerabilities identified for Portugal (Table 3):

1. Prevention of rural fires - structuring interventions in agricultural and forestry areas.”
section_header: 5.2 Courses of action and measures to address impacts and vulnerabilities
extraction_rationale: An umbrella programme explicitly structured into multiple numbered lines of action; qualifies as a parent policy for sub-actions.

parent_statement: Implement the Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC) through nine lines of action addressing key climate impacts and vulnerabilities.
policy_statement: Line of Action #1: Prevent rural fires through structural interventions in agricultural and forestry areas.
source_quote:
“This Programme complements and systematizes the work carried out in the context of the ENAAC 2020 with a view to the second objective - to implement adaptation measures, grouped into 8 concrete lines of action of direct intervention in the territory and infrastructures, complemented by a transversal line of action) which aim to respond to the significant impacts and vulnerabilities identified for Portugal (Table 3):

1. Prevention of rural fires - structuring interventions in agricultural and forestry areas.”
section_header: 5.2 Courses of action and measures to address impacts and vulnerabilities
extraction_rationale: A specific numbered line of action under P-3AC; constitutes a concrete adaptation intervention area.

parent_statement: Implement the Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC) through nine lines of action addressing key climate impacts and vulnerabilities.
policy_statement: Line of Action #2: Implement soil conservation and fertility improvement techniques.
source_quote:
“This Programme complements and systematizes the work carried out in the context of the ENAAC 2020 with a view to the second objective - to implement adaptation measures, grouped into 8 concrete lines of action of direct intervention in the territory and infrastructures, complemented by a transversal line of action) which aim to respond to the significant impacts and vulnerabilities identified for Portugal (Table 3):

2. Implementation of soil conservation and fertility improvement techniques.”
section_header: 5.2 Courses of action and measures to address impacts and vulnerabilities
extraction_rationale: A specific numbered line of action under P-3AC; concrete intervention area for reducing climate vulnerability (erosion/desertification).

parent_statement: Implement the Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC) through nine lines of action addressing key climate impacts and vulnerabilities.
policy_statement: Line of Action #3: Implement good water management practices in agriculture, industry, and urban sectors to prevent drought and scarcity impacts.
source_quote:
“This Programme complements and systematizes the work carried out in the context of the ENAAC 2020 with a view to the second objective - to implement adaptation measures, grouped into 8 concrete lines of action of direct intervention in the territory and infrastructures, complemented by a transversal line of action) which aim to respond to the significant impacts and vulnerabilities identified for Portugal (Table 3):

3. Implementation of good water management practices in agriculture, industry, and the urban sector to prevent impacts from drought and scarcity phenomena.”
section_header: 5.2 Courses of action and measures to address impacts and vulnerabilities
extraction_rationale: A specific numbered line of action under P-3AC; concrete adaptation action area focused on drought/water scarcity.

parent_statement: Implement the Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC) through nine lines of action addressing key climate impacts and vulnerabilities.
policy_statement: Line of Action #4: Increase resilience of ecosystems, species, and habitats to climate change.
source_quote:
“This Programme complements and systematizes the work carried out in the context of the ENAAC 2020 with a view to the second objective - to implement adaptation measures, grouped into 8 concrete lines of action of direct intervention in the territory and infrastructures, complemented by a transversal line of action) which aim to respond to the significant impacts and vulnerabilities identified for Portugal (Table 3):

4. Increasing the resilience of ecosystems, species, and habitats to the effects of climate change.”
section_header: 5.2 Courses of action and measures to address impacts and vulnerabilities
extraction_rationale: A specific numbered line of action under P-3AC; ecosystem resilience is a concrete adaptation mechanism.

parent_statement: Implement the Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC) through nine lines of action addressing key climate impacts and vulnerabilities.
policy_statement: Line of Action #5: Reduce vulnerability of urban areas to heat waves and rising maximum temperatures.
source_quote:
“This Programme complements and systematizes the work carried out in the context of the ENAAC 2020 with a view to the second objective - to implement adaptation measures, grouped into 8 concrete lines of action of direct intervention in the territory and infrastructures, complemented by a transversal line of action) which aim to respond to the significant impacts and vulnerabilities identified for Portugal (Table 3):

5. Reducing the vulnerability of urban areas to heat waves and rising maximum temperatures.”
section_header: 5.2 Courses of action and measures to address impacts and vulnerabilities
extraction_rationale: A specific numbered line of action under P-3AC; explicitly targets heatwaves and temperature extremes.

parent_statement: Implement the Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC) through nine lines of action addressing key climate impacts and vulnerabilities.
policy_statement: Line of Action #6: Prevent establishment and spread of invasive alien species, diseases and pests (including vector-borne diseases).
source_quote:
“This Programme complements and systematizes the work carried out in the context of the ENAAC 2020 with a view to the second objective - to implement adaptation measures, grouped into 8 concrete lines of action of direct intervention in the territory and infrastructures, complemented by a transversal line of action) which aim to respond to the significant impacts and vulnerabilities identified for Portugal (Table 3):

6. Preventing the establishment and spread of invasive alien species, vector-borne diseases and agricultural and forestry diseases and pests.”
section_header: 5.2 Courses of action and measures to address impacts and vulnerabilities
extraction_rationale: A specific numbered line of action under P-3AC; concrete adaptation intervention addressing climate-sensitive biological risks.

parent_statement: Implement the Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC) through nine lines of action addressing key climate impacts and vulnerabilities.
policy_statement: Line of Action #7: Reduce or minimise risks associated with flooding phenomena.
source_quote:
“This Programme complements and systematizes the work carried out in the context of the ENAAC 2020 with a view to the second objective - to implement adaptation measures, grouped into 8 concrete lines of action of direct intervention in the territory and infrastructures, complemented by a transversal line of action) which aim to respond to the significant impacts and vulnerabilities identified for Portugal (Table 3):

7. Reduction or minimisation of risks associated with flooding phenomena.”
section_header: 5.2 Courses of action and measures to address impacts and vulnerabilities
extraction_rationale: A specific numbered line of action under P-3AC; concrete adaptation intervention area for flood risk.

parent_statement: Implement the Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC) through nine lines of action addressing key climate impacts and vulnerabilities.
policy_statement: Line of Action #8: Increase resilience and coastal protection in areas at high risk from coastal erosion, overtopping and flooding.
source_quote:
“This Programme complements and systematizes the work carried out in the context of the ENAAC 2020 with a view to the second objective - to implement adaptation measures, grouped into 8 concrete lines of action of direct intervention in the territory and infrastructures, complemented by a transversal line of action) which aim to respond to the significant impacts and vulnerabilities identified for Portugal (Table 3):

8. Increasing resilience and coastal protection in areas at high risk from coastal erosion, overtopping and flooding.”
section_header: 5.2 Courses of action and measures to address impacts and vulnerabilities
extraction_rationale: A specific numbered line of action under P-3AC; concrete adaptation intervention area for sea-level rise/coastal hazards.

parent_statement: Implement the Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC) through nine lines of action addressing key climate impacts and vulnerabilities.
policy_statement: Line of Action #9: Develop decision support tools, capacity building, and awareness-raising actions for climate adaptation.
source_quote:
“This Programme complements and systematizes the work carried out in the context of the ENAAC 2020 with a view to the second objective - to implement adaptation measures, grouped into 8 concrete lines of action of direct intervention in the territory and infrastructures, complemented by a transversal line of action) which aim to respond to the significant impacts and vulnerabilities identified for Portugal (Table 3):

9. Development of decision support tools, capacity building and awareness-raising actions.”
section_header: 5.2 Courses of action and measures to address impacts and vulnerabilities
extraction_rationale: A specific numbered line of action under P-3AC; concrete enabling actions supporting adaptation implementation.

policy_statement: Reduce 25% of Qatar’s GHG emissions by 2030 relative to a BAU baseline starting in 2019.
source_quote:
Qatar intends to reduce 25% of its GHG emissions by the year 2030, relative to baseline scenario {BusinessAs-Usual (BAU)}.

The BAU scenario starts in the year 2019 and considers mitigation measures implemented by the State of Qatar until the end of 2019.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified national mitigation target with a deadline (2030) and a defined reference scenario (BAU starting 2019).

policy_statement: Qatar Petroleum commits to zero routine flaring by 2030 and to minimize onshore flaring to the absolute minimum, including technically feasible non-routine flaring.
source_quote: The national oil company, Qatar Petroleum (QP), is committed to zero routine flaring by 2030, with a long-term goal to reduce flaring in onshore facilities to the absolute minimum. Technically feasible non-routine flaring is also covered.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

a) Oil & Gas
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound operational commitment (zero routine flaring by 2030) that directly reduces emissions from oil and gas operations.

policy_statement: Use carbon capture and storage (CCS) as a pivotal measure in the oil and gas sector, including commissioning a 2.2 MTPA CO2 capture and storage facility at Ras Laffan and including CCS in new LNG facilities.
source_quote: Carbon capture storage (CCS) will be another pivotal measure for reducing the GHG emissions from the sector. Qatar commissioned the largest CO2 recovery and sequestration facility in the MENA region at Ras Laffan in 2019 with a design capacity of 2.2 MTPA of CO2 capture and storage. CCS is included for new LNG facilities and concepts, for remaining LNG facilities will be developed and implemented considering the economic, safety and environmental concerns.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

a) Oil & Gas
extraction_rationale: This specifies a named intervention (CCS) with a quantified capacity and an implementation commitment for new LNG facilities; it is directly tied to GHG reduction.

policy_statement: Implement methane emissions reduction actions across the natural gas value chain, including LDAR in all upstream and downstream facilities and moving toward an integrated fugitive methane monitoring and repair program across all assets.
source_quote:
QP signed a set of Guiding Principles on 22 March 2018 that aim to reduce methane emissions across the natural gas value chain stretching from production to the final consumer.

In 2019, Qatar Petroleum introduced the smart leak detection and repair program (LDAR) in all upstream and downstream facilities of the oil & gas industry. Qatar further plans to move towards a fully integrated fugitive methane monitoring and repair program across all assets.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

a) Oil & Gas
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete operational program (LDAR and integrated monitoring/repair) explicitly aimed at reducing methane emissions.

policy_statement: Enhance energy efficiency in the oil and gas sector through specific initiatives targeted for implementation by 2025 (e.g., seasonal optimization of gas turbine generators and boilers; improved fuel gas/steam measurement and balancing; improved HRSG reliability).
source_quote: Qatar is enhancing energy efficiency in the oil & gas sector as a key measure to reduce GHG emissions. Amongst the variety of measures in energy efficiency, certain initiatives are aimed to be implemented by 2025, e.g., seasonal optimization of gas turbine generators and boilers, improved measurement / balancing for fuel gas / steam, and improved reliability of heat recovery steam generator (HRSGs).
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

a) Oil & Gas
extraction_rationale: This is a set of specific efficiency interventions with a stated implementation timeframe (by 2025) and an explicit GHG-reduction purpose.

policy_statement: Optimize and share electrical generation capacity across upstream facilities to improve dispatch efficiency and reduce gas consumption and GHG emissions.
source_quote: Qatar also plans to efficiently utilize its power plant capacities by usage in other upstream facilities or feed-in from GTL (gas-to-liquid) facilities to its utility distribution / transmission grid. Electrical generation capacity shall be shared and optimized across all upstream facilities. This would allow more efficient dispatch of generating capacity and keep the units closer to their most efficient operating levels, thereby reducing gas consumption and GHG emissions.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

a) Oil & Gas
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete operational optimization commitment (sharing/optimizing generation capacity) with an explicit emissions-reduction mechanism.

policy_statement: Deploy an 800 MW solar power plant (Qatar’s first) and expand renewable energy efforts to make renewables a key driver for ecological and commercial benefits.
source_quote: Nevertheless, recently Qatar has made significant progress in reducing the emissions from the power & water sector, by introducing its first 800 MW solar power plant, which shall be operational soon. It is the goal of the State of Qatar to expand these efforts and transform renewable energy into a key driver for ecological and commercial benefits.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

b) Power & Water
extraction_rationale: This includes a specific renewable energy project (800 MW solar plant) and an explicit goal to expand renewables; both directly relate to emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Implement demand-side energy efficiency, energy savings, and local energy generation via rooftop solar panels under Tarsheed-led efforts.
source_quote: Led by Qatar Foundation, Education City and the Qatar Green Building Council, efforts are being made to enhance the demand-side energy efficiency, energy savings, and local energy generation through rooftops solar panels. So far, the Tarsheed program has been successful in optimizing consumption of electricity & water and has ambitious aims for further reductions.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

b) Power & Water
extraction_rationale: This describes specific interventions (demand-side efficiency and rooftop solar) under an existing program; while targets are not quantified here, the interventions are concrete and ongoing.

policy_statement: Systematically deploy district cooling and energy labeling for electronic devices to reduce energy intensity and mitigate household and SME GHG emissions.
source_quote: Energy efficiency measures such as district cooling and energy labeling for all electronic devices are systematically being deployed and play a growing role in the national economic diversification strategy by reducing energy intensity and the need for energy subsidies, while also mitigating the overall GHG emissions of households and small & medium enterprises.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

b) Power & Water
extraction_rationale: This is a deployment commitment for specific efficiency measures (district cooling, energy labeling) with an explicit emissions mitigation effect.

policy_statement: Implement improved specification standards for electrical and electronic equipment (e.g., air conditioners) to achieve significant electricity savings.
source_quote: Qatar has implemented several specification improvement standards for electrical and electronic equipment such as air conditioners resulting in significant savings in electricity consumption.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

b) Power & Water
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory/standards-based intervention (equipment standards) with a clear resource-efficiency outcome (electricity savings).

policy_statement: Phase out incandescent lamps and adopt energy-efficient lighting to conserve energy and reduce GHG emissions.
source_quote: The initiative to phase out incandescent lamps and adoption of Energy Efficient lighting has contributed in a major way for conservation of Energy and thereby GHG emissions reduction in the State of Qatar.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

b) Power & Water
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention (lighting phase-out/adoption) explicitly linked to energy conservation and GHG reduction.

policy_statement: Continuously upgrade sewage treatment plants to produce treated effluents suitable for reuse (e.g., landscaping, irrigation, district cooling, construction).
source_quote: Lastly, Qatar has continuously strived to upgrade its sewage treatment plants to produce treated effluents suitable for purposes such as landscaping, fodder crops irrigation, district cooling, construction industry use, etc.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

b) Power & Water
extraction_rationale: This is an ongoing infrastructure/operational commitment to expand wastewater reuse, which is a concrete resource-efficiency and resilience-relevant measure (though climate is not the sole stated driver here).

policy_statement: Modernize transport through major public transit investments (Doha Metro and Lusail Tram) to reduce emissions from the transportation sector.
source_quote: The transportation sector in Qatar has been earmarked for rapid modernization. The Doha Metro and Lusail Tram are major milestones in the development of public transportation and subsequent reduction of emissions from this sector.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

c) Transportation
extraction_rationale: This identifies specific public transport projects with an explicit emissions-reduction outcome.

policy_statement: Electrify Qatar’s public transport system and invest in nationwide EV charging infrastructure; promote a shift to EVs for private use.
source_quote: The country has also taken significant strides to adopt electrification of on-road vehicles by committing to electrify its public transport system and investing in installation of charging infrastructure across the country. Going forward, gradual adoption of Euro 6 emission standards for vehicles and promoting a shift towards electric vehicles for private use shall constitute key initiatives to reduce emissions from the transportation sector.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

c) Transportation
extraction_rationale: This is a clear commitment to electrification and enabling infrastructure, plus a stated intent to promote private EV uptake, explicitly for emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Gradually adopt Euro 6 vehicle emission standards to reduce transport-sector emissions.
source_quote: Going forward, gradual adoption of Euro 6 emission standards for vehicles and promoting a shift towards electric vehicles for private use shall constitute key initiatives to reduce emissions from the transportation sector.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

c) Transportation
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory standards commitment (Euro 6) explicitly framed as an emissions-reduction initiative.

policy_statement: Adopt GSAS building standards to transition toward green buildings and higher sustainability levels.
source_quote: Qatar has been transforming its building standards towards higher sustainability levels through the adoption of the Global Sustainability Assessment System (GSAS) standards. The number of projects registered for GSAS certifications has been rapidly increasing thereby facilitating the transition towards green buildings.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

d) Building, Construction & Industry
extraction_rationale: This is a standards-based policy intervention (adoption of GSAS) affecting building performance; it is a concrete mechanism even though no numeric target is stated here.

policy_statement: Promote decentralized renewable energy production and use in buildings (including rooftop solar) and improve building energy consumption efficiency.
source_quote: Qatar plans to promote decentralized renewable energy production and use in buildings while also making more efficient their energy consumption. The ongoing development of Lusail city is Qatar's main initiative concerning smart and sustainable cities with centralized water, cooling, waste, and transport systems as well as solar energy production.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

d) Building, Construction & Industry
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit forward-looking commitment to promote decentralized renewables and efficiency in buildings; it names a flagship initiative (Lusail city) as part of implementation.

policy_statement: Advance circular economy practices in construction by recycling and reusing construction waste and exploring battery-powered generators for construction activities.
source_quote: Qatar has been making a steady progress towards attaining circular economy in the construction sector by implementing recycling and re-using construction waste and the government further plans to explore the use of environment friendly battery-powered generators for construction activities.
section_header:
3. Economic Diversification with Mitigation Co-benefits

d) Building, Construction & Industry
extraction_rationale: This describes concrete waste/material efficiency actions (recycling/reuse) and a planned technology shift for construction equipment; climate benefit is plausible but not explicitly quantified.

policy_statement: Reduce per-capita power and water consumption and shift to less energy-intensive technologies across the water value stream as a future priority.
source_quote: In the future, it is essential to reduce the consumption of both power and water per capita and use less energy-intensive technologies throughout the entire value stream.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

a) Water Management
extraction_rationale: This is a stated future commitment direction with specific mechanisms (per-capita reductions; less energy-intensive technologies), though it lacks quantified targets and implementation instruments in this sentence.

policy_statement: Implement a new ambitious water conservation regulation and associated measures (customer awareness messaging, retrofitting aerators in government facilities, switching to treated sewage effluent for park irrigation, and expanding recycled water use).
source_quote: Besides the implementation of a new and ambitious water conservation regulation, several other measures have been started, e.g., increasing awareness via messages to residential customers with high consumption, retrofitting and replacing aerators in governmental facilities and switching to treated sewage effluent (TSE) for irrigation in parks. Additionally, savings are increasingly made by using recycled water in district cooling, the construction industry, and for a growing number of other usages.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

a) Water Management
extraction_rationale: This includes a regulatory instrument (water conservation regulation) plus specific implementation actions; it is framed within adaptation and resource management.

policy_statement: Develop Qatar’s Water Plan and Strategy through a National Water Policy and finalize national water legislation (draft National Water Law and executive by-law; draft law regulating groundwater well drilling).
source_quote: Moreover, as part of the development of Qatar's Water Plan and Strategy, the National Water Policy was developed as the draft of the National Water Law and its executive by-law have been finalized. Furthermore, a draft law to regulate groundwater wells drilling has been completed.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

a) Water Management
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete policy/legislative commitment (water law/by-law; groundwater drilling regulation) supporting water security and climate resilience.

policy_statement: Restore marine habitats by growing mangroves and plant indigenous urban trees to increase carbon sequestration potential.
source_quote: On biodiversity, Qatar is restoring marine habitats, particularly growing mangrove trees, and planting indigenous trees in urban areas and hence increasing the potential for carbon sequestration.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

a) Water Management
extraction_rationale: This is a specific ecosystem intervention (mangroves and indigenous trees) with an explicit carbon sequestration mechanism.

policy_statement: Formulate a comprehensive urban development plan and a sustainable urbanization and population distribution policy guided by Qatar National Vision 2030.
source_quote: Qatar has committed itself to formulating a comprehensive urban development plan and a sustainable urbanization and population distribution policy. The plan, which comprises detailed strategies and operational aspects, is guided by the National Vision 2030 as a general framework.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

b) Infrastructure
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit commitment to produce planning instruments (urban development plan and sustainable urbanization policy) that can embed climate resilience, though climate hazards are not specified in this quote.

policy_statement: Undertake and plan sustainability-focused infrastructure projects including integrated rail, expressways, roads and drainage, and sustainable residential complexes (e.g., Lusail City, Msheireb Downtown).
source_quote: The State of Qatar has undertaken/planned several projects to enhance the overall infrastructure in the country with a strong focus on sustainability. Besides the sustainable stadiums being developed for the FIFA World Cup 2022, several other projects such as the Qatar integrated rail project, expressway program, roads and drainage program, development of sustainable residential complexes (Lusail city, Msheireb downtown), development of parking bays, inter alia hold key to Qatar's plans of sustainable infrastructure development.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

b) Infrastructure
extraction_rationale: This lists specific infrastructure programs/projects with a stated sustainability focus; however, climate objectives are not explicitly stated for each project, making climate relevance partly indirect.

policy_statement: Use media campaigns and broad engagement initiatives to deepen climate change awareness in society.
source_quote: Traditional methods such as media campaigns will be used to spark attention and broad engagement initiatives will be applied to anchor the topic of climate change deeper in society.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

c) Awareness
extraction_rationale: This is a stated planned intervention (campaigns/engagement) aimed at climate awareness; it is a policy-type action but relatively non-specific about scope and implementation.

policy_statement: Implement workplace behavior-change campaigns (e.g., “think before you print,” “save at your desk,” “Paperless office”) to reduce waste and energy consumption.
source_quote: The Foundation has established campaigns like, the 'think before you print,' 'save at your desk,' and 'Paperless office,' that encourage employees on changing printers' settings to minimize waste and incentivize users to further reduce the energy consumption.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

c) Awareness
extraction_rationale: These are specific named campaigns with clear resource-use objectives (waste and energy reduction), though not quantified.

policy_statement: Implement the Qatar Green Building Council’s “No Paper Day” initiative to reduce waste nationwide and reduce paper, plastic, and metal consumption.
source_quote: Other organizations like the Qatar Green Building Council (QGBC) has established a project under the name of 'no paper day' in 2013, that aims to encourage the local community to adopt eco-friendly initiatives geared at reducing waste nationwide and to remind the public that reducing the use of Qatar's resources not only can improve business efficiency, but also help to preserve the environment's long-term health. The initiative is part of QGBC's efforts to help schools, companies, and institutions, find ways to reduce paper, plastic and metal consumption, engage the wider community in environmentally friendly practices, and raise sustainability awareness.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

c) Awareness
extraction_rationale: This is a named initiative with a defined intervention focus (reducing material consumption and waste), which qualifies as a resource-efficiency policy action.

policy_statement: Implement a national food security strategy built on four pillars: trade/logistics, targeted domestic self-sufficiency, strategic reserves, and domestic market enhancement.
source_quote: Qatar has launched a robust national food security strategy to optimize the use of the country's agricultural land and water resources and insulate domestic food needs from external shocks. The strategy focuses on four pillars of enhancing international trade and logistics, increasing domestic self-sufficiency in some niches, building strategic reserves and enhancing domestic markets.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

d) Food Security
extraction_rationale: This is a named national strategy with defined pillars and an explicit resilience rationale (insulating food needs from shocks, including weather-related disasters).

policy_statement: Geographically diversify trade partners for critical commodities and implement contingency plans to limit impacts of trade shocks and disruptions.
source_quote: Under the first pillar of international trade and logistics, Qatar is geographically diversifying trade partners for critical commodities to reduce exposure to external shocks. In addition, Qatar has also proactively put in place contingency plans to limit impacts of trade shocks or other exogenous disruptions.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

d) Food Security
extraction_rationale: These are concrete actions under the food security strategy to reduce vulnerability to shocks; climate linkage is indirect but explicitly tied to external disruptions and resilience framing.

policy_statement: Develop a hydroponics greenhouse cluster to reach 70% self-sufficiency in greenhouse vegetables and support greenhouse production through programs and subsidies.
source_quote: For vegetables production, it has plans to develop its hydroponics greenhouse cluster to reach 70% self-sufficiency on greenhouse vegetables and has launched multiple programs and subsidies towards greenhouse production.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

d) Food Security
extraction_rationale: This includes a quantified target (70% self-sufficiency) and explicit support instruments (programs and subsidies), aimed at resilience and sustainable agriculture.

policy_statement: Establish adequate reserves (including perishables, selected non-perishables, potable water, and groundwater reserves) to buffer against potential production disruptions.
source_quote: Qatar also plans to put in place adequate reserves, including perishables, selected non-perishables, potable water and groundwater reserves to buffer against potential production disruptions.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

d) Food Security
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete preparedness/resilience measure (strategic reserves) explicitly intended to buffer disruptions.

policy_statement: Enhance transparency and efficiency in domestic food markets through farmer support programs, food waste programs, and food standards governance initiatives.
source_quote: Lastly, it is also building transparency and efficiency in its domestic market through farmer support programs, food waste programs and food standards governance initiatives.
section_header:
4. Adaptation actions with Mitigation Co-benefits

d) Food Security
extraction_rationale: This commits to specific program types and governance initiatives; climate relevance is indirect but tied to food-system resilience and efficiency.

policy_statement: Design a National Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) System to measure and validate progress toward NDC commitments using verified sector-specific MRV communications.
source_quote: Governed by the MME Climate Change Department, the National Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) System will be designed to measure and validate progress towards the commitments made in this NDC, using verified sector specific MRV communications prepared by the national stakeholders.
extraction_rationale: This is an institutional implementation commitment (designing an MRV system) that enables accountability for mitigation/adaptation actions; it is a concrete governance mechanism.

policy_statement: Support development and operationalization of Paris Agreement Article 6 to drive sustainable development.
source_quote: Qatar supports the development and operationalization of Article 6 of the Paris Agreement to serve as a driver for sustainable development.
extraction_rationale: This is a policy position/commitment to pursue an international cooperation mechanism (Article 6); it is somewhat general and lacks domestic implementation detail, but it is a concrete stated support for a climate policy instrument.

policy_statement: Reduce sector-based greenhouse gas emissions at least 61% below 1990 levels by 2030.
source_quote:
By integrating these four climate justice commitments, the CAP proposes two ambitious and achievable climate emission reduction targets:

- An interim target of cutting sector-based emissions 61% below 1990 levels by 2030;
section_header: THE PATH TO REACH NET-ZERO BY 2040
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified, time-bound emissions reduction target adopted in the CAP, meeting the criteria for a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Achieve net-zero sector-based greenhouse gas emissions by 2040 (defined as a 90% reduction below 1990 levels).
source_quote:
By integrating these four climate justice commitments, the CAP proposes two ambitious and achievable climate emission reduction targets:

- Net-zero sector-based emissions by 2040, a 90% reduction from 1990 levels
section_header: THE PATH TO REACH NET-ZERO BY 2040
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified, time-bound net-zero target with a defined reduction level, constituting a core mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Reduce consumption-based emissions 40% below 1990 levels by 2030.
source_quote:
In keeping with its commitment to equity, San Francisco is determined to reduce the impacts of these outsourced emissions and has set two targets:

- A 40% reduction in consumption-based emissions by 2030
section_header: THE PATH TO REACH NET-ZERO BY 2040
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified, time-bound target for consumption-based emissions, meeting the policy extraction criteria.

policy_statement: Reduce consumption-based emissions 80% below 1990 levels by 2050.
source_quote:
In keeping with its commitment to equity, San Francisco is determined to reduce the impacts of these outsourced emissions and has set two targets:

- An 80% reduction in consumption-based emissions by 2050
section_header: THE PATH TO REACH NET-ZERO BY 2040
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified, time-bound target for consumption-based emissions, qualifying as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: By 2030, reduce consumption-based emissions to less than 30 mtCO2e per household (equivalent to a 40% reduction compared to 1990 levels).
source_quote: By 2030, reduce consumption-based emissions to less than 30 mtCO2e per household, equivalent to a 40% reduction compared to 1990 levels
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified per-household target with a deadline, providing an operationalized consumption-based mitigation commitment.

policy_statement: By 2050, reduce consumption-based emissions to less than 10 mtCO2e per household (equivalent to an 80% reduction compared to 1990 levels).
source_quote: By 2050, reduce consumption-based emissions to less than 10 mtCO2e per household, equivalent to an 80% reduction compared to 1990 levels
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified per-household target with a deadline, qualifying as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: By 2040, achieve net-zero emissions by reducing emissions at least 90% compared to 1990 levels and sequester residual emissions through nature-based solutions.
source_quote: By 2040, achieve net-zero emissions by reducing emissions at least 90%compared to 1990 levels and sequester any residual emissions through nature- based solutions
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified net-zero target with an explicit sequestration mechanism, making it a policy with both emissions reduction and nature-based removal components.

policy_statement: Supply 100% renewable electricity by 2025.
source_quote: By 2025, supplying 100% renewable electricity, and by 2040, supplying 100% renewable energy (no more fossil fuels).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified, time-bound clean electricity goal, qualifying as a mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Supply 100% renewable energy (no more fossil fuels) by 2040.
source_quote: By 2025, supplying 100% renewable electricity, and by 2040, supplying 100% renewable energy (no more fossil fuels).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified, time-bound fossil-fuel phaseout goal for energy supply, qualifying as mitigation policy.

policy_statement: By 2021, require zero onsite fossil fuel emissions from all new buildings.
source_quote: By 2021, requiring zero onsite fossil fuel emissions from all new buildings, and by 2035, requiring zero onsite fossil fuel emissions from all large existing commercial buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound requirement for new buildings, indicating a regulatory/standards-based policy commitment.

policy_statement: By 2035, require zero onsite fossil fuel emissions from all large existing commercial buildings.
source_quote: By 2021, requiring zero onsite fossil fuel emissions from all new buildings, and by 2035, requiring zero onsite fossil fuel emissions from all large existing commercial buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound requirement for existing large commercial buildings, qualifying as a mitigation policy.

policy_statement: By 2030, increase low-carbon trips to at least 80% of all trips.
source_quote: By 2030, an increase in low-carbon trips to at least 80%of all trips measured and an increase in the level of electrification of vehicles to at least 25%of all private vehicles registered, and by 2040, an increase in the level of electrification of vehicles to 100% of all private vehicles registered.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified transportation mode-share target with a deadline, qualifying as a mitigation policy.

policy_statement: By 2030, electrify at least 25% of all private vehicles registered in San Francisco.
source_quote: By 2030, an increase in low-carbon trips to at least 80%of all trips measured and an increase in the level of electrification of vehicles to at least 25%of all private vehicles registered, and by 2040, an increase in the level of electrification of vehicles to 100% of all private vehicles registered.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified vehicle electrification target with a deadline, qualifying as a mitigation policy.

policy_statement: By 2040, electrify 100% of all private vehicles registered in San Francisco.
source_quote: By 2030, an increase in low-carbon trips to at least 80%of all trips measured and an increase in the level of electrification of vehicles to at least 25%of all private vehicles registered, and by 2040, an increase in the level of electrification of vehicles to 100% of all private vehicles registered.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified vehicle electrification target with a deadline, qualifying as a mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Build at least 5,000 new housing units per year with not less than 30% affordable units, emphasizing retaining and rehabilitating existing housing.
source_quote: Building at least 5,000 new housing units per year with maximum affordability, including not less than 30%affordable units, and with an emphasis on retaining and rehabilitating existing housing.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified housing production and affordability commitment; while not exclusively climate, it is explicitly included as a CAP goal tied to emissions via land use/transport linkages.

policy_statement: By 2030, reduce solid waste generation at least 15% below 2015 levels.
source_quote: By 2030, a reduction in the generation of solid waste of at least 15% below 2015 levels and a reduction in the amount of solid waste disposed of by incineration or deposited in landfill of at least 50%below 2015 levels.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified waste reduction target with a deadline, qualifying as a climate-relevant policy (methane and lifecycle emissions).

policy_statement: By 2030, reduce solid waste disposal by incineration or landfill at least 50% below 2015 levels.
source_quote: By 2030, a reduction in the generation of solid waste of at least 15% below 2015 levels and a reduction in the amount of solid waste disposed of by incineration or deposited in landfill of at least 50%below 2015 levels.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified disposal reduction target with a deadline, qualifying as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Sequester carbon through ecosystem restoration, including increased urban tree canopy, green infrastructure, and compost application.
source_quote: Sequestering carbon through ecosystem restoration, including increased urban tree canopy, green infrastructure, and compost application.
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit commitment to carbon sequestration via ecosystem restoration mechanisms; while not quantified here, it specifies interventions and is framed as a CAP goal.

policy_statement: Update the Climate Action Plan every five years.
source_quote: The CAP must and will be revisited and updated regularly, with a formal update every five years. Transparency is crucial for creating a plan that serves all San Franciscans.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete governance commitment with a defined cadence (every five years) for plan updates.

policy_statement: Create a robust and accessible monitoring, evaluation, and reporting system to track CAP targets, goals, strategies, and actions.
source_quote: To that end, the City will create a robust and accessible monitoring, evaluation, and reporting system to track and review the intended results and real progress of the targets, goals, strategies, and actions. This is essential to monitoring the success and effects of climate actions across the city, quantifying the benefits of the policies, and ensuring stakeholders can actively contribute to progress toward our climate goals.

extraction_rationale: A quantified public transport infrastructure expansion plan with clear metrics and a target year, supporting modal shift and emissions reduction.

into a model walking and cycling town.

## (1) Implement climate change adaptation into all of TMG's initiatives.

The effects of climate change adaptation are appearing in a broad range of fields, including natural disasters, human health, and agriculture, forestry, and fisheries. TMG will address climate change impacts at present and in the future by incorporating climate change adaptation into all relevant initiatives.
extraction_rationale: This is a cross-government commitment to mainstream adaptation into all initiatives (a defined governance action), not just background.

policy_statement: Promote climate change adaptation based on the latest scientific knowledge and actively utilize the latest adaptation technologies.
source_quote:
## (2) Promote climate change adaptation based on scientific knowledge.

TMG will promote adaptation measures based on the latest scientific knowledge. In addition, we will actively utilize the latest technologies related to climate change adaptation.
extraction_rationale: Commits to an evidence-based approach and technology uptake for adaptation; while not quantified, it is a concrete implementation principle guiding policy actions.

policy_statement: Support municipalities' community-based adaptation efforts by actively providing information.
source_quote:
## (3) Support local efforts in cooperation with municipalities.

TMG will support local efforts by actively providing information so that municipalities can develop their community-based initiatives.
extraction_rationale: Defines a specific governmental support function (information provision) to enable municipal adaptation initiatives.

policy_statement: Develop a system to collect and provide adaptation information and actively disseminate climate risk information to Tokyo residents.
source_quote:
## (4) Promote dissemination of information, including risks, to facilitate understanding of Tokyo residents.

TMG will develop a system to collect and provide information on climate change adaptation and actively disseminate the information.
extraction_rationale: Commits to establishing an information system and dissemination activities—an operational policy instrument supporting adaptation.

policy_statement: Accelerate intercity collaboration on climate impacts and countermeasures through C40 and other organizations.
source_quote:
## (5) Promote international cooperation in C40 and other organizations to accelerate intercity collaboration.

TMG will accelerate intercity collaboration by utilizing organizations in which TMG has membership, such as C40 1 , in order to share knowledge.
extraction_rationale: A defined cooperation mechanism (C40 and similar networks) to share knowledge on climate impacts/countermeasures; implementation-oriented even if not quantified.

policy_statement: Promote utilization of state-of-the-art technologies and development of urban facilities for floods, storm surges, and landslides through structural and non-structural measures.
source_quote:
In response to natural threats, such as floods, inland floods, storm surges, and landslides due to intensified heavy rains and typhoons, TMG will promote the utilization of state-of-the-art technologies and the development of urban facilities in both structural and non-structural aspects.

To cope with increasingly larger typhoons and more frequent heavy rains in recent years, TMG will further improve our initiatives.
